InfoDisplay_102802002_Text:
(A tourism guide penned by the Pioneer Association. But the column about Egla Town hasn't been updated in quite a while.)

[The Next Big Travel Hot Spot]: Egla Town!
For those brave enough to venture to the place that inspired the adventurous plays during the Carnevale, exploring the legendary realm of the mighty "giant," listening to the songs echoing from the sea of clouds by the water, or following in the footsteps of knights in pursuit of honor and justice will no longer be mere fantasies. In Egla Town, travelers can immerse themselves in breathtaking waterside scenery, observe the majestic migration of Tumbleyaks, and watch windmills spin gracefully on the plains, while bathing in the golden light of the setting sun. Alternatively, they can simply enjoy a peaceful afternoon tea and indulge in century-old delicacies, all while being surrounded by the vibrant colors of blooming flowers.

[Dreamy Destinations] Nimbus Sanctum!
In this edition of [Dreamy Destinations], we journey to the mesmerizing Nimbus Sanctum hidden deep within Whisperwind Haven. A highlight of the enchanting Gondola cruise, the sea of clouds has long been a must-see destination, captivating visitors with its ethereal, dreamlike vistas.
Yet, few are aware that the Atrium of Reflections—often depicted in romantic tales—is not merely a creation of fiction, but the ruins of the highest spire of ancient Ragunna. To save its people, Napoli the Second invoked a miracle, turning the Dark Tide into the very sea of clouds that graces the land today.
The forgotten ruins of old Egla Town are now submerged beneath the sea of clouds.

[The Journey is the Destination] Embark Today!
It's worth noting that, although the reason remains unclear, the water level of Nimbus Sanctum has been steadily rising over the past decade, forcing the residents of Egla Town to move to the higher ground in the north.
Once, this area was a barren, undeveloped land, scattered with exposed boulders, and known as the Whisperwind Barrens.
However, the resourceful people of Egla Town began to build windmills that turned day and night, drawing water from the lower regions to nourish the land above. Their efforts transformed this rugged place into the thriving Whisperwind Haven we see today, where crops and flowers now flourish in the breeze.

[Column Memories] Voice of Travelers!
Your Egla column hasn't been updated since last Carnevale. It's just the same article over and over. You guys can't afford to pay the writer or something?
Could it be that no one's interested in Egla Town? Really? Am I actually right?

(A short novel published ten years ago.
"An outrageous best-seller, banned by the Order three times!"
"Only one-tenth of readers truly understand it—are you one of them?"
"Incredible! The Russellian's satire remains as insightful as ever, even after all these years!"
So reads the editor's recommendation page… Clearly, this book stirred up quite a bit of controversy a decade ago.)

Far out across the stormy waters filled with jagged ridges and giant beasts on the surface of Solaris lies a group of small, unregarded islands. On this archipelago, the exiles-descended cultures are so amazing that they still think a unified thought is a pretty neat idea. These islands have—or rather had a problem, which was this: most of the people on them were unhappy for pretty much of the time.

After retirement, I kept thinking back to that afternoon when my friend and I first met.
Ford Percival. He was an alien.
On his first day in Egla Town, he ate ten baton bread without paying anything. Before the Divine Envoys could punish him for theft, I quickly paid off his debt.
Since the prayer, the Oracle of Mercy had wandered in my mind in search of something to connect with—until I met him, the poor outlander. He must have been starving.
"Hi, I'm Ford. I'm an alien. I'm analyzing your weapons. Quite odd components."
He said after I saved him. "And what is this place?" he continued.
An alien? Oh, I'd heard this kind of tale once from someone who claimed to be from a federation. He said Solaris was actually a living tomato—a tomato that could turn, breathe, even dance. And aliens, apparently, were from other tomatoes, living or dead.
"Egla Town," I replied.
"Egla Town, good. Wait, what is that?" He pointed at the windmills in the distance.
"Those are windmills. A cluster of Cyclop windmills, Briareos." Born and raised in Egla, I replied almost instinctively.
"C-Cyclops! Ah, I know about those! I've seen them before! But my stars—you actually managed to kill them? How did you people pull that off? Are those auto-rotating arrays made from their dead bodies? And what exactly is Briareos? A cooling device? A propeller engine? Or something to open up a network channel?"

(Continued)

After hearing my explanation, the self-proclaimed alien Ford seemed completely fascinated by the Cyclops. His emotions became so agitated that he plopped down on the ground, muttering some unintelligible words while pointing at the windmills in the distance.
So it was true—no matter where they came from, no matter what "tomatoes" they hailed from, anyone who laid eyes on the scenery of Egla couldn't help but fall in love with the chivalric literature.
So I straightened up, took three steps forward, and adjusted the nonexistent necktie, then explained graciously, "Exactly! That's right! Once, a righteous knight guided us to defeat the giant. Before that, all the people and Echoes in Egla Town were driven to the high ground in the south, fleeing from the giant's threat. Now, that oppressor lies buried beneath the sea of flowers. We built majestic windmills to irrigate the flowers and the farmlands, and named our past home Briareos, in honor of that knight's heroic deeds!"
After hearing my speech, Ford sat frozen on the ground, as if ten thousand Cetus the Tidebreakers had roared at him all at once, shattering his perception.
After a long pause, he asked me in disbelief, "Do you still have knights here?"
What did he just ask me?
Praise be to Imperator!
I could finally deliver the ranked No. 1 answer in the Top 10 Most Satisfying Moments for Egla People.
Putting on a solemn expression like the Acolytes of the Order, I envisioned a halo of nobility above my head, envisioned the almighty Imperator spreading wings before me, envisioned myself crowning a laurel at the Carnevale, envisioned standing in the grand church, wielding a sword as I was knighted, relishing the reverent gazes of the noble lords of Ragunna!
I replied, stressing each word with great emphasis:
"OF COURSE—"
"However, there are too many outsiders who seek the path of knighthood. Are you confident enough to accept the trial?"
The alien named Ford, whose Tacet Mark was blinking along excitedly, quickly grabbed my calf and shook it furiously, as if clinging to a log in the midst of a drowning. He cried out, "I am! I am! Please guide me to the legendary knight! As long as I can return to the planet Russel and save my hometown, I am willing to pay any price!"

(The trial chapters end now. Please make a purchase to continue reading.)

(A feature on the culinary traditions of Ragunna.)

[Top Chef's Super Secrets]
Imagine yourself asking anyone on the streets of Ragunna, "Which restaurant is the best in Ragunna?"
Six out of ten will answer, "Trattoria Margherita!" Three will point to the family restaurant downtown, and the last one will say, "It's the place where the soft-tailed chef works!"
That's right! Such is the clout of Trattoria Margherita in Ragunna!
Amazing!
But what many don't know is that Trattoria Margherita is actually a family-run restaurant inspired by traditional Ragunna cuisine. From our investigation, we found that Egla Town still preserves this classic culinary tradition to this day. To maintain the special flavors of her dishes, Miss Margherita even takes time off to gather ingredients in Egla Town or Riccioli Islands!
Now, you might be wondering: "What? I can understand why Miss Margherita would go to Riccioli Islands for the fish harvest, but Egla Town? Isn't that a backwater town? And can the cuisine of Egla really be called Ragunna cuisine?"
Indeed, life in Egla isn't as thrilling as in the bustling Ragunna. People there live quietly, following the rhythm of nature. The town's trade and logistics are tied to Ragunna City. The people rise with the wind and rest by it, living a life shaped by windmills, wheat farms, and pastures.
But that's exactly why, for hundreds of years, the cuisine of Egla has remained unchanged. Here, the original flavors and cooking techniques of Ragunna have been preserved—using windmills to process crops and cooking food in traditional ways.
"This way, the ingredients and the food are especially precious! The cheese made from local pastures is creamy, and the meat is tender and flavorful! It's the perfect food to fill your belly!"
Miss Margherita commented during our interview.

[Comments from Special Guests]
Former Tax Envoy of the Order: The traditional cuisine is a remembrance of Rinascita's past. To forget it is to betray our heritage!
Orlando the Gourmet: The old man earlier sounded like he was chanting a slogan! What traditional cuisine? The bread from your town is as hard as a lethal weapon!
InfoDisplay_102802003_Text:
Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part I)
...

At dawn, the Primus and I stood to bid farewell to the Pilgrim's Sail as it prepared to depart. Both the crowd and the acolytes watched with reverence as the believers boarded the ship. Only the most devout and courageous among them were chosen to embark on the Pilgrim's Sail, destined to meet the Sentinel in the distant sea.

For countless ages, Sentinel Imperator has rarely lingered in any one place, choosing instead to roam the seas, aiding vessels on their journeys. The Sentinel's guiding light has always led those lost upon the waves, helping them find their way back home or seek new lands for settlement. The Order believes that to face the storms and tides in search of the Sentinel's heavenly voice is one of the greatest honors a soul can aspire to.

Yet only those with practical experience can grasp the immense cost of each pilgrimage. Taxes and provisions are drawn from the commoners, skilled workers and sailors are taken from prominent families, and seasoned captains and chief mates are hired at great expense. All who embark on these treacherous seas are devout, but only those truly blessed by the Sentinel return with the promised glory and honor. Reflecting on history, the number of such fortunate souls is vanishingly small.

I have never questioned the purpose of the pilgrimage. My only concern is the immense cost it demands. Can we, in good conscience, allow these devoted believers to embark on a journey that burdens both mind and body? And as for our new Primus... What are his thoughts on this matter?

I looked to my side, surprised to find that my former seminary classmate, Lord Fenrico, had his face shrouded in a strange shadow.

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part II)
...

How has it come to this? After a sleepless night, I retreated to a secluded prayer room, seeking solace as I lay my confession before Sentinel Imperator. My hands trembled as I put these words to paper.

For a time, the Order ceased organizing large-scale pilgrimages, and the burdensome taxes were lifted. Though the people of Ragunna still honored the devotion of those who once sought the Sentinel across the distant seas, the Pilgrim's Sails had become a relic of the past. But everything changed after the bloody Carnevale... No, in truth, the shift began even earlier than that...

I still remember when the Primus delivered the order for correction, and I dutifully transcribed it: the Order would send violators of doctrine aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, stripping them of all official identities and setting them back onto the path of pilgrimage. Who could have foreseen that an act once meant to embody faith would come to serve as a form of punishment?

"The power of punishment and indoctrination shall be returned to the Sentinel," the Primus proclaimed to the assembled crowd. "Those transgressors who embark upon the pilgrimage in sincere repentance will, by their journey's end, be absolved of all transgressions and granted the Sentinel's forgiveness."

Yet no one truly knows if transgressors can fulfill their salvation, for no one has ever returned from the pilgrimage alive. "Those who commit acts of foolishness shall be sent to the Pilgrim's Sails"—this has become a steadfast law of the Order Penitentiary. Vandals defacing sacred statues, disloyal acolytes distorting doctrines, and even troupe members crafting satirical comedies—all have been condemned to the Pilgrim's Sails for their acts of blasphemy. Recently, however, familiar faces have joined their ranks, faces of those who had openly questioned the Primus's decrees.

I could have sworn my integrity on their faith and character, yet I stood by and watched as they were sent aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, doing nothing. No, it's no longer fitting to call them the Pilgrim's Sails. The common folk have given them a more appropriate name—the Fool's Sails, a vessel filled with those who have committed foolish acts.

Oh, Primus Fenrico... Is this the dream world you so passionately spoke of in the seminary?

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part III)
...

I was surprised at how calm I felt upon hearing the sentence from the Order Penitentiary. Perhaps my heart had grown as still as that of a dead person.

At dawn, like others before me, I was escorted by the Executors to board a Fool's Sail. Before the ship set sail, I glanced back at the port, only to find the Primus absent. Just as I expected, that man, now in control of unmatched power within the Order, has no need to concern himself with a fool stripped of his identity.

The Fool's Sails are nothing like the Pilgrim's Sails of old. Gone are the smooth, spacious decks and well-maintained sails. Instead, all I saw were rickety planks, loose screws, and splintered masts. The narrow cabins clearly lacked food and fresh water. I stared blankly at the other pilgrims around me. For now, we still manage to maintain some semblance of decorum and restraint, but I know that, before long, this ship will become nothing more than a cage filled with rampaging desires.

And even if we do reach the so-called destination, what awaits us there?

I once read the investigation reports sent back by the expatriate acolytes. That Penitent's End, shrouded in mist, is littered with the wrecks of Pilgrim's Sails. During those fateful voyages, the Fools who braved the storms never met the Sentinel. Instead, driven by the sea's undercurrents, they were cast ashore on that island, where the eerie glow of phosphorescence mingles with an unmistakable aura of death. I've even heard whispers of something far more terrifying lurking there, and the "Fire of Judgment"—a force so dreadful that even the Privy Council dares not speak of it.

...

Food is running out... Last night, someone lost control again, trying to lock themselves in the cabin to hoard the dwindling supplies...

O great Imperator, if you can hear my prayer, please grant us your final mercy through a storm. Absolve us from our misery, and let us... find peace at last.

(The remainder of the notes has been blurred by the seawater and is unreadable.)
InfoDisplay_102802004_Text: A Transgressor's Transcript (Part I) In the ancient era, long before Ragunna was founded, the distant seas of Rinascita were the Realm of A Thousand Islands. At that time, the Fisalia family was already well-versed in the ways of the ocean. We extracted toxins and medicines from deep-sea plants, harnessed vast underwater resources, and reveled in great fortune and widespread renown. Later, with the assault of the Lament, the civilization of the archipelago teetered on the brink of destruction and our family became one of the founders of the Ark, embarking on a quest to find a new settlement. The journey across the sea was treacherous. The fleets of the Ark were either swallowed by thick fog or torn apart by fierce storms. Yet, our family's Ark, guided by a heavenly voice, led the fleet to a lush archipelago, following the faint glow of a distant lighthouse. One of those islands would later become what is now Ragunna. The newly founded Ragunna was still in a state of flux. To strengthen the family's rule, our family head declared that the manifestation of ▇▇▇▇ was a symbol of the deep-sea faith and a response from the marine divinity to our devotion. This proclamation proved to be successful. As the number of believers grew, so too did the stability of our family's power. Later, some fishermen claimed that they had been assisted by ▇▇▇▇ during their fishing trips. This entity, long known as the Giant One, had existed for ages. Its shadow beneath the sea guided Ragunna's fishermen and fleets, helping them weather storms and bringing in harvests far greater than before. The Fisalia family was the original ruler of Ragunna, and we also laid the faith foundation of the Order. Yet, why have generations of family heads chosen to conceal this history? Why can't I remember Its name? Cursed be it, the wound... it is throbbing again. Something must be wrong with the air... I must find a safer place. The soldiers will never think to search for me in the tower. I must document this secret history... before it slips from my mind entirely... A Transgressor's Transcript (Part II) The fishermen referred to the shadow in the sea as ▇▇▇▇, and they would call upon its sacred name to receive its aid. Small miracles began to accumulate, forming a powerful current of faith. The common folk grew increasingly convinced that the Giant One was, indeed, ▇▇▇▇. As the family began to investigate, they were shocked to discover that these miraculous occurrences differed greatly from those recorded in the past. So, what was the true form of the Giant One the people had placed their faith in? And what, exactly, was the true object of our devotion? This mysterious faith was quietly reshaping the history of Ragunna, and it even threatened our family's control over the Order of the Deep. Only the Ark forebears and our family heads knew that ▇▇▇▇ should be the true form of ▇▇. Yet, with the preaching of the Order, the common folk, unaware of the truth, began to place their faith even more in ▇▇▇▇. Meanwhile, rumors spread that the true form of ▇▇▇▇ was that of a fish-like deity. What's even stranger was that those who heard these rumors began to dream of ▇▇▇▇ in the form of ▇▇. Is this text truly the same record I once read in the secret chamber of the family head? I have an unsettling feeling that my hands are writing down the history about ▇▇▇▇ on their own. Ah, I remember now... Yes, even I, who have never set sail on the sea, was drawn into that dream as I fled. Beneath the tranquil surface of the sea, a giant dark shadow loomed, and my fishing boat felt like a mere sampan before it... Impossible... That impure, blasphemous form could not have been the object of my faith all this time. I must reveal the truth to the world. A Transgressor's Transcript (Part III) After the death of Napoli the Second, the Order of the Deep elected a new Primus. The spread of the faith surpassed all previous reach. Yet, the doctrines proclaimed by the Acolytes were tainted by a dark mist. Everything related to ▇▇▇▇ began to twist—its statues, its anecdotes, and even its proverbs... No one has ever suspected this mass hallucination. No one has ever resisted the dissipation of the form, for "every drop of water will eventually return to the sea." Who is speaking in the "head" on my neck? Silence, you blasphemous thing! Where's my pen? No, it's in my hand. But is it truly my hand? Why is there black... blood dripping from it? In the face of these changes, our family remained eerily silent, even turning a blind eye to the Order slipping beyond our control. Many members of the Fisalia family were tormented by strange nightmares... They all saw the giant fish shadow beneath the sea and awoke in terror, screaming. (The text becomes illegible, and the paper is marked with scratches of unknown meaning.) I hear "sacred songs" flowing from my mouth. The sound of wet scratches echoes on the floor. The ancient blood still flows within me. IT is here... IT is everywhere... Some abandoned the family, becoming devout believers of the Order. Some ventured to Septimont and never spoke of the faith again, while others settled near the seaport, growing detached from the other forces. Oh, the poor Fisalias—once powerful, once surrounded by allies—reduced to this. Cast away the innate fears, and I no longer doubt that It is ▇▇▇▇, and ▇▇▇▇ is It—they are one and the same. In the depths of reason, I feel an indescribable joy. O my glorious Fisalia, the shadows of my people are approaching, guiding me to the deep sea. It is calling me. Praise be to ▇▇▇▇.
InfoDisplay_102802005_Text: Excerpts from The Hammer of Heresy (The pamphlet presents several radical opinions that appear to reflect the theories of an extreme school of thought.) What is witchcraft? And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? A Letter of Complaint on Heresy Esteemed Lord Acolyte, I, Charles Tornatore, hereby report a heretical action—an underground troupe by the name of Panacea, which has dared to reenact the banned play The Flying Ragunnesi, adding numerous malicious metaphors and imagery of blasphemy. I have transcribed the following lines to the best of my memory: "The Primus's words are like pickled spells. Even a Gondola will tingle upon hearing them." —From Act I, Scene 1 Can't the baton bread in my hand be strong enough to smash our enemies of faith? —From Act I, Scene 3 (Note: This line, spoken by an Acolyte, degrades the Order's holy instrument, referring to it as mere bread.) By Imperator above, please witness our love, as beautiful as the morning light. —From Act II, Scene 1 (Note: This line marks the elopement of the male and female protagonists.) ... I regret that I cannot recall all the blasphemous lines from the play. How dare these individuals defile our noble faith in such a manner? Though they hid behind masks during the performance, I was able to identify them by their forms and voices. It is no surprise that they serve the Montelli family (A detailed list of names is attached). Praise be to Imperator.
InfoDisplay_102802006_Text: The Old Codex of Holy Rituals Chapter 2 Verse 17 2:17 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And lo, from the storm, the mass heard the voice of Imperator. 2:18 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Imperator said, Come ye forth, to the east. 2:19 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Sentinel Imperator cast forth a light through the rain and the waves. The mass followed the light and sailed through the mist and the storm. 2:20 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And the light, it came from the lighthouse upon the distant archipelago, where the warm currents meet, and where spices grow, and where golden fruit trees abound. 2:21 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] But from the mist behind them, dreadful Tacet Discords did pursue and tread upon the thunder, and the people cried out in wailing. 2:22 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] Then said Sentinel Imperator, I shall bring salvation. 2:23 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And the Genesis Nexus cast forth a radiant light, and the Tacet Discords were swallowed up by the lighthouse. And when Sentinel Imperator called them forth once more, they became Divine Envoys. 2:24 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Sentinel Imperator said, wherever the Genesis Nexus shines, there shall the Divine Envoys dwell. The Genesis Nexus shall be my hand. I am the lighthouse of Rinascita, Sentinel Imperator. 2:25 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] For hundreds of years, the multitude hath followed Their precepts. 2:26 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] The Divine Envoys have shown their strength to uphold Their will. 2:27 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] To the followers, regard these as Imperator's blessing and spirit. 2:28 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] Love the Divine Envoys, as ye love your family, your brothers and sisters, and your neighbors. 2:29 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] We carry out the holy sacraments in memory of this. The New Codex of Holy Rituals Chapter 5 Verse 2 5:03 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] They desired to deliver the Oracle, and so They inscribed the sacred words upon the oak tree, and from the Oracle, the first Viscum Berry did grow. 5:04 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] The berry is the essence of Imperator's wisdom. Partake of it, and your eyes shall be opened, that ye may discern between good and evil, and hearken unto its precepts. 5:05 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] Such is wisdom. 5:06 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] They turned the Dark Tide into a sea of clouds, and they cleansed the damaged Nuvola Fruit tree. 5:07 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] The healing resin is the sacred tears; it mends and restores. Breathe in the Mastic Nuvola, and the divinity within shall mend the frailty of humanity. 5:08 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] Such is divinity. (The next two lines seem to have been smeared and are not legible.) 5:09 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] The third sacred meal ascended to the heavens with Them. Such is the transgression of the Fisalias. 5:10 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] They taught us to prick our fingers with ▇ ▇ ▇ and to mix the ▇ ▇ into the sacred wine. And so shall we be as brothers, and none shall be set apart. 5:11 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] Such is the spirit. The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation Chapter 1 Verse 9 1:09 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] On that day, Napoli's brows and his hair were white like wool, as white as snow, and his eyes were as a flame of fire. 1:10 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] And They granted unto Napoli the lantern, like bronze glowing in a furnace, and the lantern echoed with the voices of the Divine Envoys. 1:11 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] Napoli lifted the lantern high in his return, like the sun shining in all its brilliance. 1:12 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] And the Tacet Discords of the Dark Tide bowed before him. He raised his right hand and spoke to the people: "Fear not. I am the Enlightened One of Sentinel Imperator. I am the first and the last, the beginning and the end. I can hear Their voice." 1:13 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] "I died, and behold I am alive forevermore, and I hold the keys to Heaven and Hell." 1:14 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] "Behold the light in my hand. The Lantern shall be the authority that connects us with Imperator." 1:15 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] Let who has ears hear: 1:16 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] And I heard, by the choirs and the trumpets beside Sentinel Imperator, a voice saying unto me, "Come up here, and I will show you what must take place after this." 1:17 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] At once I was in the spirit, and there before me was a throne on the sea. And a Divine Envoy stood forth and proclaimed, Who is worthy to take this lantern and let its light shine upon the world? 1:18 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] Then I wept greatly, for before the throne of Imperator stood the Divine Envoys, some appearing as though they had been slain, others covered with spikes. Then I heard Imperator say in a voice like thunder, "Come!" 1:19 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] After this I looked, and behold, a white horse with only half a body. It commanded me to lift my lantern and pray, that people may come to know one another and be granted victory upon victory.
InfoDisplay_102802007_Text: A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama (with Commentary) A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama: The Evolution of Tribal Cultural Fusion and Faith Systems Written by: DeLillo Quentin Proposed Grant: Ragunna Dramatic Association Regional Research Project - Aspire Scholars Grant Avinoleum Theological Seminary, Ragunna, Rinascita Abstract: This paper reviews recent research trends and developments regarding the origins of drama culture in the Ragunna and Septimont regions, with a particular focus on advancements in the "archaeology of drama" over the past decade. Drawing on the diverse research and perspective studies from the New Federation in recent years, the paper also incorporates insights from Huanglong's archaeological experience in studying historical relics. The case studies selected focus primarily on classic plays and significant historical events. The findings suggest that Ragunnesi drama culture originated from narrative performances that documented the history and life of island tribes. Keywords: history of drama, cultural studies, review, folklore studies, archaeology ...(Some of the pages are missing) As illustrated in key literature such as Chronicles of Avinoleum and The Golden Bough, the origin of drama is directly tied to the faith of Sentinel Imperator. However, technical studies of stage design, costumes, makeup, masks, and props, as found in both historical and modern literature, as well as translated foreign texts, reveal that much remains to be explored regarding the evolution of drama as a reflection of life and folklore. For instance, the Montelli Culture Foundation's Cultural Characteristics and Cultural Reconstruction in Translation: A Case Study of the Journey to Rinascita Collected in Huanglong examines the transition from folk traditions to their textual and stage representations in drama, focusing on the evolution of the translated texts. Seminary Commentary: Please do not submit the anecdotal piece for Almanacs and the Occult to our foundation. Additionally, food security must be more strictly managed to prevent potential nervous breakdowns among students caused by consuming spoiled bell crabs. ...(Some of the pages are missing) The people of Rinascita during the Age of a Thousand Islands used costumes to represent the origins of different tribes, masks to symbolize ancestors and totems, and various tribal languages to interact and communicate with one another during the Carnevale in the form of drama. This process continued until a fusion and mutual understanding among the tribes was achieved. After numerous adaptations and reinterpretations of folklore and legends, it eventually evolved into the prototype of the Ragunnesi drama, which remains popular today. Mentor Commentary: It is recommended to omit some of the details and avoid excessive research, as the paper will be reviewed by the Chamber of Enlightenment of the Order. A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design (This handwritten notebook is almost completely torn, with only a few pages from the Epilogue remaining.) Epilogue: I would like to dedicate this paper to my friends who have supported me, to those who have secretly provided invaluable literature for my research, to the work of my father, DeLillo Quentin, to the exile granted to me by the Order of the Deep, and to the expulsion by Avinoleum Theological Seminary. This paper, titled "A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design," has taken four years to complete, from its inception to the eve of my exile, and I have finally finished the first draft. I hope my friends can read it, as I originally intended. Tomorrow morning, I will leave Ragunna aboard the Pilgrim's Sail, just as my father did, in search of the Sentinel—Praise be to Imperator! If I survive, I hope you, the omnipresent Imperator, will guide my way. ...When I was a child, my father, DeLillo, said to me before he left, "Little Quentin, do you know what humans are?" I knew that would be my father's last words to me, so I replied that I didn't know. Father then said, "Keep doing your best, Mario Quentin. Humans are a blade of thinking seagrass." I didn't understand why humans would be compared to a blade of seagrass. But now, I think I understand what father meant—don't stop thinking and don't stop searching. The islands of the past were destroyed in the Lament. Under Imperator's guidance, our ancestors boarded the Ark and voyaged far, eventually establishing Rinascita on the land it now occupies. During the Age of a Thousand Islands, to commemorate their lost homes and honor their tribespeople in the Lament, people began to wear the costumes of their tribes and masks symbolizing their ancestors and totems. As concluded in Chapter 4 of this paper, the culture of drama has never been a blessing promised by the Order. Rather, it is a commemoration and symbol developed independently by the people of Rinascita. But are we truly just a blade of seagrass? If so, there must be a distinction between the seagrass that flows with the waves and those that can think independently, right? People praise the name of Imperator for its mercy and its encompassing nature, for preserving the culture that unites people from different tribes, helping them merge and support one another. They praise Imperator for the will to unite the vast patch of seagrasses to defy the currents of the Lament. Praise be to Imperator! We exalt you! But have the Ragunnesi of today truly executed your true will? Ah, great Imperator! I don't want to die... I really don't... I wish I could attend the Carnevale one more time... I'm truly terrified... Please, don't turn me into a blade of seagrass tomorrow! Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Can freedom, once indoctrinated, still be considered freedom? ...(Some of the pages are missing) [23] Charlie Welbeck, "The History of Reforms on the Rinascita Drama Aesthetics," published by Avinoleum Theological Seminary Culture Journal. [24] Mario Quentin, "A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design," published by Foreign Culture Studies Publishing House. [25] Cosimo Sorrentino, "A Study on the Readership of The Golden Bough," published by Ragunna Dramatic Association.

Timeworn Logbook 1
Logbook_Number_#00
Mom, have you ever seen a Nimbus Wraith? I saw one for the first time today, and it was incredible.
I'm so excited. I don't really know who to share this with, so I'm writing it down here.
Today feels like a real turning point for me.
Starting today, I'm working for the Montelli family. I'm part of the Montellis now, and from now on, people will call me by that name.
The gate to Rinascita has finally opened for me.
Even though I'm in a cabin right now, thousands of miles away from home, as long as I'm working under the Montelli name and wearing this uniform, maybe one day I'll have my own place in the Montelli Quarter in Ragunna.
Mom, I think I finally get why the Montelli name is so well-known across Rinascita.
While other noble families sell positions or goods, the Montellis sell hope.
I'm about to get really busy, and I'm adjusting to the job just fine. The only problem is there's just me as the security guard on board, so there's no one to talk to.
I'm going to work hard, and when I come back, I'll bring you to Ragunna so you can enjoy life here too.

Timeworn Logbook 2
Logbook_Number_#17
Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Timeworn Logbook 3
Logbook_Number_#29
Mom, don't worry. I'll be home and see you soon.
The day before yesterday was so cloudy, and I bet the Nimbus Wraiths were feeling pretty gloomy. We weren't supposed to set sail, but with the auction coming up, I have to make sure the item gets delivered on time.
This mission was given to me by the Montellis, and I can't let them down.
It's a bit of a detour, but since all the ships have already left and the Order sent Lucerna on board, I think it should be fine.
Don't worry. The Montelli family added more people to the crew, and with the Order's presence, everything will be okay. Yeah, it'll be fine.
I should tell you something to lift your spirits. Once I'm done with this job, I should have some time off to come and visit you.
Even though my job keeps me in the cabins, I get to see a lot of interesting things along the route.
Here, they don't use words like sunny or cloudy to describe the weather. Instead, they use emotions, which is kind of interesting, don't you think?
When it's "happy," we get to see rainbows, and the Nimbus Wraiths even dance under them.
When it's "gloomy," like today, it's cloudy, and we usually get to take the rest of the day off.
A "forced smile" is when it's sunny, but with a hint of rain. At times like that, the train picks up speed on purpose, and some of my colleagues will start telling loud jokes from the back of the train.
When it's "sorrowful," it rains, and the train moves very slowly.
"Unhappy" weather means thunder or strong winds. On days like that, we definitely take the day off. I just sleep through it.
And then there's "angry" weather, which is the scariest. The entire sea of clouds turns red. If we encounter that in the middle of the journey, our superiors make us wear soundproof earmuffs to work.
According to the route map, we'll be passing through a place called the Atrium of Reflections. I'd never heard of it before, but the seniors say we usually avoid it unless it's absolutely necessary.
I'll be careful, though. Don't worry about me. It's just a small challenge. Tough jobs need to be done, right?
As long as I put in the effort, I know I'll get the reward I deserve. Just wait for me, Mom. I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Timeworn Logbook 4
Logbook_Number_#31
Mom, when I get back, can I just hug you for a bit?
I've gone through the entire safety manual, but I didn't find anything about the situation I'm facing right now.
Do you remember, Mom? When I was little, and the wind picked up at night, I was always scared. It was actually because of the gauzy curtain in my room. It had the patterns of people praying in the Order embroidered on it. When the night breeze blew, the shadows of those figures would flutter as if they might break apart.
I thought I saw them in real life just now. A group of people was kneeling by the side of the train, as if they were praying with their heads lowered.
They were staring at the train, and I couldn't bring myself to look back. They were mumbling something... I finally found the soundproof earmuffs.
It's okay. Maybe I'm just too nervous. The Lucernas from the Order are still here. They'll figure something out.
By Imperator above, we will arrive safely.
(The words are illegible due to being soaked in water.)
...Mom... I will... bring you... to Ragunna.
By Imperator above
By Imperator above
By Imperator above
By Imperator above... I'm safe!
(Trembling handwriting)
I made it! I'm safe now!
But what exactly... are these things...?

... very few people, including those within the Montelli family know when the Vitreum Dancers first appeared, even though these unobtrusive, unremarkable Echoes have long served the family. In fact, most of the Montellis do not know of Vitreum Dancers as anything other than their domestic security detail. Thus it remains easily overlooked that no two Vitreum Dancers are alike.

Knowledge gleaned from the stained-glass artwork found in the ruins around Ragunna suggests that Vitreum Dancers were once Tacet Discord frequencies. They appear in stained-glass art along with general depictions of The Order's religion. To this day Montelli explorers have yet to find two identical panes of stained glass. The Order's artists took pains to alter the composition of panes that depict the same story or motif. This suggests that the frequencies of modern Vitreum Dancers each contain unique information, much like their Tacet Discord forbearers.

According to the book "The Wealth and Legend of the Montellis," the origin of the Vitreum Dancer dates back in history to a time when a Montelli ancestor received the Laurel during the Carnevale from Imperator who then instructed him to go to a tower abandoned by The Order. Upon his return, he would not divulge what he saw and forbade all Montellis from approaching the tower again. Undoubtedly this Montelli ancestor brought back the very first Vitreum Dancer. On his deathbed, his last words were that the Sentinel's Oracle would not exert influence over Montellis at present, but would determine their future course of events.

And with that the tower was barred to all subsequent Montelli, and as the family's cohort of Vitreum Dancers expanded, the legend of their origins faded into obscurity.
InfoDisplay_120101028_Title: A Lost Page from a Diary
InfoDisplay_120101028_Text:
...We still haven't found it today.
 
Such a large creature can't easily hide its tracks. Until we discover the location of its next appearance, we must not approach the shore, and no storm can stop us.
 
The roaring sea, the storm as black as the ink spewed by a dying squid, the deck swaying in the tempest, masts drifting towards the shipwrecks in the Forgotten Sea, sailors with faces weathered by time, as deep and cracked as the ocean's trenches, the hundred-meter-long octopus... And we, the cursed hunters who pursue it to the ends of the earth.
 
Think about it, what do we truly seek? I'll wager you this coin nailed into my leg.
 
Now I will tell you how we shall achieve victory. We will chase it, across the Stormy Sea, through the Forgotten Sea, past every island, both named and unnamed, to the ends of the earth. Its blood and oil will make this coin worth a fortune.
 
You, the spearman from the East, when you offer your spear to the gods, will you hesitate? Will the spear that once drank the blood of gods falter when facing the ocean? Come, raise your weapons high and cross them before me, just as you would in the arena! Let me see what glory you will embrace upon the waves!
 
Bring me wine! Come, let us swear an oath to riches, to our dreams, to all that we've left behind!
 
What we seek, what I seek… is that moment.
InfoDisplay_120101029_Title: A Lost Page from a Diary
InfoDisplay_120101029_Text: I saw it. There is no doubt. That long horn, dripping with the pitch-black blood of the sea. It has to be it. The boat we launched was capsized, its aft mast broken, and seven spears were lost. Many people were frightened and urged me to turn back... No, I will not stop. Of the seven spears, four were shaken off, but the other three lodged in its body. I saw them in its back, and the shattered crystals fell into the sea. This is day fifty-five. We are not chasing it; rather, it is standing in our way. Don't you understand? Only by killing it can we leave this room and reach the end of the infinite sea, to the place promised to us by the sails. Think! We have conquered every sea! From the Tacetite-eating Wyrm of the New Federation to the memory-devouring Dreadcurl Cuttle of the Forgotten Sea... How many of these things have I killed? Have we killed? Now this thing is in front of us! Every dream and thought that crosses your mind should be how to kill it! Give me that pipe, you old smokestack. I've walked through the haze with you all...I tell you, it took one of my legs, and I'll take it back from its heart! I have already seen the day it dies. Its blood will burn away in the sea, its flapping fins will droop, it will flip over, and finally, patches of milky white and deep red will finally appear... Then, everything I promised you will come true. You will have everything that is mine, be it money, oil, or faith—though I have no faith in any gods. You can take it all, even this ship. We will kill it. We must kill it. This is my fate, your fate, and this ship's fate. Now, I will extinguish your fire, whether it is the fear in your heart or the smoke in your pipe.
InfoDisplay_120101030_Title: A Lost Page from a Diary
InfoDisplay_120101030_Text: Impossible. Blessed by "Divinity"? I refuse to believe it. It is we who conquer the sea, not it! When storms tear the mast apart, and rocks smash the keel, where is Divinity's voice then? When we haul ropes and tighten sails, where is Divinity's guidance? We conquer it. It does not bless us! No, I will never yield. No god, no matter which one, can ever fulfill my revenge, our revenge and fate! Do not be cowered, do not be deceived! What others promise us means nothing. Only what we seize from the merciless sea matters! Prayers and blessings will not calm these waters, it is we who are the masters of this sea! Never stop! Even if it summons the entire ocean to fight against us, we must still complete our conquest! We must prove, beyond a doubt, that we are the true masters of this sea! Hoist the sails, ready the spears, and tighten the winches, lads! To the whirlpool! This tempest is the great wave pushing us forward, and this fierce wind only feeds our flames! Do not stop! Sail into the storm! Even if it means we must dive into the dark whirlpool and the abyss!
InfoDisplay_120101031_Text:
"Closer! Closer! Aim at its wound!"

"Its body glows! Hit the glowing parts!"

"Those are stones, you cabbage head! Our spears can't break that!"
 
"Hard to Port!!!!"

"Lower the mainsail! Curses, we're in deep water now! Keep the mast out of the water!"
 
"Where did it go!? Where did it go!? It just disappeared!"
 
"Keep it in your sights! Don't let it escape!"
 
"Face to face at last! Now I can finally kill you!!!"
 
"Hard to Port!!!!"
InfoDisplay_120101032_Text:
The person who escapes from the lacquered black abyss need not deliver any warnings.
 
It seemed to mock us as it danced within the swirling whirlpool. The blue crystals on its back gleamed, barely a few centimeters above the dark, rushing waters. The harpoons we had sunk into its back were gone, but we did leave three glaring holes behind!
 
Every time we neared it, it swam faster into deeper waters. The deeper it sank into the whirlpool, the faster it swam, but for us, there was no turning back.
 
It vanished first, and when it reappeared beside our port, one mast was already submerged, and the other snapped off.  

Then came the tightening of the winch and the splintering of the keel.

After that, there was nothing but darkness. In that void, I couldn't see my ship, my crew, or it.
 
At first, my "leg" twitched uncontrollably... I thought I had died.
 
I lay on the beach, alone. There was no ship, no crew, and no sign of it.
 
I had none of its blood on my hands, no ship's wheel, no ropes, no harpoons. Nothing to grasp onto. 

But the sea breeze felt unfamiliar. I realized I'd never set foot on this beach before. Since we set sail from Cape Bedford, I remembered every passing port and beach, but this one... this one was unfamiliar.
 
It wasn't until a young man, dressed in foreign attire, kicked my boot to check if I was still alive that I realized I hadn't gone to hell, nor had I ascended to heaven.
 
"Ugh...Where am I?"

"Riccioli Island, Rinascita"

"Rinascita...."

"Did you suffer a shipwreck at sea?"

"My ship... My crew..."

"There's no one else nearby."

"If that's true... then in the end, I only am escaped alone..."
InfoDisplay_120101033_Text:
...Later, I came to realize that we were "blessed."
 
The people of Rinascita said that whale guided ships and sailors who perished at sea to the afterlife, like a ferryman of the underworld. I heard that the merchants of the Forgotten Sea could weigh memories and souls on their scales, exchanging them for an equal weight of gold.
 
But for some reason, we're all still alive. Or rather, we exist in a state between life and death.
 
Yes, in time, I found Starbuck and Queequeg on this island. They're still alive. "It," the whale they call "Cetus the Tidebreaker," was also still alive.
 
How can this be a "blessing"? This is nothing but a "curse!" I cannot accept this!
 
Once I've had my vengeance, death may take me. But if my vengeance fails, I cannot bear to remain in this world as a mere plaything for those I sought vengeance against! My fate is mine to decide, and only true death can end my conquest.
 
They don't understand. That whale, though it appears tame and gentle, is cunning and violent. It transforms death into an unjust eternity, making my vengeance just a footnote in its mockery of the sea… No, I will never accept this. I will never compromise!
InfoDisplay_120101034_Text:
All whales carry oil, and this oil can dissolve many things that water cannot. This is the conclusion we reached after crossing every sea.
 
It can dissolve things of every shape and nature into one, and there are even stories of people who fell into a whale's oil-filled brain and drowned, with no bones ever found. But I have never seen what oil this whale holds... Perhaps I never will.
 
More than twenty years have passed, and Pequod seems cursed. No matter what Queequeg tries, we cannot repair her. My crew, those "resurrected" sailors, have long since forgotten how to wield their harpoons. They no longer know how to fight the sea.
 
And it seems as though the whale is toying with me. Since that time, whether at sea or ashore, I have never laid eyes on it again. I do not wish to give up. I refuse to. As long as I can kill it, I will be freed from this curse-like "blessing" to find eternal rest.
 
But I... I am too old now. I can no longer lift a harpoon. I cannot fight that giant creature aboard one of these tiny "Gondolas."
 
Yes, my ideals, my beliefs, my fate, my vengeance—everything is gone. Everything has been swallowed by these foreign seas.
 
You are, of course, welcome to mock me. The rope of that harpoon, while I lived, bound me tightly to that whale. Even now, after death, I am still bound by it. In the past, I was unwilling to sever that rope. Now, I remain unwilling still...  But I can no longer drag it into the black depths of the sea.
 
Sometime later, a young man came to find me. He said his name was Ishmael, a sailor's apprentice, and he wanted to learn how to fish.
 
At that moment, I recalled that before Pequod's final voyage, there was a sailor named Ishmael at the Bedford dock. But he did not board my ship. He stayed at the port, and if he is still alive at sea, he would likely be as old as I am now. How ironic...
InfoDisplay_120101035_Title: A Message Written Not Long Ago
InfoDisplay_120101035_Text:
If it weren't for you and that young girl finding it, if it weren't for the captain of that troupe agreeing to my request, we still wouldn't know when we could truly rest in peace.
 
For people like us, the end of the world is the end of the sea.
 
I was born by the sea, died on the sea, and finally will be buried under the sea.
 
This time, I could not kill it. But next time I will certainly kill it... certainly.

...Thank you, Captain from a distant land.
InfoDisplay_120101037_Text:
...I am Ahab and you are my crew. You must trust me and only me.
 
It can't keep us trapped here forever.
 
We have to wait till Pequod is repaired, then we can leave... never to return.
InfoDisplay_120101038_Title: Faded Words on the Ancient Stele
InfoDisplay_120101038_Text:
…Leave behind the hatred of the sea here…
Show generosity and gifts, and it will lead you… home.
InfoDisplay_120101039_Text: The strange frequency surrounding you seems to urge you to perform. A melody floods your mind, and your fingers move involuntarily as a beautiful melody flows from your fingertips.
InfoDisplay_120101040_Text: Upon discovering the secret of the music box, a familiar melody mixed with dissonant notes rises in your mind. This time, you raise your hand with purpose, knowing exactly what to do.
InfoDisplay_114514001_Text: Dearest Father, I am writing this letter to you from a corner of the library. Over time, I have slowly adjusted to life at the seminary. During my free time, I often come to this library to read the ancient texts it holds and study the doctrine of Unity. But the deeper I delve into the history of Rinascita, the more I sense that it is shrouded by an unresolved mist. There are too many unanswered questions about our faith, the grace we have received, and the disaster that once befell us. Fortunately, many publicly sensitive topics and even discussions of taboos are regarded as subjects of academic interest in the seminary. I will take time to study and explore them. Of course, I haven't neglected the swordsmanship Mother taught me. Recently, I applied for sparring practice with the Divine Envoys... Don't worry, I won't hurt myself. I remember you once told me that Avinoleum is so vast you'll always get lost. This year, I've walked everywhere in the seminary, except for those places where I'm not allowed to go. I've drawn a simple route map, which is easier to read than the one in the Order. I'll send it to you later. With my sword and lantern, I press on through the fog. My Lord Imperator from above, Rosalie
InfoDisplay_109000001_Text:
Trust thy neighbor, else land will stay fallow. Unite the isles, else levees will stay unbuilt.

Brothers and sisters, let the sky, the land, and the seas be united.

The path to righteousness is lit by the sacred fire of <color=#ffd12f>Unity</color>.
InfoDisplay_109000002_Text:
We have conquered the land and built an impenetrable fortress upon the mountain’s crown.
From the very beginning, the Echoes stood with us—loyal, unyielding, and true.
O Brave people of Rinascita, future warriors. Let this monument bear witness to your courage.
<color=#ffd12f>In the beginning is the lion, peerless in might.</color>
<color=#ffd12f>In the end is the knight, faithful to the last breath.</color>
What we leave behind will one day rise again through you.
InfoDisplay_109000003_Text:
"Even in the end… I never found the so-called power of the dragon.
As the knight who served the 17th head of the family, I failed to protect the one I swore to. I failed to fulfill her wish, to redeem her family's name.
I achieved nothing. Died in a foreign land... Ha, what a pitiful, wasted life."
InfoDisplay_101153001_Text:
Through the initial selection, you must forge ahead. Compete, strive, and fight for your place. Show your strength, wisdom, courage, and perseverance as you journey through the depths to become the Fisalia Maiden.

The Head of the Fisalia family will offer the chosen one an elixir capable of granting any wish—be it eternal beauty or miraculous healing. All desires can be fulfilled.

Candidates:
<color=PurpleD>Mandragora Fisalia, Hebenon Fisalia, Cantarella Fisalia...</color>

Chloe Fisalia, Annis Fisalia, Marina Fisalia...

First Trial:
Poison is the bedrock on which the Fisalia name stands.
Let it test your willpower.
In this trial, you must select <color=RedD>the three most toxic Sea Apples</color> from the depths and bring them back by any means necessary.
Remember: The use of any external tools to determine their toxicity or aid in retrieval is strictly forbidden.

May the power of the Fisalia bloodline awaken within you.
InfoDisplay_101153002_Text:
Dear Annis,

The Trials are tomorrow! I'm so nervous… but a tiny bit excited too.

The Fisalias are really, really scary… Some of them strut around all high and mighty, while others are just… unsettling, like something out of a bad dream.

They must be really good at handling poisons, right? Just the thought of facing them makes me uneasy.…

I overheard that unsettling Fisalia girl whispering that poison can be medicine too. She said with just the right amount, it won't hurt anyone but actually save them.

Perhaps even if I don't pass the Trials, I could pick up some of their secrets about poisons and figure out the ingredients. Then maybe, just maybe, I could make something to help Jojo.

Thinking about it that way makes things a little less scary. For Jojo's sake, what's a little poison, anyway!

Be careful tomorrow, my dear Annis. We don't have Fisalia blood, and they know a lot more about poisons than we do.

Yours,
Chloe
InfoDisplay_101153003_Text:
Dear Annis,

Today I tried four different poisons…

The first one gave me a pounding headache, the second made my stomach cramp up, the third left my bones feeling all achy, and the fourth made me so dizzy I started seeing little dancing figures everywhere!

I'm still feeling a bit wobbly, and the words on this note are jumping around as I try to write.

But that unsettling Fisalia girl gave me some medicine. After I drank it, I felt a little better, just enough to write to you.

You might wonder why I'd ever drink something from a Fisalia, but don't worry. I've been keeping an eye on her. She's… different from the others. They don't seem to like her much, and she's always by herself, mumbling and grinding herbs. What she said last time wasn't a lie, and she didn't hurt me. 

Maybe… not all Fisalias are bad.

I'm thinking about asking her for help. She knows so much about medicine, and since she doesn't fit in with the rest, maybe she'd teach me how to mix the right potion to help Jojo. I know it's risky, but if there's even a small chance, I have to try.

Oh, and one last thing—security is tighter now, so be very careful, okay? If you hear three quick knocks, that'll be me.

Yours,
Chloe
InfoDisplay_101153004_Text:
Dear ████,

The Sea Apples were extremely potent. Even smelling them was enough to make it impossible to breathe, like my throat was being squeezed. I could barely get a word out. When I finally came to, I tasted something metallic in my mouth.

I didn't have the strength to touch one, let alone bring one back. All I could do was watch helplessly from afar.

They were round and red, like apples… or maybe tomatoes. Back in Egla Town, we had fields full of tomatoes…

Is it because I'm not a true Fisalia that I can't awaken any special abilities or immunity to poisons?

No, I can't give up. It must be because I'm not trying hard enough.

Annis wasn't a Fisalia either, but she made it through, even though we'll never hear her voice again. The poison destroyed her vocal cords, and she'll never speak again... 

Now's not the time for tears. I have to be strong too. For Jojo's sake, I won't give up.

Chloe
InfoDisplay_101153005_Text:
<color=PurpleD>Mandragora Fisalia, Hebenon Fisalia, Cantarella Fisalia...

Annis Fisalia…</color>

The above candidates have passed the trial of poison.

InfoDisplay_101153006_Text:
Knight Princess, Sorceress Princess, Commoner Princess, Noble Princess, and Angel Princess assembled before the castle!

Knight Princess atop her noble mount took the lead through the castle hedge maze and opened the castle gates.

Commoner Princess consumed poisonous mushrooms which she mistook as edible. Sorceress Princess rendered aid by brewing a curative potion.

Noble Princess, who knew the castle well, elegantly circumvented all of the hidden traps.

Angel Princess followed everyone with a faint smile on her lips.

The Princesses gathered in the castle's main hall where the Queen proclaimed their first task was to find the Gold Apple in the Appletree Forest!

Appletree Forest on the castle grounds, grows apples red and round.
A few land making a thump, knocking heads and raising bumps. 
Apples fall into the earth's hold, most are red but some are gold.
Whose head will the gold apple hit? Who will leave the forest with it?
The Queen sits with her meal in place, waiting for fruit to take its place.
As the juicy bite goes down, behold on her head the Thorned Crown.

In the end, everyone will surely find their own Gold Apple that makes their dreams come true!
InfoDisplay_101153007_Text:
Knight Princess: After the Throned Crown is mine, everyone in the castle will live better lives!

Sorceress Princess: Uh-huh... I don't want anything, I'm only here out of obligation to the family. After this is over, I plan to leave this dull place and get some fresh air outside. This time of year, the flowers in the mountains and fields should be blooming quite nicely... maybe I can find a new variety suitable for making medicine.

Noble Princess: I... I'm a bit scared, and I don't want to continue. But... but...

Knight Princess: You can't back out!

Commoner Princess: To cure Jojo, I won't back out. I will get the cure-all elixir and return home happily.

Angel Princess: Everyone's wishes shall come true.
InfoDisplay_101153008_Text:
Second Trial:

To claim the title of Maiden, one must demonstrate the strength to make decisive choices.

Excessive emotions are vulnerabilities and burdens for any candidate worthy of the title.

Each participant is required to capture <color=RedD>the most venomous jellyfish</color> from the sea and return it to this location. Upon your return, you will team up with another candidate and exchange your catch. The candidate with the more potent jellyfish shall be declared the winner.

In the event that you encounter an accident along the way, the other paired candidate will be declared the winner by default.

Use your awakened abilities to endure the depths of the sea until the end.

Trust only yourself, and remember that the title of Maiden is worthy of your pursuit.

Team Assignments:
<color=PurpleD>Mandragora Fisalia and Hebenon Fisalia.
Cantarella Fisalia and Annis Fisalia.
...</color>
InfoDisplay_101153009_Text:
Dear Mandragora,

My dearest sister, I cannot fathom anything more heart-wrenching than facing you in this trial, given all the years we have spent growing up together.

As the Fisalia eldest daughter, you were always sheltered, yet you took it upon yourself to welcome me into this world with such tenderness. I still recall the way you would sew my clothes, even adding that little pink bunny design. It was so soft and fluffy, far more lovely than any strange creature from the deep.

If the Fisalias can have only one Maiden, I wish it to be you.

To show my sincerity, I'll share my newly awakened ability with you. My tears are lethal. They paralyze people upon contact and then clot their blood.

I swear by the name of Fisalia that this is true.

Please think of a way to counter my power. When the time comes, I hope you can free me from this fate.

Yours,
Hebenon
InfoDisplay_101153010_Text:
Dear Hebenon,

The head of our family has always taught us that to be born into the Fisalias is to embrace coldness, decisiveness, and ruthlessness. 

For the "greater good" our family upholds, personal sacrifice holds little weight. As the eldest daughter, it is my duty to uphold these teachings. While our ways may seem harsh, they are accompanied by the weight of expectations and the honor of our name. I have resolved to relinquish all personal desires, allowing the family's code to seep into my very soul.

Our impending duel will undoubtedly bring pain, yet we have both come this far. I trust we will become exactly what the head envisions for us. You, too, are a daughter of the senior line, and I implore you not to follow in our cousin's footsteps, who defies the head's will.

Gather your strength and determination, so that when we face each other in the trial, we shall do so as equals.

Should I become the Maiden, I will honor your sacrifices. And if you are chosen, I hope you will do the same.

Yours,
Mandragora
InfoDisplay_101153011_Text:
<color=PurpleD>Cantarella Fisalia and Annis Fisalia</color> have passed the Second Trial.

The loss of two beloved family members weighs heavily on us all. However, as Fisalias, it is our duty and privilege to continue with the Trials.

For the rise of the Maiden, we stand unwavering, prepared to bear any cost.

They'll all get swallowed up.
