InfoDisplay_120101042_Text:
Hahaha! Bravo! Let us sing another to this occasion! With Ragunna City behind us, at long last we've arrived where the knights once set camp.

Oh, those marvelous knights living the way of Korlacchi—!

We build bonfires at night and admire the windmills during the day. We play music and sing together under their turning sails. The townsfolk call us "bonfire bards."

When the windmills come to rest, we'd go chasing along the rivers and lakes. But above all these, there's nothing like flying across the field on a clear day.

From the air, I glance down at this land wrinkled by time. Sunlight blankets over the pillars of the knight's collapsed ruins, where a thousand-year-old tree stands in its silent vigil, with its roots sprawling across the stone crevices. As the wind carries me across the lake's surface, the reflections of the red roof tiles of the Egla Town gleam and dance like pomegranate seeds scattered on top of a sheet of blue silk. The red-topped windmill overlooks the town, slowly turning and beckoning homebound travelers.
InfoDisplay_120101043_Title: Ciaccona's Letter Tucked into the Book
InfoDisplay_120101043_Text:
As twilight gilds my cheeks in amber,
Shadows of trees bow down to kiss the bottomless lake.
As birds sweep past these ancient walls,
In the folds of clouds I hide my unfinished poems away.

By the time this letter reaches you, we have already parted ways.
You have embarked on a new journey, and I will be playing a new tune somewhere away from the city, per.

A tale of a girl and a Laureate treading the sea together. The girl imagined herself to be a bird called "Icarus," and with her talents she revealed unspoken wishes of abandoned instruments along the way. They offered aid to children of the Choir, unveiling the true essence of poetry. Yet the joyous girl carried secrets of her own, for she hoped to share her voice, so singers would no longer need to hide behind lies and their creativity would flow freely. In the final moment when she had to make a choice, her childhood memories as a girl who sang without worry and encouragement from the Laureate helped her defeat her doubts.

The caged bird took a fateful plunge out of the cage, but this time, she was caught and raised up by a pair of caring hands.

Just as Mister Faroll once said, "Words and music are a form of miracle capable of transcending the boundaries of time and personal experience." I understood at an early age the meanings their poems conveyed.

And now. Thank you, {PlayerName}, for understanding their messages too.

As the mist of time slowly dissipates in a sigh,
Only traces of remembrance continues to strum these strings.
Should fate's variation sounds, petals of parting may scatter.
As for us...

I think it's better to not express farewell through poetry, as I wish to tell you: We will meet again, sometime in the future!
InfoDisplay_120101044_Text:
Do not bring flowers to my grave, for I am not there, bound under this tombstone.
I am in the sea winds at Ragunna's walls. I am dawning lights that break through thorns.
I am a night hawk of wings aflame, soaring towards the Celestial Steed, whose praises I sing and whose true form I behold.
The night sky will be illuminated by wings aflame, and I shall be reborn in immortal poetry.
So long as people draw breath, lift your eyes and see: so long as this poem lives, it breathes life into me.
<alignright/>——End

Looking back at what I wrote in the preface:
This anthology is attributed to the Golden Anthem. We wish these poems might offer a glimmer of hope to those lost in fate's journey, and to readers something to contemplate.
Gather these scattered golden syllables, as they are treasures tempered by fire, and lingering sparks of human thought.
And finally, thank you for opening this book.
InfoDisplay_120101045_Text:
Literary works draw their vitality from two sources: The creator and the readers.

The creator gives it new life, while the readers help extend it through reading. Each time they share a piece of work or publish their thoughts and reviews, they breathe new life into it.

Some may find the term "life of a work" elusive, as it's too abstract and intangible.

However, a parallel can be easily drawn from human life. When discussing the concept of life, one essential topic is inevitably brought up—name. A name is a symbol of existence, one of the most important markers that separate individual lives. If one desires to feel the vitality of a work, the most direct approach would be to feel its name, the various names bestowed by creators and readers.

I once heard an eerie tale from a land in the east that spoke of a lady with skin as fair as snow who would stand in a snowstorm, cradling a wailing baby in her arms, begging the passersby to hold the baby for her. If some kindhearted individual agrees to that request, they'd soon find themselves unable to let go, bound to freeze to death.

Intriguing, isn't it? But, by this point, it's a fascinating tale that evokes many distinct images that cannot yet form the entirety of "life." 

But what if we give it a name? Like... "The Snow Woman." This name alone captures the entire narrative and defines its essence.

However, even with the name anchoring people's imaginations, the unusual nature of words means each person takes a narrative differently.

Hence... The life of a creative work is less controllable than human life.

So, if one day, people's understanding of a work is led astray, then words could turn into a devastating weapon.

What would we do then? Show anger? No, absolutely not! Anger is the cheapest outlet of dissent. As creators, all we can do is believe. Believe that our words can live in their most genuine form.
<alignright/>—Exclusive interview with the Golden Anthem
InfoDisplay_120101046_Text:
We can't just sit here and wait for it to happen. Is there anything else we can do? Anything...
Ask for help... from who...? I don't know who else is there to turn to.
The Montellis... If it's the Montellis... No, wait. They value profits over anything, we don't have that kind of leverage.
The street poets... That won't do either. We won't be able to control the spread.
What about them? They're choristers. They would...
InfoDisplay_120101047_Text:
"...
Swept away by the storm are the cicadas of the Water Kingdom,
Wheat straws lay adrift in the village's oaken wine mugs.
Prolonged nights of Summer,
Lost souls, wander between streets and alleys.

Withered leaves fall into autumn's abyssal tranquility,
Rust of decay form on utensils of holy communion.
Desolate winds of Autumn,
Acolytes measure the inclination of Divinity with rotten scales.

Frost cover pupils of stained glass,
The confessional fills with silent ash.
Sleepless night of Winter,
A wandering bard holds a frozen lute,
Playing sounds that never reach.

With our bodies to fuel the fire, the ensuing inferno shall forge Ragunna's true gold.
Like the fire that dragged them to hell, these Daemons will spread throughout the land and burn all of Ragunna.
Let this sail take us past the towers, past the surrounding walls, and past the Sentinel's sculptures, as we descend silently into hell.
Till this song drowns into the brilliance of the sunset.
..."
InfoDisplay_120101049_Text: Day 1 – Unknown (The sky looks like broken, fractured glass) 15:49. I'll never forget this number. Just one minute before the observation was complete, a dark rift suddenly tore open from the device in front of me, shredding the stream of data across the screen. My boots were still stuck to the lab floor, but my upper body had already been pulled into a strange, chaotic storm. That was the beginning. Now I find myself in a city I don't recognize, having just survived a bizarre Lament. It slices through buildings, people, space, everything two-dimensional, three-dimensional… and maybe things beyond that, though my eyes can't quite make sense of it anymore. My Forte is Sealing, something that might be considered a way to resist the passage of time. Maybe, if I keep trying, I can use it to record the abnormalities in this city and figure out how to break through it. I'm not going to sit here and wait for the end.
InfoDisplay_120101050_Text: Day 7 – Cloudy (If what's above my head can still be called "weather.") When I woke up and checked my watch, I noticed something odd. Moss had started growing beneath the glass. This city, fractured and folded in on itself, seems trapped in some kind of temporal loop. Time moves forward and backward within a fixed range. But oddly enough, the plants don't seem bound by each "reset." The moss shouldn't be able to grow between the gears... unless time isn't flowing normally here. It's eroding, rushing, and spawning things that shouldn't even exist in the first place. Still, I'm grateful for this strange, unreasonable growth. It made me realize this city isn't beyond saving. There is a way out. (The pen seems to pause, leaving a small blot of ink on the paper.) There's one thing I still can't let go of. That rift... In my blurred memory, it sealed shut almost as soon as I was pulled into the storm. But if I can't figure out what caused it, or how to stop it. There's no way to guarantee it won't open again. And if it does... someone else could get dragged in. However, time's against me.
InfoDisplay_120101051_Text: Day 136 – Abnormal Pressure (If this constant pressure in my ears counts as such) Among the supplies Chisa brought back today was a can of oranges, the label printed with a production date long past... but that hardly matters anymore. These so-called "foods" are really just compressed Remnant Energy. Chisa gave the can to me. She sat off to the side with a piece of spring steel she'd salvaged, slicing it into a curved blade using her Forte, turning it into a new weapon. Watching her, I suddenly recalled another day. She was sitting just like this, halfway through organizing supplies on the sofa, when she turned and asked me what my Forte really was. I showed her a small amber, the one containing a preserved memory of the first time we worked together at this home base: the lights were dim, she was repairing a weapon, and I was taking notes on anomalies in the city's time flow. It was a rare, peaceful night, as long as we could ignore the fact that we were still trapped in a city sealed off from the outside world. To hold out against the erratic occurrences of the Lament, I once tried to learn Chisa's practical skills, but I failed. Of course I did. Still, she taught me a few special ways to leave markings. I remember what she said back then: "Stop treating everything like a science experiment. Think of every piece of scrap metal as a blade that never misses—" (The pen pierced the page, leaving a blot of ink.) And I know she truly meant it. This city, drenched in Lament, is riddled with danger. And yet, she always throws herself forward to shield everyone else. She thinks I haven't noticed how much she's burning herself out... doesn't know her body's running at the edge of collapse. But I've done the calculations many times. I know exactly how long she has before she crosses the breaking point. The only good thing is that this Sonoro seems to have stalled time and her condition. But I can't let her stay like this forever. I want to take her back. Back to the Black Shores, to the people I trust. There has to be a solution waiting there. I'll bring her back. No matter the cost.
InfoDisplay_120101052_Text: Day 159 – Sunny (A rare clear day) Today, Chisa told me she found a new spot that could serve as a base—an old, spacious cafe. From the large terrace on the second floor, you can see a beautiful view of the city center. It's been a long time since I've seen her this excited. It feels like we're one step closer to breaking the loop. And in fact, we are making progress. (The handwriting sharpens slightly.) Based on my research over the past few days, I'm now fairly certain of this: the key to unraveling this endless Möbius loop lies at the heart of the city—Neon Tower. It is the center of the Lament. The origin. And most importantly, the point that lies closest to the outside world. If we can reach the top, perhaps we'll be able to contact the people back at the Black Shores. Perhaps that's the way out of this Sonoro. The moss has already crept past the gears of my watch and reached the surface. Still, I haven't replaced it. It reminds me of time... and that something can keep pushing through falsehoods until it reaches the truth. I'll head for the heart of Neon Tower tomorrow morning. If time here is clay, then I will mold it into a road, one that leads us home.
InfoDisplay_120101053_Text: (The handwriting is noticeably rushed.) It should be around noon. I've reached the third floor of Neon Tower. Rubble from the buildings is scattered and floating around like a shattered kaleidoscope. Some pieces have even stuck to my clothes. I must look like I'm covered in rainbow frosting. …But my body is getting colder. Turns out I was right. Either these "sugar crystals" or the entire city are slowly draining the body heat of anyone who doesn't belong here. I need to keep moving. I have to find the right path to the top, and fast.
InfoDisplay_120101054_Text: 15:23. It's been five full hours since I entered the Tower. Nearly half of that time was wasted, because I took the wrong path forward. My watch is almost entirely covered by moss. It spread so quickly. There's no doubt now. Time inside the Tower flows differently from the outside… No, the entire city of Honami is out of sync. I passed through countless time fragments, saw my tenth birthday party cake, the balloons and flowers from my coming-of-age ceremony, and the lab coat I first wore when I joined the Black Shores. It was happiness. Surreal like a dream… But I couldn't let myself get lost in it. I took off my protective gloves and ran my fingers across the corroded surfaces, trying to touch the reality in front of me. Surprisingly, it felt warm, like the vein of some living creature. (The writing wavers here, as if the hand holding the pen had started to shake.) …Or maybe that warmth was a hallucination born out of being so cold. My mind is slipping, but I can't stop now. I knew from the start this would never be an easy path... But so what? Even the most dangerous equation still needs someone willing to solve it.
InfoDisplay_120101055_Text: (The handwriting is distorted, yet forceful, pressing deep into the page.) Endless fragments of time... I didn't expect to witness my entire life play out in this place. Honestly? It was a good life. The repeated crossings and the blurring of my senses have made it impossible to judge the passage of time. Even the hands on my watch have stopped at last, caught in the moss's hold. But that's okay. I achieved my goal. After countless trial and error, I've finally mapped out every correct path. I know I probably won't make it to the top though... It doesn't matter. Even if I don't live to see the end, it doesn't matter. All I ever wanted was to lay down a clear road, so those who come after can walk across my bones and reach the light. That's enough for me. In fact… (The next words are nearly illegible, the ink smudged by a trembling hand.) I feel content. I remember that night when I was eighteen. I'd just passed the Black Shores assessment. I stood overlooking the sea by the Haven of Sprouts, gazing up at the sky. Back then, I believed the truth was hidden beyond the stars. Now I'm curled up inside the steel maze of Neon Tower, watching the Lament tear space part. Watching fragments of my past, my whole life... I've never been this close to the truth. Across time, I reach out to my eighten-year-old self. Space collapses around me. My mind catches fire in the light. I feel myself unraveling, being stripped away, broken down, and engraved. Then I hear my eighteen-year-old voice saying: "So you really made it here."

InfoDisplay_22010101_Title: Preliminary Guidelines for Operations in Septimont (Excerpt)
InfoDisplay_22010101_Text:
[This manual is distributed by the Chamber of Enlightenment to all stationed Acolytes. For internal reference only. Unauthorized reproduction, transcription, or circulation is strictly prohibited.]
 
Septimont—A City of Warriors Where Faith Runs Thin
 
In ancient times, Ragunna and Septimont were among the earliest settlements during the Age of a Thousand Islands. The conflicts in that distant age drove a wedge between the two, leading them down separate paths and shaping two distinct societies with their own customs and cultures. Unlike Ragunna, the Sentinel's blessings have not reached Septimont, for its people long ago abandoned their faith. Septimontians regard miracles and divine grace with indifference, placing their reverence instead in strength and valor. They venerate heroes born of war and the hunt, and revel in gladiating games that verge on barbarism.
 
It is worth noting, however, that these practices do not stem from disrespect. Septimontians believe the Sentinel to be a supreme hero and leader, worthy of unparalleled glory. They revere the Sentinel and sing of ancient legends, aspiring one day to stand alongside Them and achieve unmatched feats. Such thinking is an absolute transgression against the Sentinel, and we must guard ourselves vigilantly against it.
 
Septimontians have demonstrated their indifference toward the Sentinel and the Order's teachings by allowing temples to fall into ruin and altars to be dismantled. Yet the Order has remained patient and generous. Trade now flourishes between Ragunna and Septimont, and within the city itself, devoted Acolytes continue to preach and spread the Sentinel's divine grace.
 
...
 
All Acolytes stationed abroad must uphold the Sentinel's teachings, observe discretion and restraint, and respect Septimont's local customs to avoid unnecessary conflict. Should they face strong resistance, they may present their official credentials or, if necessary, request intervention from the Order's External Affairs Department.

...
InfoDisplay_22010102_Text:
Long ago, it was right at this solemn and sacred site of trial that the Blessed Maiden was bestowed Haultir, the Sword of Virtue. Now, in the same hallowed place, the Blessed Maiden raised the Sword of Virtue high, her gaze fixed upon the squire kneeling before her. The squire held his posture with perfect stillness, silent as a statue.
 
"Before our Master Imperator, do you vow to fight only for justice and righteousness, and to lend your hand to the weak?"
 
The squire could not speak. He answered with a slow, deliberate nod.
 
"Do you vow to remain steadfast in faith and oath, never to abandon the duties entrusted to you?"
 
Again, the squire nodded.
 
"Even should you find yourself in the most dire of trials? Even should you... face death itself?"
 
The squire uttered an indistinct sound. From the tone, it seemed to be an affirmation.
 
The flat of the Sword of Virtue lightly touched Cadanto's shoulders—once, twice, thrice.
 
"From this day forth, you are a true knight, Cadanto."
 
For many of the Acolytes witnessing the ceremony, this was the first time they had seen an <ano=Divine envoy>Echo</ano> rise to knighthood.
InfoDisplay_22010103_Title: Pioneer Association Special Edition: Sword of the Guardian
InfoDisplay_22010103_Text:
...
 
As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's chestplate, the duel between the Blessed Maiden and her Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was. 
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto.
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. After some explanation from the Acolyte, we learned that Cadanto had recently saved a family from Tacet Discords near Avinoleum's outskirts. The towering Echo knight remained half-kneeling and silent. He didn't seem to understand why a human would offer him flowers, or perhaps he felt unworthy of such thanks?
 
"So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them."
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs.
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people.
 
...
 
[Note: This manuscript is scheduled for official publication following the Blessed Maiden's coronation ceremony. Special thanks to Avinoleum for their generous assistance during our research.]
InfoDisplay_22010104_Text:
(This appears to be a personal memoir written by the now-retired Acolyte Julia, recounting her experiences and reflections while working at the Titular Repository.)
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold.
InfoDisplay_22010105_Title: Notice on Strengthening the Management of Dragon Echoes
InfoDisplay_22010105_Text:
To all Acolytes, faculty and students:
 
Recently, the Seminary has discovered instances of students bringing dragon Echoes into the Titular Repository and the dormitory quarters without permission, resulting in considerable chaos. In order to ensure a safe and quiet academic environment and to reaffirm reverence for the Divine Envoys, the following provisional regulations are hereby issued for all enrolled students:
 
1. Dragon Echoes should not be taken out of Zargon Garden without permission.
 
 2. The use of Fortes within designated Echo gathering zones in Zargon Garden is strictly prohibited. (Specific boundaries attached separately.)
 
3. Close contact with dragon Echoes is forbidden unless officially reported and approved. This includes, but is not limited to, feeding, teasing, or challenging them in any form.
 
During non-Carnevale periods, violators will face confinement ranging from two to five days. Repeat or severe offenders will incur escalated penalties in accordance with the Student Handbook. Regulations specific to the Carnevale period will be issued separately.
 
Praise be to Imperator.
Avinoleum Office of Academic Affairs
InfoDisplay_22010106_Text:
(Most of the contents have been lost. Only the preface remains relatively intact.)
 
You'll easily pick out students from the Fisalia family at the Seminary.
 
Not because there are many of them, but because they simply stand out. Fisalia students tend to be brooding and solitary, always slightly apart from the energy around them. Just as people from Ragunna expect them to be.
 
Among students, rumors circulate: that the Fisalias poison their own meals to build resistance, that they travel via an underground cable car, and that they swim like fish. Only one of these is untrue. Still, the fact that people believe them shows how deep prejudice runs, even here at Avinoleum, where elites from all corners gather.
 
I'm not from the Fisalia family myself, but I've befriended several. These Avinoleum-based Fisalians live closer to the family's ancient mission than most of their kin. As our bond deepened, a question began to take root in me, growing into an uncontrollable curiosity: Why does this venerable, illustrious family endure society's slander without protest? They no longer argue. They keep their silence. Only in their troubled dreams might you catch a whisper—broken phrases—hinting at the truth behind the veil.
 
What are the Fisalias hiding? Or rather, what have they been carrying? The events and interviews collected in this book have been recorded with the consent of those involved, with sensitive details omitted. If, by the end of this book, you find yourself with a different understanding of the Fisalias, then this work will have served its purpose.
 
...
InfoDisplay_160000001_Text:
The path remains hidden, inside a truth forbidden...
Messengers stand guard, like the gates of the abyss they regard.
<color=yellow>When at the center their eyes converge</color>, from the waters the path will emerge.
InfoDisplay_160000002_Text:
The bastard and that lapdog of hers are still on my tail. But this is as far as I can go for now. I need to rest. My right hand hurts so much I think it might be broken. As for my mind... I still feel dazed, but already much clearer than before. I thought I was losing it... I need to sit here for a while. Here's hoping those traps can buy me some time...

Soon I'll be able to see the sun, see the moon... the skies. Sometimes I forget I once belonged there, a place with sunlight and order. And here? Even the air reeks with despair... By Imperator, may this cursed dump and all its evil slowly rot in these dark sewers.

I couldn't find Brandon, but I have a feeling he was here—I can't tell if it's a hunch or if I'm being delusional. He must've made it out already... Yeah, that's right. The fellow's got more tricks up his sleeves than I do. He must've dropped his ID card in those vents as a distraction. Even got me fooled. Just like when we played pool... And here I am worrying about him. Ha, I'm such an idiot.

It's fine, I'll be out soon enough. Brandon, when I find you... I'm going to give you a good punch in the face. Just you wait.
InfoDisplay_160000003_Text:
Corned Tumbleyak – Seven jars. Hubert found them in a storage room piled with junk, and Sentinel knows how long they'd been there. He says this stuff must've been sitting there since the Dark Tide, at least twenty years ago. Must be emergency supplies people stocked up out of panic. Good thing they packed the jars with salt, so they're still edible.

Pickled Fish – Sixteen jars. Brandon gathered a group and fished them out of the sewers leading to the sea while those masks weren't looking. Gotta keep these jars hidden, or else they'll be taken away like the rest of our food if they find them.
InfoDisplay_160000004_Text:
<color=yellow>Henry and I found a Supply Chest behind two pipes</color>. Henry thinks it's loot the Black Alley stashed here ten years ago.
Well, I think he's full of it. Those gangsters aren't idiots. Why would they hide their loot in such an obvious place? It's gotta be a Chest Mimic that somehow found its way here from the sewers. If anyone finds this note, <color=yellow>DO NOT TOUCH THIS SUPPLY CHEST</color>.
I'll ask Talos to come check it out when she has time.
InfoDisplay_160000005_Text:
That woman who calls herself Talos took all of our food and forced us to obey her commands. She said this was the way of the Black Alley of old, where strength determines power and wealth, and the weak have no place. This order existed ten, twenty years ago, and even long before that. Brandon and the others tried to challenge her, hoping to liberate us from her "rule," but they failed. That was the last anyone ever saw of them.

Oh, I've heard plenty of stories about the Black Alley, all right. The evil they committed. How they eventually received the judgment and punishment they had coming for them. All we wanted was a peaceful life in the Black Alley. We never wanted to be like them, wreaking havoc in the city. We just want to live our own lives here. The Black Alley is our home.

I have a plan in mind. If all goes well, then I can escape this miserable dump. I heard that a hero named the "Blazing Nightwalker" took out the previous gang. Maybe I can find her and ask her to save the Black Alley again.
InfoDisplay_160000006_Text:
You missed your shift again, Cole! I'm not waiting around for you like I did yesterday. I'm heading back to my shack, grabbing a few drinks, and getting some sleep. I've done my part of the shift. If Talos starts asking questions, don't expect me to take the fall.

I'm off. I'm sure you know how to disarm the traps. Just follow the directions of the drawings on the ground. When the Runner brings in the new recruits, don't forget to open the gates for them.
InfoDisplay_160000007_Text:
Talos sent me to the city on errands for the next couple of days, so you're in charge while I'm gone, rookie.
Don't sweat it. Just follow my instructions to the letter, and you won't screw this up.

We open for business after six in the evening. During the day, put those kids on cleaning duty and make sure the broken bottles and mess from the night before are taken care of. No one likes a messy establishment. The Black Alley doesn't get any sunlight, so keep an eye on your watch and don't miss opening time.

Once people start to come in, hit the green button twice. Start things off with a track to set the mood. And remember: don't serve beverages just yet. If someone decides to make a scene about it, have Vincent take them to the ring and settle it over fists. If Vincent can't handle it, call Talos.

After a twenty-minute warmup, hit the red button once and the green button twice. Repeat this every half hour. I've prepped some banger music that they'll love. This is when you have the boys bring out the drinks. Once the vibe picks up, that's when the booze starts selling.

Keep in mind, whenever you see Talos show up, hit the yellow button right away. That'll play her favorite rock song, "The Black Alley Devils."

That's about it. She's all yours, rookie!
InfoDisplay_160000008_Text:
This is my fifth day in the Black Alley. People here are always on edge like they're afraid of something. No one says a word about it, of course.

The Black Alley is an oddity to the Ragunnesi. Youngsters these days don't even know it exists, while the old consider it a forbidden territory. Imagine the uproar it would cause in Ragunna if I wrote about its secrets and published them!

I met a nice fellow—everyone calls him the Runner, although I'm not sure who's pulling his strings. Thanks to his help, I got access to the Black Alley and its many mysteries.

The first three days of my investigation came up empty. But I did get to know a young man named Brandon over a game of pool. Seems like he's spent his fair share of time here. To be honest, he's damn good at the game, a worthy opponent, as long as he isn't cheating. Last time we played, the coat I had hanging nearby suddenly started burning. Luckily, I put it out in time, but by the time I came back, he had "scored" three points while I was gone.

Brandon is really tight-lipped about the Black Alley and always seems preoccupied with something. Still, I believe he could be the breakthrough I need in my investigation. He's not as stubborn as the old timers, nor as much of a pain to talk to as those masks. I still can't figure out where they came from. Maybe I'll figure it out someday.

Speaking of which, I haven't seen Brandon for two days. Maybe he went to help the starving old folks. As I learned during my investigation, the people here scrape by with odd jobs, barely managing to get enough food. Brandon is always sharing his rations with them.

Wherever he's gone, he'll be back for more pool. All I need to do is wait for him.
InfoDisplay_160000009_Text:
Black Alley Dart League, Season 3 Rankings (As of Today):
1st: "Lightning Ol' Joe"
2nd: "Eagle Eye Jack"
3rd: "Buckshot Cole"
(Scribbled handwriting) Looks like it's Ol' Joe's lucky day. What's the matter, Cole? Too many drinks? Show 'em what you're made of!
(Neat handwriting) Ol' Joe's a cheat, all right. There's no way he beat Jack. You saw how much his hands were shaking when he was tossing?

InfoDisplay_160000010_Text:
[Today's Drink Specials]
Vent-a-Nite: Made with aged liquor as the base, infused with refreshing herbal extracts. One sip will send a cool rush from head to toe, like stepping into a ventilation shaft after an ice-cold shower!
Recommendation: ☆☆☆☆

Dragon's Breath Octane: Featuring Pavo Plum juice swiped from the docks and a spoonful of real fossil fuel, this fiery mix is for the boldest drinkers! Dare your friends to survive the burning journey from throat to stomach. First one to take a sip of water picks up the tab!
Recommendation: ☆☆☆

Biohoard: A concoction made from pickled fish and corned meat juices. Tastes just as bad as it smells. I don't know how anyone could enjoy this, but it was made on request from an anonymous letter... Anyway, makes for a good prank on your friends!
Recommendation: ☆
To the anonymous requester: Your drink is ready. Please pay for it soon, or I'll tell Talos and she'll find out who sent this letter.

Golden Hour Special: A special blend of Tumbleyak butter and Nectarwine. A perfect fusion of the rustic charm of Whisperwind Haven and the sophisticated taste of the Montelli Quarters. Some might find it lacking a bold kick, but trust me, the creamy bubbles and velvety texture will win you over.
Recommendation: ☆☆☆☆☆
InfoDisplay_160000011_Text:
Brandon's not the only one who's gone missing. People have been disappearing left and right. Good thing I learned how to quickly memorize people's faces in school, otherwise I could've easily overlooked this.

Everyone here seems indifferent to these disappearances. They're not even remotely curious about where those people went, or what fate they'll suffer. They just go about their business numbly while enduring the dwindling food supply.

As for those masks, I'm now certain they're working for some bigshot who recently showed up in the Black Alley. They occasionally leave to return to Ragunna City. I try to keep my distance, but I once overheard something during one of their gatherings... they're a bunch of criminals. Thugs. They were in one helluva celebratory mood talking about the "rebirth of the Black Alley." Whoever their boss is, she seems to be planning on making her fortune through crime.

But then what? What happens after the rebirth of the Black Alley? I haven't the slightest clue. To be honest, I normally consider myself a brave person, but I'm scared. Scared of that boss of theirs. Scared of her plans... I just want to leave now. Let the Chamber of Discipline deal with these criminals.

I did make an unexpected discovery today, though I can't tell if it's good news or bad news. I found an ID card in a tunnel near the ventilation shafts, something the residents of the Black Alley use to identify each other. It belongs to Brandon.

Did something happen to him? Or maybe... he left it there on purpose as some kind of guide? Or as a warning? Those masks are watching every move I make, I can't just make a break for it. Maybe Brandon knows a way out. I have to find him.
InfoDisplay_160000012_Text:
Talos had me and a group of guys on fixing and patching duty. Including the flooded area out front. The amount of effort it took to figure out how this drainage system works was something else. That thing that looks like a spiral staircase is actually a dead drainage outlet. I spent some time rerouting a power line to it, and now it's working properly.

<color=yellow>There's an outlet on the central rotating column. Hit the switch and it activates. Once the water is drained, the path beneath will be accessible.</color>

Best not to activate it unless absolutely necessary. Talos said it's the last line of defense against any intruders trying to get too deep into the Black Alley, so just keep it flooded unless our guys need to pass through.
InfoDisplay_160000013_Text:
I saw what happened to those who disappeared. I can't stay here any longer. The air here reeks of madness. I'm scared... scared that if I stay here, I'll become one of them. Cruel, twisted, with a complete disregard for the law.

How long have I been here? There's no sense of day or night down in these sewers. A week? A month? Maybe by the time I make it out of here, Ragunna City will already be a burning ruin with only the criminals left, throwing an endless carnival of destruction and evil.

They will destroy me and the city. Not even the sea can douse the hellfire in their hearts. It'll rage through the ruins, and we'll all burn to nothing... 

Imperator protect me... Yes, that's right. There's still hope. They'll protect my body and soul... They will.

I have a duty now. As a student. A journalist. And a believer. I... I must leave here, tell everyone the truth, and stop Talos before she poisons us all with her evil.

...And yes, I understand. I might die in the process, or even worse... if they catch me... But I can't just watch and let it all unfold. Damn it, legs! Move! Now's not the time...

They're being called away by Talos... Now's my chance. Fewer eyes on me. It has to be Brandon... I knew it. He drew them away.

I've got a knife hidden. Today's the day I've been waiting for. I've hidden voice recordings all over the Black Alley. If something happens to me, those who come after will know what happened here. Courage... Yes, only courage, the most precious human quality... can put an end to this madness.

Oh, great Imperator, grant me mercy from the high heavens. May your gaze forever watch over your believers, and grace them with courage and victory. May your light disperse the darkness looming over this place. And may justice descend upon the mortal world through your wings...
InfoDisplay_160000014_Text:
The path lies hidden within the blessings... The messengers, though extraordinary, are not without flaws. To proceed, one must present that which can heal their hearts.

<color=yellow>The messenger on the left has lost their way, unable to escape the mire.</color>
<color=yellow>The messenger in the center is scarred by betrayal, their heart sealed because of it.</color>
<color=yellow>The messenger on the right has achieved nothing, forever consumed by doubt.</color>

Present your qualities before them to restore their wholeness.

InfoDisplay_22010107_Text:
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part I</color>
"(This appears to be a personal memoir written by the now-retired Acolyte Julia. Most pages have been lost.)
 
That day, I recognized a familiar figure by the shelves in the Titular Repository. As I'd done in my youth, I tapped his shoulder. Andrea turned, recognized me, and murmured, "Teacher." He looked just as I remembered from our last meeting, yet years had slipped by unnoticed. He had come all this way just to see me. We found a quiet corner to talk.
 
Andrea spoke of his time as a traveling Acolyte, carrying the Sentinel's blessings beyond Ragunna to Riccioli, Septimont, Lilyland... through lands rich and poor, faithful and faithless. His journey must have been arduous yet extraordinary. The new wrinkles and scars on his face told me he was no longer that headstrong young man driven only by passion. His faith and ideals had forged him into a weathered knight.
 
But then, he began to confess. Not about duty, but about his daughter. It was the confession of a father, burdened with guilt toward a daughter he had failed. That kind of regret shouldn't have belonged to an Acolyte, so I did not offer the Sentinel's absolution in Their stead. The same devotion still shimmered in his eyes, and I knew he would continue traveling. Still a devout Acolyte. Still an absent father.
 
So I told him I was writing this memoir. I want to record my experiences here in Avinoleum, and in this very library. Most of them are trivial, yet each is a vivid reflection of the era I live in. These forgotten corners of history deserve to be remembered. The Sentinel teaches us to illuminate the world for others, and it's also important not to forget to light the way for those closest to us.
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part II</color>

"…
 
On an otherwise ordinary closing day, I was carrying a stack of old books across the platform outside the library when I was drawn, almost involuntarily, into a crowd of onlookers. A duel held every gaze. As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's breastplate, the match between Blessed Maiden and Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was.
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto. 
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. After some explanation from the Acolyte, we learned that Cadanto had recently saved a family from Tacet Discords near Avinoleum's outskirts. The towering Echo knight remained half-kneeling and silent. He didn't seem to understand why a human would offer him flowers, or perhaps he felt unworthy of such thanks?
 
"So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them." 
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs. 
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people."
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part III</color>

"…
 
Retirement drew closer with each passing day, and time flowed quietly within the library. I thought there would be no more ripples.
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold."

Greetings, Challenger {PlayerName}.

The stars of this moment shine for you. Thank you for stepping into Colosseum Olymdos with courage and skill, and for keeping the flames of dueling alive.

I've been watching you since the moment you defeated your first opponent. Your strategy, focus, and passion, and the thoughts you put into the decks you build... all remind me of the authentic passion I once held for this game.

Challenger, fight with all your heart! On this battlefield, giving your all is the highest form of respect one duelist can offer another. No matter who will emerge victorious tomorrow, this arena belongs to both of us, two souls fighting for what they love.

May the dawn bring us to a horizon broader than yesterday's.

—Conqueror of Prestige, a fellow duelist sharing your passion.
InfoDisplay_125000115_Text:
Lupa gazes at you intensely, her eyes sparkling with passion.

"I swear by the eternal sun." It's more than a promise, but a testimonial to the lone wolf's raw loyalty and sincerity. She may be yet another soul you salvaged in your long journey. But for Lupa, she's found something she never had—something that offers the long-awaited release of her anguish and pain. You'll never know what that is, and she won't tell you either. But that's all right. For both of you, this is enough.
InfoDisplay_125000116_Text:
Cartethyia smiles quietly. Watching her puts a smile on you, too.

After twenty years in her solitary confinement, she’s finally stepped out of that tower—back into the warmth of the crowd, into the embrace of sunlight and zephyrs. This is the moment she's been longing for through her turbulent years as the Blessed Maiden: to experience the mundanity of life, as Cartethyia, the Wandering Knight. And those three wishes she once made? They came true because you were there with her.
InfoDisplay_125000117_Text:
This special issue offers a detailed look at the legendary figures who once shone brightly in the history of Septimont. 

From Fabius and Atilius to Valeria, tales of the Hero of Heroes occupy half the pages.

The remaining half pays tribute to those who never wore a crown, yet gave everything for the glory of Septimont. Many met their end in the hunting grounds—names like Tercules, Magna, and Taurus, lost to time, yet remembered still.

In contrast to the lyrical prose favored by Ragunnesi writers, the style here is bold and unadorned. Yet, the punchy words always evoke the most epic imagery. Though born of the same origin, the voices of Rinascita's isles have long diverged in art and expression.
InfoDisplay_125000118_Text:
A Special Issue of The Gladiator Released Ahead of the Great Agon.

This new issue offers a look back at the storied history of past champions. From gripping duels to behind-the-scenes anecdotes, the magazine dives deep, especially in its extensive profile of current Ephor, Augusta.

But one year stands out for its omission.

That year's match ended on a strange note: the expected winner, a young girl from Ragunna, disappeared just before the award ceremony. Without receiving the victor’s medal, her win was never officially recognized.

"It’s unfortunate," the writer noted, "but without a proper conclusion, the result could never be confirmed. To this day, Mya’s standing remains a topic of debate."
InfoDisplay_125000119_Text:
The start date of each Great Agon varies. Please refer to announcements from the Ephor's Palace for official scheduling.

Preliminaries
The preliminaries follow a points-based system, with events including but not limited to: Echo Duels, Echo Speed Tests, and Echo Teamwork Challenges. These matches test a team's overall mastery of Echoes. At the end of the preliminaries, the top 20 teams by cumulative score will advance to the Finals.

Finals
The Finals follow a single-elimination format. The top 20 teams from the preliminaries, along with specially selected teams, will face off in one-on-one matches. Winners advance until the final match determines the Champion team.

Special Qualifiers
Also held in single-elimination format, the Special Qualifiers pit participants against each other in matches involving Echo vs. Echo or Echo vs. Gladiator combat. Victors inherit the defeated side's accumulated points. Once a participant reaches the required point threshold, they earn a direct entry into the Finals.
InfoDisplay_125000120_Text:

Both parties agreed to settle matters with a duel, only for an unknown overseas team to crash the event and claim victory for themselves. Was this an innocent case of rookie misstep, or a calculated move to turn the conflict into a spectacle? Stay tuned for more on this developing story...

If you spot an unaccompanied medical Echo wandering the streets, please contact Machaon Pharmacy immediately.

InfoDisplay_125000121_Text:
Arriving at Cliffside Harbor, start your journey with a visit to the Farrow Bridge Ruins, a silent testament to the divide forged by faith between Septimont and Ragunna. Continue along the Hero’s Way, an ancient path once trodden by Gladiators on pilgrimage to the legendary Colosseum Olymdos. Frequencies of their emotions still linger along the route, guiding travelers toward the majestic city on top of Capitoline Hill, where the awe-inspiring Gryphon’s Fortress stands.
...
Begin your day with a visit to Colosseum Olymdos to witness a live gladiatorial match (check the event schedule in advance and pick your favorite showdown). Explore the public rest areas of top Gladiators for a glimpse behind the scenes. Next, make your way to the Vale of Glory, where stone-carved weapons commemorate the legendary heroes and Gladiators of Septimont, whose names still echo through the ages.
...
Hop on the Cable Car and glide down to the bustling Caracalla Market, where you can sip the signature blends at Solis, browse arms and armor at the Silver Helmet Store, and pick up unique mementos at the Pygmalion Workshop. Cap off your journey with a relaxing soak at the Thermes Baths, where warm waters soothe away the weariness of your adventure.
...
This guide is for reference only. Feel free to plan your day according to your own pace. The best itinerary is always the one that suits you. May your time in Septimont be unforgettable!
InfoDisplay_161000007_Text:
(The page is filled with scattered, recently penned notes.)

As the name implies, Scourgewing dragons are often associated with ill omens in folklore, their appearance believed to be a harbinger of disaster. The first wave of sightings coincided with the eve of the first Dark Tide. Since then, their silhouettes have been reported ahead of nearly every major catastrophe.

But is such a connection real? Unlikely. It's a classic case of mistaking correlation for causation. In truth, Scourgewings don't bring disaster, certainly not the Dark Tide. They merely appear beforehand.

...

Some ecologists argue that the creature's frequency dates all the way back to the Age of a Thousand Islands. Though rare, the species has endured, likely owing to their acute sensitivity to environmental changes. The antennae on their heads can detect subtle environmental shifts, allowing them to avoid danger preemptively. The pattern we've observed points to a more grounded explanation: the Scourgewings sense the coming of disaster, and perhaps, in their own way, try to warn us.

They are not harbingers of disaster, but early messengers.

...

Locations of Note: <color=YellowD>Observation Tower in the Mournfell Canyon, Ashen Dragon's Crypt in the Border Mountains</color>
InfoDisplay_161000008_Title: Worn Journal of a Gladiator I
InfoDisplay_161000008_Text:
Every Gladiator in Septimont knows this place. It's where we hunt and test our mettle.

The dragon corpse lying out there draws in all sorts of TDs, beasts, and glory-chasing Gladiators like us. I've no doubt Flavio was here. I saw his breastplate in one of those old halls. His family sigil was split in half, perhaps his way of cutting ties with his House. I also couldn't help noticing the dents and gashes all over the armor, some deep, some just scratches. To us, those are medals.

Locals say this battered piece once belonged to a man who tamed a damn dragon, a Scourgewing. Faced it alone and made it submit to his will. While I was drowning in ale over my sister's death, Flavio was out in the wilds conquering with his sword. No one knows where he went with the dragon, but I know he's walking the path toward glory... He's becoming a legend.

A pack of Gladiators swaggered past me, fully armed. I overheard them talking. They were tracking a Scourgewing near the Border Mountains. But unlike Flavio, they weren't after a duel, only a dirty hunt.

They'll probably haul it back to the city and sell it off for a good price. That's all it is to them.
InfoDisplay_161000009_Title: Worn Journal of a Gladiator II
InfoDisplay_161000009_Text:
...

It's certain now. Something unnatural is happening outside. Every exit is sealed by forces not of this world. Iaen and I have no way out. Whispers claw at my ears. Only the pain of my wounds is keeping my mind from slipping away. This journal will likely be my last testament.

Here's the truth I've choked on for too long. Flavio and I, we swore to face off fair and square in the Colosseum finals, to settle our rivalry the right way. But the night before, his House sent someone to me with a message to hold back if things got rough. The offer came with better money than the prize, and a promise to find the best doctor for my ailing sister. I said yes... sold my honor as cheaply as those scum hunting Iaen. I disgraced that sacred fight with a pathetic show, and he saw right through me. I've never seen a man look so disappointed. In me, in his House, and in the arena itself. He vanished into the wilds and never returned.

After my sister passed, I tried to find him in Septimont. Thought I could square the debt and give him a real fight. As I write these words, I realize it wasn't just guilt that led me here. It was regret that I never faced him as a true Gladiator. Now I'll never have the chance.

I'm leaving this to Iaen. It will outlive me, no doubt. If someone ever reads these words, know they are the last confessions of Levis. I pray that Flavio, wherever the wilds have taken him, has found the glory that he deserves.

May applause greet all who walk the path of glory.
InfoDisplay_161000010_Text:
On Border Mountains, amidst the remains of a fallen dragon, a battle between man and dragon started.

The Gladiator held his breath, sword pointed skyward, like a living statue. The air trembled with a thunderous roar as brilliant wings unfurled, casting the land in shadow. One would descend, and one will rise to meet it. Only one would claim the victory.

As the sun bled across the mountains, the dragon finally lowered its head in defeat, surrendering to the man who tamed the wilderness.

That day, another hero was born upon the trial grounds.
InfoDisplay_161000011_Text:
(On the crumpled paper is faint, weathered handwriting.) 

Dear brother,

I understand why you did it... but that doesn't mean I forgive you.

I never cared for glory. All I ever cared was your dream. You, more than anyone, deserved to stand in the Colosseum and become a champion. But you gave it up for a dying woman, and tarnished all you and your friend held sacred.

Whatever comes next, please take care of yourself. Whether you return to the arena or choose another path, I only hope you find happiness. May my wish travel with the winds to your side.

Your family, always
InfoDisplay_250201_Text:
The Divinity must be whole.
No matter where the divine power scatters, I shall lead it back.
I will pursue Their enemies until every last fragment of the divine power is reclaimed to the Paradise, where the consciousnesses of people shall dwell securely.
When the Divinity returns, it shall be the day we walk toward unity and light once more.
InfoDisplay_250202_Text:
Why do I forget? Is it the erosion of time, or some deeper failing…? I must inscribe these secrets. I must remember:

The Dark Tide descending from the sky is the Divine Ordeal. It is born from the shadows of our hearts, twisting faith to fuel its unjust force of destruction.
This unfathomable darkness has long shackled the Ragunnesi's subconscious mind, blinding them to the true righteous path.
On this journey of survival, the weight of the martyrs' sacrifices has become unbearable.
People cannot perceive what lies beyond their own consciousness. Yet I, who have glimpsed the truth, must use external force to restore the Ragunnesi to their true and complete selves.
From among the faithful, a powerful Harbinger shall arise, bringing both life and annihilation from the Dark Tide into this world. 
Only by striking down this Harbinger, by descending into the depths of the darkness and using Their power to merge all the trapped souls into my own body, can I lead them all away from the Dark Tide.
The safe, undisturbed Lost Beyond shall be our new sanctuary. There, these souls shall find rest.
When tens of thousands of restored spirits unite as one to form a fortress of unshaken faith, believing together that it shall not come, then it will cease to exist.
Unity is our sole deliverance from the Divine Ordeal. Should the path falter, remember, "The Lantern" endures. It will guide you to the true light.

InfoDisplay_161000012_Text:
Returning to this base after so many years, I was struck by two things.

The first: however faintly, that father and daughter still cling to fragments of their sanity. As early movements in the final composition, their resilience exceeds anything I expected. Encouraging.

The second: the Dark Tide shows an odd mercy toward that nobleman.
Or perhaps, no matter how stained the soul, Septimontian blood still carries weight?

An undying monster... interesting.
InfoDisplay_161000013_Text:
Among that girl's belongings, I came across a recipe. It appears to be for a cake made with a generous amount of starch, sugar, and honey. To call it food feels generous. It's more akin to fuel for a warrior. Such a simple, heavy-handed dish speaks volumes of a culture without nuance.
......
.........
I went ahead and prepared a batch of this so-called Honeycake. Its sweetness, used as the main motif, is overwhelmingly blunt.
Even as mere sustenance, I find it difficult to accept something so lacking in even the most basic sense of refinement.
Still, the Gondola seemed pleased with the soft texture.
......
.........
I revised the recipe with Redcurrants and a layer of jam. This time, the flavor is at least tolerable.
I shared a bit with the Gondola. It rolled happily in the water, heh.
......
Turns out, it had quietly spat it back out.
ReignsBuff_1_Desc: In a display of her extraordinary strength and hard-earned honor, Augusta used her Forte to forge the challengers' swords into a great sword.
InfoDisplay_186700013_Text:
Ragunna Echoes Archive

...The energy of the Common Echoes comes from the Sentinel and unknown realms deeper than the ocean. With the Sentinel's guidance, the Order of the Deep swiftly gained control of the Common Echoes and used them to guide Their people...

...The first serious shortage of Common Echoes emerged, accompanied by a rise in smuggling and private purchases of Echoes among the city's nobility. There is an immediate need to upgrade the frequency-cutting technology to reduce the time needed to cut and merge different TD frequencies, ultimately establishing a mass-production line for creating Echoes of diverse forms and abilities...

...The Order of the Deep has obtained direct control of long-range aggregation technology. The Common Echoes they created would remain in a perpetual frequency-aggregate state within the boundaries of Rinascita, only to be disassembled under rare circumstances. This marks a breakthrough in the spatial and temporal limitations of Common Echoes, as well as a significant improvement in their stability...

...As opposition grew, the Order developed a new kind of Echo: La Guardia. They served as the watchful eyes and forceful hands of the Order, and their creation helped restore public trust in the ordinary Common Echoes...

...The experiments on implanting and shaping the consciousness of the Echoes in the Fabricatorium have shown progress. However, the data from the first samples couldn't be applied to any Common Echo, and the stability of their consciousness requires further refinement...
InfoDisplay_186700014_Text:
"Project Echo Reborn" Meeting Record

- Many TDs inherently possess consciousness. Even after being cut and bridged, their chaotic consciousness persists. That means they still tend to evolve by absorbing Reverberations after being stabilized into Common Echoes. While we've managed to suppress their absorption instinct post-frequency cutting, preventing their chaotic evolution, but to fully eliminate their consciousness...

- Perhaps we should change course and create entirely new consciousness modules. We can implant only the consciousness we need into the Echoes, forcibly overriding their original consciousness. The power They granted to us allows this. I've tested it.

- Overwriting their consciousness will only further destabilize the Common Echoes and disrupt the established methods of their creation.

- I think there might be a solution. The new consciousness module could be planted deep within the Echoes' original consciousness, functioning only when needed. In the meantime, we can continue researching how to improve the stability of consciousness transformation. But there's one thing, if the deeper consciousness is activated, it would be irreversible.

-We must delay activation indefinitely until we can ensure the Echoes' stability after alteration.

I want to learn so many instruments. I want to understand every musical sound.

Ms. Searle told me that many conductors are well-practiced in a range of instruments. I want to be like that too.

If I could make an orchestra reproduce the perfect melody in my mind, surely that would be my greatest joy.

Will that day ever come when I can precisely identify and control the sound of each instrument to transform every note into a passionate cry?

Ms. Searle also said there are times when I should give up the urge for control and give the orchestra space to breathe and create.

But if I do that, how will I be sure that the music at my command is flawless?
InfoDisplay_250206_Text:
{Male=He;Female=She} never appeared again.
I have already found a path of my own. This new path is the right one on which I shall complete the symphony of life and death.
I no longer need friends. All I need is a sharpened sword.
InfoDisplay_317000001_Text:
I'm sorry, Misha. It's been so long since I last reached out… You must've been so worried. This letter should've been in your hands days ago. But something happened. We were ambushed. A sudden attack by the Dark Tide's creations. The captain acted fast. Thanks to him, the team survived with just a few wounds. 

We retreated to Fabianum to recover. You remember this town, right? We once brought Ina here and watched Gladiatorial matches together. But now the streets are quiet. Everyone's off on the hunting grounds.

Don't worry about me. I'll be home soon, and by the time we can...
...
Sorry, Misha. I just can't lie to you. Everyone else in the team… they didn't make it.

Just before I wrote this, I buried the captain beneath a tree outside town. I've done this before, burying a companion's body. But no matter how many times I touch blood and soil, it never stops hurting. It never gets easier.

I'm scared, Misha. I wish I could come back to you right now. I wish I could hold you and Ina in my arms one more time. But I can't—not yet. If I turn back now, no one will know where the creatures are headed. So I'll stay and record the traces, so that the main troop could make use of it and set up defenses in time.

Please wait for me, Misha. Just a little longer. Ephor Valeria and the other Gladiators will arrive soon. Once they do… I'll come home. To you and Ina.
...
You know, I always thought of myself as a coward. Someone who didn't deserve to earn a girl's love. But then I met you. How very lucky I am. 

I'm sorry, Misha. I don't think I'll be able to keep that promise... To whoever finds this letter. Please, I beg you. Bring my necklace back to Misha at Hunter's Den. 

Let it stay with you in my place and watch over you, when I no longer can. That's all I ask.

Ah, Misha… The last bandage you gave me is gone now too...

InfoDisplay_26010001_Text:
To Gladiator Lord Aeolus,

I have received your withdrawal request. It is hereby denied. The glory of Septimont shall forever shine upon you—a true Gladiator.

Also, Mr. Aeolus, you were the seventh formidable opponent I faced on my path forward. Your swordsmanship and keen battle instincts left a deep impression on me. I will carry your blade, your ideals, and everything you stood for, and lead Septimont forward.

Please, bear witness.

With respect,
Ephor Augusta of Septimont
InfoDisplay_26010002_Text:
In sum, since Kerasaurs can rapidly adapt to a Gladiator's Resonance Attribute, it's best to either prepare ample traps or ensure a swift takedown before they fully adapt. Otherwise, at least two people are needed to take turns in the hunt.

If that day, I had faced the Kerasaur together with Master Cato, then…
InfoDisplay_26010003_Text:
To anyone who finds this note:
 
If you come across my body, do not be alarmed. 

I was attacked by TDs while exploring and managed to hide behind this waterfall by the skin of my teeth. The wounds are deep... I probably won't see the dawn. But no one said you have to write some famous last words when you're dying, right? We can all relax about it.

I wasn't able to find the legendary treasure of Three Heroes' Crest, but... you're not entirely out of luck. There's a simple challenge. A puzzle. I've hidden my life's savings in a secret hideout in the hunting grounds.

<color=Highlight>It's located beside the House of Prophecy, beneath the Hornett.</color>

Go and have a look if you're interested. That shall be... the treasure I leave for fellow explorers.

Blast it, my vision... It's beginning to blur. Best of luck to you.
 
Cheery Peso
InfoDisplay_26020001_Text:
The plan with the Unwritten One... I didn't expect {Male=him;Female=her} to see through me so easily.
Has {Male=he;Female=she} been through something like this too? Still, {Male=he;Female=her} extended the offer. And I had no reason to say no.
After all, no one wants to face the one behind those hands more than I do. I need to ask him why was this fate forced upon me? By what right did he invent my life and fabricate my existence?
But… I've waited too long. I'm starting to doubt the plan was ever meant to work. Who would care about a discarded pawn?
But what other path remains?
InfoDisplay_26020002_Text:
6:00 Morning
Woke up a little earlier than usual. Still thinking about the prophecy Grandmother Lillibet mentioned yesterday, I guess… On the bright side, I won't be late for morning oration!

8:00 Morning
Breakfast was milk, fruit, and herb bread. I'm still not used to eating on a fixed schedule, but the senior Priestesses say discipline makes a proper Priestess.

12:00 Noon
Classes are over. I think I managed to see a little farther today. We all went for lunch together. Bland as ever. Nothing worth writing about.

2:00 Afternoon
The Senate sent someone to speak with Grandmother Lillibet. Something about the prophecy of Septimont and the Hero of Heroes… I didn't catch the rest. Will I be able to have visions like that?

5:00 Dusk
I wish I could go outside and play. Or just go home. But everyone else is so focused… Sister Sophia carved an entire wall today. She's amazing.

7:00 Evening
Went for a little stroll after dinner. Saw a few stars!

11:00 Late Night
Time for bed, though I'm not sleepy at all. Sometimes following the schedule feels like a chore. But today was... not bad, I guess.
InfoDisplay_26020003_Text: Attempt 1 I think I can try. No… I will try. Attempt 7 Still nothing… O light and fate above, must you torment your most faithful disciple? Attempt 23 It's no use. I see nothing... Why? How did I succeed before? Attempt 66 It's fate I'm facing. I should yield... No, no! I will not give in! Get it together, Ariadne! You are a damned Priestess, act like one! InfoDisplay_26010005_Text:
I found this Chest Mimic while treasure hunting in an underground ruin somewhere in Ragunna, after chasing after some wild myths.
I carried it with me across Rinascita, setting it as a constant reminder for myself—the purpose of our journey is not to pursue wealth. Rather, the process of exploring the unknown is a treasure in itself.
 
(Oh, by the way, I've checked with the Montellis, and due to its mint condition, it's actually worth quite a bit.)
InfoDisplay_26010006_Text:
I never imagined I would come to learn your name, only to meet you at your grave.
You were unstoppable in the arena, yet they say you cherished nothing more than petting your Ta-da. You must have been a man of both power and heart.
Sleep well, my sweet Gladiator.
Our Ta-da wakes to another dawn, and so is our peaceful Septimont.
InfoDisplay_26010101_Text:
Of the Three Heroes' Crest, besides the exploits of the Heroes of Heroes, there is another story seldom told.

A young gladiator once climbed the summit alone after a hunt. When he returned to the camp, his companions were astonished, for this "Dragon Slayer" bore upon his body more than a hundred wounds, large and small. He had clearly endured some dreadful battle, a trial beyond imagining.

The gladiator smiled wryly, admitting his defeat. Many remember this as the first failure of the "Flawless Hero." His second failure—the tragedy of Fabianum—would follow not long after.

That gladiator was Magno, the former Ephor of Septimont.

Feel free to share your thoughts! One day, I'll turn this place into the best cafe in all of Honami! ——Miki
……

I heard the best detectives in the city hang out here. I hope they can help me find Dad and Mom. ——Rika

Miki put up a wind chime in the cafe today. She says it carries the melodies of the wind. Even though I can't go outside or fly, hearing it ring makes me feel like my wish has already come true. ——Kirine

Miki and I made paper lanterns. Here's to a booming business this year! That way, I can keep working here and make more money. ——Aomame

Why are ALL the sodas Firi puts in the fridge PEPPER flavored? This is disgusting. How can a man with the heart of a tiger drink something like this? ——Shouta

Peasant with no taste. You'll understand the sophistication of pepper soda one day. ——Firi

Why are all the capybaras here named after railroad lines... If I had taken the train to look for her that day, would things have been different? ——Aoba
……

I came to the cafe that Aoba talked about. We never got to meet here, but I'd know his handwriting anywhere. ——Ichika

I got interviewed by the local news station today as the owner! My first time on TV... I was so embarrassed! But... if people's connections are like a railroad network, then maybe one day, a train from this little station will reach all the way to where Dad is. ——Miki

This is a cool little spot. It's got real investment potential! But the owner says she's happy with it like this and worries her regulars won't find it if she moves. I don't get it. You could just put up a sign. ——Eriko
……

I brought you the limited-edition Namipon plushie you always wanted as a kid.
I will carry on your dream of keeping this cafe running forever...
InfoDisplay_28050001_Text:
To my darling daughter Misha:

Mommy is going on a long trip, and I'm sorry I won't be able to come home on time this time.
One of Mommy's friends will come along to bring you Academy stickers, medicine, and food.
You need to be good, eat regularly, take your medicine, sleep well, and stay tucked in at night. Don't go out willy-nilly.
As for the Academy, we'll talk about it more when Mommy comes back.
I have many, many new stories for you. Stay at home and wait for me to return.

With love,
Mom (Vantier)
InfoDisplay_28050002_Text:
To the kind-hearted person who finds this note:

The Exoswarm and I can no longer hold on.
Where do those caught by the Void Storm go?
I wish I could return to light like the Soliskin.
How I long to become a ray of light, to forever shine upon my daughter.
Kind stranger, please take the stickers, supplies, and the previous note, and bring them to my daughter.
Follow the trail of stickers I left along the way, and you'll find my home.

With gratitude,
Vantier
InfoDisplay_28050003_Text:
To {Male=big brother;Female=big sister}:
 
When Mom said she was going on a long trip, she meant she'd be "returning to light, like the Soliskin," right?
For a long time, I knew this day would come. Mom will go, and so will I.
Really, I should have "returned to the light" long ago. I stayed because of Mom.
It hurts… Maybe once I return to the light, it won't hurt anymore? It will be warm, I think.
Anyway, I have to return to the light, to be with Mom.
I give these stickers to you, {Male=big brother;Female=big sister}.
Please remember to put the stickers on your motorbike and see the world for me.
 
Misha

Pursuant to the Lahai-Roi Voidmatter Protection and Safety Regulations, and following joint review by the Department of Voidmatters and Academy President Lucilla, approval is hereby granted for the specially confined Resonator "Denia" to conduct escorted activities within limited areas.

InfoDisplay_36050003_Text:
I never imagined a mere glimpse at the the ██'s knowledge could yield such fresh insights.

So this is how the so-called ████ of civilizations perceives Solaris.

...

No more need to hunt down those Reverberations soaked in gentle emotion just to serve as a base for the ██.

The intensity of emotion carried by the Reverberations no longer matters. Strip them away completely, and we can mass-produce ideal materials. Though this calls for further experimentation.

...
