InfoDisplay_36050004_Title: News Highlight of the New City (Excerpt)
InfoDisplay_36050004_Text:
...

The beacon fires of the Fortress and Gorges War at last burned low, and peace was restored across the realms.

Mingting issued a proclamation, calling upon the full might of Huanglong to raise a new fortified city south of the Central Plains and naming it Jinzhou. Thenceforth, the lands east of the Mountains of Spirits and south of the Norfall Barrens fell under Jinzhou's jurisdiction.

The first Magistrate of Jinzhou decreed that the city would bear no emblem of its own. Instead, it would share the insignia of Huanglong, in remembrance of the bond forged in aid with the one capital and five cities.

...
InfoDisplay_36050005_Text:
(There's messy handwriting crammed into the margins, seemingly added bit by bit over time.)

Shifu once mentioned some Nethermancer who tracked a Mirage Realm, snuck into the Sanctum... and got mysteriously dumped right back at the entrance.

Heh. Bet you anything that "Nethermancer" was him.

So this Mirage Realm was probably here in the Sanctum the whole time, not something Muyu created. Well, we're still inside the Sanctum, at least.

...

Apart from the ground, this Mirage Realm roughly divides into three layers: the <ano=Human>Ren</ano> Realm, the <ano=Earth>Di</ano> Realm... and the one above them, which I guess should be called the "<ano=Heaven>Tian</ano> Realm." Each layer's got its own Cloud Shuttles running. And there's this lightway hanging right before the whole fleet, the only way to move between layers.

Could that lightway be our ticket out of here? Need to check.

...

It's confirmed. Muyu still doesn't have full control over these Cloud Shuttles and Autopuppets. So he's basically squatting in this Mirage Realm at the end of the day.

Sure, he can somehow order the Autopuppets to attack.

But it's more like... he's hijacking the Cloud Shuttles' own defense systems.

Mostly he just rigged the mechanisms with this mist laced with Reverberations. That's how he got into the Sanctum in the first place. It's actually some kind of Disorienting Fog, and it spreads fast, corrupts fast. Any regular mechanism that touches it goes haywire real quick.

Stay sharp, {PlayerName}.
InfoDisplay_36050006_Text:
Now, let's talk about Muyu.

On the surface, he's a madman who won't shut up about his plans and ideals. But the guy's actually careful. Real cagey. He knows how to cover his real face or what he's really after.

Back in Xuanfang Hold, he had almost everyone fooled. He used the Reverberations from the Fortress and Gorges War to mess with the Autopuppets, got them to turn on the Hold and tear the place apart. All of that just to test his methods and carve out a window to sneak his true body into the Sanctum. Yes, all that trouble, every piece set just so, only to slip into this Mirage. Nobody knows the full picture but him. Not even the Zhuojun Atelier's main branch got the real story.

If you and Paragon Qingxiao get to him first, don't let him talk his way around you.
...

Good thing I attached my Resonance Energy to that Qingfu pendant I gave you earlier.

If you run into something super weird along the way, it might just come in handy.

...

Not sure if you'll ever see this. Maybe it'll just be me facing Muyu inside this Mirage in the end. Guess I never said it outright. I came to make trouble for him too, same as you.

Gonna sniff out whatever scheme that bastard's cooking, then find my moment to end him.

But since he's got all those Autopuppets with him, I'll need a few cards up my sleeve.

My money's on you, great {PlayerName}.

If you found these messages, then we're not far apart.
InfoDisplay_36050007_Title: Records of Huanglong Tacet Discord: Jinzhou
InfoDisplay_36050007_Text:
...
On Mt. Firmament, there dwells a Tacet Discord. Its form resembles a tiger, with golden eyes and a cyan face. Its back is covered in scales, and its long tail is tipped with spines. It is called the Lightstrider. Fierce by nature, it shuns company and claims the open wilds as its own. It fights with teeth and claws, its strength enough to shatter stone. When angered, it can transform its gleaming scales into projectiles, moving through the air as swiftly as a beam of light.

When an ordinary person sees its radiance in the distance, they should fall silent and take a wide berth. On no account should they provoke it.

If caught in a narrow encounter with no way to retreat, one must still the heart and act according to the moment. When it lunges from above, meet it head‑on to break its momentum. If strength proves insufficient, seize the first chance to flee and avoid its edge. Above all, do not hesitate. A moment of doubt is a moment of ruin.

InfoDisplay_102189701_Text:
It's been forty-eight hours. I don't think they'll find us now.
 
You've done well, old friend. This is where your journey ends. I never expected a Sabercat Reaver. Without the proper tools, I can't fix you.
 
It seems I was born worthless and will die the same. I had originally hoped for you to record the effects of the Void Storm on the human body and the surrounding environment when I entered it, then deliver the data to the Spacetrek Collective. A coward's last shred of dignity.
 
The Academy will find the note in my room soon enough. Yes, this is a journey to die. I intend to let the Void Storm take my life.
 
Perhaps someone will find this journal long after I'm gone. Let it serve as my farewell to you, stranger.
 
Forgive me for leaving without a proper farewell. Please understand, this isn't a sudden impulse, but the final compromise after a long and painful struggle.
 
As a researcher who once held science as my faith, I believed that the pursuit of knowledge is civilization's most noble mission. My field once granted me glimpses of the universe's profound beauty. Those elegant equations on the blackboard seemed to guide me toward pushing open the doors of progress.

But perhaps every era is destined to face the same tragedy. Researchers believe they stand on the shoulders of giants, only to look down one day and find themselves standing on the ruins of their own idealism. Failure, after failure, after failure... Was this always my limit?
 
That's when a colleague reached out. He claimed he could help me overcome my technical bottlenecks, but everything had to be done in secret. I later discovered he was a Fractsidus spy. On the day he was captured, he never revealed our collaboration. He only left me with a smile. What was he smiling at? That I was next? Or that I was no longer the man I used to be? In our work together, I had already crossed lines that violate scientific ethics.
 
The purity of knowledge in my eyes had long been corrupted. Whenever I heard my colleagues' praise during academic conferences, I felt my stomach twist. Their admiration was evidence of my betrayal of science.
 
Death is all that's left for me now. But even though my soul is sullied, I wish to leave one last, small thing of value before I go.
 
The Void Storm. None would volunteer to enter it. I imagine if someone would go into it... It would certainly garner data of immense value.
 
I do not seek forgiveness, nor do I expect to be understood. I only hope my departure becomes a question mark, lingering in the minds of those who still believe in the purity of knowledge...

Death only gives one chance. I can't waste it. First, I must observe the Void Storm. Perhaps I'll stay with the Roya tribe until I'm ready.
InfoDisplay_102189702_Text:
Time has lost all meaning to me. It's nothing but a countdown now.
 
I haven't encountered the Void Storm yet, but I've learned much from the Royan archives. Their records speak of survivors. What allows one to live through it? Where is the line that decides what gets erased and what remains?
 
Ugh... this fever won't break. I should set aside these heavy thoughts for today.
 
Why is it that whenever I relax, I am reminded of the Roya tribe members from when I first arrived?

I watched them live alongside the Exoswarm, toiling with simple tools. I saw them observe the night sky and strange phenomena with their own eyes, patiently calculating, step by step, summarizing patterns.
 
At night, they would sit around the campfire. No one dwelled on the day's troubles. They simply planned for tomorrow, then sang a song with a strange, simple, repetitive melody, as if speaking to Lahai-Roi. Or perhaps it was their way of encouraging themselves.

Watching the firelight dance on their faces—wrinkled and young—a profound confusion struck me.
 
We, in our "advanced" civilization, seek to master nature through technology, to eliminate all uncertainty and pain. When progress stalls, we despair, even betray our morals for a breakthrough. We believe human dignity lies in "conquest."
 
But for the Roya... even though a "small" storm could wipe away everything they worked so hard to build, they show no despair. Their dignity isn't about "conquest." Instead, they chose silence. Time and time again, they bend their bodies, measure the broken land with their feet, and begin anew.
 
I once despised this "inefficient" struggle, seeing it as a sign of an unprogressive society. But now, what rises in my heart is… respect.
 
Such a feeling of contradiction claws at me from the inside. The "pure science" I've pursued my entire life, if it ultimately led me to betrayal and nihilism, then where is its purity? These tribal people, who knew nothing of "science" at first, have proven a more fundamental purity through their very existence—the will to struggle and live, no matter how many times they're beaten down.
 
Here I am, the lofty professor, brought down from my high horse. I'm driven to suicide by the "impurity" of my ideals, while they, with their hands in the dirt, fight to live. In that struggle, they embody life's truest purity.
 
The rain outside grows louder, much like their song… I'll leave once the fever breaks. I need to get closer to the Void Storm, to understand it more. My old droid friend may be broken, but I still have a way to record it all. If I remember correctly, there should be an Outcast camp up ahead.
InfoDisplay_102189703_Text:
This is likely my final recording. I haven't formally introduced myself yet. I am Sestan, a professor from Startorch Academy.
 
I don't know what awaits me now...
 
I was perched at a high point, recording data on the Void Storm. While adjusting my instruments, I saw a mech reindeer, unaware, drifting too close to the edge of the distortion. Slowly. So slowly. I knew an invisible force would snuff out its fragile life in an instant.

In that moment, my mind went blank.
 
I did not weigh the value of life, did not calculate the odds of success, did not look back on a lifetime of sins and confusion. My body acted before any rational thought could intervene.
 
I rushed forward and pushed the reindeer out. And I was pulled in instead.
 
Life is full of surprises. To be honest... I had already let go of any thought of suicide. This journey, the people I've met along the way... they showed me how.
 
In the Roya tribe, I witnessed the strength of the human spirit. In the Outcast camp, among fellow traitors, I learned about forgiveness from their struggle to survive. Everyone was just trying to live, while I was wallowing in self-pity, clinging to the guise of an idealist.
 
My life and my ideals had strayed from their path. And so... in this moment, I rushed forward. Not just toward death, but toward a reunion with the true spirit of science: to protect life, no matter how small.
 
Before I vanish completely, I'll try to remain conscious. I will record my physical sensations and the frequency fluctuations, then upload the data to this Cassette and a data drive. Consider this my final observation report. I hope it proves useful.
 
Body temperature: normal... Wrist movement: normal... Feet, hmm... losing sensation...
 
………………
 
Twenty-three minutes have passed...
 
…………
 
Hmm... Death, is it always this quiet? I used to think my students were too noisy. But now, haha, I find myself missing the noise...
 
External sound... decaying rapidly...
 
Hmm... after the sounds disappear, will the light go next...?
 
Finally... I'm home...

To guarantee absolute laboratory safety, data integrity, and personnel welfare, the following guidelines form the mandatory protocol for all experimental operations. Any deviation constitutes a major breach of research conduct.

A. Qualifications and Procedures

1. Unauthorized work is prohibited. All personnel must adhere to the work permit system.
2. Do not violate, bypass, or damage lockout/tagout procedures.

B. Information and Reporting

3. Do not conceal, delay, or falsify reports of any safety incidents, anomalies, or deviations.

C. Personal Health and Protection

4. Do not enter hazardous areas without proper and effective personal protective equipment.
5. Do not report for work under the influence of alcohol or any medication that impairs mental stability.
6. Do not perform safety-critical tasks while fatigued, in poor health, or under significant emotional distress.

D. Equipment and Authority

7. Do not exceed your authority to alter equipment operating status or system configurations.
8. Do not use uncalibrated, out-of-calibration, or expired instruments and tools.

E. Environment and Responsibility

9. Keep all fire escapes and emergency exits clear. Do not misappropriate or damage fire safety equipment.
10. Do not ignore unsafe acts. Intervene if you see a safety violation. Safety is a shared responsibility.
ItemInfo_102181706_Name: What You Should Never Do As A Startorch Express Passenger (Excerpt)
InfoDisplay_102181706_Text: 1. Food and Beverages For your safety, eating and drinking are strictly prohibited while the Express is in motion. Due to potential environmental hazards or Exoswarm activity, the Express may execute emergency braking at any time. Violation of this rule may result in choking, or injury from food packaging. The risk is significantly higher during vertical transit phases within the Starward Riseway. The high acceleration forces present a severe health hazard if consumables are ingested. 2. Pets, Bionic Units, & Exoswarm To maintain onboard safety and order, all pets and bionic devices must be checked in for transport. Live animals must be placed in sturdy carriers. Bionic units must be powered down and stored in secure containers before check-in. Bringing them into passenger carriages is strictly prohibited. Exoswarm may board only in designated compartments under the supervision of a licensed Shepherd. Exoswarm must undergo prior training to prevent panic responses during sudden acceleration, which could compromise the safety of all onboard. If you require a pet carrier or storage container, please visit the loading area for assistance. 3. Jumping During Vertical Acceleration or Descent This rule may sound absurd, but every absurd rule comes from an even more absurd real incident. A rumor once circulated claiming that a person "cannot jump" during vertical acceleration or descent. While basic physics, some students took it as a personal challenge. They fabricated exoskeleton rigs, smuggled them aboard, and attempted to "challenge the laws of nature." Fortunately, staff intervened in time to prevent what would have been certain injury and significant damage to the Express. During all operations, please remain seated with your safety belt fastened. Do not attempt any dangerous behavior.
InfoDisplay_102181707_Text:
Under the stars, we are both observers and part of the cosmos itself. When you close this guide, your real journey has only just begun.

Forget the names of the constellations. What matters is that you looked up and let the starlight in. The moment you first lost yourself in the beauty of the stars is more precious than any astronomical fact.

A gentle reminder for every stargazer:
1. There's no need to bring advanced telescopes. A curious heart is all you need.
2. Pick a night when the moon is shy, and the sky is clear.
3. Bring a star chart, a flashlight, and a friend who'd love to share the quiet of a starlit night with you.

When the starlight touches you, remember this: every cell, every fiber, every element that makes you you was born in the heart of a star. You are, in your own way, stardust made manifest.

May the stars always bring you peace and inspiration.

Dedicated to all those who have ever stopped and looked up.

ItemInfo_30010006_Title: Void Energy Directional Release Project: Strategic Plan for Acquiring Core Energy Based on the Reactor Drive's Emergency Response Mechanism
InfoDisplay_30010006_Text: Abstract Spacetrek Collective research confirms the Reactor Drive is a critical component of the Exostrider. However, its extreme defenses and inaccessibility render conventional acquisition impossible. This paper proposes a groundbreaking strategic initiative: the Void Energy Directed Release Project. The core mechanism relies on the symbiotic defensive link between the Reactor and its key anchor—the Solistrees of Bjartr Woods. We demonstrate that precise deployment of specialized Voidmatter carriers into the root zone of the Solistrees can effectively compromise this ecological anchor. This contamination will trigger the Reactor Drive's highest-level immune response, forcing it to deviate from its current orbit and descend in physical form to a designated area, entering a recoverable state. This paper details the interaction model between Voidmatter and the Solistree ecosystem, the trigger thresholds of the Reactor Drive's emergency response mechanism, predicted impact trajectories, and the Spacetrek Collective Research Institute's rapid recovery procedures at the designated site. The proposed strategy provides a theoretically viable and strategically definitive pathway to acquiring the Reactor Drive, a decisive step toward the ultimate activation of the Exostrider. Keywords: Void Energy; Reactor; Emergency Response Mechanism; Exostrider; Bjartr Woods; Solistree; Strategic Acquisition Chapter 1: Introduction The Necessary Cost: On the Advancement of Civilization …… Evaluation Result: Proposal Not Approved Spacetrek Collective Research Institute

InfoDisplay_30010011_Text: Startorch Academy Traffic Safety Regulations Article 1 These Regulations are enacted to maintain traffic order within Lahai-Roi, prevent and reduce accidents, and safeguard faculty, students, and scientific assets. All traffic participants within the jurisdiction of Startorch Academy must comply. Article 2 The Academy shall establish and improve a coordinated traffic safety management system. Academic departments and student organizations shall participate in traffic impact assessments related to campus construction and research projects, and develop appropriate safety management plans and implementation measures. Article 3 Any individual applying for vehicle operation privileges within the Academy must present valid driving credentials, thoroughly study these Regulations, and pass an online assessment within three weeks of application. Article 4 The following acts are prohibited while operating a vehicle: (1) Making calls on handheld Terminals, rushing to meet thesis deadlines, watching online courses, or engaging in any other activity that impedes safe driving. (2) Coasting downhill with the engine turned off or in neutral. (3) Entering areas affected by Void Storms without authorization. (4) Parking vehicles directly in front of academic halls. (5) Preparing or consuming cup noodles in an open sidecar. (6) Using residual engine heat to warm food. (7) Feeding, provoking, or otherwise interacting with wild Exoswarm while driving. Article 5 Vehicle operation within the Academy shall adhere to the following rules: (1) A speed limit of 10 km/h shall be observed. Violators will have their vehicles impounded and be required to attend traffic safety lectures for seven consecutive days after class. (2) Vehicles may not be operated on ropeways, slide rails, or other fixed mechanical paths. (3) Driving is prohibited after more than 16 consecutive hours of work or study. Continuous driving shall not exceed 4 hours during daytime or 2 hours at night. (4) Helmets must be worn when operating expedition motorbikes. (5) Untamed or research-stage Exoswarm may not be used for towing, pulling, or riding alongside vehicles. (6) Safety structures such as doors or roofs may not be removed in pursuit of "better aerodynamics." (7) Meditation, synchronization training, or any activity likely to impair physical awareness while driving is prohibited. (8) If a vehicle's energy core is known to be overloaded, operators must report it immediately and evacuate the area. Posting a "Danger" sign alone is not sufficient. …… Violations will be handled according to their severity and may result in warnings, temporary vehicle confiscation, suspension of driving privileges, revocation of experimental access or funding, or assignment to "road-cleaning volunteer duty." Serious offenses will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with Academy policies. Reminder from S.I.G.M.A.: Please be advised that all violations will be recorded as infractions and may be publicly listed within the Academy. Do not test these rules. Safe travel begins with you.

InfoDisplay_162750024_Text:
She mixed me a drink once, called "Starfall."
It was the most exquisite taste I've ever known.
But she left no recipe.
She said it wasn't necessary. That even with a recipe, the taste could never be recreated.
"If you love it," she told me, "then cherish the moment you drink it."
InfoDisplay_162750025_Text:
She said eternity is a lie, a delusion.
"Then what is real?" I asked.
"The answer is where a river of stars falls. Come with me, and we'll see it together."
But I could not go.
Our visions of life were too far apart. I would not yield.
So I swore I would recreate the taste of "Starfall."
What was in it? Grenadine, Bols Blue, sparkling water, salt on the rim, and a lemon wedge.
Or was there something else?
Perhaps a hint of regret, or the weight of a sigh?
InfoDisplay_162750026_Text:
She always loves fleeting things.
She loves the flicker of light, the glow of dusk, the fall of a flower.
Meteors in the night sky, ripples on a lake.
She loves the tide rising and falling.
A dancer leaping in midair.
And most of all… fireworks.
Those moments are beautiful, I know.
But what comes after?
How do I face their vanishing?
I wish such moments could last forever.
But she never seemed to care.
I don't understand.
I truly don't.
InfoDisplay_102181710_Text:
Log Entry–No. 322 I
Created by: Amur
 
The Shimmer was not present, and Void Storm concentration remains within normal parameters. However, a Void Storm burst occurred moments ago, engulfing our research outpost. The storm caught two personnel off guard, sweeping them both away. Fortunately, they sounded the emergency alarm in their final moments, ensuring that Tavia and I could evacuate just in time.
 
The storm took our vehicles, and it's only a matter of time before it catches up to us.
 
Haha, I heard that very few manage to survive a Void Storm. We've already encountered a Void Storm burst, which they call a one-in-a-billion event, so who's to say we won't end up meeting another that could save our lives? My vacation was supposed to start in two days... I even planned to call my mom.
 
The storm is closing in, but thankfully, I found a sled some researcher was kind enough to leave behind. I'm going to take a gamble: if we slide down this steep slope, we might be able to outrun the Void Storm. I think our chances are pretty good—after all, the odds of finding something like this in the access-restricted Roya Frostlands were small to begin with, so it looks like our luck is holding up.
 
Wish me luck, Mom.
 
Log Entry–No. 322 II
Created by: Tavia
Amur was taken by the Void Storm. I'll be joining him soon.
 
The sled was broken—that's why it was left behind. We spent too much time checking it and lost valuable time. But even if we hadn't picked it up, the Void Storm would have still swallowed us whole sooner or later. It's unfortunate we took a gamble and lost.
 
The Void Storm is growing stronger. I'm afraid I won't make it. Even so, I'll keep running to minimize Voidmatter corruption to the FCR.
 
Hopefully, the data collected will prove useful to future researchers.
...
...
Body temperature dropping. I can't feel my hands and feet anymore. The Void Storm is fading, but I can't go any further. I'm going to take one last gamble and toss my FCR down below.
 
If this report is recovered intact, then I'll have won my final bet.
 
Wish me luck in the name of truth and science.
InfoDisplay_102181711_Text:
3.11 Introduction to Gear 
 
The standard issue clothing for scientific research expeditioners is lined with thick, insulated composite padding. This design helps maintain body temperature for extended periods in extreme cold and offers protection in the event of an accidental fall. However, falling on ice may still cause injuries to unprotected areas (such as the head). Therefore, anti-slip ice cleats are recommended when hiking across icy terrain.
 
Researcher's annotation: Don't worry too much, as long as you practice proper falling techniques, injury is unlikely. The protective properties of these clothes are no joke, but still, make sure to protect your head by using the correct posture. By the way, ice cleats aren't very effective on hard, icy surfaces, and they might lacerate or otherwise injure you if you fall. Wearing them at all times is not recommended.
 
……
 
16.2.1 Procedure for Being Stranded on Ice
 
Should you become stranded on ice after a slip or fall, do not attempt to stand up on your own, as concentrated ground force may cause the ice to fracture, or you may suffer injuries from falling a second time. Instead, remain prone and use your hands and feet to push along the ice, gradually moving your body toward the edge of the ice surface. Only attempt to stand once you have reached the edge.
 
If others are nearby, have them use a rope to pull you off the ice. Under no circumstances should you venture into an area of hazard before a careful assessment has been made of the conditions of the ice underfoot.
 
Researcher's annotation: Given the correct posture, you can remain steady even on slippery ice. The key is to keep your center of gravity as low as possible, keep your upper body upright, and use both hands to balance… All right, this might not sound very intuitive, but you'll probably understand after one or two falls. If you do end up falling, just call out to me—I'll get you off the ice with practiced ease.

In a small town, a former mercenary from the New Federation found his quiet retirement life shattered by a corporate pen-stroke. A series of wolfish policies vaporized his savings overnight and left his family shattered beyond repair.
Determined to strike back at the corrupt conglomerate, he returns to the capital, not as a soldier, but as a rising financial prodigy. And so begins a revenge that will take the capital by storm...

On a train bound for Lilyland, a weary traveler fleeing his past in Ragunna stumbles into a designer chasing inspiration. Following that fateful encounter, he resolves to write her one letter every single day until the day he dies.
A century later, the designer steps onto Ragunna's soil, his letters pressed to her heart...
InfoDisplay_32010023_Text: Once known as a legendary Discord Hunter, he abandoned the shadows and took holy vows, dedicating his life to tending the sacred Echoes granted by divine will. InfoDisplay_32010025_Text: Home on military leave, Changchuan finds himself trapped in an arranged marriage. Determined to escape, he plans to flee the day before the wedding. Leaping aboard a departing train, they set off on an unexpected romantic adventure.

InfoDisplay_320197802_Text:
Today, I walked through the valley of the shadow of death. I was surrounded by a swarm of Tacet Discords.
Right when I'd given up hope, I heard a noise. It wasn't the wind, but a crisp, rhythmic "ding... ding..." like a sharp blade tapping against ice.
I forced my eyes open. They were practically sealed shut with the frost.

A figure appeared before me. A girl, I think. White robes. She held a long, straight blade made of ice, transparent and clear. As she moved, the tip would occasionally graze the ground, making that cold "ding-ding" sound.
 She didn't say a word. Just walked toward the swarm. The snow swallowed her fast. I heard the "ding... ding..." of her blade against the ground a few more times before everything fell silent. When I looked again, both she and the Discords were gone.
 
I didn't think. I just ran. When I got back to camp, my colleagues  looked at me like they'd seen a ghost. Turns out I'd been missing for four hours. I told them everything. They said it was a hallucination.
So... was it?
Does a woman with a blade of ice truly walk the frostlands of Lahai-Roi?
Maybe I should go back there tomorrow and take another look.
InfoDisplay_102194704_Text:
My aunt hails from Egla Town, a place where the windmills never tire and the wild winds carry the legends of the knights on every breeze. I once dreamed of journeying there, but Rinascita is a world away. My studies have ever kept me from following where the knights might lead.
...
Until the day I met them. It was then I realized that Lahai-Roi had knights of its own.
Seven times they saved me. Seven times the debt weighed heavily on my heart. All I craved... was to be their guardian knight. Just once.
...
Now, that chance has arrived. The teachers spoke of a great Void Storm approaching, a calamity that could wipe them out in a single breath.
I managed to lead them to safety... but in the doing, I myself was claimed by the storm.
Is this where my journey ends? A fitting conclusion to my tale, I suppose.
But then... Hogarth, the Seventeenth Grand Commander, appeared.
Though small in stature, he pulled me into the safety of his hollow frame—his "trash bin" vessel—and with every ounce of his strength, he scaled the high ground.
"Joljotra, your summer vacation ends today as the true Seventeenth Grand Commander. You shall begin a glorious new semester for yourself... while I take up the mantle as the Grand Commander who follows."
So it declared.

InfoDisplay_102176802_Text:
Half a notebook has been stuffed into a waterproof bag. The edges are badly worn, as if someone kept grabbing it, letting go, then clutching it again.
The serial numbers are gone. They replaced them with names.

[Daniel - Entry 1]
We found it. The Cobalt Sediment is way more "alive" than the records suggested. 
It isn't evenly distributed. Instead, it gathers along fractures in the ice, almost as if something is pulling it into place.
Now that the warming period has begun, its reflectivity is increasing.
This might be our only chance to observe it fully exposed. I know Amundsen is worried about extraction, but if we turn back now, we'll never get better data than what our models produce. 
...I think it's responding to us.

[Amundsen - Entry 1] 
I told them we need to stop and wait. 
Going on foot isn't viable. The Blue Phase Layer is exposed far more than we expected, and our sense of direction is starting to exhibit discrepancies.
Daniel insisted on pushing forward. Calls it "researcher's intuition." 
I'm not buying it. Intuition doesn't replace a solid extraction plan.

[Wegener - Entry 1]
Logging an anomaly.
The Blue Phase Layer is affecting our perception, but not in the form of hallucinations. It's distorting how we register the presence of others.
Visual identification of personnel no longer reliable. This is getting dangerous.
InfoDisplay_102176803_Text:
What remains in the bag is less a notebook and more a scattering of loose pages. Ink is layered upon ink in several places, clearly written across multiple sessions.
 
[Daniel - Note 2]
I examined the sediment again.
▇ is not reactive in the conventional sense, but its alignment shifts under different lighting conditions.
It's not a chemical reaction. It's more like... The position of our bodies is the determining variable.
I saw it.
I saw it!
I saw ▇▇... *&#!
If I don't repeat, then... ▇ will become something else.
 
[Amundsen - Note 2]
The blue dust sticks to our boots. 
Our footprints are overwriting one another.
I've tried to confirm our return direction three times, but every result was different.
I'm starting to wonder... Maybe it's not a problem with the compass. Maybe the concept of "north" is just unstable here.
I'm not going crazy. I'm not going crazy. I'm not going crazy.
Snow shouldn't be blue.
Snow has never looked like this.
 
[Wegener - Note 2]
We had an argument.
Daniel said he saw "▇▇" moving under the ice. Amundsen said it was just a shadow.
I was standing between them, but I couldn't tell which of them was standing closer to me.
I heard someone call my name, but when I turned around, the figure I saw didn't match the one I remembered.
InfoDisplay_102176804_Text:
[Daniel - Note 3]
▇ has no face. So ▇ borrows them.
Borrows my judgment. Borrows Amundsen's caution. Borrows Wegener's skepticism.
▇ isn't imitating us. Something is using us, trying to become "us."
I need to move closer.
Just a little closer.
 
[Wegener - Note 3]
Violence has occurred.
Our basis for judgment has collapsed.
I can no longer confirm whether ▇▇ is human.
But ▇▇ cries. ▇▇ speaks. ▇▇ says my name.
If this is another part of "▇", then all distinctions are meaningless.
 
[Amundsen - Note 3]
I saw Daniel walking toward me, but his shadow was in the wrong direction.
I called his name, but he didn't respond.
Is something mimicking his voice? Who are you?
...I didn't write the previous line.
You turned around.
 
(Unsigned - Final Note)
I saw it. I saw it. I saw it.
I'm not crazy. I'm not crazy. I'm not crazy.
%▇ ...#** ...▇ ...&!
Blue has swallowed the snow.
Blue has swallowed me.
Blue has swallowed the world.
I am not ▇▇. The world is closing in around me.
If I keep walking, if I keep distinguishing, if I keep confirming, then ▇ will keep watching me.
 
And so I stay. I put myself back where ▇ cannot see. I put myself back beneath the ice.
That's the safest place.

InfoDisplay_102176806_Text:
[Large sections of the notebook are illegible, corroded by some unknown force. From the remaining fragments, you deduce it's the diary of a Roya girl named Lotta.]
...
Today, Papa took me to see the Solsworn lady. She said a lot of things I couldn't really understand... something about my Forte being special. So that's why the Exoswarm flee the second they see me. On the way home, Papa wouldn't stop sighing. I've never seen him look so worried before.
I think I know why. Last time, when I tried to play with the Exoswarm he was herding, they just... snapped. They panicked and ran wild. They even hurt Mama.
"Was that my fault?" I asked him. He just sighed, then reached out and rubbed my head with his big, warm hand.
"Do not fret, little one," he said, his voice light like always. "If you are not meant to be a Shepherdess, you are still a good girl."
...
Papa came home with nothing today. He said he gave the Exoswarm to the other Shepherds. I know he is afraid they will hurt Mama again.
This is all my fault. If I weren't like this, Papa wouldn't have lost his job. He'd still be out there, like one of those proud Shepherds guiding the Exoswarm across the frostlands, paying tribute to Baldur for the sunlight and everything we have.
...
Papa seemed happy today. I think it's because Mama is almost healed. He took me to a village far, far away. There's an old granny living there, and he asked me to stay with her to learn stone carving. The granny told me she has a power just like mine, something that makes the Exoswarm angry, so she moved out here to be alone. Papa promised me that carving is a lot of fun, and that he and Mama would come visit me as often as they could.
...
He was right. Stone carving is fun. The granny has taught me everything she knows. She even told me I have a "natural gift." That's the first time anyone has ever said that to me! Mama and Papa must be really busy, though. They haven't visited in over ten days. But it's okay, because I've made some new friends: Fenrir, a Toskr Lemming who can't stop dancing; Dallas, a Fluffguin who loves eating fish, and Bori, a Kronapuff who loves to nibble on flowers.
I carved all of us together onto a big stone slab. Granny says that means we'll be friends forever and ever.
...
Mama and Papa still haven't come. I asked Fenrir, Dallas, and Bori to go to the village and look for them. I miss them so much.
But I waited and waited... and nobody came back. Not Mama, not Papa... not my fluffy friends.
A few days later, Uncle Vilhelm from the village came to talk to Granny. He didn't look like the proud, strong Shepherd I remembered. He looked exhausted. They talked for a long time while I hid outside. I caught Papa's name, something about our village, and things like "Void Storms" and "Tacet Discords."
Just hearing those names makes my stomach do flips... I think I should sneak back to the village and see for myself. As long as I stay away from the Exoswarm, it should be fine.
InfoDisplay_102176807_Text:
[Large sections of the notebook are illegible, corroded by some unknown force. From the remaining fragments, you deduce it's the diary of a Roya girl named Lotta.]
...
...
It's all gone. Everything.
I searched for so long for where the village used to be. All I found was a small patch of scorched fur, a tuft of feathers... and half a beak. Papa. Mama... everyone in the village... my friends... they're all gone.
Something is watching me. I don't want to run anymore.
...
It took me a long, long time to learn how to speak again. Even longer to find the courage to open this diary.
The woman who saved me from those monsters called herself a professor from Startorch Academy. She's beautiful, but she doesn't look like anyone from our village. She told me I have a rare kind of Forte, something that makes me a "potential Synchronist."
I told her everything that happened to the village. I asked her: is this a blessing from <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano>? Or the cruelest curse <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> ever devised?
She was silent for a while. Then, she told me her own homeland had been swallowed by a similar disaster. She crossed an ocean so vast I can't even imagine it, all to find a way to free the world from this fate. She asked me to join the Academy. She said that whether my power is a blessing or a curse, it might be the key to opening the door to our future.
...But I have nothing left. Even if <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano> is waiting behind that door, it can't give back what I've already lost.
...
I went back to Granny's place to say goodbye and thank her for everything. I told her I was leaving for the Academy.
"We Roya carve our words into stone," she said, her voice as kind as ever, "so that <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> cannot erase our existence. And those children at the Academy use something they call 'Cassettes' to do the same. To me, you're just going somewhere else... to carve the statue that belongs to you."
"As long as the memory remains, so does the soul."
After I arrived at the Academy, I read this notebook from the very first page to the last. Papa, Mama, Fenrir, Dallas, Bori... Granny was right. They're still alive here in these pages, and deep within my mind. Maybe, without even realizing it, I've become a living statue carved with all their names.
I'll carry their souls with me, wherever I go. I promise.
...
Void Storms. Even the name is terrifying.
I've spent my life trying to outrun its shadow. It's one of <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr's</ano> venomous tendrils, dragging everything I love into the nothingness. I thought... I thought I had learned how to ignore it.
But seeing it appear again, I realized something. All these years of study... they were just preparation for this exact moment. Again and again, I've pushed my Forte to its limit, right to the edge of Overclocking. And now, I finally understand. I'm ready.
Just like the professor said, only I, only my Forte, can save that village from being wiped out. I couldn't save my own home back then. But this time, I won't stand by and watch the dark take the people I love.
It's time to go.

Background A powerful Tacet Discord, designated "Inferno Rider," has been observed near the Port City of Guixu in Huanglong. The vehicle it utilizes operates with remarkable stability in post-Lament environments. Its structural design and movement patterns are expected to provide critical reference points for the development of our prototype expedition motorbike. II. III. Technical Applications By reverse-engineering its movement patterns and structural features, the engineering team has implemented the following improvements to the expedition motorbike prototype: …………………… Researcher's Handwritten Note: The prototype is finished. I never imagined old tech from my hometown all those years ago would find a new life in an expedition motorbike. Even now, the mention of the "Inferno Rider" still strikes fear into people's hearts. I cannot erase the shadow cast by that Tacet Discord, nor can I truly give rest to the souls who perished long ago. MapMark_3380013_MarkDesc:
Dhalifa has never been much of a talker—hardly surprising, given she only recently found her voice again.
After submitting her application, she stood adrift in the crowd, clutching her notice tight. That's when they approached and invited her in. 
So, let's go together. Maybe saving the world is something only heroes get to do. But us? We'll just do what we can, the best way we know how.
MapMark_3380014_MarkDesc:
Since when has she been here? 
No one knows. 
How long will she stay? 
Until "here" ceases to exist.
MapMark_3380015_MarkDesc:
They are the last teams to leave the Research Institute. 
They've probably thought about giving up more than once. And probably, over and over, they've found their courage again.
Anyway, they are still standing here, aren't they?
MapMark_3380016_MarkDesc:
Normally, no teacher would let their students walk into harm's way, even if that danger is about to sweep across the world.
Unless… those students willingly choose to confront the void head-on.
Then so be it. Let's move out together, till the very end.
MapMark_3380017_MarkDesc:
We have never feared the threats of Aleph-1.
Only the truth has the power to test our resolve.
MapMark_3380018_MarkDesc:
In the past, it saved us once. Now, we won't give up on it. 
"Science," "the world," "future"... We aren't fighting for any of those big ideas.
This is our home. We will defend it.
MapMark_3380019_MarkDesc:
Everyone in Lahai-Roi knows that the Cassettes made by the Spacetrek Collective are just "backups."
They carry our hopes and our resolve to fight the Threnodian to the bitter end. 
But deep down, we all know this portable device won't keep one alive when things go south.
No one wants to be the one who only brings back a teammate's Cassette.
We're all going home together.
MapMark_3380020_MarkDesc:
A team led by Nastasha. An experienced researcher-in-the-making, she has navigated them through countless dangers.
Of course, the young must eventually weather their own storms...
But there is always someone who volunteers to stand in front of them, even if that someone has only just stepped out of the role of "student" herself.
MapMark_3380021_MarkDesc:
They are the first teams to leave the Research Institute. 
Don't worry about them. They know exactly what they're walking into.
If all they wanted was a quiet, peaceful life, they never would have set foot in Lahai-Roi to begin with.
InfoDisplay_102194705_Text:

The First Letter
To the nice Scavengers,
I heard you find things taken away by Void ■■. My friend Jacob was taken away. I have some toys he gave me, but I want more back.
I don't have a lot of Shell Credits. Can you still help me? Lollo ■■ said they would help deliver this letter. I hope you get it.

To the nice Scavengers,
Mom says I already have toys and I shouldn't want other people's things. But after Jacob left, when I look at his toys, I can remember him and not feel so sad.
If I feel too sad, I think I need more toys. I have more Shell Credits now. I'm not a bad kid. Can you please help me?
—Mojel

The Third Letter
To the nice Scavengers,
When Jacob left, he had his slingshot with him. 
...
I have 136 Shell Credits now, two very pretty stones, and one useful ■■ Shell.
Can I trade these for the slingshot? I don't need anything else. Just the slingshot.
—Mojel

InfoDisplay_35000008_Text:
Sonija:
There's something I have never told you.
Shenyuan approached me, and I helped him with a few things. The Autopuppet rebellion... Part of the blame lies with me.
I know you would say this isn't entirely my fault, but I wanted you to know that I

<color=GreyA>(The letter remains unfinished)</color>
InfoDisplay_35000009_Text:
Sonija:
You once said that a craftsman's techniques should be used to protect Xuanfang Hold. I've always remembered that.
I wanted to be the kind of craftsmen you look up to... but I don't think I can anymore...
<s>I chose the wrong person to learn from.</s>

<color=GreyA>(The last line has been fiercely scratched out)</color>
InfoDisplay_35000010_Text:
Sonija:
I'm sorry.
My mind is in a whirlwind. The Ministry of War has come for me...
I never meant to hurt anyone, but it seems I truly have done something wrong... I don't know if I should say more... 
I'm sorry. The only thing I can think to do is write these words down. The list I gave you...

<color=GreyA>(The text cuts off. Jiuwu has stopped writing again mid-sentence)</color>
InfoDisplay_35000011_Text:
Sonija:

I have lost count of how many times I have written this letter... 

I did things for Shenyuan that allowed him access to more Autopuppets. I thought it was merely an opportunity to sharpen my technique, but I didn't realize... until the day of the rebellion that I had become his "accomplice."

If the truth were to come out, everyone would be consumed by guilt, and the Ministry of Development would be in turmoil... and you, as my friend, would surely be implicated... 

I wanted to clean up this mess on my own before telling you—perhaps when the dust has settled, it will be easier for you to hear, or easier for me to say. 

I'm sorry, Sonia. I am truly sorry. After I fix this, I'll accept any punishment. When that day comes... can we still be friends? 

Jiuwu
InfoDisplay_35000019_Text:
That technical question Huihuan raised a while back... actually worth looking into. No one at Zhuojun Atelier or Huaxu Academy has approached it from that angle. I should find some time to discuss it with him, but I can't let it slow down my experiments. Pity we don't share the same ideals. If I could bring him on board, we'd get twice the results with half the effort...

… 

The new Artisans from the Ministry of Development are completely useless. They don't even have basic skills. I have no idea how they passed the exams. At least their attitude is decent. They still respect knowledge. Not a total lost cause. I'll compile a handbook for them. Save them wasting my time with questions... 

…

The Fractsidus... a bunch of lawless fanatics. They've approached me so many times. Do they really think I'd become their lapdog? Ridiculous. Still... their network could be useful for my research. The timing is perfect now. Not a single step can afford to go wrong. The next time I see that woman in red,  I won't turn her away immediately. No harm in hearing what she has to say... 

…
InfoDisplay_35000020_Text: Experiment Log 01437 The compilation and restructuring of Reverberations... I've completely mastered it now. There are no more useful samples left in the Bladepuppets. Time to move on to Autopuppet kernels. Intact kernels are hard to come by. Might need to "create" a few incidents... … Experiment Log 01489 Still no progress on cracking the Autopuppet kernel code... Heh, I'd expect nothing less from the Sentinel's technology... Even though nearly two centuries have passed, in Her eyes, humanity's understanding of mechanics probably isn't any different from a toddler learning to walk. … Experiment Log 01541 Every attempt so far has failed... Is using Reverberations to control Autopuppets a dead end? No... impossible. There's no mistake. This Tacet Mark—this ability—must mean something... … Experiment Log 01776 Using Reverberations to ■■ the Autopuppet kernels... it's finally stabilizing. But maybe I can push further. By "fusing" and "stitching" different Reverberations together, could I multiply the efficiency? Maybe I can do more than just ■■ Autopuppets. Maybe I can... make them even stronger... … Experiment Log 01801 The Reverberations collected from ■■ don't fuse well... The leftover ■■ is too strong, and they just end up repelling each other... Maybe I need a mild, gentle ■■ to act as a sort of "glue?" If that's the case, the Reverberations from ■■ are useless. I have to find a way to collect others... People who have lived quiet lives, untouched by war or disasters, might carry the exact "materials" I need... ...

InfoDisplay_35000003_Text:
Still haven't learned that song from last time... Grandpa said he's going to hire a musician from Mengzhou City to teach me, but I'm kind of over it. I should tell him soon so he doesn't waste his money.

...

Grandpa took me to Xuanfang Hold today. It's huge and impressive! So much good food and fun stuff. On the way back, I saw someone flying in the sky on a sword... Was that a real Transcendent?

...

Duzhong taught me a few moves today. He said I'm a natural! I think so too. Swinging swords and spears is way more fun than playing the liuqin. If I can get into the Ministry of War, it'll really make Grandpa proud.

...

The exam results are out! The examiner said my scores are good enough to work at the Mengzhou City branch. I've only been there once. It's very different from Xuanfang, and I'm not sure how I feel about it... But moving somewhere new could be fun. 
Grandpa and the elders want me to go, but if I leave, who's going to take care of him? He doesn't have any kids of his own. I'm all he has.
It's a lot to take in. I need more time to think.

...

When that Tacet Discord pushed me off the cliff, I thought I was dead for sure. I can't believe I became a Resonator! Controlling wind is actually quite handy. Just one thing... why did my Tacet Mark have to appear on the back of my neck? I can't even see it...

...
InfoDisplay_35000004_Text:
Qingyan keeps asking me to teach him a few moves. Our sister won't allow him to practice martial arts. She wants to send him to school to study instead... I can understand where she is coming from, but he is just a kid. We should let him decide his own future.

Speaking of which, his birthday is coming up. He has been dreaming of having his very own wooden sword. I should head over to Mengzhou City on my next day off and have a carpenter there craft one for him.

But if I give him that, Sister will probably scold me again... Well, whatever. Worst-case scenario, I will just buy her a few nice fragrant pouches to help her cool off.
InfoDisplay_35000005_Text:
Brother Qian,

The doctor from Mengzhou City came yesterday. He said there's no curing it anymore. Just leave it to fate now.

To have a daughter so late in life was already my greatest joy. It breaks my heart that I won't see Liangyu grow up. But I don't blame heaven or fate. I just feel for my child. As a father, I've let her down.

I know my time is short. A few more months, maybe, and I'll follow her mother. When I'm gone, please look after Liangyu. Keep her safe. Let her grow strong. If you can do this for me, I'll rest easy...

InfoDisplay_35000007_Text:
Ling,

This latest Tacet Discord outbreak is coming on strong. It's hard to say if the defenses at Yuan Fortress will hold.

Liang is still young, and it really would be best for you to take him to Mengzhou, where it's safe. Please don't worry about me. I am, after all, a genius mechanist from the Court of Savantae. If worst comes to worst, I can always ask a Xuanling Bird to find the Sword Transcendent.

Please start your journey to Mengzhou soon. Keep moving forward, and don't look back.

Ruoyun

InfoDisplay_34000002_Text:
"A bird that yearns for the sky will never be imprisoned by a cage."
"In plain English, please."
"Do you want to go to the moon?"
"Huh?"
"A trip to the moon now costs only 250,000 eddies, and there's a 20% discount if you book for two!"
InfoDisplay_34000003_Text:
People in this city are always paying for someone else's Braindance—using fleeting moments of joy to numb the pain of reality.
...Me? I'm one of them. Out of my entire collection, my fav is titled Sunny Beach.
The recorder was an athlete with 20/20 vision. He's lying on a quiet beach, feeling the breeze, humming a tune that's not half-bad, watching waves rise and fall in the distance.
A piece of work like me could never wind up in a paradise like that. All I can do is listen to the static and leach off the scenery through someone else's eyes.
...Why do I keep bringing up his vision? Dammit, it's obviously you've never been scammed by a lowlife!
InfoDisplay_34000004_Text:
Sprawled under the bushes are the bodies from last night's gang war. I didn't know the man, but I recognized the gun tucked in his waistband.

Most of the gun frame was stained red, but those pinstripes, the matte finish grip... There's no mistaking it. That's my handiwork.

I modded that gun two months ago. It was a rush order. Owner was flush with cash and had specific demands. He wanted me to use the best paint money could buy to ink his favorite rock star—clutching a guitar while flipping the bird—onto the frame. To show he meant business, he gave me a huge deposit, which I repaid in three days and nights of work... Shame, really. I kinda liked that piece.

Things being what they are, there's not much to say or do. I look up and sigh...
"M*********** could've at least paid it off before dying!"
InfoDisplay_34000005_Text:
"F***... now of all times..."

Parker snapped the call shut. He looked up. Lightning tears through the gray sky as the piss-slick rain washes over his cheap coat.

As a gang "cleaner," Parker had no choice. His life was on standby, always on call to mop up the bossman's mess.

After a brisk, cold shower, Parker left home. True to his routine, he circled the block three times in a ride rented under a fake ID before finally heading to the destination. Body Heat Radio was playing his favorite track. Parker headbanged like a psycho. Cars behind sounded off at his erratic driving, but he didn't give a damn.

"This is the last one, Parker. Finish this job and you're done. Take the eddies and fly, far away."

He couldn't have known that a year ago, his predecessor had been humming this exact tune on the same road, speeding to the final job of her life.

"Let me go Ponpon-shiru, let me go Ponpon-shiru!"
InfoDisplay_34000006_Text:
MIL-SPEC Sandevistan? Keep dreaming. That tech isn't something a punk like you can handle.

...David? Where'd you hear that name?

Yeah, I'll admit there was a kid like that once... but he was a freak, you hear me? Few can chrome up like that and still be kicking about. Your scrawny ass? I'd be f***ing impressed if you managed to stay sane with a Sandy lodged in your brain.

...Johnny? Dammit, you messing with me? Spewing legends to prove a point? That's completely different!

...Back to business, kid. Value your life. Stop all that "be a legend" crap. Go join a nice gang, or find a netrunner to teach you some tricks. At least spend more time practicing your aim... Beats recklessly stuffing yourself with chrome.

Learn to walk before you run. In three years—no, let's say two—if you haven't changed your mind, come back. I'll give you a deal on the latest cyberware in the clinic... You have my word.
InfoDisplay_34000007_Text:
"Look in the mirror, John. The wiring in your left retina is shot. Those exposed metallic strands hurt me when I look at 'em... Dammit, how many days has it been since you slept? Up close, I can smell the stench from your fried brain implants."

"...Ninety-seven hours. Maybe more. I wrote myself a program. If I lapse into deep sleep before the job is done, it shocks my brain till I wake up. The smell you're picking up... it's probably that."

"You goddamn lunatic... You tryna to kill yourself!?"

"No. I'm doing this 'cause I wanna live. Sixty percent of my body is corporate property. The moment I stop, the suits from the Legal will show up with their contracts and laser-scalpels. They'll carve everything out and dump it on the black market to clear my debts."

"......"

"You dig, buddy? This is a city where surviving the day earns you the privilege to suffer tomorrow."
InfoDisplay_34000008_Text:
As a Braindance director, I've recorded thousands of BDs.

I'll admit my skills aren't world-class, but unlike your average third-rate hack, I still pursue a semblance of artistry in my work.

The blood must spray at exactly a twenty-seven-degree angle. The gunfire must achieve the ultimate sense of immersion...

To bring the audience the most visceral of thrills, I've risked life and limb to investigate a legendary murder case in Dogtown, a place of danger and violence...

"So, what do you think of the take, Ms. Tisma? That... That's my—"

"Pick another subject and reshoot it. How many times do I have to tell you? In this day and age, movies about 'chasing your dreams' are a goddamn money-loser."
InfoDisplay_34000009_Text:
Richard was old, so old he could no longer remember exactly what his gang sign looked like.

But his body remembered. Richard's newly installed cybernetic tendons fluidly executed the dodge command he issued. An onyx blade pierced a throat and exited through the skull. With a purposeful slash, a coolant-soaked brainstem explodes into a work of modern art.

Sheathing his blade, Richard turned back. He pulled a pair of reading glasses from his coat and wiped them with a clean corner of his shirt.

"Maelstrom lackeys... Guess I got the wrong guys."

Richard scratched his head and spat at the dead punk, then he pushed his glasses back into place.

He wanted Kiroshi optics, but his body rejected ocular implants. The Immunoblocker shots required to keep them riddled his body with track marks in just a few days. Left with no choice, Richard went back to his "original part," donning reading glasses while plying his trade.

"Now, where did those five Animals run off to..."

Hugging the wall, Richard followed the trail left by his inside man, stepping ever deeper into the dark alley.

"Hang in there, Richard. Kill 'em quick, and go home early."
InfoDisplay_34000010_Text:
What's behind that door... Mars? No, wait, is it the Moon? Whatever, I've never been to either, so it's all the same to me. Anyway, to keep my clothes and hair from floating all over the place, I took a minute to find the override and shut off that weird gravity control.
Don't mention it. Love from Night City.

InfoDisplay_35000014_Text:
Fuling,
I'm off to Huaxu Academy for your medicine. You looked so peaceful asleep this morning, so I couldn't bear to wake you. Please have a good breakfast when you're up. You're still recovering and can't afford to skip meals.
Xuanfang Hold has so many pavilions, towers, and little courtyards to explore. When I get back, we'll go sketching together.

InfoDisplay_35000014_Title: Letter Sealed in a Rafter Kite
InfoDisplay_35000015_Text: Blades churned, blood spilled, corpses heaped. Scars of old wars still mar the Dreaming Cavern.
InfoDisplay_35000114_Text:
To the Revered Sentinel,

I am deeply moved and honored to have received your invitation and to be favored by your recognition.

As merchants, our calling is to gather the strength of the masses to build communities and unite the hearts of many to foster thriving markets. If we might follow in the footsteps of the wise and virtuous to help alleviate the burdens of the realm, it would be the utmost aspiration, and indeed, the greatest privilege, of the Zhaoming Commerce Guild.

Please accept this humble reply. May you preserve your precious health. 

With highest regards,

Suisui
Zhaoming Commerce Guild
InfoDisplay_35000114_Title: A Written Reply with Elegant Handwriting
InfoDisplay_35000115_Text:
Strange... The Sentinel holds a gathering, yet doesn't even bother to show up? Instead, I ran straight into several people who consider me their rival... There's no business to be made with a boring crowd like this. I'll just ignore them.

I blew off so many meetings just to come here. What a waste of my time... Though, I have to admit, the pastries here are actually pretty good. I suppose it wasn't a total loss after all...

ItemInfo_71300509_BgDescription: The pain of losing her family left a lasting stain on the girl's jade pendant and her heart. Though she struck out countless times, her blade could never cleave her nightmares, only carving the trauma deeper into her mind. Fortunately, the bond once broken has been mended by the warmth of companionship. That heartfelt devotion has finally chased away the haunting mists of her suffering. Now, the girl smiles again—as soft as wind dancing across clear waters, as bright as jade regaining its luster.

InfoDisplay_35000018_Text:
Ugh, why is there an Ironhead at Daddy's place? It even chased me out...
...
Today the Ironhead caught me again. Next time, I definitely won't let it find me!
...
Today, I won! Ironhead, you can't catch me!
I finally got to see Daddy. Even though he said I shouldn't have come, he didn't blame me, and on the way home he bought me a sugar painting. The sugar painting was so sweet, so yummy.
...
How could there be a monster in here?! Good thing Ironhead saved me... Maybe it chased me out to protect me?
...
Ironhead... or should I call you Archival Autopuppet?
Never mind, Ironhead suits you better!
...
Ironhead, I've almost finished all the books here that I'm allowed to read... but as for the books I'm not allowed to read, I suppose I'll never get to see them.
<color=RedD>Just like I'll never get to see Daddy again.</color>
...
Ironhead, sometimes I think Daddy is a really selfish person.
Did he go there just to read your books? After he got there, did he never think about me again?
...
Ironhead, I'm walking slower and slower. Maybe I won't be able to come see you often anymore.
...
Ironhead, can you come see me? Uh... but you can't leave Fogveil Pagoda, can you?
...
<color=RedD>Ironhead, I want to see you one more time.</color>
...
Ironhead...

InfoDisplay_35000130_Text:
We've successfully tested the core functionality using the Sunken Warren. To be honest, when I first looked at the Sentinel's design, it seemed completely wild and reckless. But when it's in execution, every single phase locks perfectly into the next flawlessly. Once a Tacet Discord gets trapped inside, there is zero chance of escape...

Groundbreaking on the Skyworks is coming up fast. Even though the data from the Sunken Warren is solid, we have to keep our heads out of the clouds and account for real field conditions during actual construction...
InfoDisplay_35000132_Text:
The Sentinel... I never expected we'd meet like this. And of all things, She actually wants to offer me a "deal?" It's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, but the whole thing is shrouded in mystery...

Still, whether this is an opportunity or a trap, I'll never know unless I dive in myself. I didn't get to where I am today by playing it safe. Since the Sentinel is putting Her own stakes on the line, I might as well play along and make this wager with Her.

The Land of Xuanfang... It sits right on the border of Mengzhou, close to Jinzhou. What could She possibly be plotting by setting our next trade location there...? I can't rush in blindly. First, I need to hire someone reliable to scope out the situation for me... Ah, "that man" might actually be useful here...

InfoDisplay_35000116_Text:
Another day on watch... It's been a whole month now. Same post, same walls. When do I finally get to go on patrol like the seniors?

It's been quiet this past month, though. Not a peep from those Exiles. I guess that counts as good news...

...
InfoDisplay_35000300_Text:
In those days, the heavens above the Land of Xuanfang were stained crimson with blood, and the very earth wept. The Xuanling Birds defended the Fortress to the bitter end, never wavering, until at last, it fell.

Following the devastation of the Fortress and Gorges War, the land was left desolate, its people broken. Yet, by the grace and providence of the Sentinel, the survivors were brought under the protection of Mengzhou to heal and rebuild. Thus, Xuanfang endured, surviving into the present day.
InfoDisplay_264800001_Text:
Today's Ingredients:
Fowl... Raw Meat... Bird Eggs... Salt...
Note: Raw meat's gotten a bit cheaper lately, but bird eggs went up again. Can't those birds just lay a few more?
InfoDisplay_264800002_Text:
The last stage of the ritual is done! Grandpa can talk again. He kept calling out to me: "Grandson... come back..." He must have returned because he missed me.
Used Waterlamp and White Jade Beauty to finish the second stage...
Whew. Just one stage left. Though the Soulwrought Jade the ritual needs is still a bit pricey...
Found a place that'll sell it to me at a discount. Great news. With what I've saved, I should just about be able to afford the Soulwrought Jade. Maybe this time I really get to see Grandpa again...
Let's try it tonight, then.
InfoDisplay_264800003_Text:
Buling: Tab... settled
Buling: Tab... settled...

Note: That girl keeps hanging around. She must have found something about Grandpa. Ugh... I dressed up as a ghost to keep people away, but instead a real Taoist came knocking. Now I have to move Grandpa away... At least the ritual's almost ready. Just a few more days.
InfoDisplay_264800004_Text:
Investigation indicates that the "ghosts" are connected to shopkeeper Lyu Yi. Deceived by certain persons, he sought to summon his grandfather through a "Soul Summoning" ritual, but what he actually summoned was a Tacet Discord.

Attachments:

Evidence 1: Tab Records written by the shopkeeper

"Buling: Tab... settled
Buling: Tab... settled...

Note: That girl keeps hanging around. She must have found something about Grandpa. Ugh... I dressed up as a ghost to keep people away, but instead a real Taoist came knocking. Now I have to move Grandpa away... At least the ritual's almost ready. Just a few more days."

This evidence confirms the "ghosts" are connected to the shopkeeper. Buling's investigation forced him to move the Tacet Discord. Its current location is unknown, and acting rashly may tip Lyu Yi off.

Evidence 2: Ritual Log written by the shopkeeper

"The last stage of the ritual is done! Grandpa can talk again. He kept calling out to me: "Grandson... come back..." He must have returned because he missed me.
Used Waterlamp and White Jade Beauty to finish the second stage...
Whew. Just one stage left. Though the Soulwrought Jade the ritual needs is still a bit pricey...
Found a place that'll sell it to me at a discount. Great news. With what I've saved, I should just about be able to afford the Soulwrought Jade. Maybe this time I really get to see Grandpa again...
Let's try it tonight, then."

This evidence confirms that Lyu Yi was deceived into believing a "Soul Summoning" ritual could bring back his grandfather. We request the aid from the Ministry of War to further investigate this matter....

Still no good. Even with Lady Hsin's technology, the prototype burns through its energy too quickly, and its structure collapses into an irreversible cascade of its own making...
What am I to do... Have I been going about this all wrong?
No, impossible. Jiening and I gave our lives to this. For her sake, I have to finish it.

[A single line is written below. To your surprise, the script is nothing like the hand above. It is unmistakably your own, and it was clearly written here a very long time ago.]

Face the vase: forward, left, left, right.

InfoDisplay_37010001_Text:
...It has been ██ days since the Formrenders first appeared, and at last we have found a way to relight the Moon Lanterns.

Those faint glimmers scattered through the alleys—Luobin calls them <color=Highlight>Nightlight Tokens</color>—carry some very peculiar frequency. <color=Highlight>Burn them in the Moon Lanterns, and the darkness gives way.</color> They suppress the Formrenders too: the brighter the flame, the heavier their limbs, the slower their approach. But each lantern lit also draws their attention, so we must move with care.

Where the glimmers come from, none of us knows. Faint as they are, one always rekindles somewhere just as the oil runs dry and the wick burns out. Whatever the truth of it, so long as we have the Nightlight Tokens, there is still hope. Jianwei believes it is a blessing bestowed by the Sentinel... But if it truly is a blessing, why has She never shown Herself?

...Last night I heard the wind sweep down the corridor, and in my terror I snatched up a weapon and rushed outside, only to frighten my neighbors half to death. Then I remembered the Fortress and Gorges War ended long ago. My memory really has been failing me of late. Best to write it all down.
InfoDisplay_37010002_Text: ...Those who have seen it call it the Formrender. Blue of face, long of fang, it wears the shape of an Autopuppet, yet the air about it is foul. Its voice grates like a rusted blade scraping bone, and a red light sits in its eyes. It keeps to dark places, and loathes above all the joys of mortal men. At the sight of them it wakes to wrath, and in its wrath it devours that light.
InfoDisplay_37010003_Text:
To my wife, Mingxi,

I hope this letter finds you well. Your note and the dried fruit reached me safely, and I am in good health. There is no need to worry about me. Not a single piece was crushed on the way, and I confess I could not bring myself to share any with my colleagues; I ate them all myself. Each one was wonderfully sweet, and I was quite content. I only hope that next time you might spare a few more words for me.

Matters at the Ministry have kept me busy of late, so this reply comes later than it should. Forgive me. I have picked out a hairpin for you, one of the styles now fashionable in the city, in a pattern I know you like. As for the reassignment, it is still under discussion, and my posting has not been decided. I mention it only so that it will not sit on your mind later.

By the time this reaches you, autumn will likely have set in. Remember to dress warmly in the mornings and evenings. Do not give all your attention to the children. Perhaps you might treat yourself to a few new garments? Counting the days, I may be able to take leave around the time of the Waking Moon Festival. If the leave is granted, I will be home before dusk, and we will go to see the lanterns together.

There is more in my heart than this page can hold. Take good care of yourself.

Yours,
Guilan
InfoDisplay_37010004_Text: A carefully preserved family photo, capturing an ordinary yet precious moment of happiness.
InfoDisplay_37010005_Text:
To my wife, Mingxi,

I hope this letter finds you well. The paperwork has piled high of late, and I have not written back in time. Forgive me for leaving you to worry. I am in good health.

The Tacet Discord Outbreaks along the border have grown worse, and there have been some transfers within the Ministry. One of them... concerns me, though it is still under discussion. If it is settled, <s>I am to be stationed in the Land of Xuanfang</s> and I will be even farther from you than I am now... As for where I am bound, and when I set out, I am not yet at liberty to write...

(The letter breaks off here, leaving only a few blots of ink, as though the writer had held his brush poised for a long while and, in the end, set it down without going on.)
