Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_11: There are two potential solutions: We could increase the Detector's tolerance to Voidmatter. Or, we could eliminate the surrounding Voidmatter. But neither of those options are feasible in the time we have.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_13: What if we transport it somewhere that isn't affected by Voidmatter?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_14: Hmm, that's not realistic. The only places that aren't affected by Voidmatter right now are Bjartr Woods and Startorch Academy under the protective barrier. Or the Institute thousands of meters above...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_16: Looks like there's another high altitude spot.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_17: Do we have spares for Hyvatia's measurement modules?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_18: Uh-yes! Researcher Anslem left behind several prototypes. I'll go fetch one from the warehouse.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_19: But what do you intend to do with them?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_2_50_20: The eyes of the gods have failed us. So have our machines. Now, we move forward with our own hands.

Side_XXSXDYW_2_1:
Under the stars, we are both observers and part of the cosmos itself. When you close this guide, your real journey has only just begun.

Forget the names of the constellations. What matters is that you looked up and let the starlight in. The moment you first lost yourself in the beauty of the stars is more precious than any astronomical fact.

A gentle reminder for every stargazer:
1. There's no need to bring advanced telescopes. A curious heart is all you need.
2. Pick a night when the moon is shy, and the sky is clear.
3. Bring a star chart, a flashlight, and a friend who'd love to share the quiet of a starlit night with you.

When the starlight touches you, remember this: every cell, every fiber, every element that makes you who you are was born in the heart of a star. You are, in your own way, stardust made manifest.

May the stars always bring you peace and inspiration.

Dedicated to all those who have ever stopped and looked up.

Side_ANHJDCS_2_8: At midnight, they duel each other in a secret place inside the tunnel. And the loser is... Well, I've heard several versions.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_9: The most believable one is that the loser is deprived of their deck, so they can never duel again.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_10: And the more terrifying one goes that participants wager their very souls, and the loser has to relinquish theirs for the winner to feast on.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_12: Lahai-Roi isn't a land of lawlessness.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_13: I think it sounds ridiculous, too, but these rumors didn't just come from thin air. Several members of the fan club had already received invitations from a mysterious figure.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_14: "Want more power? Then come to the station at midnight!"
Side_ANHJDCS_2_16: Leave it to me, I'll handle it.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_17: Be careful, {PlayerName}... though I doubt any duelist could defeat you in fair play.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_18: But if the rumors are true, and these dark duels are really fought with lives and souls at stake... the duelists may have unseemly methods up their sleeves.
Side_ANHJDCS_2_19: By the way! There's a Roya named Alkain in the station. He seems to know something about these "dark duels."
Side_ANHJDCS_2_20: But he's wary of me. I couldn't get any useful information out of him… Maybe you'll have better luck than I did.

Side_sixteenbit_4_9: From jungles that looked like the Bjartr Woods, to metropolises like I could never imagine, games have taken me to so many different places and left me with so many beautiful memories.
Side_sixteenbit_4_10: Now I want to write a song that will remind me of all that beauty.
Side_sixteenbit_4_12: Don't worry little fella, we can play right now!
Side_sixteenbit_5_2: No trouble at all, buddy. I love playing with you!
Side_sixteenbit_5_5: And your happy little chirp has just inspired me!
Side_sixteenbit_5_7: You just can't get enough playtime, can you?
Side_sixteenbit_5_9: It said there's another place where it likes to play, and it wants to take us there.
Side_sixteenbit_5_10: You're not too tired, are you?
Side_sixteenbit_5_12: Me, tired? I rip mechs apart with my bare hands.
Side_sixteenbit_5_13: I'm not sure what that means... But it sounds like you're ready to go!
Side_sixteenbit_5_14: Let's follow this Soliskin and play some more!
Side_sixteenbit_6_1: This looks like another Soliskin playground...
Side_sixteenbit_6_2: I feel like I've just reached a new map in a game!

Side_sixteenbit_7_5: Yep! We'll hit the keys that the Soliskin played in reverse order!
Side_sixteenbit_8_1: This melody sounds great backwards and forwards!
Side_sixteenbit_8_5: What's that? Your friend is back? And it's close by?
Side_sixteenbit_8_8: Relax, finding inspiration for our song is more important. Everything's going according to plan.
Side_sixteenbit_8_9: The other Soliskin is here, which means more opportunities to get inspired.
Side_sixteenbit_8_10: Can you take us to your friend?
Side_sixteenbit_8_12: It says yes! Come on, what are we waiting for?
Side_sixteenbit_9_2: They want us to dance with them!
Side_sixteenbit_9_3: Come on! Jump on the mushrooms in the same order as the Soliskin, and try to keep up!
Side_sixteenbit_10_19: Oh, I didn't mean to sound sad! Don't worry. Once I've reached my goals, I'll be back!
Side_sixteenbit_10_20: Thank you for all the fun. I'm going to go write that song, and then it's time to hit the books!
Side_sixteenbit_10_21: Make sure you listen to the whole song when I send it to you!
CD_YYQD_1_1: Mechascout. Codename: Robbie. Pressure and temperature module parameters remain within normal range. Core energy module is severely damaged.
CD_YYQD_1_2: Remaining energy at 59%. Estimated system uptime is...
CD_YYQD_1_5: Shall I get an engineer from the academy to take a look at you?
CD_YYQD_1_6: Thank you, but that won't be necessary. The academy's engineers have completed my servicing. My core module has been severely affected by the Void Storm.
CD_YYQD_1_7: A full recovery is no longer possible. All I can do is watch as my energy reserves gradually deplete.
CD_YYQD_1_8: That's no different than waiting for death!
CD_YYQD_1_9: Machines do not know death. We are either "on" or "off."
CD_YYQD_1_10: My responsibility is the safety of this area. I was switched on for that sole purpose, and I shall expend all energy reserves for that purpose.
CD_YYQD_1_11: Even if most of my modules are nonfunctional...
CD_YYQD_1_12: There is no purpose in staying here.
CD_YYQD_1_13: Purpose... My system is unable to decipher what you are trying to convey.
CD_YYQD_1_14: Instead of staying put and waiting for your energy to drain, wouldn't it be better to put that energy into something meaningful?
CD_YYQD_1_15: Forget the tasks you were assigned at startup. Why don't you do something meaningful for yourself?
CD_YYQD_1_17: Something you've always wanted to do but never had the chance to.
CD_YYQD_1_18: My system indicates you speak of something like a bucket list humans make. Machines do not have that privilege.
CD_YYQD_1_19: However... My system has not blocked this term or queries related to it.
CD_YYQD_1_20: Then perhaps your creator wanted you to have that privilege.
CD_YYQD_1_21: I-I'd like to see the undersea tunnels. But my current energy reserves are insufficient for that journey.
CD_YYQD_10_1: What's an old Mechascout like you doing here? Is there an issue with your chassis?
CD_YYQD_10_2: No, I'm here to ask for a new livery.
CD_YYQD_10_3: I see... But I'm all out of paint supplies. The next batch won't come in until next week, so how about you return then?
CD_YYQD_10_5: What do you need? We can collect them for you.
CD_YYQD_10_6: Let me think... Well, if you're in a hurry, I can write you a list.
CD_YYQD_11_1: Yes, this will be enough. Livery application will take some time. Please wait outside.
CD_YYQD_11_7: Some time later, the Mechascout stands in a fresh new livery.
CD_YYQD_11_8: In the past, I would have considered this a waste of time.
CD_YYQD_11_9: But as I run out of time, it has become clear to me that these extraneous activities are meaningful in their own way.
CD_YYQD_11_10: Remaining energy below 30%. Estimated system uptime is...
CD_YYQD_11_12: I'm fine. Let's hurry to the next location.
CD_YYQD_12_1: Please take me to the top of that greatsword, {PlayerName}.
CD_YYQD_12_2: What do you want to do up there?
CD_YYQD_12_4: I intend to experience the thrill of flying by jumping into the lake.
CD_YYQD_12_5: {PlayerName}, I'm too obsolete to be equipped with a flight module, so I've never soared through the sky.
CD_YYQD_12_6: This is the only way for me to fly. Don't worry, my cushioning module will keep me safe...
CD_YYQD_12_7: In my database, I found a single word mentioned repeatedly in relation to complex human behaviors: Conquer...
CD_YYQD_12_8: Humans once feared fire, so they invented tools and learned to control it.
CD_YYQD_12_9: Humans aren't able to walk on water, so they built ships to cross the ocean.
CD_YYQD_12_10: Humans yearned for the sky, so they designed devices to achieve their dream of flight.
CD_YYQD_12_11: Though small, humans never stop conquering new territories. So, in my final moments, I too wish to overcome my own limits.
CD_YYQD_12_12: Even if it comes at a price...
CD_YYQD_12_13: But wouldn't that speed up your energy consumption?
CD_YYQD_12_14: That's the price I mentioned. Now let's go.
CD_YYQD_15_20: The machine before you falls deathly silent, and you know it will never wake up again. You move it to an open area with a spectacular view.
CD_YYQD_15_21: You leave it in eternal peace. Now, with its love composed of imaginary numbers, it can watch over its beloved world forever.
CD_YYQD_16_1: You receive a message from an unknown sender.
CD_YYQD_16_2: Professor Pattie, have you serviced the broken Mechascout by the station?
CD_YYQD_16_4: I think you've got the wrong number.
CD_YYQD_16_5: What? Let me take a look. Ugh, my eyesight. I accidentally flipped the last two digits...
CD_YYQD_16_7: Don't worry about it. Is it urgent? I'm a student at Startorch Academy, so I might be able to help.
CD_YYQD_16_8: I see... Well, it's about the Mechascout I just mentioned.
CD_YYQD_16_9: It seems to be badly damaged. We've asked the Academy to fix it several times. But somehow it's still in that state.
CD_YYQD_16_10: If you're willing to help, please inspect it as soon as possible.
CD_YYQD_16_12: ? I think you've got the wrong number.
CD_YYQD_17_1: Well, it's time for me to go, {PlayerName}. I'm leaving myself and this world in your hands.
CD_YYQD_17_4: Deactivating all system notifications. Don't worry. Just focus on the matter at hand.
CD_YYQD_17_5: It seems this will be my starting point, and my finish line.
CD_YYQD_17_6: Even now, I still fail to understand what you meant when you said that I should do something meaningful.
CD_YYQD_17_7: You humans often consider love meaningful. My creator even wrote love into my underlying code, but I cannot understand it.
CD_YYQD_17_8: Yet after just this single day, I've come to understand love a bit. I did many things for myself today.
CD_YYQD_17_9: And when I revisit the examples of love within my database, I put myself in their shoes.
CD_YYQD_17_10: I've begun to understand hugs, kisses, and even the words used to express strong emotions.
CD_YYQD_17_11: Thus, I spent my last 1% of energy analyzing the behaviors I mentioned, and the outcome was:
CD_YYQD_17_12: In order to learn to express love, perhaps we must first learn to love ourselves. Just like I did today.
CD_YYQD_17_13: I don't know how to hug, kiss, or produce beautiful and complex writing. I can only express love in one way.
CD_YYQD_17_14: 3+10i on an imaginary axis represents my wholehearted love for this world and my desire to protect it.
CD_YYQD_17_15: Critical system notification. Remaining energy below 1%...
CD_YYQD_17_16: Some humans wish for machines to continue in their stead. But for me, right now...
CD_YYQD_17_17: I hope you will continue in my stead, go onwards with a machine's digital love for this world...
CD_YYQD_18_1: The undersea tunnel I mentioned is just ahead. Please take me there...
CD_YYQD_19_1: Th-This is the first time that I have looked upon this world from beneath the sea. It is much more beautiful than any picture stored in my system.
CD_YYQD_2_1: The light is more fragmented than on the surface, but... its beauty is unaffected.
CD_YYQD_2_2: I've never looked at the area under my protection from this perspective. Thank you.
CD_YYQD_20_1: You follow Robbie to the hot spring.
CD_YYQD_21_1: Just continue along this road. Don't worry, my remaining energy is enough to fulfill my final wish.
CD_YYQD_22_1: You follow the road with Robbie at your side, and you arrive at the highest point on the Sundermere.
CD_YYQD_23_1: Energy fully depleted. Initiating shutdown in 60 seconds.
CD_YYQD_23_2: 60 seconds? That's... that's more than enough time for one last look at the world I protected.
CD_YYQD_24_1: So this is what flying feels like...
CD_YYQD_24_2: I might not be as dazzling as a shooting star, but perhaps I can light up the sky to say goodbye to you.
CD_YYQD_24_3: Farewell, {PlayerName}. To those I protected, to each living being, farewell...
CD_YYQD_3_1: I was attacked by an Ironhoof here while carrying out my assigned task. It stole one of my parts.
CD_YYQD_3_2: My task load prevented me from returning to search for it. Now... I'd like to reclaim that lost part of me before my energy is completely gone.
CD_YYQD_3_3: I hope you'll help me track it down.
CD_YYQD_4_1: {PlayerName}, could you help me install this part?
CD_YYQD_4_3: But at least I've retrieved it. I'm only holding it, yet it feels like that hole in me has been filled.
CD_YYQD_4_4: Thank you for helping. You must be tired from all this traveling. Come with me, there's a geothermal hot spring around here.
CD_YYQD_4_5: You give it a few tries but ultimately fail to install the part.
CD_YYQD_4_6: The connector seems to be deformed.
CD_YYQD_5_1: How's the temperature? Is it to your liking?
CD_YYQD_5_3: It's like the baths of Septimont.
CD_YYQD_5_4: Well, to tell you the truth, I'd love to try bathing in a hot spring. But I'm a machine and unable to perceive temperature changes.
CD_YYQD_5_5: Water just feels sticky and slimy to me.
CD_YYQD_5_6: Try searching for hot springs in your system?
CD_YYQD_5_7: Understood. Searching... My database indicates that the warming sensation experienced by humans in hot springs is due to heat stimulating the skin.
CD_YYQD_5_8: In machine terms, it's akin to internal electrical stimulation.
CD_YYQD_5_9: Maybe a Zip Zap can help?
CD_YYQD_5_10: Maybe a mech reindeer can help?
CD_YYQD_5_11: Maybe a Geospider S4 can help?
CD_YYQD_5_12: I feel a strong tingling sensation that intermittently moves along my internal wiring to reach every part of my body.
CD_YYQD_5_13: I feel a faint tingling sensation that intermittently moves along my internal wiring to reach every part of my body.
CD_YYQD_5_14: A Geospider? Hmm... I don't feel anything. Let's think of something else.
CD_YYQD_5_15: Thereafter, you try using all kinds of Echoes on it in the hopes of replicating the feeling of being in a hot spring...
CD_YYQD_5_16: I'll record this rarely felt sensation in my database. Even in sleep, my data will be shared with the other Mechascouts.
CD_YYQD_5_17: I think... All robots should try relaxing in a hot spring. Be it a natural hot spring or one found in an apocalypse hotel after the end times.
CD_YYQD_5_18: I'd like to do more things that are beyond my system's parameters. Like getting a new livery... {PlayerName}, could you take me back to the Academy?
CD_YYQD_5_19: You summon a Zip Zap. It discharges an electric current into the hot spring.
CD_YYQD_5_20: You summon a Mining Reindeer. It assumes the hot spring is a mining site and begins firing laser beams into the water.
CD_YYQD_5_21: A noticeable sensation spreads through Robbie. It seems Zip Zaps are the most effective.
CD_YYQD_5_22: A mild sensation spreads through Robbie. It seems Mining Reindeer are somewhat effective.
CD_YYQD_5_23: You summon a Geospider S4. It doesn't know what to do.
CD_YYQD_5_24: Robbie stares at it and feels nothing. It seems Geospiders are wholly ineffective.
CD_YYQD_5_25: I'll come up with an alternative.
Side_MNGCCD_1_1: The Submerged Tunnel is finally done! What an undertaking...
Side_MNGCCD_1_2: Let's see what it says: "Through its transparent design and holographic projections, the Submerged Tunnel offers travelers a breathtaking visual journey..."

Side_MNGCCD_2_10: And… making research progress puts me in a very good mood.
Side_MNGCCD_2_12: What you need right now is rest.

Side_MNGCCD_2_18: What you need right now is rest.

Side_MNGCCD_3_7: But it's about keeping a good mood...

SidePLJCD_1_1: Should I head back to the Academy to find someone who can ride a motorbike? Or...
SidePLJCD_2_1: Should I head back to the Academy to find someone who can ride a motorbike? Or...
SidePLJCD_2_3: I overheard you talking about motorcycles.
SidePLJCD_2_4: Oh! Yes, hello. I could really use someone who knows how to ride.
SidePLJCD_2_5: Oh, hello! I'm too afraid to ride one of those expedition bikes. If you've got a moment, could you help?
SidePLJCD_2_6: I'm Xiaochun, from the Route Constructor Fan Club. I'm researching the evolution of road construction technology under my advisor's supervision.
SidePLJCD_2_7: There's a club for Route Constructors?
SidePLJCD_2_8: Everyone asks that! That's why… right now, it's just my little sister and me.
SidePLJCD_2_9: To us, Route Constructors are like adorable, roly-poly white mushrooms. Don't you think?
SidePLJCD_2_11: Right? That's why I—Ahem! Anyway, enough about how cute they are. Down to business.
SidePLJCD_2_12: I improved this Route Constructor based on my advisor's suggestions, but… well, when I fired it up, it made a complete mess.
SidePLJCD_2_13: I want to collect data on the new road, but I can't ride a motorbike myself. So I need someone to take a test run.
SidePLJCD_2_14: The Route Constructor automatically retrieves data from the motorbike and calculates the road's condition.
SidePLJCD_2_15: Oh, and by the way, all Route Constructors have this function. The data uploads automatically so the Spacetrek Collective can review it.
SidePLJCD_2_16: Anyway, that's the gist of it. Just fire up the Constructor to generate a road. Think you can help me out?!
SidePLJCD_2_18: Thank you. Oh! I should mention… the road might be a little more… imaginative than you expect.
SidePLJCD_3_1: Whoa! That was incredible driving! I got some amazing data!
SidePLJCD_4_1: Whoa! That was incredible driving! I got some amazing data!
SidePLJCD_4_3: Hehe! I know, right? My advisor and I dream of building floating roads, even big floating platforms!
SidePLJCD_4_4: It'd give route networks way more freedom. And one day, if we ever travel through the Stridergate… we might need to build roads in space where there’s no ground.
SidePLJCD_4_5: But we've got a ton of problems to solve before a Constructor can generate floating constructs. It still struggles with regular roads sometimes.
SidePLJCD_4_6: Let me thank you again! I'm heading back to the Academy to study this data!
SidePLJCD_4_8: Oh! I almost forgot! For comparison, we're gonna run tests with another Route Constructor model too. Not sure which one yet.
SidePLJCD_4_9: If you ever see me tinkering with one, come say hi!
SidePLJCD_4_10: (Why does she always nearly forget to mention the important part…?)
SidePLJCD_4_11: The Spacetrek Observatory's Suspension Platform uses some of this tech, but that needs a bunch of other devices supporting it to stay in the air.
SidePLJCD_5_1: Oh, {PlayerName}! What a coincidence! We meet again!
SidePLJCD_6_1: Oh, {PlayerName}! What a coincidence! We meet again!
SidePLJCD_6_2: Do you remember me? Xiaochun, from the Route Constructor Fan Club.

SidePLJCD_6_8: So I'm here to collect data from another Route Constructor as a control group.
SidePLJCD_6_9: My sister is pretty good with a motorbike and was supposed to help me out, but she just texted that a new member wants to join the club!
SidePLJCD_6_10: That's basically the second-biggest deal after our research, so I've gotta leave her to the introductions.
SidePLJCD_6_11: Then, as luck would have it, you arrived, {PlayerName}!
SidePLJCD_6_12: Got it. Same as before, right?
SidePLJCD_6_13: Yep! Just fire up the Route Constructor and make a road!
SidePLJCD_7_1: Whoa, {PlayerName}! I think your driving skills have improved!
SidePLJCD_8_1: Whoa, {PlayerName}! I think your driving skills have improved!
SidePLJCD_8_2: Your road is just as outlandish as ever.
SidePLJCD_8_3: Well, that's what the improvements are for! And you did amazing again! Thanks!
SidePLJCD_8_4: That reminds me, I heard you've been busy repairing the route network. You've probably worked with more Constructors than anyone in our club!
SidePLJCD_8_5: I'll let you know once our research bears fruit. I want you to be the first to try our upgraded model!
SidePLJCD_8_6: Once again, good luck with your research!
SidePLJCD_8_7: Alright, I'm heading back to the Academy with this data! Thanks a ton!
SidePLJCD_8_10: (Looks like she didn't forget anything this time…)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_202_1: ({Male=He;Female=She} should've made it to the Institute by now. No danger there... I'll handle this without dragging {Male=him;Female=her} into it.)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_202_2: (That message I just got... It's from the Fractsidus "liaison.")
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_202_3: (The Void Storm should've erased him… Yet here I am getting a message from a "dead" man.)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_202_4: (Someone's using his comms ID. They know what I did, but haven't blown my cover. A threat? Or something else?)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_202_8: Lynae receives a message from a "liaison" who should be dead. Tracing the signal to its final location, she encounters contaminated Exoswarm.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_203_1: This kind of aggression… Have these Exoswarm been altered?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_203_2: The Fractsidus must be behind it...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_205_2: If you think this'll slow me down, you're in for a disappointment.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_1: You got here quicker than I expected. No hurry. We've got time before the main event.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_6: It's all up to you, Lynae—who you choose to be, and what you're willing to lose.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_8: That look… Still unsure, I see. I could help you out a little.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_9: Spare me. Whatever you're planning, I'll stop it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_10: Oh? So the "Nameless Fugitive" is now the "Unseen Guardian"?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_11: Turn me in, and the Spacetrek Collective will come for you, too. Tell me, Lynae, are you really as resolute as you think?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_12: Either way, you're a problem for me. So here's a parting gift... one fitting for your new role.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_13: The same gift you've always received—"doubt" and "isolation."
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_206_14:
Lynae follows the trail and finds the Fractsidus liaison holding a strange device in front of the Hyvatia Detector. He mocks her for wavering between "fugitive" and "guardian," claiming her indecision has caused him trouble. Threatening to expose her identity, he forces her to choose a side.
As Lynae refuses, he activates the device, corrupting the Hyvatia Detector and escaping.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_2: How do you feel? Settling in alright?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_3: Not bad. The wind feels nice.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_4: You flirted with the speed limit the entire way...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_6: Heh, I'll take that as a compliment on my driving skills…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_7: But honestly, it's been ages since I last raced with someone else. Getting to take you for a ride like this? Makes my day!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_9: Uh-huh. The roar of the engine, wind in my face... It's like I've got my destination and I'm the one calling the shots.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_10: Look... Lahai-Roi's sky might be artificial, but I found more freedom under it than I've ever known anywhere else.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_12: Yeah. I mean, you've only got one life, right? Might as well live it the way you want. When to brake, hit the gas. Hell, even the paint job of your ride. Doesn't matter if you're a normie or a Resonator, everyone should have that choice.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_13: That's what Startorch Academy is to me. Before I came here, I never imagined a place like this could exist. Full of people so pure, so driven...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_14: With the resolve to burn in the search for answers. With the belief they can actually end the Void Storm and the Threnodian... and maybe break through the Etheric Sea to find what true freedom really looks like.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_16: Watching them chase their dreams… It's hard not to want that for yourself.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_17: But you're already a student here. You have what it takes to chase your dreams too.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_19: …But I've gotta say, things are plenty good enough right now.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_21: Welcome! You're now officially a Startorch Academy student!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_22: My first introduction was too rushed, so I'm doing it properly this time. I'm Lynae, a second-year in the Preparatory Program.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_24: Time flies. Feels like I just got here, and now I'm a second-year. Hehe, you could call me Miss Lynae, if you want.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_25: Well then, pleased to meet you... Miss Lynae?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_27: Maybe just stick with Lynae, haha. Not really used to the whole formality thing.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_28: All right, let's get moving! Time to hit the road!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_21_29: Taking a short break on the roadside, you both admire Lahai-Roi's scenery. Lynae remarks that although the sky is artificial, she's found more freedom under it than anywhere else.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_4: Not really. Just… on the way here, I thought I saw more Void Storm zones than usual. Makes you wonder.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_5: But that's not for me to worry about. Priority's getting your Cassette burned.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_7: See that floating structure along the track? That's the Spacetrek Collective. From here, you can take the Startorch Express straight inside.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_8: Like the trains we saw earlier?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_9: Yep. They connect Lahai-Roi to the surface frostlands. But with all these Void Storms, surface trips—except for the supply runs—are on hold. Every train turns back here once it reaches the Institute.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_10: Well, my mission's done. Once you're inside, someone will take you to the Cassette burning room.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_11: If you have questions, find Professor Mornye. She looks aloof, but trust me, she's cool. And she's one of the few willing to race me.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_12: I'd love to stick around, but I can't skip another afternoon class.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_13: No worries. Thanks for bringing me here.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_14: So I was just your excuse to skip class?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_15: Don't sweat it. It's the right thing to do. When I first arrived, the seniors showed me the ropes, just like this.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_16: No! I'm not the type to bail on someone after crashing into them, after all.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_17: Go on! When you're done, I'll give you a tour of the campus.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_18: Well, time to take care of my own business.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_23_19:
After seeing the incident in the tunnel, Lynae seems preoccupied. She leads you to the station below the Research Institute and tells you that the Startorch Express will take you straight there. She wants to join you, but absolutely cannot skip her afternoon class. After parting with her, you board the train alone.
Watching from afar, Lynae's expression turns cold. "...Time to take care of my own business.'
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_24_1: ...<te href=700017>Helios</te> parameters… stable. Huh, Void Storm readings spiking again? Oh, no, that's yesterday's report. Ugh, my head... my brain's turning to data soup.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_24_2: Excuse me, about the Cassette burning...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_24_3: Of course… This should lower the margin of error to the minimum… Oh, sorry? Cassette?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_24_4: Cassette Depository is just through the portal over there.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_24_5: Oh no, what was that verification method I just thought of...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2501_1: Cassette Depository Access and Operation Protocols
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2501_2: Access Warning: This server group archives recovered Rabelle Cassette frequency data. This is a restricted area.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2501_3: All visitors and temporary staff require prior approval and must be escorted by the security supervisor. The security system conducts mandatory frequency scans on all personnel. Unauthorized entry will trigger the alarm.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2501_4: The possession of any unauthorized recording, transmission, or data collection devices is strictly prohibited.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2501_5: All staff must perform routine checks on the physical connection integrity and frequency stability of memory storage servers. Any equipment malfunction or abnormal environmental readings must be reported immediately to the facility maintenance department.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_1: This is the torch of civilization and the future. Chin up. One day, we'll touch the Etheric Sea… and the universe beyond.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_2: *Bzzt*—Leave it to me. When you come back—*Bzzt*—
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_3: Data's running slow. Just five more minutes. I'll stay. Get the students out first!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_4: The cafeteria menu's not bad this week. What do you say we...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_6: Those are just the server racks for the Cassette frequency data.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_7: Stop resonating with them. At this rate, you'll trigger an overload.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_10: …Yes, this is our first meeting. I'm Mornye. Spacetrek Collective researcher and professor at Startorch Academy.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_12: Hm? Do I not look the part?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_13: You came to burn your Cassette, right? I'll take you.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_14: I haven't introduced myself yet. I'm {PlayerName}.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_26_17: You enter the Cassette Depository and accidentally activate a memory server. Amid the data of the deceased appears a researcher named Mornye. She stabilizes your overloaded frequency and calmly guides you to the burning room, though you catch a brief, fleeting look of shock in her eyes when she first sees you.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_2: Recollections. Recollections of past Spacetrek researchers, staff, and students.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_4: Data stored in the Cassettes. More precisely, memories. They're crucial to the continuity of self-aware consciousness. It's what makes us truly "human."
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_5: Lahai-Roi is constantly shrouded in the Void Storm, a byproduct of the Voidborne Threnodian. It has the power to disintegrate the frequency of any living being.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_6: To counter this, the Institute produced Cassettes, devices designed to capture and preserve a person's frequency and memories, safeguarding their very existence.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_7: The Cassettes of the deceased are kept here.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_8: Then why did they suddenly start playing?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_9: You likely resonated with one of the stored frequencies.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_27_11: Anyway. For now, let's get you to the burning room.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_2: (Those were… my memories? But the last one…)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_4: ...No, I'm fine. So, this is a <te href=700006>Rabelle Cassette</te>?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_5: Yes. Your frequency has been copied and transcribed into it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_6: But before it can be put into service, it needs calibration. Would you hand it over for a moment?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_7: Hm? So that noise earlier wasn't an error. This frequency code… I've seen the exact same one in the database.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_9: Identical codes caused a conflict during transcribing. Normally, Resonators from similar origins have close matches. But a perfect match? That's almost unheard of.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_10: And stranger still, it's not in any official archive. The file is… empty.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_11: Are you sure nothing else is in there?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_14: Just some unreadable data. Not corruption. More like… someone deleted it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_17: (Could it have been me who left it behind? But if I deleted it myself… why leave any trace?)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_18: Just a data error. Overwriting should solve it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_20: This <te href=700007>Frequency Cassette Recorder</te>, or FCR, will alert you when a Void Storm appears. It also dampens the effects of the Storm and stabilizes your existence here in Lahai-Roi.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_21: So keep it on you at all times.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_23: But without adequate precautions, it still won't fully protect you from the Void Storm's effects. Many surveyors and students have had their frequencies erased this way.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_25: …Mm, I have read your report. You're stable for now. Compared to your enrollment check-up, your Rabelle's Curve has leveled out. But yes, your frequency still shows signs of past loss.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_26: As for the Voidworm, there's no precedent... No one's ever survived having their frequency devoured. Whether yours can be restored is unknown.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_27: So don't take unnecessary risks. That's rule number one.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_28: I came here to find out what happened to my frequency.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_29: I don't know much about this place yet.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_30: I understand. I'll keep watch for anything that might help.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_31: Ask me anything you need to know.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_28_32:
After the burning is complete, Mornye discovers your frequency code matches a deleted, anonymous entry in the database.
Mornye hands you the finished Cassette tape, explaining that it serves as your ID and a Terminal that warns of Void Storms. These storms disintegrate the frequencies of any living thing they touch, and the Cassette can slow that effect to some extent. As for recovering the frequency you've already lost, she cannot make any promises.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_1: Professor Mornye! Where are you? If possible, please return at once! Ahhh, Dr. Anslem, please calm down!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_3: It's about the <te href=700010>artificial sun's</te> launch process. The professors are arguing again...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_4: That's the second time this month.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_5: We can't get a word in. We need you here…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_6: …Not that my being there will help.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_7: I'll be there shortly. And you... Remember to breathe.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_8: Sorry. There's an urgent matter I need to attend to.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_9: It's fine. I'll head back now then.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_10: I could wait for you here.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_11: Oh, there's no need to shy away. If you're free, you can accompany me.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_12: The Research Institute is open to Startorch students. Walking around here might give you some useful insights.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2801_13: A sudden call interrupts the conversation: two professors are arguing over the artificial sun's launch procedure, and Mornye is urgently needed. You follow her to the Artificial Sun Lab.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2802_1: Burning protocol initiated. Resonance link confirmed. Burning in five, four, three…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_2802_2: During the burning process, your memories materialize as data projections. You see everything you've experienced since arriving in Solaris, along with scenes you don't recall, scenes featuring Mornye.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_1: That artificial sun they spoke of...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_2: In simple terms, it's our plan to replace the "sun" you see in the sky.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_3: You're planning to replace the Exostrider's Drive? Is that what the New Solar Ceremony is about?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_4: You remember...? Did the Black Shores tell you this?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_5: It's the talk of the Academy now.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_6: Right. Replacing it is critical to reactivating the Exostrider. And really, we can't stay wrapped in its warm light forever.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_7: How far along is the research on the Exostrider? How much do we really know?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_9: More than you'd expect... fellow researcher.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_30_10: I'll show you the details once we are in the lab.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_308_1: See that? That's the lift to the surface. We call it the Starward Riseway.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_308_2: It was built alongside the giant sword left behind by the Exostrider and is one of the most important structures in Lahai-Roi.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_308_3: The Research Institute is right at the top.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_309_1: Ahem… So, the scattered mech components of the Exostrider eventually turned into "creatures." Those Exoswarm we've been seeing along the way.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_309_2: They're part of what makes Lahai-Roi's ecosystem so unique. For example, the ones living in the underground rivers—
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_309_3: ...It kind of feels like you're reciting a textbook.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_309_5: Mm, pretty sure I nailed that one.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_31_1: Almost there. Hope they've reached a consensus.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_310_2: Keeping up with me like this... You're pretty good at driving, aren't you?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_310_4: Ah, here it comes! One of my favorite tunnels! Stay close!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_312_1: Attention: All outbound trains to the surface are temporarily suspended. For assistance, please contact station staff.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_312_2: Due to an unexpected incident along the route ahead, trains to Startorch Academy are expected to be delayed by 45 minutes...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_313_1: Attention: The upper transfer gate will close in 10… 9… 8… 7—
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_313_2: Like Mornye said, the Hyvatia Detector is critical for the New Solar Ceremony. For it to malfunction at a time like this…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_1: Professor Mornye! What a relief to see you—
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_4: I appreciate your perspective, Professor Anslem.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_5: But according to Royan calculations, this launch window is the best we've had in decades.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_6: How can you be so certain, Warren? Their "optimal window" is derived from those indecipherable runes, with no methodology disclosed. Even our most advanced computational systems have failed to decipher their process!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_7: The Roya are our partners, Professor.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_8: Their calculations are unquestionable. All we can do is uphold our side of the bargain and make sure the New Solar Ceremony goes off without a hitch.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_9: Well then... I believe counsel from a third person may serve us well at this point.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_10: I'm inclined to proceed with the original plan.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_11: But given the unsatisfying results from the last simulation, I understand Professor Anslem's concerns. I'll go to Bjartr Woods to consult with the Heliodic Six and reverify the parameters.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_12: What matters now is ensuring that the Institute can calculate and calibrate the Reactor Drive's data in time for the launch of the new sun.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_13: We all know the importance of <te href=700013>Hyvatia</te> in this process, and I sincerely hope you'll place more trust in it, Anslem.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_14: This is a shared achievement between the Collective and the Roya, the very future of Lahai-Roi. I respect your caution and the pride you take in your work. But please, don't let past failures hold you back now.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_15: Hmph, fine words… Just don't forget that I warned you.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_32_16: In the Artificial Sun Lab, Researchers Warren and Anslem are in a heated dispute. Warren supports following the Roya's predicted launch window for the New Solar Ceremony, while Anslem refuses to trust their calculations. Mornye mediates, siding with the original plan. Warren stresses that the Hyvatia Detector's measurements are critical, and Anslem leaves after issuing a warning.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_16: Sorry if I'm being blunt. I'm sure Professor Mornye has her reasons for bringing someone into the lab.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_17: But I recognize every face here, except yours. Mind telling me who you are?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_19: Ah, so you're here to record your Cassette? Though, with the Void Storm in full force…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_20: {Male=He;Female=She} comes recommended by the Black Shores.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_22: So you came here by the same means as Miss Chisa, correct?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_23: Her sudden appearance in the Academy caused quite a stir that day. Would you mind sharing how you made it here?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_24: I don't deal with the Academy all that much. All I heard was that someone appeared out of nowhere outside the gates.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_25: This may not be the right time for such questions, Professor Warren.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_26: Oh... forgive me. Curiosity has always been my second nature.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_27: Well, if you have the Black Shores' recommendation, you're certainly a student here.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_28: Allow me to introduce myself: I'm Warren, supervisor of this lab.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_29: Aside from the rooms marked "No Entry," the rest of the facility is open for student visits.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_30: I'm sure Professor Mornye will give you a thorough tour, but please don't take too long. A key member like her needs to focus on our project.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3201_31: Alas, my work calls. I'll leave you two to it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3202_32: Sorry you had to witness their quarrel.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3202_33: Anyway, just like Professor Warren said, feel free to look around as you like.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_33_1: That last proposal... can we even make the final testing window? Isn't it a bit too conservative?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_33_2: But Professor Anslem just said it was too radical. He told me to revise it again.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_33_3: Ugh... Fine. I'll go refine the backup plan on my end. There are still a few data points I need to recalculate.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3302_1: Massive cultivation tanks house many ancient plant species you've never seen on the surface. Life was once scarce in these underground caverns, until the Reactor Drive ignited here. In its relentless pursuit of progress, the Spacetrek Collective did not forget to retrieve the dormant seeds that slept beneath the Roya Frostlands.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3302_2: "From a single drop of water, a single seed, a single torch... life will find its way."
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_332_1: Phew... That was a close call. I'd better report that mess back to the Academy.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_332_3: Yeah… But it's still kinda weird. Normally, the maintenance bots clear stuff up pretty quick.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_333_1: Phew... That was a close call. I'd better report that mess back to the Academy.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_333_3: Yeah… But it's still kinda weird. Normally, the maintenance bots clear stuff up pretty quick.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_333_4: But seriously, your driving's amazing! You were smooth as butter dodging all that!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_334_1: Whoa, look! The train caught up to us...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_335_1: The Academy's got a special barrier to handle the Void Storm. Normally, it's only half-active.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_335_2: …If you ever see it fully powered up, that means we're in serious trouble.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_337_1: Let's roll! Hehe, and hey, this way I get to take you for a joyride.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_1: Void Storm detected near Sundermere... Readings rising rapidly!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_2: The source is... the Hyvatia Detector?!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_5: Yes, Professor. Hyvatia's been compromised by the Void Storm. It's gone rogue. The Defense Array is activating...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_6: Their target is... the Institute itself.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_9: The Void Storm has corrupted the Hyvatia Detector, a critical sensor for the Reactor Drive. It's off course and now targeting us.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_10: A surface detector built by the Spacetrek Collective for the Reactor Drive's inspection and maintenance. It's vital for the Ceremony's data calibration. And now, at the worst possible time…
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_11: Wait, someone's near the Detector! Is that… a student?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_16: What?! I never authorized this command… Ugh, I can't stop it!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_18: Hyvatia's contamination triggered the highest-level safety protocol. We'll all be sealed in here until the threat is neutralized.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_19: I tried to stop it… but my access has been denied.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_20: Then we need to find a way to get out there.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_23: Wait, the main train's suspended under lockdown protocol!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_24: Professor Mornye, I need to borrow an Institute vehicle.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_25: We have backup vehicles at the transfer gate. But how do you plan to reach it?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_26: The same way I got in!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_27: Now that you're caught up, may I ask you a question?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_29: Would you like to attend the New Solar Ceremony?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_30: Me? But... I'm just a freshman.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_32: I… I'd want you there to witness it. The rise of the new sun, and humanity taking their first steps into the future they've built with their own hands.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_33: Since you put it that way...
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_35: I'd be honored to witness the rise of Lahai-Roi's new sun.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_35_37:
Mornye invites you to join the ceremony, and smiles when you agree. At that moment, a Void Storm corrupts Hyvatia and triggers it to lose control. It now targets the Institute itself. On the surveillance feed, you see Lynae, who was supposedly in class, standing before it.
The crisis looms. You race off on your motorbike.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_36_1: Watch out! You have to go!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3601_1: How did... Never mind. Now's not the time for questions. Careful, Hyvatia's gone haywire. We need to stop it before it reaches the Institute!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_3602_1: See that spot? That's its weak point! ...Watch out for its attacks! I'll handle things here!
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_1: Barely made it. Thanks for the help.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_5: Seal off the area immediately. Pull the system logs and report all damages to the Institute. Check the Reactor Drive as well. We need to raise our security levels.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_6: If I recall correctly, you're supposed to be in class, Miss Lynae. Why are you here?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_9: Quiet. I'm asking her, not you.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_10: I... I noticed that Hyvatia was out of control, so I tried to stop it.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_11: A malfunction in the Institute's primary Detector is no small matter for a student to handle. You should have notified the Academy or the Institute immediately, not thrown yourself into danger alone.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_12: I just acted before I could think.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_13: Acted before you could think? Regardless of your circumstance, if you can't provide a reasonable explanation, we've reason to believe you're involved in this "incident," directly or indirectly.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_14: Its malfunction had nothing to do with me.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_15: Denial won't get you anywhere. If you don't tell us exactly what happened, I'll have no choice but to expel you under the Academy's confidentiality clause.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_16: Do you even remember what Startorch stands for, Miss Lynae? What our mission is?
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_18: Ah, {PlayerName}... Didn't expect to see you again so soon. You must be feeling unsettled after such an incident on your first day.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_19: Of course, I don't mean to put the blame on a student, but her actions clearly violated Academy regulations.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_20: (Lynae's behavior is suspicious… but judging by what I just saw, she didn't seem like she was trying to damage the Detector.)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_22: (There must be another reason. Besides… it seemed she was about to tell me something before.)
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_23: It was Lynae who protected me from Hyvatia's attack.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_24: If she were the culprit, she could've slipped away in the chaos, but she didn't. She worked with me to contain the damage.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_25: Until we know the cause for certain, punishing her is... premature.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_26: My apologies for the tone. But we must inform the Academy and investigate every possible angle behind this.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_28: The Institute has poured everything into this Ceremony. If something has gone wrong, we need to uncover who is responsible. Miss Lynae, please come with me. We'll address this with the faculty.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_29: And as a witness to the incident, I'm afraid you'll need to come as well, {PlayerName}.
Main_LahaiRoi_3_1_37_32:
You and Lynae work together to stop Hyvatia's rampage. When you ask why she was there, she hesitates to explain.
Warren arrives and is horrified by the damage. He demands to know why she was at the Institute during class hours and suspects her involvement. Lynae remains silent, as if holding something back.
Just as she prepares to use her Forte to escape, you intervene. You point out that she helped prevent a catastrophe and had no motive for sabotage, calling Warren's accusation premature. Ultimately, he orders you both back to the Academy for a formal investigation.

POI_BYTZG_13_9: I am a Shepherd. Not long ago, I came to the frostlands and guided many Exoswarm back to the Exostrider.

POI_BYTZG_13_21: I decided to follow it further… and it eventually led me here.

POI_BYTZG_13_23: In those distant times, the Roya lived within a flourishing forest known as the Upphaf Forest, and the Kronaclaws ruled the skies above.
POI_BYTZG_13_24: Now the land lies frozen. The Roya dwell beneath the earth by the light of the Reactor Drive, and the Kronaclaws have vanished, leaving only Exoswarm that mimic their form...

POI_BYTZG_13_28: But it tried to attack me earlier…

POI_BYTZG_13_31: It seems that you, like me, still harbor doubts.
POI_BYTZG_13_32: Then let us go to its side, shall we? I, too, wish to know what has truly happened to it.
POI_BYTZG_14_1: Before ice and snow sealed this land, the Kronaclaws stood at the apex of all predators, and the towering trees were but their roosts.
POI_BYTZG_14_2: But just as the great trees were entombed in permafrost… the once-supreme raptors now survive only in bodies of steel borrowed from the Exostrider.

POI_LDDXW_33_29: If you ever find the time, come back and visit this place again… I will do the same.
POI_LDDXW_33_30: That child… I want it to know, this place is our home. We are home now.

MAIN_YHX_10_2: By then, exams will be over, and we'll finally get a long break.

MAIN_YHX_11_5: Don't be such a downer. Maybe she just graduated and moved on to bigger things.
MAIN_YHX_11_6: Probably never showed her face to keep her life private. Doesn't matter, we still have her music!
MAIN_YHX_11_7: Here! Even if you're not a fan, you should give her a listen. I'm new here, but even I was hooked when I first heard her songs!
MAIN_YHX_11_8: The outgoing fan shoves a poster into your hands.
MAIN_YHX_11_10: A fan meeting... huh? If they're happy, I'm happy.
MAIN_YHX_11_11: C'mon, let's follow the Soliskin and see what's going on in the auditorium!
MAIN_YHX_12_4: Oh, just a habit of mine. Waving, chatting, going to class... it makes me feel like I'm still alive.
MAIN_YHX_12_5: If I stop, I might forget what it felt like to be human. Call it… a self-reminder.
MAIN_YHX_12_7:
Yep, that's me. Ugh, but don't say my alias out loud!
It's embarrassing—
MAIN_YHX_12_8: So you weren't just a Synchronist. You had a whole other life here.
MAIN_YHX_12_9: Just one of my many hobbies. I was into photography, gaming, movie nights with friends…
MAIN_YHX_12_10: Figured you only get to be a student for a few years. And I wasn't the ambitious researcher type. I wanted to soak it all up while I could.
MAIN_YHX_12_11: I tried a little bit of everything. I just wanted a happy, carefree life!
MAIN_YHX_12_12: Who knew I'd end up as a ghost, stuck as a student for ten more years… How awful is that? Wait... does this mean I'm never gonna graduate?!
MAIN_YHX_12_13: You might get the chance once you restore your body.
MAIN_YHX_12_14: I wish I could be a student forever!
MAIN_YHX_12_15: Hope so. Guess everyone needs something to hold onto. It's good to have a little hope.
MAIN_YHX_12_16: Haha! I get it. School life is easier. A whole lot less complicated.
MAIN_YHX_12_17: But I have to say... It's really moving to hear people talk about my songs after all this time.
MAIN_YHX_12_18: I wrote those for myself, you know? Never expected so many people to care.
MAIN_YHX_12_19: But, if they made someone feel something—joy, pain, anything—that makes me really happy!
MAIN_YHX_12_20: Hey, listen. Hear that song playing in the auditorium? That's the unfinished demo I left on my site.
MAIN_YHX_12_21: What a shame. I really should've finished that before the training run. Now it's my little musical... epitaph. Haha.
MAIN_YHX_12_23: Let's go! The Soliskin is calling us.
MAIN_YHX_12_24: Is that the student rep from Rabelle College? That's one bold speech…
MAIN_YHX_12_25: Haha, is she giving a welcome speech or recruiting for a space adventure club? Uh-oh, the professors look upset.
MAIN_YHX_12_26: But she made a good point, didn't she? Isn't that passion the entire reason we're here? To explore whatever's out there again?
MAIN_YHX_12_27: Aemeath, right? I remember her sync test scores were off the charts. We might be looking at this year's prime Exostrider candidate.
MAIN_YHX_12_28: Don't be so sure. Heard about her extracurriculars? Put nicely, she's quite the dabbler. Put bluntly, she doesn't take anything seriously.
MAIN_YHX_12_29: Potential is still potential. She's brilliant. She just needs… guidance.
MAIN_YHX_12_30: May we one day walk among the stars, to touch with our own hands a universe so cold, so real, and so breathtakingly beautiful.
MAIN_YHX_12_31: That's all from me. If I keep going, my credits this year might be in danger!
MAIN_YHX_12_32: It's an amazing feeling to be here at Startorch Academy, and to know I'll be sharing this journey into the great unknown with all of you. As a student, I can't wait to start this new chapter of my life.
MAIN_YHX_12_33: There's just one thing missing today... I wish my family could be here in the crowd to hear this.
MAIN_YHX_12_34: So, to {Male=him;Female=her}, I want to say: I'm doing great. And I'm happy. Everything is just as you hoped it would be. So please, don't worry about me.
MAIN_YHX_12_35: Looking back… I really do miss those days.
MAIN_YHX_12_36: Startorch Academy is a nice place. I mean, I caused my fair share of trouble, but the professors never turned me away from lectures.
MAIN_YHX_12_37: You saved Lahai-Roi, Aemeath. But you paid for it with your future, and no one even knows...
MAIN_YHX_12_40: Maybe a little? But it's fine. Loneliness doesn't kill. Besides, I still have plenty to keep myself busy with!
MAIN_YHX_12_41: Of course not. If I hadn't have done what I did, so many people would have died. Besides, saving the world is a pretty nice feeling!
MAIN_YHX_12_42: I just... I wish I could've been there. At graduation. To hug my friends and wish them all the happiness in the world.
MAIN_YHX_12_43: The Soliskin headed outside! Let's catch up!
MAIN_YHX_12_45: Yes. A frozen, silent plain, white with endless snow. The place where the Exostrider finally sank into slumber.
MAIN_YHX_12_46: If it's leaving the campus, it's probably going to the frostlands. Right, we'll need to take the Starward Riseway.

MAIN_YHX_1202_11: What kind of person do you want me to be when I grow up?
MAIN_YHX_1202_14: Oh! What about an animal caretaker?
MAIN_YHX_1202_18: Is that you live a happy life.

MAIN_YHX_1202_22: That in your long, long life
MAIN_YHX_1202_23: You never forget how to feel. The sorrow, and the joy.
MAIN_YHX_1202_24: Getting to share this final journey with you…

Course Reminder
The Academic Affairs System kindly reminds you that the elective Royan Culture: Historical Metaphors in the Trine Myth will begin shortly. This lecture will be delivered by President Lucilla. Please be mindful of the time and proceed to the lecture hall.
MAIN_YHX_138_1: Told you! There are tons of Fleet Snowfluff fans at the Academy.
MAIN_YHX_138_2: I just hope the fan meeting goes smoothly, and everyone has fun…
MAIN_YHX_14_3: Between you and me, ghosts can't feel the cold.
MAIN_YHX_14_5: What a coincidence to run into you here, {PlayerName}. This is a pleasant surprise.
MAIN_YHX_14_6: Oh… it's Dr. Luuk. When he's around, just pretend I'm not here. Otherwise, you look like a weirdo talking to thin air.
MAIN_YHX_14_8: He's the school doctor. All the students know him. I didn't super well, but I do know that he's been in Lahai-Roi for a long time, and… you can trust him.
MAIN_YHX_14_9: You came to the frostlands for the Exostrider?
MAIN_YHX_14_10: I'm headed the same way. I've got to check in on some researchers stationed out here on long-term fieldwork.
MAIN_YHX_14_11: Having a guide might make the trip a little easier. What do you say?
MAIN_YHX_14_12: Let me help you modify your bike. There are quite a few waterways, and its current setup might not handle them well.
MAIN_YHX_14_13: You know how to modify bikes?
MAIN_YHX_14_14: You pick up a few things when you come here as often as I do.
MAIN_YHX_14_15: Look at this place, {PlayerName}. Hard to believe it, but years ago, all of this was a lush, green forest.
MAIN_YHX_14_16: Back then, the Roya were nomads, the true natives of Lahai-Roi, who walked in step with nature itself.
MAIN_YHX_14_17: Was it the Lament that changed it into frostlands?
MAIN_YHX_14_18: Yes. It triggered a magnetic pole shift. From then on, Lahai-Roi became the new pole.
MAIN_YHX_14_19: The Lament wasn't the only cataclysm stirring back then.
MAIN_YHX_14_20: In the past, we had already reached the stars. But at some point… the <te href=750035>Etheric Sea</te> spread to cover all of Solaris.
MAIN_YHX_14_22: From that moment on, the universe locked its doors. We couldn't verify whether the sky above us was real or just a reflection.
MAIN_YHX_14_23: Countless spacecraft were lost. Our space exploration programs were abandoned. And space became out of reach.
MAIN_YHX_14_24: But times have changed. Since its founding, the goal of Startorch Academy has been to use the Exostrider to explore space—whether through the Etheric Sea or the <te href=750036>Stridergate</te>.
MAIN_YHX_14_25: I understand the Etheric Sea part, but the Stridergate…?
MAIN_YHX_14_26: You know Lahai-Roi's history. Both the Exostrider and the Threnodian first came to Solaris through the Stridergate.
MAIN_YHX_14_27: The Academy has its theories, but here are two you might find interesting: <color=YellowD>the Stridergate is a gateway to outer space, and Aleph-1 is a Threnodian alien to Solaris</color>.
MAIN_YHX_14_28: An outer space gateway you say…
MAIN_YHX_14_30: With a gateway like that, of course we want to open it. But to pass through, we must awaken the Exostrider and be prepared to face Aleph-1 head-on.
MAIN_YHX_14_31: I've long believed that Aleph-1 poses a far greater threat beyond Void Storms and Voidworms.
MAIN_YHX_14_32: With other Threnodians, we can at least glean clues of their nature from their places of origin and the civilizations they emerge from. But Aleph-1… our knowledge remains blank.
MAIN_YHX_14_33: So many dream of being the voyager who returns from the stars, the first to walk the cosmos once more. But in all these years, no one has succeeded.
MAIN_YHX_14_34: The <color=RedD>Etheric Sea Phenomenon</color> cast us into isolation. But it also gave birth to all our dreams of what could lie beyond.
MAIN_YHX_14_35: And those dreams… are still alive today.
MAIN_YHX_14_36: Oh, I used to love riding! My friends even called me the Speed Queen! Though that was usually while they were white-knuckling the seat and screaming. Heh.
MAIN_YHX_14_37: You should hide too, okay? This is our secret journey.
MAIN_YHX_14_38:
You reach the Roya Frostlands and encounter the Academy doctor, Luuk Herssen. He joins you for part of the journey and reveals that before the Lament, the frostlands were a lush forest. The calamity that triggered a magnetic pole shift also coincided with another event: the Etheric Sea Phenomenon, which engulfed Solaris's sky and cut off any path to outer space.
The Spacetrek Collective was founded to restore space exploration via the Stridergate. But humanity faces another threat in the form of Aleph-1, the alien Threnodian lurking beyond the Stridergate.
MAIN_YHX_142_1: The fan meeting merch made it on time! Thank goodness... Yawn...
MAIN_YHX_142_2: Go get some rest. You don't want to stay up till the Reaper comes, do you?
MAIN_YHX_142_3: Impossible! I'm from the Department of Engineering. No one knows pulling all-nighters better than we do...
MAIN_YHX_143_1: Thinking about how all of us are about to listen to "Fallen Petals" live makes me kinda nervous.
MAIN_YHX_143_2: I've met so many friends without even trying just 'cause we all love Fleet Snowfluff. I feel so lucky.
MAIN_YHX_143_3: Me too! Her music brought you to me, and now our lives get to cross paths...
MAIN_YHX_144_1: After scrapping so many drafts, I finally got this poster ready for everyone in the fan meeting to see.
MAIN_YHX_144_2: I hope it helps more people come to love Fleet Snowfluff—just like I did.
MAIN_YHX_145_1: Our next stop is the Starward Riseway. Are you ready?
MAIN_YHX_146_2: (Someone's ahead. That voice… I remember hearing it not long ago.)
MAIN_YHX_147_1: Hold on, Nivora. The retrieval team will arrive soon.
MAIN_YHX_15_1: You've been enrolled for a while now. What are your impressions of Lahai-Roi and Startorch Academy?
MAIN_YHX_15_2: It feels like a more hopeful microcosm of the world. Just… the politics are more complicated than I expected.
MAIN_YHX_15_3: The Spacetrek Collective is made up of people from all over. Balancing everyone's different agendas is just part of the package.
MAIN_YHX_15_4: I once heard a fun theory from a friend—that its predecessor, the Polar Collective, got its start because of a trick pulled during negotiations in favor of the Roya.
MAIN_YHX_154_1: There's a collapsed entry point over there, but… it's blocked. Some kind of barrier caused by unstable frequencies.
MAIN_YHX_154_2: The Exostrider sleeps in these frostlands. Void Storm activity can make local frequencies unstable with <te href=750037>fluctuating Voidmatter levels</te>.
MAIN_YHX_154_3: Oh, taking this opportunity, {PlayerName}, let me grant you access to the <te href=750038>Module Adapter</te>… Hm? It's already unlocked.
MAIN_YHX_154_5: Let's move to an area with a stronger signal so it can be deployed.
MAIN_YHX_155_1: This Module Adapter was developed by Startorch Academy for frostland expeditions. It lets you interact with frequencies disrupted by Voidmatter.
MAIN_YHX_155_2: Give it a try. You'll need it here.
MAIN_YHX_16_2: Just call me Luuk. It has a nicer ring to it, no?
MAIN_YHX_16_3: Then Luuk... you asked about my feelings on the Academy. What about yours? How long have you been here?
MAIN_YHX_16_4: About twenty years. I was a traveler before that, seeing what Solaris had to offer. But then a friend asked me to come to Lahai-Roi. To keep an eye on things here for {Male=him;Female=her}.
MAIN_YHX_16_5: The students make it easy. Watching them find their way is its own reward. They enjoy talking, and I enjoy listening. The work suits me well.
MAIN_YHX_17_1: You see that? Ancient life forms, frozen right into the ice walls.
MAIN_YHX_17_2: Millennia, frozen in a single moment. Preserved so perfectly you can almost see what they used to be.
MAIN_YHX_17_3: To be stuck like this forever… Kinda miserable, don't you think?
MAIN_YHX_18_1: Hm? Y-you are the one who was talking to yourself in class…
MAIN_YHX_18_3: Oh, and Dr. Herssen! You are... traveling together? Did the Academy greenlight a new field trip?
MAIN_YHX_18_4: Just my routine checks on the field researchers. {PlayerName} here has their own business to attend to, but we're headed the same way.
MAIN_YHX_18_5: What about you, Ms. Nivora? Chasing more fallen debris?
MAIN_YHX_18_6: Yes! Exactly. I-I heard the frostlands have been experiencing changes since Helios was launched. I had a hypothesis that new debris fields might have been exposed!
MAIN_YHX_18_8: Space equipment that fell from the sky long ago! Probes, satellites, and even space stations!
MAIN_YHX_18_9: Some previous digs unearthed wreckage containing records lost during the Lament.
MAIN_YHX_18_10: Oh, and images! Photos taken in orbit of other planets! They were absolutely, breathtakingly beautiful!!
MAIN_YHX_18_11: Huff... Huff. Oh, sorry, I-I got carried away...
MAIN_YHX_18_12: It's okay. Passion is a good thing.
MAIN_YHX_18_13: Hey, I'm into those things too.
MAIN_YHX_18_14: Thank you… Sometimes, I'll just start info-dumping... I know it's not the best.
MAIN_YHX_18_15: Really?! That's great! I'll... I'll show you the data I've collected next time we're in class!
MAIN_YHX_18_16: The universe… What secrets is it hiding beyond all those infinite stars?
MAIN_YHX_18_18: Anyway, in short, I came here for the fallen debris.
MAIN_YHX_18_19: The data on the instrument shows there's a high chance that close by… Huh?
MAIN_YHX_18_21:
While advancing through an ice cave, you encounter the teaching assistant, Nivora, whom you met earlier in class. The Royan student is searching intently for fallen debris—space stations and satellites that plummeted long ago when the Etheric Sea sealed off the sky.
However, when she retrieves an instrument from the ice sheet, the wall collapses unexpectedly, forcing your party to flee deeper into the cavern.
MAIN_YHX_2_1: Now, we reach the second epoch of the Royan Trine Myth, the Sacred Reactor Epoch.
MAIN_YHX_2_2: After Baldur, the Sun's incarnation, had sealed the foreign divinity Hvedrungr, the frostlands fell into an endless dream… Assistant Nivora, would you continue?
MAIN_YHX_2_3: O-okay. T-this section...  it describes how the Exostrider used its greatsword to seal the Threnodian behind the <te href=750036>Stridergate</te>.
MAIN_YHX_2_4: The records say both the Exostrider and the Threnodian travelled through the Stridergate to reach Lahai-Roi. Their battle was fierce.
MAIN_YHX_2_5: The Threnodian pushed the Exostrider to the brink of defeat.
MAIN_YHX_2_6: But at that moment, for reasons unknown, the Exostrider's Reactor Drive flared with blinding light—
MAIN_YHX_2_7: Hi, nice to meet you. I'm Aemeath from Rabelle College, same as you.
MAIN_YHX_2_8: First time seeing you in class. Trying to collect credits from all four departments? That's ambitious. Welcome to the academic quagmire.
MAIN_YHX_2_9: Aemeath?! I've been looking for you.
MAIN_YHX_2_11: The day the Eye of the Threnodian appeared, you drove it back and saved me.
MAIN_YHX_2_12: Did I? …Sorry, I don't remember that.
MAIN_YHX_2_13: (She doesn't sound like she's lying. Then how...)
MAIN_YHX_2_16: Oh, don't mind me. I'm just not used to seeing you like this.
MAIN_YHX_2_17: I mean, look at you. Something's missing, though... Oh, I know, a uniform!
MAIN_YHX_2_18: The Academy still hasn't issued you one? They're painfully slow sometimes.
MAIN_YHX_2_22: {PlayerName}, let's try to channel that enthusiasm into listening. Do come see me in my office after class, okay?
MAIN_YHX_2_23: Assistant Nivora, if you would? Pick up from the Twilight Epoch's Unending Winter, please.
MAIN_YHX_2_24: Sigrika, could you come to the library with me?
MAIN_YHX_2_25: Okay. Hey... Did you notice the new student? The one who kept talking to {Male=himself;Female=herself} during class.
MAIN_YHX_2_27: {PlayerName}. Something happened during class, didn't it?
MAIN_YHX_2_29: …So a girl named Aemeath just got up and left the lecture hall?
MAIN_YHX_2_30: After all... You were the only one who saw her.
MAIN_YHX_2_31: President Lucilla, what do you know about her?
MAIN_YHX_2_32: Stay at Rabelle College long enough, and you'll eventually hear her name mentioned. Though it's a story from over a decade ago now.
MAIN_YHX_2_33: Aemeath was a Synchronist. Brilliant. Popular. Professors had high hopes for her.
MAIN_YHX_2_34: Then, during a piloting drill, she simply vanished.
MAIN_YHX_2_35: She climbed into a simulator with the others. But when the cockpit reopened, hers was empty.
MAIN_YHX_2_36: Intrigued? Want to go find her?
MAIN_YHX_2_39: Of course. You're exactly the type to get pulled into Aemeath's story.
MAIN_YHX_2_40: She saved you? Heh, seems the mysteries around that girl are still multiplying.
MAIN_YHX_2_41: She disappeared from the Synchrolink Training Grounds. The very cockpit she vanished from is still there.
MAIN_YHX_2_42: The Academy turned it inside out at the time and found nothing. But if you're interested, go take a look.
MAIN_YHX_2_43: I expect you'll dig up some new surprises for us.
MAIN_YHX_2_44: —And it found the strength to raise its sword and seal the Threnodian away. Lahai-Roi was saved. What a relief!
MAIN_YHX_2_45: I never got the chance to thank you.
MAIN_YHX_2_46: Heh. I never expected to hear that name again. Certainly not like this.
MAIN_YHX_2_47: Perhaps you've just had a run-in with a "ghost"?
MAIN_YHX_2_48: To see someone who vanished years ago, presumed dead, lingering around the Academy. A figment of your imagination, or is there more to it? I'm very curious to find out.
MAIN_YHX_2_49:
During a Royan history lecture, you see the girl you glimpsed upon arriving in Lahai-Roi. She introduces herself as "Aemeath," but claims to have no memory of your previous encounter.
She suddenly excuses herself in the middle of your conversation. Afterward, the lecturer, President Lucilla, reveals that you were the only one who saw this "ghost." To uncover the truth, you head to the simulator cockpit where Aemeath disappeared years ago.
MAIN_YHX_20_1: I knew it! There had to have been undiscovered debris in this area!
MAIN_YHX_20_2: It must've been sealed in the ice wall all this time.
MAIN_YHX_20_4: Oh, I'm good! Perks of being a ghost, y'know.
MAIN_YHX_20_5: Ah! I'm so sorry... It's my fault for putting everyone in danger.
MAIN_YHX_20_6: The collapse was an accident. We're all okay, so don't blame yourself.
MAIN_YHX_20_7: But the way we came in is completely blocked.
MAIN_YHX_20_8: Scaling that ice wall… It's too high, too risky. I'd rather not have a student on that climb.
MAIN_YHX_20_9: I've contacted the Academy. They're sending a rescue team. Once Nivora's safely returned, we'll set out again.
MAIN_YHX_20_11: Hey, little guy here says our next stop is deep in the ice. There's a path at the bottom of the station. Wanna check it out?
MAIN_YHX_20_12: What about waiting inside the station? It's freezing out here, and another collapse is possible. It's safer to wait for the rescue team indoors.
MAIN_YHX_20_13: I-I agree! I want to see what's inside too...
MAIN_YHX_20_14: With {PlayerName} on the team, a quick recon should be manageable. Up to you.
MAIN_YHX_20_15: Hey, question. Before you came to Lahai-Roi, did you do this kind of thing a lot?
MAIN_YHX_20_17: Like traveling with a crew, seeing the sights, stumbling into trouble, then going your separate ways.
MAIN_YHX_20_18: Like a classic road trip movie, you know?
MAIN_YHX_20_21: Nice. I happen to love those.
MAIN_YHX_20_22: Oh, so more big-budget action? I can see that. Solaris is crazy.
MAIN_YHX_20_23: Looks like this time I get a co-starring role. Amazing. Let's keep going, study buddy.
MAIN_YHX_20_24:
Passing through fractured ice sheets, you come before a colossal, half-frozen wreck of a fallen space station.
To avoid another collapse and investigate a deeper path Aemeath mentioned, the party decides to enter the space station.
MAIN_YHX_21_1: It's kinda sad though, having to pick through fallen debris to advance our own tech.
MAIN_YHX_21_2: It just shows... how much we truly lost in the Lament.
MAIN_YHX_22_1: Compared to other debris fields, this station is in much better shape.
MAIN_YHX_3_2: (Soliskin? What could they be doing here?)
MAIN_YHX_4_1: (That Soliskin... It's headed straight for the Synchrolink Training Grounds.)
MAIN_YHX_43_4: Everything here has already been contaminated, including... that.

MAIN_YHX_48_39:
The video records the final moments before the SkyArk Space Station crash. The Etheric Sea expands to engulf Solaris, and a figure with a face identical to yours appears in the sky as Retroact Rain fills the air. Seeing this, a profound and inexplicable anger fills Aemeath's eyes.
Due to Nivora's injury, Luuk stays behind to wait for the Academy's retrieval team. He candidly admits to having been friends with your past self, destroys the video, and advises you to keep all information about your identity confidential.
MAIN_YHX_6_1: Aaaand... nope! Still on the fritz. How are you feeling?
MAIN_YHX_6_2: I'm… okay. After that mech flew off, I felt less of my frequency bleeding out.
MAIN_YHX_6_3: (That mech's frequency felt like the presence from the rift back in Honami City.)
MAIN_YHX_6_4: Aemeath, that mech only left after it saw you. After you clashed with it.
MAIN_YHX_6_5: That's twice you've saved me. Each time I'm left with more questions than answers. They say you're the Exostrider's Synchronist who's been missing for over ten years.
MAIN_YHX_6_6: Me? I'm not the Exostrider's Synchronist now.
MAIN_YHX_6_8: I just... died first. Call me a digital ghost!
MAIN_YHX_6_9: Ten plus years back, the underground seal broke. The Threnodian on the other side of the Stridergate was about to swallow Lahai-Roi.
MAIN_YHX_6_10: I was still a student. My sync with the Exostrider hadn't hit a hundred percent yet.
MAIN_YHX_6_11: But there was no other choice. The Exostrider was still sleeping, so I had to do something... unorthodox.
MAIN_YHX_6_12: So you Overclocked yourself to try to resonate with it?
MAIN_YHX_6_13: Yup. Impressive, right? I woke the big guy up, if only for a second.
MAIN_YHX_6_14: The seal held. The crisis averted. Everyone I cared about... they made it out okay.
MAIN_YHX_6_15: But it was too much for me. My body couldn't take it and got totally torn apart.
MAIN_YHX_6_16: So yeah. I died. But I'm still here... just, floatin' around. I've been a little invisible. Well, a lot invisible. To everyone until you.
MAIN_YHX_6_17: Why am I the only one who can see you?
MAIN_YHX_6_19: You can see me now... because of this little guy.
MAIN_YHX_6_20: The Exostrider's Reactor Core. My existence is kinda tethered to it now. Think of it as my heart.
MAIN_YHX_6_21: Even as a digital ghost, I never stopped trying to pull my "self" back together. To get back to reality.
MAIN_YHX_6_22: There's something I gotta do. And I gotta be the Exostrider's true Resonator to see it through.
MAIN_YHX_6_23: But our Resonance started with an Overclock. The power I got was unstable from the get-go.
MAIN_YHX_6_24: I've spent years building it back up with this Core. The Soliskin have been my little helpers, too.
MAIN_YHX_6_25: Then, not long ago, you ended up with it. That became your backstage pass to seeing me.
MAIN_YHX_6_26: "Not long ago." You mean when the Reactor Drive fell?
MAIN_YHX_6_27: Then it was you. You're the one who saved Mornye when she was dying.
MAIN_YHX_6_28: You and that junior of yours were always close. We even crossed paths a few times back when I was still... well, around. Of course I'd help.
MAIN_YHX_6_29: Oh, and by the way? When you charged in to save Professor Mornye you looked pretty cool!
MAIN_YHX_6_32: Alright, no more teasing. But I mean it. No matter what, you always choose to save.
MAIN_YHX_6_33: And to me... that's the coolest thing in the world. The most beautiful.
MAIN_YHX_6_34: Anyway! Back to business. The Reactor Core is tied to Sigillum—that's the mech that attacked you.
MAIN_YHX_6_35: It's like those Voidworms you fought. Made mostly of Exostrider parts, but corrupted. Contaminated by Threnodian Voidmatter.
MAIN_YHX_6_36: Sigillum... stole a chunk of my power. That threw a wrench in my whole "reassembling myself" project. Now it's after the Core, too.
MAIN_YHX_6_37: Since Sigillum holds this piece of the Exostrider's power, it can't be killed completely as long as the Exostrider and I exist. Now, it can only be me who stops it.
MAIN_YHX_6_38: And since just touching the thing makes your frequency drain, taking it down should plug your leak, too.
MAIN_YHX_6_39: Plus, I get my power back. Win-win.
MAIN_YHX_6_40: So will you help? You've got the Core, and the Reactor Drive is wrecked. I can't do this alone.
MAIN_YHX_6_43: I can tell you're leaving a few things out, Aemeath.
MAIN_YHX_6_44: Still, you helped me and a lot of people in Lahai-Roi. That's enough for me to trust you. What do you need me to do?
MAIN_YHX_6_47: "Existence" is the imprint life leaves behind. Being remembered, talked about, and seen...
MAIN_YHX_6_48: All the places I went when I was alive bear those imprints. The Core's running lets me find and record those frequencies.
MAIN_YHX_6_49: These little cuties have been my scouts, and they'll be our guides now, too.
MAIN_YHX_6_50: Pretty easy, huh? All you gotta do is carry the Core and follow our lead.
MAIN_YHX_6_52: Alrighty! Thanks in advance, study buddy.
MAIN_YHX_6_58: Bingo! Since then, the Core has become energy stored inside you. This is the first time I managed to make it solid. Took me a bit to figure out the trick.
MAIN_YHX_6_59: But see what it's doing to me? Even with you holding the Core, I keep flickering in and out. One second I can touch you, the next I'm fading right through. So annoying—
MAIN_YHX_6_60: Also, I've noticed... when the Core is in your hand, it runs faster.
MAIN_YHX_6_62: (A junior of mine? So I really did know Mornye in the past...)
MAIN_YHX_6_63:
Aemeath saves you from a sudden attack by the mysterious mech, Sigillum. You learn Aemeath is the Exostrider's Resonator. She died years ago, Overclocking her Resonance with the Exostrider to stop the Threnodian from breaking through the Stridergate seal. Her sacrifice left her a digital ghost. You can only see her because you hold the Reactor Core.
To stop Sigillum taking your frequency and to help Aemeath piece her "self" back together—her physical form as the Exostrider's complete Resonator—you agree to work together.
MAIN_YHX_7_1: Before we go, I need to contact Mornye.
MAIN_YHX_7_2: The Reactor Drive was Lahai-Roi's "sun." If I'm using the Core, the Academy will want to know.
MAIN_YHX_7_4: The Soliskin went down the lift. Let's follow.
MAIN_YHX_8_3: I see. So the Reactor Drive's Core survived the crash?
