PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1001: Ludens has volunteered to promote Peaks of Prestige, aiming to introduce the game to a wider audience.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1002: Agrippa the Ironheart, Septimont's renowned blacksmith, now accepts your challenge as a Lord of Prestige.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1004: I shall dedicate all my victories to Liliania!
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1005: I am Liliania the Splendent. Do come and enjoy my performance!
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1009: Marcia the Lifespring's healing treatments have returned countless Gladiators back into the arena.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1010: A Gladiator from House Grandino, willing to betray his partners to prove his worth.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1011: The manager of House Grandino, a shrewd man always preaching "Total Cost and Efficiency Management," making him the most hated figure among Gladiators.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1012: The Domino of House Grandino. He knows absolutely nothing about duels or the Peaks of Prestige, except, of course, that it's a very profitable venture.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1013: Raul the Dustbound once swore to fight for glory, just like the other Gladiators. What, then, twisted his ideals?
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1014: A man with strange behavior, seemingly obsessed with finding something.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1015: A hot-tempered woman who appears to be troubled by something.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1016: A quiet, reserved old man. Perhaps only one thing can unlock the heart he keeps sealed.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1017:
Gallus the Nightmare may be a genius, yet even geniuses have problems they can't solve.

Gallus's Tactics: Increase Base HP to 45. Gallus draws 2 additional cards during the deployment stage each round.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1018: An elated Duelist whose joyous expression seems fueled by the thrill of the duel itself.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1019: An arrogant Duelist who has never faced a worthy opponent and is convinced of his own invincibility.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1020: A contemplative Duelist who is constantly troubled by conflicting thoughts.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1021:
Furius the Firebrand, the Conqueror of Prestige and the creator of this game, is the ultimate challenge that Duelists must face before reaching the pinnacle of glory.

Furius's Tactics: Increase Base HP to 50. Draw 8 cards of his choice and gain 6 extra Energy at the start of the first round.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1022: The Captian always wins, because fortune always smiles on him!
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1023: For Ciaccona, Peaks of Prestige could also be a kind of musical instrument.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1024: Glory isn't only won in the arena, and Lupa knows this well. That's why she'll fight until the very last moment.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1025: Calcharo, head of the Ghost Hounds, hereby challenges you to a duel.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1026: Challenge other Duelists and prove your unmatched power!
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1027:
Challenge elite Duelists and prove your unmatched strength!

Elite Duelist's Tactics: Increase Base HP to 45. At the start of the Deployment Stage, Elite Duelist draws one more card. Elite Duelist's Echoes have their STR and CON increased by 2 in this duel.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1028: Danvers's deep enthusiasm for Peaks of Prestige has inspired many retired Gladiators to give the game a try.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1029: Fulvia's got too much work on her plate and barely any time left for duels.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1030: Furius is busy handling all sorts of investors, but he can never resist a good duel.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1031: Raul has lost his ticket to freedom and is once again bound by the chains of reality.
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1032: Your attention, everyone! This star is ready to dazzle again!
PhantomBattleChallengeDes_1033: No more bitter pills for me… I've got to win this time!

FavorRoleInfo_1409_Info: Cartethyia, the wandering knight who travels across <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>. Formerly known as the Blessed Maiden, the vessel of Divinity, and the Queen of Gale and Tide, she went by the name Fleurdelys. Now, she is simply a free and unfettered wandering knight.
FavorRoleInfo_1409_TalentDoc: [Resonance Evaluation Report RA-X006] Time of Awakening unknown. It is speculated that due to the opposing influences exerted by Sentinel Imperator and Threnodian Leviathan, Cartethyia's Spectrum Performance data exceeds standard values by ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇. Calculation of accurate data using existing methods is impossible. Analysis of test samples has revealed a non-convergent Rabelle's Curve with a pronounced periodic waveform. Therefore, Cartethyia is classified as a Congenital Resonator. System has classified Cartethyia as a unique subject. Her file has been sealed under a special project group. Access clearance: ▇▇▇ System will conduct continuous monitoring of Cartethyia.
FavorRoleInfo_1409_TalentCertification: Cartethyia's waveform graph shows elliptical fluctuations with a stable Time Domain. Peak values between upper and lower bounds show intermittent upward trends, with peak values not yet exceeding critical threshold. No abnormal fluctuations have been observed. External and internal forces within Cartethyia have nearly reached a state of fusion. Resonant Criticality: High. Stability is high with minimal risk of Overclocking. However, it is worth noting that Cartethyia's body shows unstable power fluctuations when distant from Rinascita. Cartethyia is a rare individual who has undergone a Second Awakening, enabling her to transition freely between two forms. It must be emphasized that this is not a case of Overclocking, but rather the precise invocation of her powers. Note from a Bloom Bearer: When Miss Cartethyia... No, wait, Fleurdelys, demonstrated her powers, the storm nearly tore the entire simulation apart! My, oh, my. We gotta take extra precautions with our next test!
FavorStory_140905_Title: The Wandering Knight Marches To Freedom
FavorStory_140901_Content:
A retired dramatist enjoys telling a certain story: Once upon a time, in the countryside of Egla Town, there was a wandering knight. With sword in hand, he journeyed far and wide in search of a legendary giant. A giant who stood as tall as a windmill, with arms long and slender like its blades. Time after time, the wandering knight fought with everything he had against the giant, but the giant never spoke a word, only ever waving its arms, rendering the knight's attacks futile.

Some mocked the knight's foolishness, some pitied his delusion. After all, that so-called giant was nothing more than a windmill, and his battles were but a fantasy. But the countryside's most mischievous girl saw it differently.

She found herself a knight's helmet and begged the dramatist for a small wooden sword. "To fight for such a giant," she said, "he must possess a heart of pure nobility." And so, she too wished to be like the knight, to seek out the giant who destroyed homes and scattered livestock, and see that the Golden Thiefbats lurking along roads could no longer steal a single treasure from travelers.

Riding flamboyantly on a Tumbleyak, she raced through the wheat fields. The world had never felt so vast. This was where the Blessed Maiden's legends began. Through the fields, through the festivities, and into the Inverted Tower.

It would be a grand quest.
FavorStory_140902_Content:
This quest continued for some time.

In those unnoticed moments, the girl visited every field in Whisperwind Haven. Mischievous and free-spirited by nature, she even stole sips of sacramental wine under the watch of guards, danced away on high platforms, and turned a solemn ceremony into complete madness. Even the Order's prison walls became her personal canvas.

"She's really the most rambunctious girl in the countryside," people would say. "A serious fate isn't one she's meant for, and no wall, no matter how strong, could ever keep her from spreading her wings."

Yet to everyone's surprise, she was chosen by the Divinity.

Why her? Some questioned. She was only the daughter of an official, a peasant girl lacking discipline! Not a drop of noble blood ran in her veins. How would she ever come to understand the hierarchies of the world?

"She is the one!" others exclaimed. "She listens to our sorrows and replaces them with joy! If anyone is worthy of Divinity's crown, it is her."

But what would the one bearing the name Fleurdelys think of all this? Before the ceremony to receive her holy name, in a dull and stuffy hall, she performed her final dance as Cartethyia.

Was she confused by Divinity's whispers? Fearful of an uncertain future? Confident that she could wield the sacred sword?

She simply kept the name "Cartethyia" hidden deep within her heart. Farewell, grain fields swaying in the breeze, and the Tumbleyaks roaming so free. In a world so vast, someone must take up the sword. Someone must bind themselves in thorns. Someone must accept the weight of responsibilities. Someone—

Must become Fleurdelys, the guardian of <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>.
FavorStory_140903_Content:
As Fleurdelys, she must march to war with a sword in hand.

For this, she learned everything she could. She studied Order scriptures and honed her combat skills. She listened to the voices of the people, devoting herself to fulfilling their wishes. When someone prayed for good health, she arranged for the delivery of valuable medicines. When someone sought peace, she would listen to their confessions, taking in their past sorrows. When a <te href=850081>Tacet Discord</te> Outbreak occurred, she drew her sword and crushed it in its infancy. These actions were no different from what she had done back home.

The only difference was that she was no longer facing a small village or familiar faces. Most of those seeking her help were strangers, and she understood that each of them was like a small lamp. The more she helped, the more they would shine in the night sky of <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>.

Yet, the world was so vast, and the Order was far from flawless, as the books had claimed. The nobility were fixated only on their own interests, and self-proclaimed devout Acolytes merely performed their faith, turning a blind eye to the people's cries. She saw nobles who boasted of their good hearts while stuffing their pockets, refusing to hear the pleas of those suffering.

At times like these, all she could do was tighten her grip on her sword.

She experienced doubt, disturbance, and disappointment. And because of this, her grip only tightened as she faced the Dark Tide—She would question the Divinity. She must.

No matter the answer that awaited her, Fleurdelys was ready for it.

With this resolve, she walked into the tower. Alone.
FavorStory_140904_Content:
She seemed to have dreamed for a very long time.

In that dream, hymns and praises poured toward her in endless waves, engulfing her. She raised her sword to cut through the waves again and again, battling the giant sea creature in those waters. She fought with all her might. Even when the waters turned into blades sharp enough to slice flesh, she did not take a single step back.

When she opened her eyes, she found herself alone in an unfamiliar place.

Where was she? What was her purpose? Who was she? Questions whose answers had slipped beyond memory.

She wandered the tower in search of what was lost. She even tried to find a way into the central tower to seek answers. But after exploring every corner she could reach, she found nothing but herself. There was no "other" existence. She was the only soul there.

So she began to converse with herself. She stitched dolls from scraps. She invented stories.

Curiously, the fog of her memories began to lift, little by little, beneath her fingertips.

She made one doll of a sword-wielding girl and another of a sea monster. She muttered a few lines of dialogue between them, then paused. She knew this story. She'd heard it before. The <ano=wandering knight>sword-wielding girl</ano> had journeyed to confront the terrifying <ano=sea monster>giant</ano> of legend. Time and time again, she fought it with everything she had. 

No matter what the <ano=wandering knight>sword-wielding girl</ano> was fighting for, she understood one thing—

Each time she raised her sword, she did not care about her past. She only cared about what needed to be done at that very moment.

And if that were true, then losing her memories was no great loss. In a world so vast, she would find herself again.

And when that time comes, whether she turns out to be the warrior or the monster, it's an answer she would be willing to accept.
FavorStory_140905_Content:
Inside a small restaurant in Whisperwind Haven, a young girl orders several Laurus Salads. While waiting for her food, she quietly sneaks into the kitchen, following the head chef and carefully observing her culinary techniques.

"Hmm. A few more of these Viscum Berries, please. Ah, yes, yes. And another!"

"You can add more honey as well... Yes, thank you!"

"And where did you come from, little rascal? If you're waiting for your food, you need to wait outside." The head chef puts down her utensils and looks up, pausing in astonishment. The girl before her seems familiar, but she can't quite place a name.

"I-I'm so sorry! I just wanted to pick up some of your cooking skills. I have a long journey ahead of me, and I might not have the fortune to come across a restaurant serving such delicious food again. If my apology isn't enough, I'll chop some firewood for you instead."

"Is this your first time eating at our restaurant? I have a feeling I've seen you before." The head chef hands the curious girl her food. 

"Was it from that stained glass window...?"

"This isn't my first time, actually! But it's been quite a while since I last visited," the girl replies, taking the plate. "Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cartethyia. I'm a wandering knight preparing for a new quest. If you ever need help, do let me know."

"I just had to try this before I begin my journey!" The girl scoops up a spoonful of salad and takes a bite.

In a world so vast, a salad full of Viscum Berries made the beginning of her journey feel just right.

"How delicious." She praises from her heart.
FavorWord_140901_Content: Here, this is for you. Be careful, it's just been baked and is still hot. But trust me, it tastes best when you tear into it right away. This little trick is just for you, since we're good friends. Coming back home feels different, even though my house has been empty for so long. But the bread from that bakery still tastes the same. The last time I had it was when I won the <te href=850103>Laurel</te> as the Blessed Maiden. Back then, the town was covered in posters of me dancing at the <te href=850102>Carnevale</te>. That dance... would you like to see it?
FavorWord_140902_Content: ...Back in the tower, I felt uneasy just hearing you mention it... but actually hearing a play about my life was utterly surreal. If you hadn't stopped me, I'd have jumped out of my seat and run away! When I was younger, I used to daydream about being the heroine in one of those adventure stories. But now that it's actually happening, it's nothing like I imagined. The poets of <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> have added so many embellishments. FavorWord_140903_Content: We meet again, Righteous One. Heh... So, how was I? Was I helpful? I'm no longer the lost, confused girl I once was. Now, I stand ready to fight alongside you. This is the promise I made, and to honor it, I will sharpen this sword even further. Though it may never come to pass, if fate wills it... I will defeat you as I vowed... and set you right.
FavorWord_140904_Content: After merging Fleurdelys, I finally understood why I hesitated when "I" first saw you as I danced on the water's surface. When you first arrived in <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>, "I" could feel your presence. A strange joy surged through "me." Deep within the tower, "I" wondered… what would the one who could both destroy and liberate "me" look like? Would you be a righteous knight, as in the legends, slaying "me" with your sword? I couldn't choose how I was born, but I could choose how I would die. And that, in itself, is a kind of happiness. You gave "me" that chance, "Godkiller." And the ending of this story is more beautiful than I ever imagined.
FavorWord_140905_Content: The turmoil in <te href=850096>Rinascita</te> is far from over. Born of mankind's ill will, Leviathan may yet rise from the raging currents of civilization's soul... I cannot stray too far from this land. Everyone has their limits, often bound by responsibility, and true freedom remains elusive. You and I are no exceptions. But the sword you wield was forged from our shared frequencies. It is a mark of our bond and a manifestation of my power. As long as you carry it, I will be your sword and faithful companion... ever present in the depths of your gaze.
FavorWord_140906_Content: I love seeing people smile! That’s why I adore the <te href=850102>Carnevale</te> and any lively occasion. The cheerful crowds, the joy in the air, the laughter filling every corner... I just love being part of it. Whenever that happens, I want to blend into the crowd, singing, dancing, and spinning hand in hand with everyone...
FavorWord_140907_Content: ...Whenever I transform into Fleurdelys for battle, I have to constantly remind myself—My manners, my tone... everything has to be composed and solemn... Ah! It's actually really hard, you know? Truly!
FavorWord_140908_Content: My favorite dish is Laurus Salad, of course. It's not only delicious, it's also healthy. I'd gladly eat it for three meals straight. Hm? Oh, I wouldn't get tired of it, not at all! The sweet Viscum Berries coated in dressing have the perfect crunch and flavor. It's easy to prepare, and even I can make the dish taste just right.
FavorWord_140909_Content: I'm not really fond of fish. I don't know why, but every time I try to eat it, I just can't, even my fingertips seem to resist. When I was little, my parents used to say I was picky. Living by the sea, there aren't many food choices, especially if you don't like fish. But I've never been able to get over this instinctive aversion.
FavorWord_140910_Content: My current dream? I want to be a wandering knight, just like the ones in the stories passed down in Egla Town. A knight of righteousness, always ready to draw my sword in the face of injustice, then riding off in the most heroic way! Before the Order chose me to be the Blessed Maiden, that was my deepest wish. But now... that title no longer belongs to me, and it never will again. I must step away from the adoring gazes and become a nameless guardian. To that end, I've been revisiting the survival skills I once learned during my days roaming the hills. Oh, do you think you could help me come up with a new knight's name?
FavorWord_140911_Content: Haultir is my sword and my very first companion. In the stories passed down in Egla Town, every true knight always has a sword they hold dear, so when I got mine, I was overwhelmed with joy. Though I've wielded many swords since, Haultir remains the most precious. Every time I grip the hilt, I can feel… that my heart hasn't changed. Even if it was a heart born from lies, I know that, when given the choice, I will always choose "to save."
FavorWord_140912_Content: I was born from the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>'s curse and malice. It made me wear the crown, bathe in the glory of the Blessed Maiden, surrounded by the reverence of countless faithfuls. I fought against Its false faith, day after day, until I was finally overwhelmed by the tides... In that long slumber, those familiar prayers no longer felt warm, but cold and sorrowful. At one point, I thought I'd never want to hear them again. But after you saved me from the tower, I secretly visited <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> City… Oh, then I knew, I've never resented the prayers of those longing for happiness. And to ensure these pure voices aren't twisted, there's still much I need to do, and can do.
FavorWord_140913_Content: I… took away the brilliant future she was meant to have. The future of being the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s true Blessed Maiden. All the goodwill and hopes placed upon me, and the power I now possess… all of it should have belonged to Cantarella. Yet, she never seemed bothered by it. Someone as mature as her must have already found her own path within the <te href=850094>Fisalia</te> family. But still, I'll always remember that I owe her so much… so much.
FavorWord_140914_Content: That girl has a kind and gentle heart. Duties aside, she always does her best to be there for others. Honestly, when it comes to knowledge of the Order's doctrines, I'm nowhere near as good as Phoebe. It's because of so many true and faithful believers like her, I find it difficult to reveal the truth to the people of <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>. People turn to faith for many reasons, not just out of devotion to the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. To unveil such unsettling truths would bring forth countless difficult choices and challenges...
FavorWord_140915_Content: As the daughter of <te href=850101>Montelli</te>, she has really brought fresh ideas to the city. If this island were to stay isolated, the air would grow stifling. The people of <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> need new ships, new horizons, and new discoveries. I'm not very skilled in business matters, though. My nanny in the Order always said I didn't even know how to haggle... If I ever get the chance, I'd love to learn a few tricks from Miss Carlotta!
FavorWord_140916_Content: When I was a child, I used to beg the bards passing through town to sing me stories of knights. After I was freed from the tower, I wandered through a field one day, and the wind carried a piece of beautiful music to me. I stood beneath a tree in the distance, listening as Ciaccona sang a new poem, one with the melody of Egla Town's folk songs… In the blink of an eye, noon had already given way to dusk.
FavorWord_140917_Content: The nature of the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>'s power to converge often makes me appear dangerous and unsettling after battle, but Lupa has never once recoiled. She never treats me as more or less than I am, and she has never distanced herself. She is honest, tenacious, and unwavering in her care of her friends. Even though I'm shorter than her when not in my Fleurdelys form, I still feel that I should take on the role of the "older sister" in our friendship.
FavorWord_140918_Content: Happy Birthday, {PlayerName}! You're probably wondering why I brought you here. Just look at the clouds, the soaring birds, the Inverted Tower, and the golden glow of the morning sun... As long as you hold my hand, I can guide you to float above the sea like this. It's fascinating, isn't it? Later, when the sun sinks into the ocean, the view will be even more mesmerizing. I used to stare at this every day from the tower, and I grew weary of it. But now, everything feels different, all because of you. I'm not the true Maiden. I don't have the power to grant blessings, but I still want to offer you my best wishes. May your heart's deepest desire come true.
FavorWord_140919_Content: Today's story is... the great battle between a righteous knight and the wicked <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>! The victor is—Cartethyia the Knight!
FavorWord_140921_Content: Time for a little nap... It's... It's just a dream...
FavorWord_140922_Content: Cartethyia, now a wandering knight. The <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>'s malicious creation, the Order's unsuspecting <te href=850103>Laureate</te>, the defier lost in the tides of fate... These titles, once portrayed in poems and books, have long since slipped from my grasp. As for what lies ahead... let’s explore it together,  "Swordbearer."
FavorWord_140923_Content: The crown of winds... has been engulfed by the sea. Tell me, are you the one who summoned this blade?

FavorWord_140927_Content: My swordsmanship has reached new heights!
FavorWord_140928_Content: Can you feel it? The frequency of the wind... it's resonating between us.
FavorWord_140929_Content: During my studies at the seminary, I knew that to uphold justice, I would need to work harder and sacrifice more than others to overcome the shadows that sought to destroy it.
FavorWord_140930_Content: The power within me once terrified me. I wondered how monstrous I'd become if it consumed me... But such terrors have started to fade, with you by my side.
FavorWord_140931_Content: The currents of fate pull everything into their depths. At times, as I drift in its grasp, I sometimes feel resistance. FavorGoods_140901_Content:
A small wooden stage prop sword. Even the quiet countryside of Egla Town wasn't untouched by <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>'s popular stage plays. Spinning windmills and brilliant knightly legends shaped Cartethyia's childhood. This wooden sword was a gift from a retired dramatist. Each day after her lessons, she would patrol the village with bright eyes and high spirits, brandishing it as she dealt with every "injustice" she encountered.

This should have been the start of her journey to becoming a wandering knight.

Fate is full of what should have been, but it never unfolds as we imagine.
FavorGoods_140902_Content:
A small golden <te href=850103>Laurel</te>.

When the golden crown was placed upon her head, the Divinity's whispers reached her ears for the first time.
From that moment on, she was no longer Cartethyia. She would become <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>'s Blessed Maiden, the "Fleurdelys" spoken of by all.

Fate can be too kind at first, only to become a rain that never stops falling.
FavorGoods_140903_Content:
Hand puppets locked in a scuffle.

She had searched the tower for what felt like forever, yet found no trace of another soul. So she made puppets, staging play after play, just to keep from forgetting how to speak, and to fill the silence of being alone.

She missed the plays she had seen in the world of the living, missed the wheat fields of the countryside, missed sweet drinks and the sounds of people laughing.

Fate can fill us with nostalgia, even as it sends us onward alone.
FavorGoods_120701_Content:
Ever since Lupa's parents severed ties with her, their faces began to blur from her memory.

What lingers is the way they used to reminisce about their days on Capitoline Hill, far from the small village she called home. They had once borne the name Silva, until they were cast out, shamed by defeat in the arena. From then on, their lives were marked by regret, hardship, and finger-pointing. 

And yet, when they heard Lupa had won her first match, they still went to the blacksmith and had this medal forged, a gift to commemorate her victory.
FavorGoods_120702_Content:
This was one of many bouquets Lupa received in the arena. Bloodleaf Viburnum, the flower of Gladiators, a mark of victory and glory.

The first time she stepped into Colosseum Olymdos, she fought like a creature unleashed. Relentless. Instinctive. Wolf-like. The crowd gathered and roared. Applause crashed over her like waves, the lights above sharp and dizzying. 

Only when she returned to the waiting room, the bouquet still in hand, did she hear herself laughing out loud.
FavorGoods_120703_Content:
The people of Septimont have a deep love for sculptures. They immortalize many things with that art. Gryphons, heroes, legends... and of course, the ever-lovable <te href=850082>Echoes</te>.

Lupa's favorite? Ta-da. Just one glance at those cheerful, chubby little things is enough to make her day. That's why she chose a pair of Ta-da figurines as a gift for her fellow warrior.

Captured mid-flap with their oversized ears and fearless charm, they look ready to charge into the arena, just like Lupa and {PlayerName} once did. That journey they shared remains one of her brightest memories.
FavorStory_120701_Content:
Scorching. That was Lupa's earliest memory of the small village where she was born.

Summers stretched on endlessly, the heat so intense that even the lake seemed to boil. But the children of Septimont hardly cared. Far away, in the city atop Capitoline Hill, the Great Agon was about to begin. The village had rarely produced a Gladiator skilled enough to enter the match, but the excitement still pulsed through the air. Even the children couldn't resist picking up weapons and staging their mock battles in celebration.

Lupa was called home halfway through one of those kids' Agons.

Stepping through the door, she was greeted by the same old conversation. Her parents asked if she would be willing to move to Capitoline Hill. She said yes. They asked if she would be willing to become a Gladiator since she showed signs of being a Resonator. And again, she said yes. These questions had been repeated many times, and her answers stayed the same. Yet each time, her parents seemed relieved, as if they feared she might someday refuse, even though she never had.

Then the usual arguments began. Should they try to mend ties with the House of Silva, who had once turned their backs on them in their darkest hour? Or should they start over somewhere new? Whenever they spoke of that glittering city on the hill, and the House they once served, their voices would take on a tone—one caught between yearning for acceptance and fearing for rejection, just like when they spoke to Lupa about her future.

Lupa sat for a while, listening. When it became clear her parents had drifted into their own quarrels again, forgetting she was even there, she quietly got up, stepped outside, and made her way back to her arena. The stifling heat inside her body seemed to cling, heavy and wet, growing larger as it loomed over her. It burned in her veins, a restless, humid anger that only grew hotter. It drove her forward, made her run faster, strike harder, and lunge at her opponent with everything she had.

And it was then that she heard the gasps from the crowd.

Lupa looked down and saw flames spilling from her limbs, fierce and untamed, curling to engulf her whole.
FavorStory_120702_Content:
Later, Lupa followed her parents to the City of Septimont.

White stone walls, the crisp chime of windbells, and sculptures of heroes at every turn—the city was a dazzling spectacle. But what captivated Lupa most was the most common sight in the city, the Gladiators. Their weapons, their <te href=850082>Echoes</te>, the way their eyes lit up as they talked about the teams and scores... They all sent a spark through her veins. That little flame in her heart roared to life, urging her to dash straight to Colosseum Olymdos and throw herself into the thrill of battle.

But that didn't happen. Instead, her parents led her to the Silva estate, where many other young hopefuls like her stood waiting.

Match after grueling match, Lupa fought. Until at last, teeth gritted and spear clutched tight, she stepped over her fallen rivals into the Silva's grand hall.

That was when Domina Julia singled her out from the crowd.

Lupa stepped forward and found herself pinned by the Domina's sharp gaze. Those clear green eyes were like deep, fathomless wells, weighing her worth as a potential asset. Instinct made her glance back, but her parents were already gone, their figures swallowed by the shadows.

They had likely received a reward generous enough to drown any guilt over abandoning their own child.

However, Lupa didn't linger in sorrow. The packed schedules and the endless social obligations allowed no room for grief. Soon enough, Domina Julia thrust her debut match into the spotlight. And her voice, whatever it might have been, was lost beneath the thunder of the roaring crowd, swallowed by silence.
FavorStory_120703_Content:
By the time Lupa returned to the training room, the teammate she had partnered with for the past few months was already gone.

She stood there for a moment, dazed, before moving forward through the unlit room. Her Forte had gifted her with many things: fire, a sharpened sense of smell, and the ability to see in the dark. Without hesitation, Lupa made her way to a chair and sat down, settling quietly into the darkness.

"Well," she thought, "the Domina or manager will send someone new soon."

This farce was finally over.

They had found the mole, the one leaking the team secrets, the source of the rumors. Julia wasn't one for mercy. Therefore, that former teammate who sold them out would likely be barred from setting foot on any arena of Capitoline Hill for a very long time.

Over the years, as Lupa's fame grew, her teammates had come and gone. Some couldn't keep up with the way she fought. Others were dismissed simply because Julia didn't like them. A few, like her former teammate, had come with ill intent from the very start. And then there were those who... simply couldn't stand how the crowd's cheers always found her, leaving them forgotten in her shadow.

Lupa had tried to say something about it, but she quickly learned that even the act of "trying to say something" could cut like blades.

Maybe it was because she had never truly been in their shoes. After all, she had never tasted failure. Or maybe it was that unspoken "You'll never know what it feels like," and the fact that, when the dust settled, she was always the one who came out ahead.

Eventually, Lupa learned to stay silent.

After sitting there a while longer, she got up and walked over to the cabinet where the match recordings were kept. From the shelves, she pulled out one particular recording she had watched many times before. Perhaps it was a kind of self-consolation, clinging to the idea that even those without talent could still find joy in the arena, even though the Gladiator in that recording didn't last long and disappeared from the arena all too suddenly.

The light from Breen the Screen cast flickering shadows across Lupa's face, leaving deep, hollowed patches of darkness behind.
FavorStory_120704_Content:
The Nameless staggered forward, passing a silent Giant of Glory.

Her legs were leaden, her memories fraying at the edges. Even piecing together a complete thought was becoming a struggle. Sometimes, when Cartethyia spoke to her, she had to pause for a long while before she could muster a reply.

This brief journey was likely nearing its end.

Septimont, her city, the city of splendor, now drenched in the Dark Tide… The Nameless no longer knew if it could still be saved. Maybe the investigation they were clinging to was already doomed to fail. Cartethyia didn't think so, but the Nameless could no longer hold on. That nauseating sensation of the cold sea creeping up from within her was growing through her bones and blood, slowly turning her into something else.

The good news was that she could feel her existence weakening. Perhaps she could simply fade away before she was completely possessed by the Dark Tide. At least then she'd spare Cartethyia that final burden.

When working alongside others, the Nameless was rarely the one being looked after. Now, this helplessness gnawed at her for the first time. Cartethyia had to slow down because of her. Shame burned inside the Nameless, but there was nothing she could do except hope—yes, hope that the Righteous One Cartethyia had trusted would arrive soon.

"Wish I could still be of use to my new friend here."

Gritting her teeth, she braced herself against her weapon and forced another step forward.

"Wish I could still do more..."

The Nameless lifted her head. Above her, a hero who had once claimed glory in the history of Septimont stood tall, spear in hand, gazing down. The stone-carved face seemed to hold a silent compassion, shielding her from the dark rain falling from the sky, offering a wordless shelter to those who came after.
FavorStory_120705_Content:
After the "story" ended, Lupa kept her promise. She whisked {PlayerName} and Cartethyia on a carefree whirlwind tour through Septimont.

Only the three of them would ever know the truth, but it truly was a winding, thrilling journey worthy of being told in an epic poem.

But as everything was settled and the tension finally eased, a faint, nagging worry began to stir again in Lupa's heart, a worry for {PlayerName}, her best teammate ever.

She had seen {PlayerName}'s strength firsthand. Saving Septimont would have been impossible without {PlayerName}'s help. But it was precisely because {PlayerName} had once again won so naturally that Lupa felt a new kind of unease. She was no stranger to victory, and she knew better than most the double-edged nature of constant triumph. After the winning streak, a true defeat—not just a minor stumble, but a real fall—could sometimes destroy a person.

True, {PlayerName} was formidable. Lupa couldn't imagine what kind of fate could bring {Male=him;Female=her} down. But if that day ever came...

Yet she had no words for that. All she could do was silently talk herself into believing that she would always be there, ready to offer help. Somehow, Lupa could feel that {PlayerName} was destined for something greater, something too vast to reach or change for her. Yes, some things were big, and others were little. Saving a city was a great thing. Winning a match, a small one...

...Or maybe not.

She never told {PlayerName}, but while saving the city had been a grand achievement, the short journey they had walked together had gifted her just as much. Even though for {PlayerName}, it had likely been no more than another easy victory, for Lupa, it meant a lot. When they won the semi-finals and leaned against each other for a brief moment in the waiting room, she was filled with a happiness she had never known before. It was exactly because {PlayerName} treated it as another effortless routine that hardly warranted a second thought, Lupa was able to savor that pure, unclouded joy of competition once again.

In that moment, the wild, restless flame that had always howled within her finally, at long last, fell silent.
FavorWord_120701_Content: Ugh… I didn't expect the paparazzi to be on us during our stroll. A-actually, no, they weren't just after me, they wanted your picture too, Warrior. After all, you're a champion and the talk of the town now! But I bet you're not too keen on ending up in those gossip rags. Don't worry, I'll handle it tomorrow. Our good times are for us, and us alone!
FavorWord_120702_Content: Sparring with you always takes me back to my childhood. Back then, we'd fight with cardboard "weapons." No crowd, no cheers, no glory, just pure fun. Whether we won or lost, we'd always laugh and hug it out. Warrior… can I get a hug now, too?
FavorWord_120703_Content: You wish to try? Sure, go ahead! Here, take this comb, my assistant bought it. They say you need a whole collection for a tail like mine. Mmm… wow, you're really good at this! Even I can't run a comb through it like that... Why am I suddenly so sleepy...
FavorWord_120704_Content: Being apart, going solo... I remember feeling a little uneasy. Cartethyia had passed the hope to you, and you entrusted it to me. It was a fight I had to win. I wasn't afraid of failure, but I knew that someone who couldn't face failure with dignity would never truly know victory. And... I was the "protagonist" you chose, wasn't I? I couldn't let you down.
FavorWord_120705_Content: I have received many honors, but the championship medal I won with you is the one I cherish the most. I love this city, the land it rests on, its sights, and its people. It is a place of glory and pride, of filth and despair, but I love it all. I don't suppose you can stay in Septimont forever, this is just a small part of your journey. But for me, it will burn like fire. No matter what darkness comes next, this memory will always light my way.
FavorWord_120706_Content: I love going to the Septimont baths after a training session. The warm water does wonders for easing weariness. You should give it a try.
FavorWord_120707_Content: Every winter, my tail becomes a hive of static... Very annoying when I'm grooming...
FavorWord_120708_Content: A Saltimbocca made with fresh meat. I'm a Septimont traditionalist by palate, so a pinch of hot sauce is okay, but no weird sour cream. Don't be like the <te href=850097>Ragunnesi</te>!
FavorWord_120709_Content: The "vittles." Oh, it means food cooked exclusively by <te href=850082>Echoes</te> sans human input. All "vittles" taste very bland... Do Septimont Echoes hate seasoning?
FavorWord_120710_Content: I just want to enjoy the thrill of competition, win or lose. I can hear my heart pounding when I strike, weapon in hand, my cheeks burning as the crowd cheers... It's simple. Pure. No need for extra pomp or returns. The hard work, the strategy, the sacrifice... It's all worth it to feel that joy! Sticking with this for life won't be easy, but would I have to quit? Not a chance.
FavorWord_120711_Content: This spear? It was a gift from Domina Julia... Yeah, the same weapon I carried into my very first match in Septimont. Back then, I was just a child with "some natural talent." She spotted me in the crowd and brought me into the limelight. So, in the following years, I turned a blind eye to the outrageous contract terms, willfully ignoring the fact that she sought to use me for her own gain. I used to believe her pride would hold her back, that it would stop her from crossing the line...
FavorWord_120712_Content: It's now all a blur to me... the memory of being trapped in that empty city... Walls crawling with Tidal Blight, monsters prowling the streets. Everyone had vanished without a trace. It was the lowest I'd ever seen Septimont. I couldn't bear to see such hellish sights. But I told myself, "I can still hold on." I had to keep going... keep searching for a way to save this city, no matter how many times it took.
FavorWord_120713_Content: In that empty city, Cartethyia was there for me during my most delirious and painful moments. At first, our conversations were a bit stiff. Guess she hadn't spoken to anyone in who knows how long. But as we spent more time together, I realized that she was actually easygoing and carefree. For someone like her, being trapped in one place for so long must've been unbearable... Now that our long journey is over, I hope my friend can fully enjoy this moment of peace.
FavorWord_120714_Content: Whenever I watch videos of the Ephor's past fights, I do wonder if she stepped into the arena for political reasons, or-or to prove herself. Whatever her reason, Augusta's rise to power was a good thing for Septimont. Change is always toughest at the beginning. And for that, I have respect for her.
FavorWord_120715_Content: I rarely visit the Temple to pray for revelations, so I can't say I know the Priestesses well. But I do like Iuno. Many of the nobles can't stand her unconventional ways, but I find her boldness entertaining. Don't you?
FavorWord_120716_Content: A spirited, nimble girl... That's my impression of her. Once, I saw her sprint along the narrow bricks at the top of the high wall and leap onto a statue like a cat. No clue who was chasing her, but I cheered loudly along with everyone else at the foot of the wall!
FavorWord_120717_Content: Many Gladiators of the Blue Furies come from the <te href=850108>Troupe of Fools</te>. I remember once, at Cliffside Harbor, I saw their captain leap off the deck just to hug his crew. They chattered on for a while, and then suddenly broke into song...!
FavorWord_120718_Content: When I first saw the footage of Contender Mya, I was merely impressed by her raw, unfiltered determination. At the time, my team had some problems, and my teammates accused me of not understanding what it felt like to be left behind. Normally, I'd brush it off, but the sounds of sorrow grew louder and started to weigh on me. Strength, weakness, winning, losing... I began to question if I had only made it through by luck. But Mya has shown me the answer with her whole life. Victory is about giving everything you've got.
FavorWord_120719_Content: Happy birthday, Fellow Warrior! Hahaha, did I scare you? How could I ever forget your special day? I've already set up a party at the Leonidas Hotel—whenever you return to Septimont, I'll be there waiting. Now, look out the window! These fireworks are for you. We Septimontians know how to put on a show, thanks to all the contests and celebrations we throw. Okay, let's kick things off with a cup of wheat juice! No? Seriously? Alright, fine. Then close your eyes and make a wish.
FavorWord_120721_Content: In my previous match, I slipped and left an opening, but my opponent failed to notice. He gradually lost his advantage... and here, he started to panic, until... I knocked him down with a single blow!
FavorWord_120723_Content: Lupa, Gladiator of Septimont. Just ignore the attention, Warrior. This victory is ours to savor!
FavorWord_120724_Content: Oh, is a new match calling?
FavorWord_120729_Content: Awesome! I'll record our training and savor every detail of it.
FavorWord_120730_Content: Do I look overexcited? Because in truth, I am. All I want is to keep sparring with you.
FavorWord_120731_Content: More... Get me more... One more round, Warrior! I want a rematch!
FavorWord_120732_Content: As we advance from one battle to the next, do you ever feel tired? I want to become stronger, wiser, and better. I want to be someone who's got your back, to be your... most trusted Fellow Warrior.
FavorWord_120763_Content: Does the Vale of Glory await me?

StoryReview_Miya_1_Content:
Mya heard those voices.

They incessantly reminded her of her failures, her lowly origin, and the disappointment she brought to her fans... The people who once shouted her name from the stands, laughing in celebration at her victories. That coarse, unrestrained laughter had at one time felt warm, giving her strength in the early days when she first stepped into the arena. But now, everything had changed.

Mya covers her ears, yet the voices still thunder in her mind, refusing to fade.
The finals were about to begin. In the empty locker room, she sits alone as shivers wrack her body and screams tear through her throat.
StoryReview_Miya_1_Abstract: Mya is haunted by maddening voices that whisper constantly.
StoryReview_Miya_2_Content:
Mya crouches in a quiet alley, trembling as panic surges through her.

She had won the semi-final, yet the voices in her head never ceased. Struggling to hold herself together, she had fled the arena.

A light touch on her arm makes her look up. A small Septimontian stands, holding out a bouquet. Face flushed, the child stammers, "You fought well!" before running off.

The Bloodleaf Viburnum is dotted with broken dewdrops. Mya clutches the bouquet, cold and damp, as a trickle of moisture slides down her cheeks.
StoryReview_Miya_2_Abstract: A small Septimontian hands Mya a bouquet of Bloodleaf Viburnum.
StoryReview_Miya_3_Content:
The sword that had accompanied Mya in countless battles pierces her chest.

The pain and blood loss overwhelm her. Her grip on the sword falters, and she stumbles to the edge of the cliff in the Vale of Glory.

She glances back at Septimont, the place that had given her both joy and suffering. It had won her heart and broken it in equal measure. The ancient city stood ablaze beneath the fiery sunset, its reflection in Mya's eyes as vivid as when she first crossed the sea with her family and set foot on this land.

How beautiful...

That was her last thought as she fell into the sea.
StoryReview_Miya_3_Abstract: Mya sacrifices her life and plunges into the sea.
StoryReview_Lupa_APart_4_Content:
That dark sea rolled over Septimont's jagged cliffs, surging down, down the pristine cobblestone streets, drenching the golden flags and wind chimes, and engulfing men and women, young and old. Like a mist descending from the blackened ocean above.

It dragged its writhing mass across the land, toward the far side of the sea on its pilgrimage across the world.

Lupa is swallowed by the tide's relentless churn. The Hymn swells from her chest, crawling forth to escape from her parted lips. An esoteric melody fills the boundless darkness.
StoryReview_Lupa_APart_4_Abstract: Lupa is swallowed by the tide's relentless churn.
StoryReview_Katixiya_0_Title: From the Depths of the Sea
StoryReview_Katixiya_0_Content:
Cartethyia steps in front of the incubator.

The salty hint of seawater drifts in the thin, still air. She can feel the one she's been searching for lying in the incubator, curled up like a newborn.

Cartethyia raises her sword and cuts the device open without a blink.

The dark water within explodes forth. Immediately, Tidal Blight starts to crawl and proliferate. As the fluid drains, a Gladiator girl's face is revealed. She opens her eyes.
StoryReview_Katixiya_0_Abstract: Cartethyia slices through the blue incubator in the darkness, her sword aimed at the girl curled within.
StoryReview_Katixiya_1_Content:
Cartethyia chases the enemy from the incubator through the Dark Tide-ravaged streets of Septimont until she vanishes from sight.

The fallen Guardian of Septimont looms ahead, halberd raised in a battle cry. Cartethyia draws her sword, just as she did countless times in the Inverted Tower facing the Dark Tide's aberrant creatures. She defeats the Lioness of Glory, but after dealing with the Dark Tide before her, she feels a cold gaze from behind her.

Cartethyia turns to see the Gladiator girl, her face marred by Tidal Blight, her eyes hollow and empty. She stares, unblinking, like a ghost.
StoryReview_Katixiya_1_Abstract: Cartethyia defeats the Guardian Arsinosa's fallen form.
StoryReview_Katixiya_2_Content:
Cartethyia had roamed the desolate city with the Gladiator girl for days before she was "erased."

She had caught a fleeting glimpse of the massive fish's silhouette and saved the Nameless One from the Dark Tide. Cartethyia was certain this place was not part of the real world, but the widespread destruction had stalled her search for answers.

The Gladiator girl had forgotten who she was, but her survival alone marked her as extraordinary. Cartethyia hoped this very uniqueness might serve as a beacon to carry their story forward.

Cartethyia could only keep searching. She had to find the monstrous half-human, half-sea creature, the Threnodian's abomination... Its very "sister."
StoryReview_Katixiya_2_Abstract: Cartethyia travels with the Nameless One in the desolate city, searching for the abomination created by the Threnodian.
StoryReview_Katixiya_4_Title: To the Place of the Quill
StoryReview_Katixiya_4_Content:
The story was drawing to its close.

Cartethyia could feel the world around her shifting. The buildings, statues, and even the land itself were cracking like damp paper. But it no longer mattered. She had uncovered the clue that pointed to the one responsible and was heading toward the Playwright. With more Fractsidus members lurking here, she was prepared for the coming battle.

As for the rest, Cartethyia had no doubt that {PlayerName} would handle it. She was {Male=his;Female=her} sword, and she believed in {Male=him;Female=her} completely.
StoryReview_Katixiya_4_Abstract: As the story nears its close, Cartethyia sets off to hunt down the Playwright who's behind all of it.
StoryReview_Rover_APart_0_Content:
Your sword clashes with the Septimontian Gladiator's spear, steel meeting steel in clanging force. Those wild, fiery eyes look straight at you, unashamedly revealing a glimmer of admiration.
 
Lupa invites you, the outlander, to join her in the Great Agon. Drawn by the faint traces of Cartethyia frequency that you sense in her, you agree. And yet, you can tell that Lupa's cheeriness is somewhat of an act, stemming not from her nature, but from a force of habit.
StoryReview_Rover_APart_0_Abstract: You cross paths with Gladiator Lupa in Septimont.
StoryReview_Rover_APart_2_Content:
You fight a battle unseen.
 
The Colosseum, once full of glory, is swallowed by darkness. Monsters swarm from curtains of black mist as you cut them down, one against a hundred. At the final blow, the world abruptly returns to its former state, the crowd oblivious to what just occurred.
 
You recall three blades falling from the sky, each radiating with Cartethyia's frequency. Though you had not seen her, it felt as though you were fighting side by side.
 
Where is she?
StoryReview_Rover_APart_2_Abstract: You and Cartethyia fight side by side in a battle no one sees.
StoryReview_Rover_APart_3_Content:
When Lupa's form was overtaken by the girl resonating with the Threnodian, all your suspicions align. 
 
The Threnodian had set Its gaze on Septimont's Central Hub, a vessel for Imperator's lingering power. Only you, with your unique permissions, could sever the Hub's connections and thwart the Threnodian's plan.
 
You make your choice in the flash of a heartbeat.
 
You refuse to end the story by becoming the "protagonist" and murdering Lupa, as Phrolova suggested. Instead, you place your trust in your fellow warrior and stay behind, trapping the Threnodian's essence within the Hub. In the next story, the lone wolf throughout this journey will repay this trust.
StoryReview_Rover_APart_3_Abstract: In the final moments, you decide to leave Lupa with the seed of hope.
StoryReview_Lupa_BPart_3_Content:
Lupa's eyes flutter open, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The sudden explosion of memories in her mind nearly made her choke. Cartethyia, her brief companion, her fellow title-winner {PlayerName}, the chaotic shift in the Central Hub... and the countless cycles before where Septimont was swallowed by the Dark Tide. 
 
The sky above remained as clear as ever, and everything that had just happened felt like nothing more than a nightmare. 
 
Lupa opens her hand, the medal she and the Warrior had earned together resting in her palm, damp with sweat. 
 
She takes a deep breath, then another, before closing her fingers around it. The sharp edge digs into her skin, and the pain pulls her back to reality. It urges her to push forward.
StoryReview_Lupa_BPart_3_Abstract: Lupa regains her lost memories and moves forward, guided by the trust you placed in her.
StoryReview_Lupa_BPart_4_Content:
Blood ignited, body and soul aflame in the crucible of battle. Lupa's spear plunges into the monstrous half-human, half-sea creature, her fight unfolding on a stage conjured by illusion. Her mind is calm as the world fades away. Only the enemy, her weapon, and herself remain.
 
The Gladiator's Agon, interrupted decades ago by the Threnodian's corruption, finally reaches its conclusion.
 
At this moment, Lupa is no longer weighed down by questions of strength, weakness, Sentinel, or Threnodian. Only a single, pure thought remains: To be a Gladiator is a thing of joy!
StoryReview_Lupa_BPart_4_Abstract: Lupa defeats the Lady of the Sea. After a relentless battle, Mya's Reverberation is finally freed from its curse.
StoryReview_Rover_BPart_0_Content:
As you walk out of the Central Hub, a familiar connection pulsates within your Tacet Mark. You turn around and see Cartethyia slowly gliding down from the sky and landing before you.

After days of separation, you're finally reunited. She looks into your eyes, cracks a smile, and gestures in a different direction.

Together, you walk to welcome the lone wolf returned from the flames. Lupa embraces both of you tightly, and you feel her tremble as worry gives way to delight at seeing both of you. Her words choke as tears fall... You pat her gently on the head to soothe her. 

This is a story co-written by you, Cartethyia, and Lupa. Now, it's coming to an end.
StoryReview_Rover_BPart_0_Abstract: The three of you reunite. Together, you are the true playwrights of the story.
StoryReview_Rover_BPart_2_Content:
The world is collapsing. Pages curl as fiction slips away from reality.
 
Phrolova stands silently upon the still waters, bending to retrieve an unfamiliar object from the depths.
 
It is a gem.
 
Originally from Ragunna, this gem passed through many hands before reaching Septimont, brought here by a young girl. To avoid drawing attention to the faith the jewelry symbolized, she had the gem removed, melting down the gold to forge it into a Gladiator's helmet.
 
The gem's natural cerulean hue has been tainted a deep purple and bears the mark of Tidal Blight. Deep within the crystal's depths, the silhouettes of fish drift slowly.
StoryReview_Rover_BPart_2_Abstract: Before the scripts burn and fade into oblivion, Phrolova takes the gem from Mya's helmet.

AreaReportContent_Text51:
A helpful introductory pamphlet to Septimont, included with your Gladiator match tickets.

Dear friends from afar, may applause greet you!
Thank you for supporting our Gladiators. We sincerely invite you to attend the Great Agon at Colosseum Olymdos, Septimont’s grandest arena.
The Great Agon, the largest and most prestigious of Septimont's Agons, is held once every four years, spanning multiple rounds to determine the mightiest warrior of the era.
Top-ranking gladiators will win generous rewards, and the championship team will be awarded a prestigious title of noble recognition by none other than the esteemed Ephor of Septimont.
If the thrill of the arena calls to you, why not personally join the battle? The gates of the Great Agon are always open to brave challengers ready to carve their names into history.
AreaReportContent_Text52:
If you're a first-time visitor to Septimont, we highly recommend beginning your adventure at the Thermes Baths, a cultural gem unique to this glorious city.
Here, bathing isn't just for relaxation, it's a vital part of life. You’ll hear legends of heroes, gossip from the streets, and if you're lucky, you might even meet the Gladiators you’ve been cheering for and hear tales of past battles straight from their mouths!
After a good soak, what better way to unwind than with a drink? Make your way to Caracalla Market, where two local favorites await: Solis Tavern and Passa Inn & Restaurant. Certain tickets entitle you to exclusive discounts at these spots, so don't miss out!
Happy hunting, travelers! May your time in Septimont be filled with unforgettable moments.

PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_1: Agrippa the Ironheart's Medal of Prestige. It was forged by Agrippa himself while Putini studied his every move.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_2: Liliania the Splendent's Medal of Prestige. Liliania treasures every glance from her fans, and she works hard to never let them down.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_3: Marcia the Lifespring's Medal of Prestige. Gladiators often complain about her bitter potions, yet they still call her the "Lifespring" with admiration.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_4: Raul the Dustbound's Medal of Prestige. Raul once stood in the arena, fighting with all his heart for glory.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_5: Gallus the Nightmare's Medal of Prestige. But enough of that, care for a round of Peaks of Prestige?
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_6: Furius the Firebrand's Medal of Prestige. Peaks of Prestige brought him risk, fatigue, and burden, but in the end, passion won out.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_7: A Medal of Prestige for novices. Every duelist starts here, even the most gifted.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_8: A Medal of Prestige for trainees. Practice is always part of the path to victory.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_9: A Medal of Prestige for adepts. It marks a player who is now recognized as a professional duelist.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_10: A Medal of Prestige for veterans. Duelists hone their tactics and minds through countless battles, like sharpening a spear on stone.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_11: A Medal of Prestige for victors. Few are blessed with victory again and again, and you are one of them.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_12: A Medal of Prestige for conquerors. You've bested the strongest, and now no one can wrest glory from your grasp.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_13: Brant's Medal of Prestige. To him, Peaks of Prestige is just another uncharted sea. No big deal.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_14: Lupa's Medal of Prestige. It may not be the arena, and no one's dying today, but she'll still give it her all.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_15: Ciaccona's Medal of Prestige. A true epic is never without glory and legend. Now, she's a part of that very legend.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_16: Calcharo's Medal of Prestige. The fate of the Hounds is nothing but destruction and fear, but he is still searching for a way to break free.
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_17: An unknown Medal of Prestige. It looks like... a Chop Chop? But what's that behind it?
PhantomBattleBadgeBgDes_18: An unknown Medal of Prestige. Let's say the name out loud—

Farm_ForoloVideo1: At least for this moment, it's a shared performance.
Farm_ForoloVideo2: Can this improvisation bring about a new chapter in the song of life?
Farm_ForoloVideo3: The rift between worlds shall reveal itself within dreams.
Farm_ForoloVideo4: The prelude has sounded. What kind of finale will this paradise reach this time?
Farm_ForoloVideo5: A great performance needs not two conductors. I will yield for now and allow you to command.
Farm_ForoloVideo6: "Fate grants us sweet slumber. To where shall the traveler of this prolonged dream wander?"
Farm_ForoloVideo7: Perhaps I should rejoice how a chaotic dream such as this can still be woven into harmony.
Farm_ForoloVideo8: This is the future you chose, the fate upon which "they" in paradise depend.
Farm_ForoloVideo9: The illusion of paradise will fade... But these miracles, these revelations will echo forever.
Farm_ForoloVideo10: So... this is where paradise meets its end. Shall we surrender, or begin anew?
Farm_ForoloVideo11: Unexpected noise mingles with the melody. How shall we address it?

PhantomProject_TotalDes:
[Echo Management]
You can create multiple management plans for Echoes based on COST, Sonata Effects, and Mainstats.
When a new Echo is obtained, it will automatically be locked or marked for discard according to the enabled plans.
Echo Management Plans do not affect already upgraded Echoes.
When a plan is enabled, newly obtained Echoes will stack with your owned Echoes of the same name and take on the highest-priority tag among them, following this order: Locked > Discarded > Unmarked.

[Presets, Sharing & Importing]
You can import recommended management plans via the Suggested Plans feature, or import other Rovers' configurations via the Sharing & Importing feature.
After importing, all local plans will be overwritten and enabled.
When importing a shared plan via a code, if the imported plan is not up to date, please wait for a while and try again.
