FavorRoleInfo_1412_Info:
Sigrika, a student of Startorch Academy and a Resonator of Royan Runes.
Determined to live up to others' expectations and become a true Solsworn, she devotes herself fully to every challenge.
FavorRoleInfo_1412_TalentDoc: [Filed by Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy Student Records] [Forte Examination Report: RA2326-G] Student Name: Sigrika Synchronist Qualification: Negative Forte Overview: Tests reveal a Rabelle's Curve with a pronounced periodic waveform. Therefore, the student is classified as a Congenital Resonator. Her Tacet Mark is located on her back. According to the pre-admission personal file and the student's own account, the student demonstrates exceptional aptitude in deciphering rune frequencies and converting them into usable power. However, she reports that this ability remains unstable and is highly dependent on her mental state as well as her depth of knowledge regarding particular runes. "In the field of rune deciphering, Sigrika displays a rare talent, one that may pose a significant risk to herself if not treated carefully."
FavorRoleInfo_1412_TalentCertification: Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows high-amplitude, non-periodic fluctuation patterns. Partial waveform blurring is observed, along with visible abnormal waveforms. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is within normal range. However, subject stability is poor, with a potential risk of Overclocking. Currently, Resonator Sigrika has no history of Overclocking, and her Rabelle's Curve remains stable. Routine psychological counseling is required. "Sigrika is too hard on herself. Honestly, if she just eased up a little, her Resonator stability would improve dramatically." "...Students like her are not uncommon at Startorch Academy. They come in thinking their talent means something. Then they realize that here, it just gives them an edge in a few courses. Nothing more." "Still, I don't want our students to feel defined by grades, talent, or ability. They deserve to see how much more the world has to offer."
FavorGoods_141201_Content:
A diary dear to Sigrika, filled with the traces of her life and thoughts.
In <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>, it held her joy and discoveries. At <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>, it holds her doubts and sorrow.
Life stretches far beyond the pages of a diary. Growth, too, never happens overnight.
FavorGoods_141202_Content:
A bird journal Sigrika keeps, though most entries are just blurry silhouettes. The sketches and notes brim with the collector's unfiltered excitement.
"Stay still! Don't flash me your tail, Blubbin Puffin! Stay there! Stop moving! Ugh, your tail AGAIN?! Please stay still! Ugh, again?! Blubbin Puffin!"
"New species discovered! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird!"
FavorGoods_141203_Content:
A pouch sewn by Sigrika's mother, filled with candies, hairpins, and little trinkets whose purposes are anyone's guess.
When Sigrika left home, her mother pulled her into a warm embrace. It left Sigrika with encouragement, love, and the gentlest of tethers.
FavorStory_141201_Content:
"I'm back..."

The moment Sigrika closed the door, a round Kronapuff that could've been a ball launched itself into her arms, sending her stumbling back two steps.

"Hey, Crackle! Did you have fun at home?" she laughed, steadying herself. "You look bigger again. Have you been eating too much? Alright, alright, let go of me! Where's Mother? Wait, don't tell me. My nose already knows."

She dashed into the kitchen. The fatigue of the journey melted away the instant she spotted the pot of rich, bubbling Smoked Meat Stew.

"You're back?" her mother glanced over. "Look at you, filthy from head to toe. Off chasing birds with your friends again, were you? In a few days, you will receive the <te href=700010>Reactor Drive</te>'s blessing. After that, you'll be considered a grown-up. A Solsworn can't be seen running around like that."
"No, no! I was helping Aunt Astrid with her herd. That doesn't count as running around."

Her mother reached out and pinched her cheek. Sigrika winced and scrunched up her face. It only made her mother's smile soften.

"Alright, alright. Go wash your hands. We'll eat once your father gets home."
"Okay!"

Sigrika grinned. She washed her hands carefully, then took the plates and utensils from the cupboard and laid them out neatly on the table.
When her father returned, their small home welcomed a dinner that wasn't lavish, but was warm enough to fill the room.
At the table, Sigrika counted the little gifts her father had brought back—flower crowns, hairpins, clear bits of glass, and a few small blocks whose purpose she couldn't quite guess. As she tucked them away, her mother sighed and began to complain about his buying strange trinkets again. Her father scratched his head, fumbled for an explanation, then, catching Sigrika's eye, seized his chance to change the subject.

"So, feeling confident about the coming Trial?"
"Of course," Sigrika answered without hesitation.

She liked this. Being with her family. Even when her parents nagged and rambled, she never felt annoyed. She knew, deep down, that all of it came from love and their high expectations for her.

Her parents wanted her to become an outstanding <te href=700025>Solsworn</te>. They hoped she would use her talent to help others, and more than that, they hoped she would grow into an outstanding person. Sigrika knew how to live up to those expectations. That was why she studied runes every day. Learned something new every day. Even when exhaustion crept into her bones.

Still, as the Trial drew closer, she couldn't help but feel nervous.

"It's alright," her parents said. "Our little Sigrika will pass with flying colors. After that, you'll be heading to <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>. That place has trials of its own waiting for you."
"Mhm!" Sigrika nodded, pushing her anxiety out the front door along with the dust of the road. For now, she would just enjoy dinner. After all, the stew really smelled good.
"Oh, right, Mother," she added suddenly. "Has Crackle put on weight? I could barely pick it up."
"Ask your father."
"Papa?"
"Haha… I might have... fed it a bit more than a little."
FavorStory_141202_Content:
The rune unfolded before her eyes, like a sun rising into the sky.

Few people knew that runes were never meant to be flat symbols, but something with great depth—just like what she was witnessing now. This small sun rose and unfurled, spilling its light freely and generously onto everything around it.

Sigrika watched in silence. If she were asked to explain what was happening, she would just say that runes carry meaning. She was only interpreting that meaning and allowing it to manifest in the world.

"Only?" she thought to herself.

People called it her gift. As if she had been born able to read the True Names of runes, born able to draw on the power sealed inside them. And so, of course, she could apply this gift elsewhere, like calculating the paths of the stars, fulfilling everything a <te href=700025>Solsworn</te> was expected to do.
 
But... that was all it was. A gift.

A gift meant that this was the one place where she could give her all and nowhere else. She could recreate the True Names of runes, but she could not truly understand their essence. Why did runes hold such immense energy? What were those fleeting visions she sometimes glimpsed when touching them? And when she deciphered runes, what were those syllables hinting at, the ones she heard but could never understand? 

She didn't know.

Standing here now, waiting to be marked with the "blessing of the <te href=700010>Reactor Drive</te>," she held a quiet hope: that once the blessing was imprinted onto her, once she crossed this threshold into adulthood, understanding would come naturally to her. But of course, it didn't.

The rune merely unfolded before her eyes. Nothing more. Even if it shone like a sun.

This was what being "gifted" meant. It meant that it ended here and only here. Anything beyond that, she would have to seek out herself. See it for herself. Think it through on her own.

Even now, when she had no answers at all.

Even if this <ano=Rune>gift</ano> felt like a <ano=True Name>shadow</ano> cast upon her by some <ano=civilization>greater entity</ano>.
FavorStory_141203_Content:
The frostlands.

Sigrika exhaled softly, a plume of white drifting into the air as she watched the herderless <te href=700022>Exoswarm</te> roaming in the distance.

She had been trailing them all night.

It had taken her hours to pull the Exoswarm out of their extreme agitation. Now, they wandered the frostlands in loose, aimless loops, but Sigrika knew this was not a good sign. Something in their command and navigation units had malfunctioned, leaving them to trace one pointless circle after another. And sooner or later, without warning, they would spiral back into a frenzied rampage. When that happened, the nearest Royan settlement would be the first to suffer.

It was a riddle. And she didn't have much time left to solve it. But that was fine. She was ready.

"These True Names… Illuminate."

The next instant, runes flared to life across the Exoswarm, then detonated. The aimless circling stopped. And in its place came rage. The Exoswarm recalibrated as one, locked onto Sigrika, and charged. 

Their thunderous steps shattered the silence of the frostlands. The ground trembled beneath them. Sigrika tightened her grip on her dagger and began tracing runes in the air.

Calm. Focus. These were the absolute requirements when drawing and deciphering runes. Stroke by stroke, the runes formed before her. And all the while, the Exoswarm bore down, their fury heating the very air, melting the snow beneath their pounding steps.

Three... They carved deep, stretching grooves across the ice. Runes flickered on their bodies, but did nothing to slow them down. Driven by the single command to charge, they only accelerated, faster and faster—

Two... Sigrika tapped the final point with her blade. She vanished. At almost the same instant, every rune on the Exoswarm ignited, and Sigrika slipped between them, shuttling through their ranks on the paths her runes had carved.

One! The rune trap activated. Chain explosions erupted. Wind blades tore through the Exoswarm, cutting off their advance. And at the center of it all, Sigrika's dagger found its mark—the key to the riddle. When the shockwaves finally faded, she landed lightly, pulled forward by a <te href=700026>Soliskin</te>. Behind her, the Exoswarm herd that had raged all night finally fell silent, and the last rune clenched in her fingers scattered into specks of starlight.

"That was… close."

If not for Soliskin steadying her, she would have collapsed right there. Her hands were still trembling. Her heart hammered against her ribs. She knew why. The most important rune had never lit up. It hadn't responded to her deciphering. It hadn't worked at all. If the pre-set traps hadn't triggered exactly as calculated… If the wind blades had been even the slightest bit weaker…

In that moment, she understood her limits. And she understood that the gift she relied on was far from omnipotent. There would be times when runes could not be deciphered. Her gift, too, had boundaries.

And this—only this—was what she had to rely on. She had to read the runes correctly. Because if she made even a single mistake, everything would turn out differently.

No one said those words to her. So now, she said them to herself.
FavorStory_141204_Content:
She stood still.

Students streamed past her, some eagerly debating club activities, some rushing to class, others grumbling about the weight of their coursework. They flowed past her into the Academy in an endless current, a stream that didn't seem to run dry.

And there she stood among them. A stake driven in place, struggling just to hold her ground.

This was the new life waiting for her.
 
Sigrika jolted awake. It took her a moment to realize she wasn't home anymore. She was a freshman at <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>.

What awaited her wasn't just runes. New courses. New knowledge. New people. A buffet of novelty lay spread before her. But the light of it all cast shadows. Heavy ones.

She still hadn't found her footing here. Just yesterday, working as a teaching assistant for the first time, she had been asked to explain Royan customs to her classmates. Halfway through, a strange confusion and pressure had washed over her, something she had never felt before. Two days ago, she hadn't even known how to make TARD-E stop its incessant singing. And before that…

She had stood at the Academy gate, watching people pass by, unable to decide which way to go.

All of it was new. Vast. Overwhelming. Unlike runes, these things weren't built from points and lines. They offered her no familiar handholds.

Sigrika threw off the covers and sprang out of bed. She washed up quickly, then gathered her things: the notes she had organized yesterday, her Bionics assignment, the preview materials for Ecology and Communications, and...

Moments later, arms full of books, she hurried out the door and merged into the stream.

She would bite into these shadows. She would find their shape, their structure. And she would wrest the knowledge from inside.
FavorStory_141205_Content:
Sigrika stood at the front door of her childhood home, her hand resting on the handle. She didn't open it for a long time.

Ah... It was still hard. Hard to say everything out loud, to admit how tired she was, how unhappy. Even facing her own family, she found it difficult.

Or maybe... it was because they were her family that made it so hard.

After all, she didn't want them to worry.

"It's okay," she comforted herself. "If I can't even face my own family, how can I ever face myself?"

At last, she made up her mind and reached to turn the handle—but the door swung open on its own.

Her mother stood there, looking at her with helpless fondness. "Why didn't you come in?"

"Mother..."

"What's wrong?" her mother asked gently. "You've been out there for so long. Did something happen that you're afraid to tell me?" She smiled softly. "It's alright, we can take our time."

Sigrika stepped forward and wrapped her arms around her.
 
Something inside her crumbled all at once. Maybe it was the wall she had built, brick by brick, stone by stone, between herself and her family. Built from her pride. Her exhaustion. Her love. She had wanted so badly to be someone they could be proud of, so she never spoke of how tired she was. Never let it show. But now… she felt that she finally could.

"I've met some friends," she began. "Really good friends."

And there was so much more she wanted to tell them.
FavorWord_141201_Content: Hey, are you free next weekend? Want to come with me to <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>? I know a secret spot there with lots of Dusk Honeypots!
FavorWord_141202_Content: These <te href=700026>Soliskin</te> are my friends. I know one day they'll eventually return to the Solistrees, turning into tiny sparks. It's sad when friends leave, of course. But they told me that this is their choice.
FavorWord_141203_Content: I've been studying these runes since I was very little. To me, they're never flat in my palm. They have depth. A piece of history, or a coordinate... like the grooves etched into Ashen Ironwood to mark the past. When I decipher them, I see projections of civilizations not yet known. What I see feels so vast that it makes me wonder. When I'm deciphering them... are they, in their own way, deciphering me?
FavorWord_141204_Content: After what happened, I called Mother and told her everything. About the riddles we solved together, how I'd been scared I wasn't good enough, and the times I almost gave up. And how every time, you were there to comfort me, telling me it was okay, even if I failed. Maybe that's how I managed to overcome the version of me in the Dark Side. Mother... She went quiet for a long time. When I asked if she was alright, she finally said, "You've been carrying so much all this time." I... I never thought she'd say that. But then I closed my eyes and thought: That feels really, really good.
FavorWord_141205_Content: Now, I want to learn more interesting things and see places I've never been. I won't run away from what everyone hopes for me, but I also want to listen to my own heart a little more. To try things that only I can experience. You've told me about so many amazing places, like <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>, <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, Septimont... If I ever get the chance, I'd really love to visit them! And when that day comes, would you come with me?
FavorWord_141206_Content: Back home, a hug means something special. When someone leaves, we send them off with a hug full of blessings. And when they return, we welcome them with a hug full of joy. The frostlands are so cold that it feels like the air itself might freeze. In a world like that, what you need most is the kind of warmth that's light as feathers. So... would you like a hug, Senior?
FavorWord_141207_Content: If possible, I really wish we could all stay friends for a long, long time. But... I know time has a will of its own.
FavorWord_141208_Content: Every time I leave home for school, Mother packs a huge jar of Fruit Crackle for me. She makes it all herself, and it's always so sweet. She wraps the jar carefully in ice so it stays crisp until I open it. That's why the jar always feels so heavy when I carry it… It's heavy with a warmth too big to hold.
FavorWord_141209_Content: Have you ever tried Grilled Fern Spore? Don't, seriously don't! It's so bitter just thinking about it makes me grind my teeth... If I ever had to eat something that awful, I'd rather eat at the cafeteria! Not that we actually call the cafeteria food "food," right? ...Wait, you're saying the cafeteria's serving Grilled Fern Spore Jelly tomorrow? Oh no, no, no, no! Grilled Fern Spore is already a nightmare, and jelly made from it? I...
FavorWord_141210_Content: I still want to live up to everyone's expectations! But now, I won't push myself too hard, and I won't stop just because I'm afraid of failing. Because now I know... this is the path I chose. And I want to give it everything I have!
FavorWord_141211_Content: This hair accessory? It was a gift from Father. He's always trekking across the frostlands, bringing home all sorts of strange trinkets. He used to tell me that our lives shouldn't end within <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>. Well, someday, when I get the chance, I want to travel around too. Then maybe... I can bring back some interesting stories of my own, bright enough to make the little ones in the tribe smile.
FavorWord_141212_Content: When I was little, Mother would take me out to the frostlands to herd the <te href=700022>Exoswarm</te>. At night, I'd lie on their backs and look up at the stars, one by one. Mother said stars are the endpoint of a riddle. She would connect them, one to another. And just like that… everything looked different! The stars were no longer scattered pieces of gold. Each one held its own meaning. That was my first understanding of "riddles." What is a riddle? What is the solving? What is the answer? The riddle is the <ano=Rune>starry sky</ano> itself. The solving is finding the hidden connections within it. And the <ano=True Name>answer</ano>… is in the very moment you see those connections come together.
FavorWord_141213_Content: Nia always says, "If you can't finish it, just drop it. Toss away whatever's hard or sad. Running away makes everything so much easier." But whenever I'm up late studying, she's always right there beside me. Sometimes I think… maybe she's actually the one who least wants to run away. She never talks about herself, so I can't quite see what's going on in her heart. Still... I hope we can stay friends for a very, very long time.
FavorWord_141214_Content: Lynae always comes and goes like the wind. Wherever she passes, she leaves behind these dazzling colors. Those colors are her riddles, and the smile on her face? That's always the answer.
FavorWord_141215_Content: I really, really love Fleet Snowfluff's songs! But the last time she held a fan meeting, I was out on a frostlands field study... I-I hope I'll get another chance to attend! I would love to see her!
FavorWord_141216_Content: After the New Solar Celebration incident, some students said we should make a banner for Dr. Luuk. It seems that whenever someone's feeling down, he's always there, checking on them, talking with them for as long as they need. They suggested things like "<te href=851069>Startorch</te>'s Best Counselor" or "Best Doctor and Best Advisor." But if you ask me… I think I'd just write, "The One Who Always Has Candy."
FavorWord_141217_Content: President Lucilla's classes are so much fun. When she taught the history of Royan clothing, she even turned it into an impromptu styling workshop! But getting into her classes is almost impossible. Every time the course listings go up, I have to glue myself to the screen and click as fast as I can, or they'll be gone in seconds! And on the professor review forum, her page is just full of students complaining, "How can someone who teaches everything have classes that fill up in seconds?!"
FavorWord_141218_Content: Today's your birthday, right? Happy birthday, my dearest Senior! This whole box of gifts is for you! Look! A jar of Fruit Crackle, a scarf woven with rune blessings, and a fluffy Soliskin plushie… and this Sunstone I made. No matter where you are, it'll always point you toward the sun. I hope sunlight always follows you, and that every wish you make comes true!
FavorWord_141219_Content: Smile for the camera... Three, two, one...
FavorWord_141221_Content:
Hello. Mother—Mm, I'm doing well. Made a few new friends...
How are you doing? ...Yes, I know. Just promise me you're looking after yourself.
I really want to eat the Fruit Crackle you make... 
My grades? Oh, not bad! Come on, don't worry about me! Yes, yes, I will. I promise...
FavorWord_141222_Content: Hi, I'm Sigrika! Want to understand the meaning of runes? Need a hand with something? Then I'm the one to ask!
FavorWord_141223_Content: I'll keep all of this in my heart forever.
FavorWord_141226_Content: The runes will be our guide.
FavorWord_141227_Content: Now, time to mark the next starting point...
FavorWord_141228_Content: When the True Name is unveiled, the rune illuminates.
FavorWord_141229_Content: I can see more now... So that's what was troubling me all along.
FavorWord_141230_Content: From something flat to something with great depth, the meaning of the runes unfolds before my eyes. It feels infinite...
FavorWord_141231_Content: Am I... crying? I-I never imagined I would touch the True Names themselves. They're beautiful, dazzling... To come this far and see so much... Thank you, Senior.
FavorWord_141260_Content: Can I keep going like this?
FavorWord_141262_Content: Couldn't live up to... those expectations...
FavorWord_141272_Content: A reward for solving a riddle.

QuestTree_Summary_120010: The Liondance Troupe is gearing up for a new performance. Lingyang invites you out for a meal while scouting potential customers along the way. At the last stop, you learn a food stall owner has been threatened by something called the "Jingle Beast" and a gang known as "The Savages." Moved by his story and a request from the Bei siblings, you expose the gang's scheme, and in doing so, come to learn the secret Lingyang has been carrying. After the lion dance, Lingyang tells you an old legend about the "Jingle Beast"...
QuestTree_Summary_120020: A team set to compete in the Jinzhou Riverside Games suffers an accident. You came only to watch, but you invite Jiyan to join you in filling the vacant spot. At the end of the race, the Gulpuffs suddenly erupt into chaos. To find the source of the anomaly, you trace it to a Sonoro Sphere upstream. After a fierce battle, you free the reverberations of Jiyan's fallen comrades from within it...
QuestTree_Summary_120030: Several residents of Jinzhou City have gone missing recently. As you investigate, you cross paths with an organization known as the Séance Society, as well as Patroller Yinlin, who is investigating them too. Working in tandem, you and Yinlin set out to uncover the truth behind the group. In the end, you defeat its leader, the Dollmaker, and bring him to justice. Then Yinlin bids you farewell and departs on a new journey of her own.
QuestTree_Summary_120040: Changli asks to meet you at the pavilion, and to uncover the Secret of Immortality hidden within an unfinished Weiqi game, the two of you once again venture into Mt. Firmament. Through the machinations of the Fractsidus, the adventurer Wuli, trying to save his lover Fuling, is swept into a Temporal Disruption and survives only because you arrive in time. Within the Sonoro Sphere, you witness Changli's past and recover scattered fragments of your own. After the remaining Fractsidus members are captured, Wuli and Fuling decide to keep chasing distant horizons, and you and Changli play out the final moves of the Weiqi game...
QuestTree_Summary_120050: Rumor speaks of an Arcane Artist in Jinzhou whose paintings can come to life. While investigating that artist at a client's request, you meet Zhezhi, who is looking into the same matter. Together, you discover that the mysterious artist, Mingyan, already knows Zhezhi and is being forced to forge her work. Determined to bring the mastermind's crimes to light, Zhezhi confronts the Shanyun Art Exchange in open court. With your support, she wins the argument and exposes the truth...
QuestTree_Summary_120060: To find the wish-granting relics from Encore's story, you, Encore, and a young listener named Ying, who holds the treasure map, set out on an adventure together. Along the way, Ying learns that she will never see her mother again, and you discover that this story was a gift Encore's mother left for her. Wanting to give the tale a happy ending, Encore gathers everyone's signature flowers and asks Verina to create the final treasure, fulfilling both her own wish and Ying's. Then you and Encore makes a pinky promise to write new stories together in the future.
QuestTree_Summary_120070: A corrupted Stellar Matrix has escaped the Error Cell and may threaten the safety of the Black Shores. To track it down, you need Camellya's help. As the investigation unfolds, the past you shared with Camellya, or rather with "Lady Flora," slowly comes to light. After crossing countless junctures, the two of you find each other again, along with the core of the corrupted Stellar Matrix. You meet Camellya at Veiled Rock, where the many timelines overlap and become one the moment she offers you a flower.
QuestTree_Summary_220010: An invitation draws you into the dangerous undercurrents of the Montelli family. To investigate the mysterious death of one of its members, you join forces with Carlotta once more. When the truth is finally stripped bare, it points to the sender of the invitation: Carlotta's uncle, Capollo. Carlotta evades his snare and reunites with you, and together you destroy the plan he had devised with the Order of the Deep. Before parting, Carlotta gives you a Cat's Eye gem...
QuestTree_Summary_220020: To lift the spirits of the Pilgrims they rescued, Roccia decides to stage a welcome play and perform "Pegasus" with the troupe. In search of the perfect stage prop, a "star," the two of you return to the Strand, only to become trapped in a maze of fog. At its far end, you discover plushies and the "star" who are looking for their owners. You bring them back to the troupe, and the performance is a success. After the curtain falls, the plushies finally reunite with their owners, and Roccia invites you to join the troupe...
QuestTree_Summary_220030: After accidentally winning a wager, you become captain of the Troupe of Fool for a day. You and Brant set off in search of lost treasure and cross paths with the greedy pirate Aldric. At the heart of the hidden treasure, Brant sticks to the plan, taking only the sea chart before slipping away with you. Aldric, however, is consumed by his own greed and meets his end. When the adventure ends, Brant tells you the tale of the chart and the Golden Captain. You become the troupe's honorary captain, and the next adventure awaits somewhere on the horizon.
QuestTree_Summary_220040: Guided by a message carrying a strange frequency, you arrive in Egla Town and join Cantarella for the Night of Remembrance. When you retire to the Porto-Veno Castle to rest, past and present begin to overlap within its halls, leading you to the answer behind the festival's riddles: the Divine Trials held by the Fisalia family. With your help, Cantarella returns the girls she once saved during those trials, and the dreamy illusion of the night fades away in a veil of gentle smoke.
QuestTree_Summary_220050: The Black Alley and Talos, both destroyed years ago at the hands of the Blazing Nightwalker, suddenly reappear in Ragunna. You begin investigating alongside Zani. In the course of that search, you learn that Zani herself is the Blazing Nightwalker. After a hard-fought adventure, you defeat the current Talos and rescue the residents suffering under her tyranny. Zani then tells you why she became the Nightwalker: to protect the precious, fragile peace of ordinary life. That, she says, is how heroes are born.

FavorRoleInfo_1108_Info: Hailing from Ashinohara, the Miko of Flaming Sakura now remains in Lahai-Roi as the last and only member of the Special Response Force.
FavorRoleInfo_1108_TalentDoc: [Spacetrek Collective: Classified Archive] Interview Dossier: Hiyuki Due to multifaceted considerations, we have foregone a truly comprehensive evaluation of the representative from Ashinohara—the Miko of Flaming Sakura. The majority of the intelligence gathered herein is based on her personal testimony. In the recorder's professional estimation, corroborated through subsequent cross-referencing, she appears to harbor no intention of concealing any information regarding her background. "After all, information regarding the 'Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura' can be found in just about any Ashinohara elementary school textbook..." According to Hiyuki's own account, the source of her Forte is the "Suzu," a Legacy Talisman worn on her right wrist. Hiyuki describes the Suzu as follows: It grants the bearer the ability to perceive and utilize "future possibilities" of oneself, though it does not allow for direct communication with these "shadows of future possibility." The freezing power she often wields in combat also stems from the "Suzu." "Verified via official Ashinohara reports: The Legacy Talismans are five relics left behind by the Sentinels, distributed among the internal factions of Ashinohara for safekeeping." "Among them, the Suzu is described as granting its bearer the power to 'draw upon the future.'" Consequently, it is determined that the fundamental source of her exceptional combat prowess remains her own inherent skill. However, the "futures" available for her to draw upon are not infinite. Out of concern for her physiological lifespan, aggressive deployment of her abilities is strongly advised against. "Investigation confirms that every Miko of Flaming Sakura has shared a singular cause of death: vanishing from the battlefield without a trace following excessive use of the Suzu."
FavorRoleInfo_1108_TalentCertification: The subject's Rabelle's Waveform diagram exhibits an elliptical oscillation pattern with a stable Time Domain representation. No abnormal fluctuations were observed. Examination results are determined to be within normal parameters. Current Overclocking threshold is exceptionally high, and subject stability remains robust. There is no risk of Overclocking, and the subject has no prior history of Overclocking. However, a course of psychological intervention is recommended. "This miko... How should I put this..." "Ashinohara textbooks never show her face, but they're clear about one thing. She is the strongest living warrior in all of Ashinohara." "And yet, with all that combat, her readings stay perfectly stable. Something about that just doesn't sit right..." "I get your concern, but the data is clear. There's not a single irregularity." "...Then what about those shadows? Like parallel-universe versions of herself from some movie?" "Hardly. It must be the Suzu's power. Just as the Ashinohara records describe, it allows her to 'draw upon the future' to a certain extent."
FavorRoleInfo_1211_Info:
Denia, a Department of Voidmatters student at Startorch Academy. Also, a professional slacker who has mastered the art of dozing through courses.
Still, she hardly misses any campus event, always there to flash her "gentle" smile to one and all.
FavorRoleInfo_1211_TalentDoc: [Filed by Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy Student Records] [Forte Examination Report: RA2499-G] Student Name: Denia Synchronist Qualification: Negative Forte Overview:Tests reveal a Rabelle's Curve with a pronounced periodic waveform. Therefore, the student is classified as a Congenital Resonator. Her Tacet Mark is located on her chest. Based on the files from her recommender, the subject can generate bubbles infused with Remnant Energy, which can serve as a defensive or supportive measure in combat. The Remnant Energy of the bubbles can also be detonated on command when needed. Test results also reveal that the bubbles have a unique fluid structure, allowing them to block Voidmatter at a grade comparable to the Exostrider coating. "Wait, isn't that the bubble maker from those Lollo Logistics ads? My niece has that same exact toy! How in the world are you supposed to stop Voidmatter with bubbles like that?" "How did this get filed in the first place?! My goodness... Is anything in this report actually true?"
FavorRoleInfo_1211_TalentCertification: Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows elliptical fluctuations and a stable Time Domain. No abnormal fluctuations were observed. Examination results are within normal parameters. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is within normal range. Subject stability remains robust. No history and present risk of Overclocking. Rabelle's Curve stable. Psychological counseling is currently deemed unnecessary. "No history and present risk of Overclocking? Have you ever seen a Resonator that can roll Voidmatter into cubes and start flinging it at people? Hiyuki even mentioned in her combat report that her Tacet Mark started tearing!" "That's it... I'm not buying a single word from this report now. Arman, I want the complete record from the Dimmr Plains ASAP!"
FavorRoleInfo_1308_Info:
An Edgerunner like Lucy, though completely different in her M.O.
A whimsical fireball who's always ready to raze out your troubles with her shotgun.
FavorRoleInfo_1308_TalentDoc: [██ Record Modification Log] Modification Target: Rebecca Modification Code: RA2██-G The subject is identified as a Mutant-Type Resonator, with the Tacet Mark located on the right shoulder. Forte Manifestation: When utilizing firearms originating from ██, the subject can enhance the weapons' own ballistic precision and terminal effectiveness. Building upon this foundation, the subject's attacks can neutralize and disrupt the frequency surrounding specific Nightmare Tacet Discords, inflicting additional damage to targets hit. Firearm Summoning: The subject can summon three specific firearms tailored to different combat scenarios, using her Forte to materialize and dematerialize these weapons. While a weapon is being summoned, its damage output fluctuates in response to the subject's emotional state, suggesting a direct feedback loop between her Forte and the weapon's performance parameters. "The subject's frequency sample exhibits up to 97% similarity to the frequency of Nightmare Tacet Discords in the region. It is speculated that the two share a certain correlation." "███ intervened. Related research terminated."
FavorRoleInfo_1308_TalentCertification: The subject's waveform diagram exhibits elliptical oscillations with a stable Time Domain. No abnormal fluctuation tendencies were observed. Examination results are determined to be within normal parameters. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is high and subject stability remains robust. No immediate risk of Overclocking. No history of Overclocking; however, the subject exhibits emotional instability. Psychological counseling has shown minimal efficacy. "****! In Night City, I'm practically the poster child for mental health!" "This sample is way too textbook... You sure someone didn't just copy-paste it from a manual?"
FavorRoleInfo_1511_Info:
An Edgerunner from the Night City. The Netrunner of her crew.
With a heavy debt in her heart, she deliberately keeps a distance from people. Even those who are closest to her know little of her past.
FavorRoleInfo_1511_TalentDoc:
[██ Record Modification Log]

Modification Target: Lucy Kushinada
Modification Code: RA2██-G

The subject is identified as a Mutant-Type Resonator, with the Tacet Mark located on the right shoulder.

Forte Manifestation:
The subject can hack targets within a five-meter radius to achieve objectives such as information retrieval, data manipulation, or target control. Testing indicates this Forte can affect up to three targets simultaneously, with more pronounced effectiveness against mechanical constructs.

Bio-organic Hacking:
This Forte can also be used against Tacet Discords. After hacking a Tacet Discord, the subject can inflict damage or exert control by disrupting its frequency. The underlying mechanism and upper limits are currently unknown. The scope of control is speculated to be affected by the Resonator's own physical and emotional state. 

Under ███ guarantee, the Research Institute has agreed to limited ███ of the subject.

Cyberware Technology:
The subject exhibits multiple mechanical modifications grafted into her body. According to the subject's testimony, these modifications originate from ███ and are classified as cybernetic technology. Test results indicate this cyberware does not match any known existing technology, and this type of implant places significant strain on the user's body and psyche. On ██ ██, ███ intervened, canceling the research project on Night City technology.
FavorRoleInfo_1511_TalentCertification: The subject's waveform diagram exhibits spike-type fluctuations with an unstable Time Domain, indicating abnormal fluctuation tendencies. Examination results indicate moderate risk factors. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is low and subject stability is moderate. Potential risk of Overclocking. No history of Overclocking; however, based on clinical evaluation and diagnostic criteria, the subject exhibits psychological distress and stress responses. Routine psychological counseling is recommended. "Counseling recommendation has been rejected by the subject." "The subject previously used Forte to alter test results. Partial data has since been restored."
FavorRoleInfo_1109_Info: Lucilla, President of Startorch Academy and idealist with both feet on the ground. She holds quiet vigil over her students as they rise to challenge the very sky.
FavorRoleInfo_1109_TalentDoc: [Filed from: Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy Faculty Records] [Forte Examination Report RA2399-G] Name: Lucilla Forte Overview: Examination confirms the subject's Tacet Mark is located at the outer side of the right calf. Based on records from the New Federation, the subject is presumed to have awakened her Forte during a childhood birthday party after receiving a camera as a present. In addition to the memory regression ability common to memory-type Resonators, the subject possesses a unique ability to extract and materialize memories. Utilizing this ability, the subject can even "construct" previously experienced scenes and "events" to some degree within a limited time frame. However, this reconstruction exhibits extreme instability, and the Overclock incidents reported by the subject are strongly correlated with her attempts to recreate memories. In accordance with the Spacetrek Collective Information Security and Protection Act, further investigation into President Lucilla's Overclock history is hereby discontinued. Second revision: Based on reports from the New Federation and evidence submitted by Lucilla's blood relatives, President Lucilla has never undergone Overclocking. Records pertaining to her Overclock history have been deleted.
FavorRoleInfo_1109_TalentCertification: Analysis Performed: Rabelle's Curve Fluctuation Stability Test Result: Rabelle's Curve of the subject exhibits a fluctuating elliptical waveform and a stable Time Domain. No abnormal fluctuations were observed. Assessment: The subject shows no history or risk of Overclocking, and exhibits none of the long-term or short-term memory loss symptoms common to memory-type Resonators. In accordance with the Spacetrek Collective Information Security and Protection Act, Rabelle's Curve Fluctuation Stability Test on President Lucilla is hereby discontinued. Second revision: It is confirmed that President Lucilla meets New Federation requirements for the repatriation of elite and special talent advisors.
FavorGoods_130801_Content:
Rebecca's ride or die gun. Just like her, this kinetic shotgun hits like a freight train and kicks like a psycho. Every shot's a gamble, and you never know where the recoil might throw you next. 

To most, the risk of using it isn't worth the reward. But for Rebecca, this beast is what built her name in the streets. She even installed a pair of oversized cyberarms just to absorb the shock of the recoil.

"Handle it carefully, unless you're looking to paint the sidewalk with your own guts."
FavorGoods_130802_Content:
The collar that once belonged to Rebecca's dog, Cup-Cup. She became his owner after "scooping" him up in the middle of a gig. Her reason...? Just a soft heart she'd never admit to. He was a pug. Cute. Obedient—when he chose to be. During windy nights spent on the street, he'd curl up in her arms and share the heat.
 
She doesn't say it. Doesn't need to. But whenever Cup-Cup comes up, there's a look in her eyes. Sometimes she takes out his collar and runs her fingers over it. Wondering what she could have done differently.
FavorGoods_130803_Content:
Pilar's golden cyberhand, one of the few things left of his.

It didn't fit her own chrome, but selling it never crossed Rebecca's mind. Nobody ever asked if they could take it. All knew the treatment they'd get: a barrel in the face and a boot out the door.
FavorGoods_151101_Content:
A poster advertising trips to the Moon. There was a time you couldn't walk a block in Night City without seeing a travel promotion. In these ads, it was sold as an untouched paradise. Clean, free from the rot of corporate greed. A place where everyone lived equally. Without worry, without care. But the price tag was steep. The facilities were a joke. Word spread that it was just another corporate scam. And like all of them, it faded from the conversation.

Now, dreamers dismiss it as just another corporate con. But there's still one girl standing on a rooftop, looking up, hoping that one day she might escape to the Moon.
FavorGoods_151102_Content:
Braindance is the most popular form of immersive media in Night City—a technology that records and replays memories and experiences. For many, it is an escape from reality; a place to sink into illusory lives that feel better than anything the real world can offer. 

For Lucy, it is a lifeline. She has a braindance of a trip to the Moon, and it is one of her most treasured possessions. Late at night, alone in her apartment, she jacks in and lets the digital reality take her far away. She savors the tranquility, imagining a future where this dream finally comes true.
FavorGoods_151103_Content:
The Moon Tarot Card. It symbolizes fear, the subconscious, illusions, and truths waiting to be discovered. In the illustration, one wolf howls at the distant, unreachable moon. The other waits in silence, its gaze fixed on the first.
 
The card was a gift from Misty, who gave her a tarot reading. Lucy took it with her to the Moon—one of the few pieces of Night City she brought up there. It held a strong meaning to her. Almost magical.
FavorGoods_110901_Content: An action camera Lucilla used during her time in the Pioneer Association. Though her own abilities far surpass the camera's performance, she still enjoys recording through a physical lens. Particularly on lonely nights, when she silently revisits small, unguarded moments she overlooked at the time.
FavorGoods_110902_Content:
Lucilla loves to immerse herself in the lives of characters on screen. These old film rolls of classic movies were the one thing she could not bear to part with when she left the New Federation.
After becoming President of the Academy, she rarely found the time to watch movies. That changed the day she noticed one of her students had appeared on a movie poster.
Now, Lucilla cherishes these film rolls more than ever.
FavorGoods_110903_Content:
Why take time out of a busy day to put on makeup?
Once, the answer might have been to fit the image others expected of her. But now, Lucilla simply does it to please herself.
Just as she tells her students, "Never mind what others think. Become the person you imagine yourself to be."
FavorStory_130804_Title: Let's Go, All the Way To the Top of Arasaka Tower
FavorStory_130801_Content:
Unlike her brother, Rebecca never planned on becoming an edgerunner. They were both raised by the notorious merc known as Papa Sunrise—their only parent. But while he spent years hammering his legacy into both of them, Rebecca never shared Pilar's stubborn hunger to inherit their father's dream.

She wanted freedom. She wanted cute things. She wanted to find her own dream in Night City... which meant she spent a lot of time butting heads with her old man.

Life doesn't wait for anyone to make up their mind. When Papa Sunrise vanished without a trace, Rebecca and Pilar's lives took a sharp turn for the worse. They found themselves sleeping in the back of a busted-up car—once their father's loyal ride on every gig, now the only inheritance they had left.

It was Wakako, the legendary fixer and long-time associate of their father, who threw them a line—or rather, a gig. She gave them a chance to prove they were worthy of Papa's legacy. But there was still a ways to go before the siblings could truly fit edgerunner-sized shoes.

Just as Papa Sunrise had always warned, Rebecca was too emotional, too unpredictable, and far too hotheaded for Night City. She nearly tanked mission after mission; instead of following simple instructions from her fixer, she always chose to follow her gut. Pilar couldn't stand it, and the two of them would tear into each other after every job. But in the end, despite all the quarreling, she still wanted to help him achieve his dream. 

It wasn't until they fell in with Maine's crew that things finally started to turn around. Rebecca and Pilar's habit of jumping down each other's throats became the crew's daily bread—often a loud, profanity-laced background track to their lives. Others would wonder why they kept hanging out if they hated each other so much.

But deep down, they really cared about each other.
FavorStory_130802_Content:
Everyone who crossed paths with Rebecca came away with the same take: loose cannon, hair-trigger temper. David knew that better than anyone; he'd lost count of the messes he'd had to scrub clean after her. To an outsider, she was a different breed of edgerunner. She didn't care about the payout or the risk—as long as a job didn't cross her moral line, she'd take it. Slip into whatever role the gig demanded. One night, she was the innocent girl caught in the crossfire; the next, a bored punk looking for trouble at a bar. But she always preferred being the muscle. Point the gun. Pull the trigger. Sort out the details once the smoke cleared. Her recklessness drove her partners up the wall, but nobody ever really hated her for it. Not when she had their backs every step of the way.
 
In Night City, surviving as an edgerunner takes more than a steady nerve; you need an edge that sets you apart. Maine had his hand cannon. Dorio, her fists. Kiwi had her tech. David had his Sandevistan, sure, but it didn't make him a killer. He was still a rookie, rough around the edges. He needed to learn how to handle iron, and he needed to learn fast. Rebecca was the natural choice to show him the way. As the crew's self-appointed weapons expert, she knew her guns like the back of her hand. On the range, she was surgical; in the streets, a bullet-storm of terror. When David realized he needed that extra bit of lethality to survive, she didn't hesitate. She threw him headfirst into the deep end. Walked him through every drill. Tried cramming a lifetime of survival know-how into the kid before the city could eat him alive.
FavorStory_130803_Content:
Rebecca never bothered hiding it. She had feelings for David—plain and simple. But for someone who lived her life like a live grenade, she was surprisingly disciplined when it came to him. She kept a level head. She knew she'd never be the girl he pined for. No matter what gesture, angle, or trick she pulled to show him how she felt, it was obvious his heart would never be hers. But white flags were never in her playbook. If she couldn't have him, she'd pour all that energy into keeping him alive.
 
This was a task made all the harder—and more vital—after losing half her crew. One by one, familiar faces were reduced to cold names on a mausoleum wall. Even for a girl as tough as Rebecca, who had known loss all her life, it was too much to bear. She found a corner in a dead-end alley and emptied clip after clip into the dark, screaming curses like the noise could smother the grief clawing at her insides. Why had it turned out like this? Hadn't she paid enough? She didn't have a grand dream. She didn't care about becoming a legend. All she wanted—the only thing that mattered—was not to have to watch another person she loved flatline before her eyes.
 
So when David started loading up on chrome, carrying Maine's torch as if it were his alone to bear, she couldn't stop the dread from curling in her chest. A leader of a crew? Some hotshot merc with military-grade hardware? No. To her, he was still just a kid. A cocksure gonk with dreams big enough to swallow him whole. And Rebecca wasn't about to let that happen. Not without a fight. With new chrome arms built to handle heavy recoil, she stepped up as his second-in-command. Ready to be both his sword and shield. To make sure this fool she loved didn't get himself killed.
FavorStory_130804_Content:
The fear Rebecca had carried all this time finally became a reality. Even with David's freakishly high tolerance, his body couldn't keep up with the chrome he kept stacking. That, combined with the weight of the choices he had to make, sent him sliding toward the edge of cyberpsychosis. She wanted him to go easy on himself, terrified for his mental state, but David always acted fast—just like her.
 
Their last gig was highly dangerous—if not impossible. But David insisted on having his way. Rebecca was furious, but there was no turning back. Only when it was too late did she realize the truth: they'd walked into a trap. Meticulously laid. Perfectly executed. They never suspected that their own crewmate had sold them out.
 
When they learned Lucy had been captured, David went out of his way—and out of his body—to get her back. It was a suicide mission, plain and simple. The dominoes were already falling, one bad call cascading into an avalanche of disaster. There was no time to untangle the mess. No time to second-guess. Rebecca grabbed her iron, looked at that idiot who was ready to risk everything for the woman he loved, and let out a long, tired sigh.
 
"...Fine. Sign me up, choomba. Into the fire."
 
Night City would never forget that night. Their ride speeding towards Arasaka Tower, MaxTac units spraying lead at them from both sides. David burning the Sandevistan. Again. Again. Again. To carry out a plan so reckless it might as well have been a one-way ticket. Rebecca had no choice but to support him—to make sure he made it to Corpo Plaza alive. All beneath the neon glow of Night City bleeding across the skyline.
 
Despite the odds, Rebecca held onto her hope.
 
She bet it all on Lucy. One last time, she loaded her love and courage into the chamber.
FavorStory_130805_Content:
After finding herself in the Somnoire, Rebecca knew immediately that she was dead. She chose only to keep quiet about it to avoid putting that weight on Lucy.
 
"Saying it would only have twisted Lucy up even more. If she started feelin' guilty or sorry for me, that'd just piss me off."
 
On the train tearing through the dream dimension, Rebecca shrugged and fed rounds into her iron, one by one. Outside the window, stars bled past—as bright and blinding as the neon that had once painted the Night City sky. She was on her way to save someone. Same old story. She was still fighting for Lucy, someone she couldn't understand but couldn't stop admiring, either. But this time, David wasn't beside her. And the girl they were going to save wasn't running away anymore.
 
She hated admitting it, but somewhere along the ride, she'd figured out why she was really here. Even if David hadn't asked, she still would've picked up her gun and gone after that pain-in-the-ass netrunner. She was part of the crew. And the crew were the chooms Rebecca cared about the most.
 
Choose her own path, make her own decisions—it's all she ever wanted. And she's gonna keep doing exactly that. No matter the risk, she will jump into fire if needed to save her friends.
 
"A flying train, a talking kitty-cat, you and Abby... Heh, this crew of ours is scary stacked."
 
"I told you, I'm not a cat, meow... And don't forget, the goal is to recover the Dream Band..."
 
"Relax, I got it memorized! We turn that chrome-dome into scrap metal, right?"
 
"You didn't catch a word, did you..."
 
Rebecca flashed a crooked grin and scratched the white cat behind the ear, shoving her hands in her pockets as she plopped down next to you. Rover.
 
"So, uh… kinda late to say sorry for dragging you into this, huh?"
 
A fist bump. That was all it took for her to know she was forgiven. Rebecca smirked, swung Guts onto her shoulder, and strolled up to the train doors.
 
"End of the line! Let's go do what we came here to do!"
FavorStory_151101_Content:
Lucy keeps most of her past to herself for a reason. Few know that this mysterious netrunner was, in fact, shown the ropes by a top-secret Arasaka educational program for kids. One might say that's not the worst hand to be dealt; that a roof over your head and a full belly is more than many can hope for in Night City. But for Lucy, there was never any other path. She was brought up in this megacorp's black site—locked away and forced to train. Day after day, year after year, breaching the Blackwall, diving into the scattered depths of the Old Net. And trying to survive the rogue AIs that lurked there.
 
As a child, Lucy's worldview was built upon Arasaka's core pillar: obedience—often mistaken for loyalty. And she was not the only one taught to believe in it. A group of children took part in the program, either taken from their parents or scooped from the street. To serve the most powerful corporation on the planet—that was the dream Arasaka planted in their heads. Within that facility, they were forced to deep-dive the Old Net, running suicide gigs on repeat. None of them knew the perfect future they'd been promised was just a chimera. An elaborate fantasy spun by Arasaka handlers to serve the company's own ends. By the time Lucy figured out the truth, it was already too late.
 
The will to survive drove them to claw their way out of the prison they had long mistaken for home. They ran as fast as they could, bullets tearing through the air all around them. Gunfire and screams exploded in Lucy's ears, one after another. But she would survive. She squeezed her eyes shut, blocked everything out, and just kept running. The exit. She just had to reach the exit.
 
She woke up in some scrapyard with no memory of how she got there, and no idea if anyone else had made it out alive. She'd escaped the chase, for now, but the fear Arasaka had carved into her wasn't going anywhere. She knew they'd be hunting her. Could feel it under her skin. After that, she never stayed in one place for too long. Always moving. Always hiding.
FavorStory_151102_Content:
It started with a poster: a man in a spacesuit, pointing the way to a better future. For Lucy, it was a promise of escape. And maybe, just maybe, finding a place so far away from danger that she could stay put. On countless nights, curled up with her arms wrapped around her knees, that dream took root. Planted by fear. Loneliness. A need for a place to call home.

"Maybe on the Moon, I'll finally be free?"

Cynics laughed at the idea, certain there was no corner safe from corporate dominance. To go there would be pointless; a propaganda-fuelled pipe dream. But these were the opinions of people who had never been to the Moon. So what did they know? Lucy would go there. See for herself. Someday.

Night City seemed like a good place to hide for a while. A concrete jungle. When she first arrived, she feared Arasaka's reach was too prominent, but soon she learned to haunt the corners of the city where corporations turned a blind eye. She realized that crime and violence were the true governors here. And with her skill set and caution, she was natural merc material. An edgerunner already long in the making. Her new home wasn't completely safe for her, but for the first time in years, she felt like she could survive.

Erasing every trace of her past became her new identity. To stay alive without blowing her cover, the former netrunner prodigy lived by a simple code: Stay low. Ask nothing. Tell less. Avoid Arasaka. That was her disguise. A small principle, but it was hers. Life only truly changed when Kiwi came looking for a preem netrunner to fill a slot in Maine's crew. She brought Lucy into the fold and gave her the most useful advice she'd ever get:

"Remember. Never trust a soul in Night City."
FavorStory_151103_Content:
One night, Lucy took David to her place and invited him to experience a braindance of the Moon. Since she couldn't afford to travel there yet, this was the closest she could get to the real deal. Feeling the sun on her face. Jumping and floating like a feather. Serenity. Without corpos, without gangers. It was the most precious part of herself she could share.

She couldn't deny that David piqued her interest. An Arasaka Academy dropout with the reckless ambition to become an edgerunner. Wielding extremely demanding—extremely dangerous—military-grade cyberware as if it were a toy. But he was a good kid, sincere, pure at heart. Someone she felt she could possibly trust. But Lucy had spent so long keeping the world at arm's length that she didn't know how to reach out.

After David joined Maine's crew, Lucy grumbled about being saddled with babysitting duty. But despite her protests, she took him under her wing. Became his first teacher on the streets of Night City. She showed him the ropes of a merc's day-to-day, assuming he wouldn't be cut out for the life. But as she watched the boy come into his own, the knot in her chest finally started to loosen.

Her certainty about him came the day he saved her life.

A routine night turned into a bloodbath. When Pilar fell, the crew shattered into a blur of instinct and rage. Hot-headed members like Rebecca threw themselves at the killer, while Lucy took cover to strike with caution. In the chaos, David froze. Unable to move, to fight, or even save himself. But through the mayhem, he was the only one to notice Lucy being cornered. That was all the motivation he needed. In an instant, he lunged into the fray, guns blazing. To save her.

Bang.

Smoke. Silence. A turning point for both of them.

After that, Lucy led him to the rooftop—the place where she'd always gone to look at the Moon. For the first time, she didn't go alone. She brought a boy who had nothing, who promised her everything.

He told her he'd take her there. To the Moon. Someday, somehow. A promise that burned brighter and felt more real than any neon in the city below.

So how could she not love him?
FavorStory_151104_Content:
Some say that tragedy is the only truth in Night City. That happiness is just fleeting smoke.

Maine and Dorio fell on a job gone sideways. David picked up the weight. Took over the crew. Maine's legacy. The life of an edgerunner. Rebecca switched to stronger cyber-arms and swore she'd never lose anyone else. Everyone moved forward.

Everyone, except Lucy.

She stepped back. Pulled away from the crew and secretly worked to protect David from the shadows, making sure Arasaka couldn't trace him. She told no one. Especially not him. She knew David would try to stop her, or worse, follow her into the fire. That was his nature. He was obsessed with protecting her. But for once, Lucy was determined to be the one holding the shield.

She was careful, but as it turned out, not careful enough. She'd underestimated Arasaka. Their fixer, Faraday, saw the opening. Found the crack in the armor. And in it, he discovered a way to exploit the love between two edgerunners to secure his ticket up the corpo ladder.

Having snatched Lucy, Faraday forced David into a desperate rescue mission as the boy teetered on the edge of cyberpsychosis. David didn't give up, not even with MaxTac hot on his heels. Rebecca and Falco—the remains of a loyal crew—threw themselves into the line of fire just to keep him moving.

The cyberskeleton did its job. David got Lucy out... only to fall into a trap set by Arasaka. A trap with Adam Smasher waiting inside.

David held Lucy close and jumped towards the Moon, which hung cold and white above the chaos. In that moment, her kiss pulled him back from the edge. Just long enough. Just enough for a final goodbye.
FavorStory_151105_Content:
Rebecca and David were gone. Only Lucy and Falco survived that day. The two of them split ways after leaving Night City, and when the dust settled, it was time to move on again.
 
There was only one place she considered her destination. A too-obvious choice. A promise, never fulfilled. Did she go there to honor it, to make a dream come true, or to hide away for good? Lucy found herself on the Moon with no answers.
 
The real experience was different than the one from the braindance, and yet, the place had felt somehow familiar. For a moment, she could've sworn she saw David out of the corner of her eye. That was when the grief finally broke through. The Moon was still the same, but the boy who'd been beside her in the braindance wasn't there anymore.
 
Yet, maybe the story wasn't over.
 
"There… is a method. To let you stay."
 
On the day she left the Somnoire, Lucy stopped at the threshold of the gateway and turned to Rover. Took one last look at the silent Moon beyond.
 
"That's not what they would've wanted, is it?"
FavorStory_110901_Content: A letter lies quietly in the files box, stamped with the seal of Lucilla's mother, Kamerel. For a memory-type Resonator, diaries, notes, or other memo-keeping tools are dangerous media. They are the driftwood a drowning sailor clings to in a shipwreck. Faced with the crashing waves of memory fluctuation, you must rely on them lest you sink beneath the tide of recollection. But the moment you begin to unconsciously depend on external objects to fill the gaps in your memory, you also accept a certain risk. That someone, for instance, might tamper with your diary to rewrite who you think you are. Therefore, Lucilla, I forbid it. I forbid you to record your private matters by any means beyond your own mind. I forbid you to speak of them. I forbid you to form such a dependence. As a memory Resonator, you must become its master, the strongest, most dangerous being in your own sea of recollection. I wish for you a life without driftwood, without refuge. Without the need for me, or anyone else. And yet, as my own body began to fail, I found myself, without realizing it, keeping a diary. Perhaps memory-type Resonators are, in a way, premature inheritors of memory itself. The side effects you endure are merely a stage of life that every aging soul must inevitably experience. Lucilla, by the time this letter reaches you, I will have likely passed. You should know that I am not rambling to you out of sentimentality. This is a warning, a precaution, lest you forget who you are over something trivial. I have prepared materials for you—records of your past, to help you rebuild your Memory Palace. Of course, whether you use them is your choice. As with every choice before this one, it is entirely voluntary.
FavorStory_110902_Content: A surveillance master tape, carefully housed inside a protective case of excellent quality. But its time registration has been ripped off, and the faces of everyone captured on it have been erased. A strange, almost twisted way to preserve it. A note can be found along with it: The Forte you awakened disrupted all the plans I had for you. By now, you should understand the challenge of protecting a "gifted" Resonator in the New Federation. I don't just want you to survive. You need to earn the right to live. "This is Madam Kamerel. Just tell her what you just told me, and then you can go, Andy." "Yes, sir. So, we received a report of a young girl who awakened her Forte..." "Just start from how you found her." "Ah, of course! My apologies... Using the camera's location-tracking system, we were quick to track her to a park about five kilometers from the reported location." "You're telling me a young girl ran five kilometers into the woods. Barefoot. In the middle of the night." "I..." "Take your time, Andy. Answer her truthfully." "Yes. When we found her, there was a bicycle. I'm certain I saw one. But then it just vanished. Turned into... a photograph." "This photograph right here, Madam Kamerel." "Are you sure you saw it? The bicycle turning into a photograph, I mean?" "Uh, I..." "Go get some rest, Andy. You've been up all night. You can go home." "Yes, sir. Thank you, madam. Please excuse me!" *Sound of door opening and closing* "This photograph was taken the day she first learned to ride a bicycle." "Luci's ability is a rare one even among memory-type Resonators. Try to remember, when did she awaken her Forte...?" "...I have no idea." "Her gifts will draw too much attention. We can't even use our contacts inside the government to protect her." "She has to leave." "Leave? Kamerel, where do you want to send her?" "That will be her decision."
FavorStory_110903_Content: Two letters, one from a school in the New Federation, the other bearing Kamerel's seal. Her handwriting is so heavy that it nearly tears through the envelope. A small note is tucked inside: Don't forget, the world is full of incompetent teachers. [Letter Received] Dear Madam Kamerel, Please forgive my presumptuous letter. In accordance with the school's guidelines, I am writing to report on Miss Lucilla's conduct over the past several months. Overall, the situation is rather concerning. While her academic performance is impeccable, we have received reports from several students that her behavior at school is somewhat... inexplicable. Most of the time, she appears very withdrawn, yet occasionally she will suddenly become overly intimate with certain peers, claiming false memories as though they had been close friends for years. When her classmates calmly point out that they are not well acquainted, she immediately becomes depressed and utterly distraught. Madam Kamerel, as we discussed during Miss Lucilla's enrollment, while the school does not discriminate against Resonator students, all of this is predicated on the stability of her Forte. Her current condition, I regret to say, leaves much to be desired. [Reply Letter] Dear President Sofia, A presumptuous letter indeed. I am sorry to learn that your institution lacks the capacity to provide Lucilla with a sufficient, comprehensive education, as well as the basic awareness to guide students in normal social interaction. To my understanding, an educational institution that lacks even the fundamental ability to educate might be what is truly "inexplicable." Furthermore, I am astonished that your institution would mistake a child's clumsy attempts at making friends for instability in her Forte. I will be conveying this inappropriate characterization to the school inspector as well. It would appear your institution is not fit for Lucilla. Please have her belongings packed. I will be collecting her tomorrow.
FavorStory_110904_Content: A scrap of paper carefully torn from a notebook. It bears the Spacetrek Collective's emblem. A short message is written on the back. I was very curious as to the kind of fortune that healed you, until I found that particular Roya man and asked him a few simple questions. If your old illness ever returns, his seemingly nonsensical remarks might help to stir your memory. I exhausted nearly every means of transport available to reach this remote Royan observation station mentioned in the report. I also confirmed once again that the one who saved her was nothing more than a shabby old man in his twilight years. No conspiracy. No hidden design. Her survival was purely by chance. This Roya also showed me the objects Lucilla had used her ability to read—random trinkets, nothing more. I cannot fathom what magic these objects possessed that allowed Lucilla to escape the hysteria brought on by her ability. Naturally, I would not believe this old man understood memory-type Resonators better than the New Federation's finest doctors. Truly a pointless journey. My interest in this place was spent almost immediately. "Madam, a simple truth, it is. If you only see through a camera lens, only observe through photographs, you will never grasp the cold of the frostlands, nor their vastness." "Don't play coy with me." "I am not. It was President Lucilla who told me this. After she laid her hands on these trivial little objects, she finally understood." "Understood what?" "That life is not a photograph. Life is flesh. Life is blood. Life must not be survived, but lived." "...Lucilla has always chosen her own way of living." "I have a child too. That is why I understand why you fail to see it. Just as I observe the frostlands, President Lucilla observes others. Tell me, have you always watched her the same way you do now?" the Roya asked me. An arrogant question. One that presumed to understand me. I did not answer him.
FavorStory_110905_Content: Inside a heavy safe box lies a roll of film with no descriptive labeling. Only its material gives away its age. It appears only readable and playable through a device in Lucilla's posession. Upon playback, the screen stays pitch black, audio only. "It's so dark!" "You need to pop the lens cap off first to see anything." "Oh. Then I'll just leave it on for now." "Why?" "I'm not ready yet. I want my first photo to be you looking pretty!" "I don't need pictures to remember how I am. I have you." "Okay!" "Make a wish, Lucilla." …… …… "I wish... I can remember these moments forever."
FavorGoods_110801_Content:
Few would guess that the white birds soaring above the skies of <te href=260004>Lahai-Roi</te>, the very ones under the Miko of Flaming Sakura's command, could look so endearingly adorable up close.
 
Hiyuki's fingers are nimble, yet they seem to fail her whenever she attempts a "professional" origami bird. She even resorted to eavesdropping on origami lessons from outside a window, but the final result was always this same, harmlessly cute shape.
FavorGoods_110802_Content:
A fortune lot from the Flaming Sakura. Its sakura motifs and divination text have been wholly obscured, buried beneath tiny white flowers gathered from somewhere unknown.

Hiyuki first drew this lot when she sought guidance, asking whether she would smoothly inherit the title of Miko of Flaming Sakura. Only days later, she discovered that someone had, in secret, stitched and reshaped her fortune into this form.
FavorGoods_110803_Content:
In her spare time, Hiyuki retreats to a secluded corner to carve. 
 
Figurines of people, animals, miniature landscapes, or scenes from art, she attempts to render them all with her carving knife. Recently, there is a rumor that her interest has shifted from the <te href=700022>Exoswarm</te> to the <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te>'s various mechanical constructs. Students have even reported glimpsing her in the frostlands, attempting to carve the likeness of the <te href=700008>Exostrider</te>.

Perhaps one day, the carving knife in her hand will finally replace the blade sheathed at her waist.
FavorGoods_121101_Content: A doll that Denia carries around. Far from the pretty thing you usually see, its worn body is now stitched all over with clumsy repairs, and the Voidmatter that once stuffed its shape has long since bled away. "A broken, stubborn vessel, once shaped by the world's gaze. Now, it whispers a plea, over and over: Please, give me a heart. Any heart will do."
FavorGoods_121102_Content: An ornately decorated photo album, meticulously maintained. It is clear at a glance that its owner treasures it dearly. The Photography Fan Club at Startorch Academy gifted each member a personal album as a vessel for their cherished campus memories. Most of the pages are filled with group shots where Denia smiles quietly from the corner... It was simply her way to earn credits. "The wilderness has no word. Perhaps it sees nothing, hears nothing, and cares not what we say. It simply reaches out, stretching toward the infinite horizon."
FavorGoods_121103_Content: A device that generates massive bubbles, nothing extraordinary except for its dreamy design. It looks more like a toy than a weapon. Denia uses it to hide Voidmatter inside the bubbles. A small illusion of being able to protect others. "To be honest, Aleph-1 never harbored any hostility toward us. It's simply indifferent to all things. Life and hope are insignificant noises for it. Meaningless. That's exactly why it could never understand how the darkness of Voidspace is filled with color. Those are lights from a cosmic graveyard. Starlight that faded trillions of years ago. Proof that the stars were once there."
FavorStory_110805_Title: Even Should the Path Have No End
FavorStory_110801_Content:
The first time Hiyuki heard the truth of her own past, it spilled from Gyokuro's drunken lips. Hiyuki's mouth tightened. Without a word, she poured herself a glass of the bitter liquor.
 
"Hiyuki... My dear Hiyuki..." 
"You can't do this. You can't be the damn Miko of Flaming Sakura... Your life was never meant to be like this!"
 
Hiyuki's eyes narrowed. If the people of <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> saw their usually dignified and poised Miko of Flaming Sakura acting like this behind closed doors... 
 
The second hand ticked. The minute hand followed. At last, the hour hand lurched forward. By Ashinohara time, this very moment marked Hiyuki's transition into adulthood. She sighed and downed the drink in one burning gulp.
 
"You managed. You think I cannot?"
 
The liquor scorched her throat and settled like lead in her slight frame. So this was what they called the "drink of adulthood." Its taste, she decided, was hardly worth the wait. Hiyuki stood and draped a blanket over Gyokuro's muttering form. She lingered in the corner for a long moment. At last, she stepped forward, tucked the edges tight, and closed the door softly behind her.
 
The next morning, Gyokuro's fury toward the steward tasked with the Legacy Talisman's succession rang out loud enough to be heard two streets away.
 
The Suzu's power lay in "drawing upon the future." In simple terms, it meant every use exacted a toll from the bearer's remaining lifespan. In the worst case, it meant a successor who inherited the bell today might vanish into nothingness in their very first battle against a Threnodian. Because the price was so high, successors were usually chosen early. Hiyuki had stayed at Gyokuro's side for more than a decade. Even if Gyokuro refused to name her... who else could possibly be chosen?
 
The steward, unable to handle Gyokuro's temper, could only offer a strained, placating smile. "Even if not Hiyuki, surely you must name someone, Lady Miko."
 
Gyokuro fell silent for a few breaths. She sighed, cleared her throat, and prepared to resume her tirade.
 
It was Hiyuki who finally opened the door, ending the farce.
 
"For years, I have journeyed with you through Ashinohara. I know what each duty demands." 
"I have mastered every art a miko must know. The weaving of charms, the ceremonial dances—all from teachers of your own choosing."
"Only I can ensure the name of the Flaming Sakura remains untarnished, Gyokuro... No. Lady Miko."
 
Gyokuro's brow furrowed. She waved a hand dismissively. 

"You've learned it all, have you? Then don't you realize the Suzu will be the death of you?"
"I was an orphan you took in. My family lies buried beneath the snow from that Threnodian attack. I have no attachments left."
 
The room fell suffocatingly quiet. The only sound was the raspy, obsessive scrape of Gyokuro's thumb as she rubbed the bell on her wrist. She tried to speak, but in the end, no words came.
FavorStory_110802_Content:
The days following Hiyuki's succession were inevitably frantic. Where once she had simply walked in Gyokuro's shadow, she now found the weight of every duty resting on her own shoulders.
 
<te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> had long suffered under the <te href=850074>Threnodian's</te> shadow, forcing the land to weave its very survival around the mikos. As the bearer of the Suzu, Hiyuki's status was as uniquely sacred as it was heavy, and her jurisdiction covered the entirety of Ashinohara. She became a nomad of necessity, racing between different places to assist the local mikos and turn the tides of battle.
 
Yet a miko was as much a living symbol as a blade. Wherever people would gather, a miko must appear to remind them why they fought. The Miko of Flaming Sakura was no exception. Hiyuki carried both burdens well. Perhaps it was because she had learned each duty at Gyokuro's side since childhood, combat and ceremony alike had long since become second nature. The only thing missing was Gyokuro's specific Flaming Sakura swordsmanship. Gyokuro had stubbornly refused to pass down the forms, even going so far as to distance herself from Hiyuki.
 
"Fine. If you will not teach me, I will learn in secret. One day, I will master it. One day."
 
But that day never came.

"The Suzu allows the bearer to draw upon the future, and a successor who inherits the Suzu today might vanish into nothingness during their very first battle with a Threnodian..."
 
Hiyuki couldn't remember the words the steward whispered when placing the Suzu in her hands. She couldn't remember the clumsy way she tied it to her wrist, mimicking a gesture she had seen so many times. She couldn't recall the weather that day, or the face of the person who handed her the small wooden box containing Gyokuro's legacy.
