By the time the world rushed back into focus, she was sitting alone in the hollowed halls of the seat of Flaming Sakura, clutching the wish slip that had been inside the box.
 
Blood froze in her chest. A creeping frost left her fingertips numb. Inch by inch, Hiyuki dragged herself to that familiar corner of the room and curled up. She had crumpled the wish slip earlier. Now she smoothed it flat. 
 
"...I see."
"...I accept your wish."
"...There will never be another Miko of Flaming Sakura."
FavorStory_110803_Content:
"Lady Hiyuki, you have served as the Miko of Flaming Sakura for a century now. If we are to renew the contract..."
"It is of no consequence."
"Then, as per our previous arrangement... for how many years shall we set the renewal?"
"Fill it as you wish."
"I did not expect you to be quite so like the previous Miko... Ahem. Very well. As you wish, Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura."
 
The steward bowed and withdrew, closing the door with practiced reverence. Hiyuki noted that the staff accompanying him had changed three times over the decades. She shook her head, eyes narrowing as they fell upon the envelope on her desk. After a pause, she reached instead for a teacup that had long since gone cold.
 
"Just like the previous Miko... am I?"
 
How long had it actually been since she took up the title? 
Long enough that "Hiyuki" was now a fixed entry in <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>'s history books. 
Was it a long time? 
Not long enough.
 
True to the fortune lot she had inherited that year, Hiyuki had used her own strength to prove a silent vow: There will never be another Miko of Flaming Sakura. Gradually, the voices urging her to select a successor had faded. The Office of Legacy Talismans now treated its visits to the shrine as a mere formality. Even the steward, she suspected, believed a successor unnecessary. To them, Hiyuki had become the title itself.
 
Yet Hiyuki often heard a voice. It wasn't the grating, persistent lure of the Fractsidus. It was a peaceful murmur stating facts plainly in her ear.
 
"Hiyuki, you have held on for so long. But your enemy, the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>, has a far longer lifespan. It will wait until you die, until every miko, and every successor of every miko, has passed into memory."
"Does this path of resistance truly have an end?"
 
Cold tea is always the most bitter. The over-steeped acridity clung to her tongue, making each breath feel heavy. Hiyuki tapped a finger against the envelope on the desk. Instantly, a layer of frost raced across its surface. With one more light touch, the unopened Fractsidus seal shattered into crystalline dust.
 
Hiyuki rose and called out to the child who had volunteered to help clean the shrine, reminding her to stay vigilant and watch for intruders while she was away. Her lips curled into a smile as she ruffled the girl's hair and pressed a protective charm into her small palm.
 
"Lady Miko, where are you going to help this time?"
"Honami. I will be back soon. Keep this charm with you during this time, all right?"
 
Hiyuki waved goodbye to the little girl. As she turned to leave, the bell on her wrist caught the light, shining as brilliantly as ever.
FavorStory_110804_Content:
The people of <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> had long grown accustomed to the distortions wrought by the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>. Survival was a matter of routine: seek shelter, wait for the local miko to deploy, and if the situation spiraled, wait for the recovery teams and the Miko of Flaming Sakura to arrive.
 
To Hiyuki, this felt like just another fight among thousands. She cut through the monsters with practiced efficiency, checking the integrity of the barrier as she always did. As the civilians emerged from the shelters, parents pointed her out to their children with reverent relief. "Look, that's Lady Miko of Flaming Sakura."
 
Hiyuki offered a slight nod in response. She stepped over a fallen "No Entry" sign and turned back toward the barrier to finish her sweep.
 
Focus. Strike. Sheathe... Hm?
 
The blade passed through the air as it always did. Yet something was different. Subtle, but unmistakable.
 
Hiyuki reexamined the entire barrier. Everything appeared intact, yet a lingering, visceral wrongness clung to her fingertips. She released her hilt. Flexed her wrist. Pressed her fingers together—
 
A single drop of iridescent black mire welled from her skin. It pooled in the creases of her palm before dripping to the ground, spreading silently beneath her feet. 

Hiyuki drew her blade. Frost snapped into existence around her. First, contain it. Evacuate the civilians. Then find a way to—
 
She turned, but the cry died in her throat. There was nothing before her. It was as if the air itself vanished. For one frozen moment, Hiyuki could not breathe.
 
Honami was gone.

Aside from the shattered sign at her feet and a trace of mud creeping up the hem of her dress, there was nothing left.
 
Hiyuki reached out, but her hand recoiled on its own. She gasped for breath, but there was no oxygen. It was as if the atmosphere itself had been erased from existence. She raised her blade to strike, but found no enemy to sever. Only a faint, residual frequency remained, proof that the Threnodian had acted, for a fraction of a second, with power never before recorded.
 
According to Ashinohara's records, Honami had been pulled into another dimension at that moment. Even after a desperate appeal to the <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te> for their most advanced tracking technology, not a single trace could be found.
 
When the others finally led Hiyuki away, she was still mindlessly rubbing the bell on her wrist, her mind trapped in that moment of shock.

Was this silent disaster her fault?
Of course it was her fault. As the Miko of Flaming Sakura, she had failed to protect Honami.
And of course, it was not her fault. Against the power of a Threnodian, a single person didn't matter—even one who could draw a million futures to safeguard the present.
 
Hiyuki returned to the Flaming Sakura. She took the protective charm from the child at the gate, forcing a ghost of a smile. Then she walked slowly to her room and pushed open the door. There, sitting quietly on her desk, was the envelope she had destroyed.
 
"Hiyuki, oh Hiyuki... Does this path truly have an end?"
FavorStory_110805_Content:
Hiyuki didn't linger on the Fractsidus's many offers. No sane person would collaborate with those who viewed human lives as mere expendable fuel.
 
Instead, she traveled across <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>, leaving behind white paper birds infused with her own frequency. She instructed the local mikos that her mind was linked to these messengers, and should any insurmountable incident occur, she would be there the moment they crushed the bird.
 
The path of resistance against the <te href=850074>Threnodians</te>... it had to have an end. It had to.
 
It was then that Hiyuki heard word that the <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te> was grappling with a critical lack of safety provisions for its expeditions. She saw an opportunity and proposed a "trade." She would ensure the safety of their exploration efforts, and in exchange, the Collective would forge her a blade using the pinnacle of Solaris technology. A weapon sharp enough to cleave through a Threnodian.
 
Hiyuki joined the Spacetrek Collective as part of the Special Response Force. The unit had once been large, but casualties mounted as Aleph-1 grew more active. So Hiyuki submitted a request, proposing that henceforth, she alone would handle Threnodian containment and ensure the safety of those conducting surveys.
 
When she first arrived here, the Collective was little more than a plot of foundation in the dirt. She watched as Lahai-Roi was built, step by step, and began to grasp the true measure of human potential. The facility's construction was a miracle, perhaps the greatest engineering feat in the history of <te href=850079>Solaris</te>. Yet it came not from gods, nor from any single hero. It was built, brick by brick, by people across all Solaris who dared to dream.
 
"Lucilla."
"Hmm?"

Lucilla casually pulled a bottle of fine liquor from beneath the desk, a specialty from Ashinohara. A student hoping to pass their finals had left it at one of Hiyuki's frequent haunts, tucked under a neat note asking for the miko's blessing.
 
Hiyuki sighed, set out two glasses, and pushed one toward the restless Lucilla.
 
"The Spacetrek Collective... it was built to explore the stars beyond Solaris, was it not?"
"That's the idea."
"How fares the progress?"
"Ugh..." Lucilla drained her drink in one go. "Still a long way off. Research is hitting walls everywhere, and the higher-ups keep breathing down our necks with impossible demands."
 
Hiyuki rubbed the bell on her wrist, her eyes downcast. 

"Have any of you ever wondered... where the end of this path is?"
 
Lucilla toyed with her empty glass, then gently clinked it against Hiyuki's.
 
"There is no end, Hiyuki. Just like what you're trying to do... No end."
"But we have to keep moving forward anyway."
"Not to reach a finish line, but to take one more step alongside the people standing next to us."
 
Hiyuki remained silent for a long time. Finally, she gave a soft nod and raised her glass, drinking deeply. The liquor scorched her throat and settled like lead in her slight frame.
 
The bell on her wrist chimed—a solitary sound, but the Miko of Flaming Sakura would take her next step regardless.
FavorStory_121101_Content:
To those who raised her, "Denia" was merely another asset of the Fractsidus, another pawn for the Grand Architect.

And "Denia," strictly speaking, isn't a real name at all.

In the region where she was born, people usually say "Dasvidaniya" when parting ways, meaning "until we meet again."

For human beings, a name is a parent's first gift to their children, aside from life itself. From that moment on, the child steps into the world as someone new, growing day by day, slowly adding depth and meaning to that name.

The girl chose Denia as her name because it was the only gift her family had left for her.

Even if that family only ever existed in some fleeting fever dream.

She had scoured her birth records. She even questioned if she was not something artificially constructed. But in the end, all she ever found was a blurred image of farewell in her memory.
And it's so hard to tell anything from this little piece. Whenever she brought it up with the Grand Architect, the answer was always the same: "Memories are unreliable. Let it go. It's best you don't know."

Maybe the Grand Architect had a point.

Once she had a chat with Nastasha about her friends' names, and learned of the blessings and stories they carry. Some were hopes for peace or joy. Others were wishes or dreams. All of them, in one way or another, pointed toward happiness. Yet when she asked what "Denia" meant, she received no clear answer.

It was obvious Nastasha didn't want to talk about it, so Denia stopped asking. After a year of observing and imitating humans, she had long since mastered the arts of masking and deception.
Maybe some things could never be found out.

She wasn't even sure if that hazy memory was really hers. Maybe it came from the biological original she was modeled after... Maybe it was nothing more than something the Fractsidus planted in her to keep her in line.

She had once overheard the Fractsidus researchers mention that while the human body replaces its cells and substances every few years, something always stays, to be refined time and again. That's what makes life so special.

That's especially true for those who never find their way back... Anything that manages to stick to the memories carves deep into their souls. Even just a scent. That is why some love to watch rainstorms, while others are obsessed with an unremarkable melody. Such is the human being. Always pretending to be rational, while venting all their emotions through irrational acts.

Maybe there really was a girl named Denia, once. A girl who waved goodbye to her mother.
But was that girl truly her?
FavorStory_121102_Content:
Leaning against the solid, cold side of the Voidmatter Pod, bubbles and foul liquid forced their way into Denia's mouth and nose.

Drip. Drip. Drip.

Her senses dulled. Time seemed to stretch into forever.

She felt that everything that made her was being pulled apart. Her frequency splintered into countless threads. Her body dissolved into grot, swept away into the ocean. Then she rose again, a drift of mist moving across the world from one end to the other like the wind, brushing over colorless wastelands until she reached that familiar, decaying stretch of sky.

And the silent world gazed down at her, as it always had, without a word.

When the Grand Architect chose Denia as the "vessel" for Aleph-1's powers, the decision went beyond mere physical and frequency compatibility. Unlike other Resonators—people shaped by rich lives and deep emotions—Denia was empty. A hollow shell. And the one thing a hollow shell feels toward themselves and the world, more than anything, is "nothingness." A quality that perfectly aligns with Aleph-1's logic of existence.

And just as expected, Denia managed to embrace the power. For a split second in <te href=750040>Voidspace</te>, her eyes met Aleph-1's. A fleeting moment, but long enough for Voidmatter to flood her veins and organs. It granted her the power to manipulate Voidmatter particles and forged a link to Voidspace itself.

At the time, she felt only a familiar silence in the void, along with the peace that came with it.

But as the plan progressed, the Fractsidus noticed that the Resonance between Denia and the Voidborne Threnodian was rapidly declining.

The power itself remained unchanged. Something else went wrong. The vessel meant to remain hollow... wasn't. Undoubtedly, Denia failed to reach the perfection they desired.

In trying to imitate human behavior, in mimicking emotions she was never meant to feel, she had grown a fragile, aching heart.

The heart of the weak.

And with a heart like that, she could never truly become the incarnation of Aleph-1. As a result, the Fractsidus needed to fill this vessel with something strong enough to command the "void" and complete the final step in forging Aleph-1's Resonator.

Denia had always known this day would come.

Yet when that day arrived, how was she supposed to judge the life she had lived?

A puppet. A twisted monster... Or simply a single drop in an ocean that no one will ever miss.

Sometimes she would think of the time she spent at Startorch Academy. The girl in the crowd with the unexpected smile. The girl whose gentle laughter lingered in the memories of others. The lazy girl who was sometimes flustered.

Was that girl really her?

But then again, was she really not the girl?
FavorStory_121103_Content:
A smile is a convenient tool. A low-cost way to narrow the distance between you and others.

Denia first met Sigrika during a group assignment. She sat in a corner of the classroom, idly twirling a strand of hair behind her ear while observing her classmates pair up.

An afternoon breeze drifted through the doorway, kneading the hums of vehicles from the parking lot with the clamor from the square. On the wall, a poster for a Fleet Snowfluff fan meeting rustled with a sharp, paper snap.

A hesitant voice suddenly found her, pulling her out of the little moment of comfort.

"Would you like to work on the assignment with me, Denia?"

Denia turned her head and saw the orange-haired girl with her hands clasped behind her back. Habitually, she tilted her head slightly, just to be sure the question was really for her, then deepened the smile on her face.

"Sure, why not?" she replied. "But why me, Sigrika?"

Sigrika explained that, while she knew Denia usually kept to herself, she noticed the joyful smile on Denia's face as she watched her classmates make a fuss.  That made Sigrika think she must be a gentle person. The kind she'd want to be friends with.

Gentle.

Denia looked up the word later. After hearing the Grand Architect's explanation, she was certain that, when applied to her, the term carried a heavy sense of irony.

If given the choice again, Denia might have refused the invitation. A great deal of trouble could have been avoided had they never met.

Yet in that moment, she simply nodded, smiled, and told Sigrika, "Okay."

Nastasha's words from a few days ago still echoed in her ears: "The truth is, it's not that most people are not afraid of death... people simply try not to think about it."

Don't think. Don't See. Don't hear. Don't wonder.

Denia discovered that inside <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>, something stood between the students and the concept of death, shielding them from its weight.

By day, the campus was a hive of youthful energy, where something new waited to be discovered at every turn. At night, they gazed at the star charts, watching the dreams Professor Mornye painted across the sky. This sense of happiness shrouded their senses, blinding them to the harsh realities that "it" sees.

But all dreams eventually end. "It" will arrive one day.

At the time, Nastasha had ruffled her hair and told her, "Most kids your age don't think about things like this. You're still young. You've got a whole future ahead of you. You should be more vocal and happy, like your peers, instead of curling up in the library all day, or sitting here with a librarian like me talking about such heavy things."

"Death is the ultimate question of life, Denia, but it's a bit too early for you to be solving it. First, you have to find your own path."

Denia didn't really understand what Nastasha meant by those words. All she could do was visit the library less often afterwards.

She didn't want to make Nastasha sad.
FavorStory_121104_Content:
Those close to the Grand Architect have all heard that tired story one time or another.

Once upon a time, there was a fool who became a great hero by sheer accident. To save those who were suffering, {Male=he;Female=she} bore an unimaginable price, a price that was never {Male=his;Female=hers} to bear...

The Overseers had their own takes on the story's hero. Some mocked {Male=him;Female=her}, some hated {Male=him;Female=her}, and some felt sorry for {Male=him;Female=her}. Others just laughed it off or barely paid attention.

Yet the name the Grand Architect kept bringing up, the name that often worked wonders, was nothing more than a distant, vague lie to Denia.

She didn't even know if she counted as one of "those who were suffering." She only knew that whenever she mentioned that name, the Grand Architect would respond with mocking laughter—half aimed at Denia, half at themselves.

"You know, I also think {Male=he;Female=she} should be here," they'd say. "But since {Male=he;Female=she}'s not, I guess {Male=he;Female=she} isn't as all-knowing or all-powerful as you'd hope."

"Such a shame, Denia. The god you needed most doesn't seem to need you."

Except Denia never thought of {Male=him;Female=her} as a god. If anything, she pitied {Male=him;Female=her}.

If everything the Grand Architect said was true, then the one they hailed as a savior was just another prisoner in a cage, left abandoned in this world. A person who bleeds. Who grieves. Who dies.

And that was exactly why there was one thing neither the Grand Architect nor that person seemed to understand: she would have stood before the Keystone anyway. Even without the Grand Architect's order.

Because Denia couldn't find an answer.

If people who chase ideals always end up paying a heavier price, doesn't that mean the ideal itself is flawed?

After all, in places that the person cannot see, there are always those who survive by more "elegant" rules. Exploitation. Betrayal. They enjoy the world {Male=he;Female=she} has sacrificed to protect, all while mocking the ones who throw themselves into the storm.

Why does the world always show its teeth to the kind souls? Why are those who put a price on everything the ones who endure?

And if {Male=he;Female=she} could so easily let go of {Male=his;Female=her} own past, why would {Male=he;Female=she} ever give up the little happiness {Male=he;Female=she}'d fought to grasp, just to face something as absurd and horrible as Aleph-1 for everyone else's sake?

To protect them? But who would ever understand that? What would happen when that person fell?

If the <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te>'s plans could already save the majority... then what was that person struggling to achieve after all?

Most of the time, the thoughts Denia kept buried under layers of masks were simple.

She just thought that between that person, this world, and herself, at least one of them had to be wrong.
FavorStory_121105_Content:
Denia's consciousness kept falling, down through the endless dark.

Absorbing the final fragment of Aleph-1 into her <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> had pushed her physical form past its limit. The Voidmatter overwhelmed her once more, just as it had countless times before.

Her senses dulled. Time seemed to stretch into forever.

Funny how the ending mirrored the beginning. Everything fit nicely, enough to form a perfect circle.

But unlike the first time she'd found herself here, Denia realized she had somehow stopped trembling. Her breathing steadied, and the dread that once tightened her chest had vanished.

When that gaze met hers again, she slowly reached out a hand toward the hollow eye. Then, the same hand reaching for something clenched into a fist. She raised her index and middle fingers, pointed them right at the center of that pupil, like she was taking aim.

She saw it now. How laughable Aleph-1 really was.

A god born of a meaningless world naturally possesses nothing at all. Driven by the instincts of the void, it craved everything. Still, no matter how much it consumed, how much it destroyed, it remained as it was—alone in a world of eternal silence, forever thirsting, never satisfied, leaving nothing behind.

And the solid ground for her mockery? A heart of her own. The very thing that set her apart from Aleph-1.

Even if that heart was small, fragile, and nothing much in the grand stretch of time.

Yet this "meaningless" heart had allowed her to harbor expectations for tomorrow. Just like anyone else.

There would always be those willing to live for a lie. As a certain annoying friend once said: The heart defines who we are. And with it, one gains the right to choose. Much like how humans celebrate the day they were born, a day that marks their escape from the void with a fleeting memory and a transient shape. From that day on, they could feel the world. Feel joy. Reach out to others. And because of all that, they could create something the void could never.

Denia closed her eyes. She pictured her friends across the lands of <te href=850079>Solaris</te>. Sigrika, chasing birds through a sunset field. Nastasha, bent over old books in the library. And the wanderer she'd once tricked, packing up again for another long journey, somewhere far, far away.

The thought almost made her smile. She wanted to borrow that person's tone for a second and say the words with the same serious face:

"I hope they're all happy. Joyful. Free. I hope every one of their wishes comes true."

But the words caught in her throat. Too dramatic, she thought.

So she let it go. Maybe this was enough.

Not many things in this world had ever really belonged to Denia. But now, at least, she wasn't a vessel. Not a sample. Not a pawn. The void didn't own her anymore. Neither did the orders. Neither did the lies.

She just offered up the wish, quietly. From now on, she'd be right there beside them. Never leaving.

Denia had found her own path.

——

Bang.

Now that could be the sound of a good joke being cracked. The endless dark actually had an end.

Somewhere in the gloom, someone let out a soft sigh, as if they had been waiting for a long time.
FavorWord_110801_Content: Aleph-1 has been driven back, for now. But its shadow lingers. There are still complications in <te href=260004>Lahai-Roi</te>, matters unfit for researchers that require my hand. Once they are settled, I intend to return to <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> to see it for myself. Though it has already been... Well, perhaps we will meet again there.
FavorWord_110802_Content: About the Fractsidus... You remember how I can draw upon my futures with the Suzu's power? Among them was one where I became a <te href=850074>Threnodian</te> Resonator. That possibility proved I could bear its power, and marked me as a threat in the eyes of many. That is why the Fractsidus sought me out, time and again. But you need not worry. I burned that future to ash before your eyes. The line is drawn.
FavorWord_110803_Content: Tales of your exploits abound. Folk legends across countless regions, <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te> reports, slander from the lips of your enemies...Yet those remain merely the evaluations of others. It was not until I met you that I understood why they depict you as they do. Had our paths crossed sooner... I wonder, might mine have taken a different turn?
FavorWord_110804_Content: There is something I wish... No, something I must confess to you. Even now, after our time together, a sour sentiment lingers within me. If I were to name it, I would call it "jealousy." I find myself imagining your power as my own, wondering if I, too, could have... Forgive me. I simply needed to exhale this poison. If my words trouble you... then I will bear whatever judgment you deem fitting.
FavorWord_110805_Content: I once wielded my blade to see it shatter. Each strike was my prayer for spring, for the snow to thaw, and... for my own release. I believed solitude was a fate I could not escape. But when I looked at you, I realized that perhaps I may yet cling to something in this fate. I am not you, and I will never become you. Our paths may have crossed but briefly, yet knowing you walk the same path as well... I no longer feel alone.
FavorWord_110806_Content: I sculpt figurines in my leisure time. It is an intricate process, demanding one's complete focus. A state I find grounding. And no matter the medium or style, there is always a reference, a clear set of steps to follow. Adhere to them, and a repeatable result is assured. Such certainty is rare to find these days.
FavorWord_110807_Content: <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> still occupies my thoughts... but I would not call it a burden. The past is settled. What remains is to handle what was left behind. Even if it is nowhere to be found on any map, the land still carries a legacy meant to endure.
FavorWord_110808_Content: Gyokuro tea. It is <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>'s specialty. When I was young, I would steal sips from the adults' cups. All I tasted then was bitterness. But by the time I learned to appreciate the sweet aftertaste, I realized I had begun to miss that bitterness instead.
FavorWord_110809_Content: Confections, I suppose... Not from any preference of palate. It is simply that sweetness, upon tasting, stirs memories of a bitter kind. The sweeter the past I once held, the more bitter the aftertaste that lingers.
FavorWord_110810_Content: My wish is... that there will never be another Miko of Flaming Sakura. That no further fate need be bound to the <te href=850074>Threnodians</te>. Perhaps... all we have ever sought is a world where every soul is simply granted the right to live an ordinary life.
FavorWord_110811_Content: The bell I wear on my wrist is what we call a "Legacy Talisman" in <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>. For us Mikos of Flaming Sakura, it is a sacred relic passed down through generations—a vessel of Ashinohara's wishes. Through it, I gain the power to burn my futures, a power said to originate from Ashinohara's Sentinel. I know you share a close bond with the Sentinels. If you wish to see it, I can show it to you. Oh... the cord tied to the bell? Gyokuro braided it for me when I was a child. That alone is mine. The only thing that is.
FavorWord_110812_Content: If you wish to know more about my past, you will find snippets of it in the records of <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>. They tell a far more vivid tale than I ever could. After all, my only memory of the past is me striking that blade, again and again and again.
FavorWord_110813_Content: She is a bright spirit. I am aware of certain secrets she carries. In a sense, we are both bound by our pasts. But she has a future she is galloping toward, one filled with light and hope she wholly deserves. That said, I still believe she should refrain from using her Forte to slip into class when she is late.
FavorWord_110814_Content: Chisa is also from <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>. I have made a point to avoid meeting her. After all, in our homeland, Mikos only appeared in the darkest of times. We were never omens of good fortune—perhaps a parallel can be drawn to those detective comics popular nowadays. Besides, it may be unsettling to see a name from history standing before you in the flesh. Also, please do not speak to her of what transpired in Ashinohara. That burden is not hers to bear.
FavorWord_110815_Content: A resilient child. She surely endured unimaginable hardship to return here. When she vanished within the simulator cockpit, I was out on a field assignment. The investigation team later briefed me on her case. The detail that made me pause was her writing "saving the world" as her career aspiration... Hm, I find myself wondering... what in her upbringing instilled this level of conviction?
FavorWord_110816_Content: She bears an awful load for a child of her age. She seeks to shoulder the expectations placed upon a <te href=700025>Solsworn</te> far ahead her own time. I have noticed her watching the Shiratori I send forth. Perhaps I should fold one for her before I depart?
FavorWord_110817_Content: I... believe I failed her, in a way. Had I been quicker to see through the Fractsidus's plot, she might not have suffered as she did. I borrowed your strength when I delivered that strike. Only then was I able to restore a whisper of her true self back to her. I pray it caused no lasting harm. I am told that she is recovering. If we meet again, I will offer my apologies in person.
FavorWord_110818_Content: Though Lucilla insists our partnership is only contractual, I am well aware that without her discreet arrangements, I would have no place in the <te href=851071>Spacetrek Collective</te>, much less have obtained that blade. She carries herself lightly, yet the weight on her shoulders is plain to see. She often visits me, half in jest, declaring that she intends to "call it quits"—it is her way of venting. Before returning to <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te>, I should at least see her through the troubles presently at hand.
FavorWord_110819_Content: A joyous birthday to you. The day of one's birth signifies the commencement of all things. It is a guidepost to your origin and an anchor should you ever drift. I first thought to prepare a traditional gift. Yet upon reflection, there is no offering more fitting than this single, blank paper. Please, write your wish here. Hold nothing back. Whatever it may be, I shall make it come true.
FavorWord_110823_Content: I am Hiyuki, the last Miko of Flaming Sakura. Should you seek to slay the Threnodians, my blade and I stand at your service.
FavorWord_110828_Content: Hm, I feel it now. A sharper edge now rests within my grasp.
FavorWord_110829_Content: To refine one's skill is a lifelong pursuit. Perhaps we may reach greater heights together.
FavorWord_110830_Content: With this strength, I shall safeguard more wishes.
FavorWord_110831_Content: The path I walk stretches into the future. The wishes laid upon me… perhaps one day, I can finally make them...
FavorWord_110832_Content: You hear the ring of my blade, do you not? It is the sound of my conviction to see through your wishes. Any of them.
FavorWord_110840_Content: Is that the best you can do?
FavorWord_110843_Content: Follow my moves, if you can.
FavorWord_110845_Content: You've prepared for this, have you not?
FavorWord_110859_Content: A life as fleeting as the first snow.
FavorWord_110860_Content: Take your final dive, into Naraka.
FavorWord_110861_Content: May the sakura incinerate. Burn this self away.
FavorWord_110862_Content: Roam above the inferno, gazing at the snow.
FavorWord_110863_Content: For all wishes spoken, this vessel I offer.
FavorWord_121101_Content: What's so bad about a pretty illusion? Even an empty gift box is still nice to look at, right? Since people only believe the "truth" they want to believe, maybe the real truth isn't all that important. If the world is made of little lies to begin with, why be afraid of all the deception in our lives?
FavorWord_121102_Content:
So, how've you been sleeping? I heard if you get enough rest, you wake up refreshed and happy every single day. Haha... Must be nice, I wouldn't know. But sleeping itself is nice, I think. After all, every time I drift off, it feels like a death rehearsal.
So... if falling asleep feels like a kindness, then maybe death isn't really all that scary, right?
FavorWord_121103_Content: You seem so sweet and dependable on the outside, but deep down… you're always a little guarded... What? Got fooled too many times that now it's just a reflex? Poor thing, that's got to be tiring. Well, it's not like I have anything to hide from you. So maybe, every now and then, you could try trusting me.
FavorWord_121104_Content: I used to think the world was rotten right down to its core. Like everything was hopeless. Meaningless. And I never believed any of the things the Spacetrek Collective likes to say. I mean, if life is such a gift, then why do babies cry the moment they're born? It's like they're scared, like they already know. They know it all just goes back to the Void, back to darkness. But... whenever someone holds my hand and shares their heart with me, I can feel that annoying warmth again. It feels real. It coaxes me. Tries to show me happiness might actually be real... Ha. What a joke.
FavorWord_121105_Content:
Even now, I still believe the Void is unbeatable.
For most people, suffering has an end. They live their lives, close their chapters, and get their happy ending.
But you? Where does your suffering end? Not in any future that I can see, at least.
Still, if you do end up in the Void one day, don't panic... Because somewhere inside all that nothingness, I'll be there.
FavorWord_121106_Content: I'm a total sucker for those obscure lectures from sweet professors, plus anything warm and sugary... Oh, and those reference books that make zero sense. They help me pass out so much faster! You get it, right? It's impossible to get good sleep at home.
FavorWord_121107_Content: Well, the side effects aren't as bad now, but I'd give anything for Aleph-1 to just stop mumbling nonsense in my head.
FavorWord_121108_Content: A birthday cake, of course. The kind with tons of fresh fruit and way too much whipped cream. And candles on top, for sure... Why? Because I've never actually had one before.
FavorWord_121109_Content: I hate eating anything raw! Especially that fancy sliced meat on a platter.
FavorWord_121110_Content: Good sleep, good food, and... good friends together. Every single day.
FavorWord_121111_Content: People keep asking why I don't wear the uniform... Well, the whole point of the Academy uniform is its Voidmatter protection, right? But guess what the Academy has my Forte registered as? "Capable of creating bubbles that can isolate Voidmatter and offer protection." Hehe, surprise, surprise.
FavorWord_121112_Content: It was just... a lot of time in a dim room. Surgeries. Performance tests. Over and over... Nothing but bad memories, really. But I did like that little garden outside my room. True, they were just plants that grew under the Voidmatter's influence, but they had these colors... Unique and beautiful.
FavorWord_121113_Content:
I find myself wondering... how nice would it be if Sigrika were just an ordinary girl?
Without all that weight on her shoulders.  They say you eventually have to pay for being innocent, but what did the kind and pure ever do to deserve that? The world can be so cruel. It punishes the kindest people and calls it "growth." Like that makes any sense.
But through it all, Siggy has never been afraid... She really is amazing.
FavorWord_121114_Content:
That miko from <te href=851074>Ashinohara</te> is so powerful. Like she's cheating, you know? Yeah, I'd heard the stories before. But facing that power myself was a whole different story.
She wasn't exactly what I pictured, though. Beyond all that strength and the gentleness you can tell right from her face, there's something else, almost... clinging to her. Something that won't wash away. Loneliness... or maybe regret?
If growing stronger really comes with a price, I wonder… what has she given up to get this power?
FavorWord_121115_Content: She was one of the few Overseers in the Fractsidus who would talk to me. When I was floating in the Voidmatter pod, she'd even play the violin for me. I really enjoyed her music. It's just... I never figured out how someone who could make such beautiful melodies... would ever want to help a maniac like the Grand Architect.
FavorWord_121116_Content: Professor Mornye fits every idea I've ever had of a perfect teacher: She has a soft voice, a sweet heart, she knows her stuff inside and out, and her classes are seriously intense. And the best part? She never, ever calls on me to answer questions when I'm napping in her class! Although... it might also be that no one has ever dared to sleep in her class before.
FavorWord_121117_Content:
She's the legendary Fleet Snowfluff, right? I totally recognized her back in <te href=750040>Voidspace</te>.
The Academy's former beloved star—even the toughest professors still talk about her after all these years. Plus, she still holds the top score on every single machine at the Mind Dive Arcade! Honestly, if you want your classmates to trust you, all you have to do is try to act like her... Her charm is seriously next level.
Speaking of which... you must be really proud of her, huh? Make sure you protect her well this time. Don't ever lose her again.
FavorWord_121118_Content:
Seriously? You picked me to celebrate your birthday with you? But your cake does look pretty good... Mind if I steal a bite?
Haha, just kidding. This is your big day, huh? Happy birthday!
I sincerely wish that, as you journey forward, your heart stays full of happiness, and that nothing—no matter how absurd or painful—ever truly defeats you.
FavorWord_121119_Content: Better start running. Oh? You actually got away. Hmph, lucky for you.
FavorWord_121120_Content:
One. Two. Three. Four… A bit off, maybe?
Fi-five! No!
FavorWord_121121_Content:
Now, a volunteer from the audience...
Want me put you down? Well, since you asked nicely… Hehe.
FavorWord_121122_Content: Surprised to see me? Haha, relax. I told you we'd meet again.
FavorWord_121123_Content: Shh... Keep this between us, will you?
FavorWord_121125_Content: Fighting alongside you? Okay, that's new.
FavorWord_121126_Content: I'm not much of a fighter... Can I just slack off?
FavorWord_121127_Content: It feels like I can control more Voidmatter now. Hmm... Getting stronger is always a good thing, right?
FavorWord_121128_Content: So you just need more power? I see... But to borrow my power? That's far too risky.
FavorWord_121129_Content: Be careful. I can feel it, Aleph-1... It never really left.
FavorWord_121130_Content: You knew the risks, and yet... you still came this far. You are just... impossible. Always. But thanks to you, I can stabilize Voidmatter now. It's a bit embarrassing to say, but... I think I want to use this power to protect everyone.
FavorWord_121131_Content: Existence is meaningless. Life is meaningless. We are meaningless. And thinking about this meaningless world is meaningless too—or so Aleph-1 says. But meaningless as I am, I can still hear my own heartbeat. I can still hear the laughter we shared... And now, I believe some things are real. Maybe that's how it's always been: I'm more afraid of being alone than I ever was of the void.
FavorWord_121189_Content: It's okay to fly sometimes, I guess.
FavorWord_121194_Content: Can I trade these for desserts?
FavorWord_121197_Content: Make sure no one sees it.
FavorWord_130801_Content: Gotta admit, Solaris ain't a bad place to live. But the peeps here are nova-level sticklers. So freakin' polite it's even got me swearin' less... Didn't know I could talk 'thout droppin' so many f*ckin' F-bombs.
FavorWord_130802_Content: Say, you ever had a dog? I did, name was Cup-Cup. Cutest little scruffball you ever saw. Knew how to listen, too. Had his own threads, a dog tag, the whole deal. Man... slept a helluva lot warmer with him around...
FavorWord_130803_Content: ...Y'know, never once stepped foot in a school. Everything I know 'bout stayin' alive, I learned on the streets. Constant threat of gettin' flatlined is the best education there is—just never know how high a price you're gonna pay... But hey, even if learnin' how to survive costs a literal arm and a leg, I still call that a bargain, choom.
FavorWord_130804_Content: I can crash, like, literally anywhere. I mean, who needs a pillow when ya got hands?! Sure, fluffy bed's nice 'n' all, but once you've zonked out in a shot-up convertible on the street, you can get your beauty sleep any place, any time.
FavorWord_130805_Content: I don't bother with "right n wrong," "pros and cons"... it's too damn exhaustin'. See somethin' tasty—scarf it down. Hear someone's bullsh*t—call 'em out. Land a gig—lock 'n' load. Strike it rich—hug your crew. Life doesn't gotta be complicated.
FavorWord_130806_Content: What am I into? Do gig afterparties count? Nothing beats grabbin' a fizzy and plantin' myself on the hood of a car. My sh*thead brother clownin' around. Kiwi and Falco clinkin' glasses. Maine "mentoring" David, gettin' sloshed... Dorio tearin' him a new one. Even Lucy the loner would stick around... But I guess that's gone now.
FavorWord_130807_Content: I'm thinkin' all these Echoes are way too cool. Pickin' just one's killin' me! Can't you rig the Terminal to deploy all the Echoes you want at once? Turn a one-on-one into a full-on swarm. Now that'd be preem!
FavorWord_130808_Content: Pizza is peak. Cheap, easy and, most importantly, it's great party fuel. Perfect for sharin' while kickin' it with the crew.
FavorWord_130809_Content: Food I won't eat...? Hmm... Nope, never heard of it!
FavorWord_130810_Content: A dream? I guess... just makin' sure everyone gets to live a decent life? I dunno, choom. Too busy thinkin' about the next stunt we're gonna pull!
FavorWord_130811_Content: Ya like Guts? My own custom job. Talks the talk, packs a mean punch. Before I chromed up my arms, the recoil would send me flyin'. Total pain in the buns.
FavorWord_130812_Content: Becomin' an edgerunner wasn't my dream. Was what my pops wanted for me and my bro. Took a little while for things to click, but by the time we joined Maine's crew we'd already built ourselves a pretty savage rep... Whatever. All in the rearview now.
FavorWord_130813_Content: Lynae and I just click. Got a lot in common—graffiti, motorbikes, badass vibes... Even went racin'. I ate her dust, but whatevs. Not many students 'round here are as nova as she is. Rare breed for sure. Be cool as hell if I got to be her classmate.
FavorWord_130814_Content: Lucy... Dunno where to even start. Known her a while now, but can't say I really get her, y'know? Far as her netrunnin' skills go, she's a freakin' code wizard, can't deny that. I guess... no matter what, Lucy's crew. That answer your question?
FavorWord_130815_Content: Mornye's chrome legs and what I've got installed are toootally different. Hers are see-through! Can look right through 'em 'thout seein' a single wire or chip! Like, how's that even work? Uses 'em like she was born with 'em, like the kid's had 'em since forever—Wait, what...? She's OLDER than me?! The hell?!
FavorWord_130816_Content: At first, he gave me creepy scavenger vibes. Boy, was I wrong. Hear he's good at patchin' peeps up, even their minds. Might let him scan my skull sponge when the dust settles. See if my grayware needs tuning, or if I'm just a certified whackjob.
FavorWord_130817_Content: Sigrika's a good kid. Too good. Bein' that responsible, with everyone expectin' so much...? Gotta be exhaustin'. She oughta cut loose more. Go wild sometimes, y'know? ...Speakin' of, think she'd be down to hit the arcade with me next weekend?
FavorWord_130818_Content: It's your freakin' birthday, choom! That's a once-a-year license to raise hell! We're throwin' a rager, downin' bottles 'til sunrise! ...Oh, guess some peeps can't drink yet... Fiiiine, guess we'll make do with fizzy sodas!
FavorWord_130819_Content: Aww, where'd you come from? Who's a good baby?! Yes, you are! You're a good baby! Look how cute he is. Good boy, good boy. Aren't you cute. Buh-bye, see ya 'round!
FavorWord_130822_Content: Name's Rebecca. Edgerunner from Night City, just like Lucy. Look forward to rollin' with ya.
FavorWord_130827_Content: Woo! Can feel that juice kickin' in!
FavorWord_130828_Content: Looked like a standard immunoblocker, but this stuff feels totally different.
FavorWord_130829_Content: If Echoes got this Resonance Potion stuff too, then... Huh? Wait, they get somethin' else? What's the deal?
FavorWord_130830_Content: Thanks, choom! Now that's what I call a solid tune-up!
FavorWord_130831_Content: Check the specs! Got yourself a fully-loaded Rebecca now! Next fight, just cozy up by me. I got your back!
FavorWord_130868_Content: You chooms like this stuff, huh?
FavorWord_130869_Content: Ugh, no ammo? Who stocks these things?
FavorWord_151101_Content: Don't really understand the peeps here. One friendly convo makes someone a choom? One fight, and you trust 'em to watch your back? Can't imagine any of you survivin' a day in Night City.
FavorWord_151102_Content: ...Askin' about my cyberware? Guess you're not sportin' a scanner. Sorry, but I ain't interested in talking about me or my specs... Rather change the subject.
FavorWord_151103_Content: I fell into the edgerunner life by chance, but got the gist of crew dynamics pretty quick. Us havin' two netrunners proved a real advantage. When things got messy, I could hand off hacking duties and flank the enemy with my monowire... Adaptive and effective.
FavorWord_151104_Content: Ahem... So yeah, should apologize for tryin' to hack you. If it's any comfort, I got zilch. My scans couldn't read your biodata—your identity's a total black box. Piqued my curiosity, sure, but I decided against digging. Who you are now... is someone I trust.
FavorWord_151105_Content: You ever been to the Moon? I have, but it cost me a lot... Still remember exactly how I felt when I first arrived. Even though David couldn't take me, I knew we were there together.
FavorWord_151106_Content: I used to slip outside city limits on still nights to go see the stars. The peace, the silence... I could let my worries melt away, y'know? From the desert, Night City looks like a neon prison, a cage of light. And everyone's trapped inside... myself included.
FavorWord_151107_Content: Sleep doesn't come easily. I close my eyes, and he's there... the cyborg boogeyman. My memory of that day follows me everywhere, even to the Moon. But after what happened here, think I feel strong enough now to face it. So... thank you.
FavorWord_151108_Content: Do energy drinks count? A deep dive into the Net saps you fast, in body and mind. Glug down one of those, it's a fast and efficient refuel. Got in the habit of crackin' one open after every ice bath.
FavorWord_151109_Content: Hm, can't say there's anything I won't eat. 'Ganic foods in Night City are crazy overpriced, so by comparison this place has it beat in both taste and cost. No complaints here.
FavorWord_151110_Content: Used to dream of going to the Moon. Escape there, I thought, and I could leave everything behind. That dream came true... just not in any way I would've ever wanted.
FavorWord_151111_Content: "The David Martinez"—it's a cocktail found at a bar in Night City called The Afterlife. Vodka, ice and a splash of NiCola. It's funny... David never liked fizzy drinks... For most, that drink honors a merc legend. For me... a man my heart will never forget.
FavorWord_151112_Content: Night City's a cage, yes... But as I fled my past, it kept me hidden, kept me safe. And just when I started gettin' comfortable, it was all ripped away... Right back to square one.
FavorWord_151113_Content: She always saw me as a choom, as part of the crew. But in all our time together, I never once opened up to her. It wasn't until she was gone that I realized... just how much I left unsaid.
FavorWord_151114_Content: "Tragedy did not extinguish her ideals. She works tirelessly to reach the stars with her own two hands." I mean, sh*t, you can feel the weight of these records just by reading them. If I hadn't met 'er myself, I'd call it a fairy tale. No one holds onto hope that tight... I respect her for it.
FavorWord_151115_Content: When my Resonance Ability awakened, I hacked Lynae. Not on purpose, but I did see the memories she'd locked away. Hard to reconcile the weight of her past with that big, bright smile. Can't say we're all that different, her and I. I'm just glad she's finally free.
FavorWord_151116_Content: We've never crossed paths, but her rep's solid. Hear she did a lot of heavy lifting with the Somnoire situation. The approachable Madam President, former editor for the Pioneer Association... Official file reads like a press release though. Bet the real story's a helluva lot more interesting. Wouldn't mind a face-to-face, see the woman behind the curtain.
FavorWord_151117_Content: Sigrika is an interesting girl. Has a way of puttin' people at ease. But what gets me are the runes she uses. What are they? They seem to follow a unique operational logic... some kind of unparsed assembly language? What's the transmission method...?
FavorWord_151118_Content: When I hacked into the Second Coming of Solaris's database, I found a sealed file with your birth date. Sooo... surprise, happy birthday. Rebecca's been on my case for weeks 'bout a party. Whenever you're ready, I'll take you there.
FavorWord_151119_Content: Hm? Buried payload. Someone left a present.
FavorWord_151121_Content: Yeah, could use a little unwind.
FavorWord_151122_Content: Well, well... Don't think I've ever seen a score that high.
FavorWord_151123_Content: Not bad. It's good to shake off the rust.
FavorWord_151124_Content: Pff... That was server lag. Doesn't count.
FavorWord_151125_Content: All right, a tune-up should do the trick for now.
FavorWord_151126_Content: Lucy. When I was takin' gigs as an edgerunner, my specialty was netrunning. If this is just biz, that's all you need to know.
FavorWord_151127_Content: I know... the dream had to end.
FavorWord_151131_Content: Not like any upgrade I've ever had, hardware or soft. It's like... my whole system's hummin'.
FavorWord_151132_Content: Cyberware benchmarks keep climbin'... What kinda architecture's driving this?
FavorWord_151133_Content: 'Preciate the assist... I'm startin' to get used to this.
FavorWord_151134_Content: Startin' to understand what's behind these upgrades. Your world sure has its perks.
FavorWord_151135_Content: Not in the biz of owin' favors, so consider my arsenal of tech wizardry at your disposal. In other words... I got your back.
FavorWord_151172_Content: Run. I'll erase you at the finish line.
FavorWord_110901_Content: Sometimes, it feels a little strange when you call me "Professor." Feels like since you enrolled, I've been the one taking instruction. In any case, glad to have you around, {PlayerName}. Or should I say, "Professor {PlayerName}"?
FavorWord_110902_Content: Seeing you takes me back to my Pioneer Association days. Oh, the anticipation of setting foot on one strange land after another. Sometimes you'd stumble onto something wonderful. More often? Brutal challenges. Absurd misadventures. Lying flat on your back in camp, staring up at the stars, too exhausted to move... What do you think would cross your mind? Who would you think of?
FavorWord_110903_Content: When I first joined the Pioneer Association, it was pure rebellion. A way to spite my mother's plans. A little "self-sabotage" just to get under her skin. "Look," I wanted to say, "your carefully cultivated protege just joined an organization with zero political capital." Feels arrogant now, looking back. She raised me too well. Made me just like her...
FavorWord_110904_Content: Coming to Startorch Academy was mostly by chance. I was first dispatched to Lahai-Roi for an extended expedition. Then one thing led to another, and I was reassigned to the Spacetrek Collective, eventually ending up here at the Academy. At first, they wanted me to use my Forte to trace ancient memories buried in Exostrider material. But how was a small life form such as myself ever to resonate with an alien civilization?
FavorWord_110905_Content: I left that cold home. Left the New Federation. Left the Pioneer Association, too. Back then, I was just running for the sake of running. I loathed where I had come from so much that I tried to erase my memories of it. But you can't erase who you are... I thought the Academy would be another stop on the road. Then the views here took hold of me. And now, when I look back, all I see is them.
FavorWord_110906_Content: Busy afternoons on the first day of the semester. Hosting orientations, listening to reports, and delivering speeches at ceremonies. Then heading straight back to my office, lying face down on the cold desk, and listening to the little gremlins chattering and laughing away outside. Those are my favorite moments.
FavorWord_110907_Content: I swear, the new jokes and memes around campus are evolving faster than I can keep up...
FavorWord_110908_Content: Burnt cookies, soggy instant noodles, desserts where someone confused salt with sugar... If they made it for me, I love it.
FavorWord_110909_Content: I like to think I'm quite open-minded about how each department runs things. But, how shall I put this... Sometimes I do feel the cafeteria's canned foods are a bit of a letdown.
FavorWord_110910_Content: My dream now is just to see all my students' dreams come true.
FavorWord_110911_Content: That camera, or rather that gun, has always existed in my memories. It seemed to have been with me ever since I awakened my Forte. Was it a present from someone? Or is it a "gift" from my memories? I can't quite remember.
FavorWord_110912_Content: I have to admit, being editor-in-chief, a researcher, and President all at the same time probably means I didn't escape her plans for me. Which is all the more reason for me to be the kind of President students adore and bigwigs can't stand. Perhaps this is my "rebellious phase."
FavorWord_110913_Content: You, me, and Hiyuki. If I may, I'd like to presume we're "cut from the same cloth." Each of us had our reasons for starting down the path we're on now. Difference is, I journey to stay, whereas you and Hiyuki...
FavorWord_110914_Content: Behind that lovely smile is pure steel. I feel inspired just hearing her voice—Heh, see? You're a better teacher than I am!
FavorWord_110915_Content: He's got just a few too many mysteries for a doctor... But as a colleague, his skills speak for themselves. And that's what I trust.
FavorWord_110916_Content: She's just the cutest, isn't she? Pure, honest, trying so hard to carry the weight of the world on those tiny shoulders. Breaks my heart. But given my position, even a gentle pat on the cheek would likely only make her more anxious.
FavorWord_110917_Content: She's kept it hidden so well, for so long. That just makes me blame myself and my heart ache for her more.
FavorWord_110918_Content:
Happy birthday, {PlayerName}.
As your instructor, I hope you've taken something from every challenge we've faced together. Experience. Strength. For a dream like yours, you can never be too prepared.
But as your friend, my selfish wish is that you'd let yourself live a little more freely. At least today on your birthday, step out of the shadows of the past and look toward the future!
FavorWord_110919_Content: I believe it's this one? ...How nice.
FavorWord_110920_Content: ...Yes, I'm here. Of course. Proceed as planned. Bye-bye.
FavorWord_110922_Content: Lucilla, President of Startorch Academy. What surprises do you have in store for me today?
FavorWord_110923_Content: Life's a reel of memories. And memories? Life, recut.
FavorWord_110926_Content: Tell me there's no sweating involved.
FavorWord_110927_Content: So it's my turn to be the student this time?
FavorWord_110929_Content: Slow and steady. Let's not bite off more than we can chew.
FavorWord_110930_Content: You may not have memories of power, but you can always draw strength from memories.
FavorWord_110931_Content: Every challenge we've faced, every obstacle we've overcome, and every memory we've shared... All of it has become my strength.
FavorWord_110947_Content: Illusions of the past... Step forward!
FavorWord_110961_Content: Oh, this gadget has seen some upgrades.
FavorWord_110962_Content: Well, well. What do we have here?
FavorWord_110963_Content: Let's pick up the pace, hm?
FavorWord_110966_Content: Nothing motivates like a little reward.

ConsumptiveTaskTitle24: Obtain 500 2nd Anniversary Coins in "Second Coming of Solaris: Collab Season"
ConsumptiveTaskTitle25: Obtain 1,000 2nd Anniversary Coins in "Second Coming of Solaris: Collab Season"
ConsumptiveTaskTitle26: Participate in and complete 2 matches in total in "Cubie Derby: Championship"
