ExploreProgress_65_Desc_Text: Part of the ecological information network, Resonance Beacons collect field data within their radius and transmit it to the Resonance Nexus.
ExploreProgress_66_Desc_Text:
The Four Chime Shaftpost is a mechanism structure designed to report potential hazards within the Land of Xuanfang.
Through its Mingshen System, one can investigate the locations of past incidents and collect evidence at any time.
ExploreProgress_67_Desc_Text:
Interact with Unclaimed Rafter Kites to collect or use, or use Grapple to pull them close.
Rafter Kites carry letters, and each Unclaimed Rafter Kite holds a message undelivered for over a century. Deliver these to Qiuhong or Chiwen, and they will use them to learn more about Xuanfang Hold's past and better plan how to protect its future.
ExploreProgress_68_Desc_Text:
Large mechanism boxes containing Automatons.
Obtained Automatons can be handed to King Auto or stored in the Automaton Collection Cabinet.
Censure Courts often require repairs or replacement parts for their Autopuppets. To train Artisans before they officially take up their posts, "Auto Caskets" have been placed across the Land of Xuanfang. Only after achieving satisfactory results within these Caskets may an Artisan assume their duties.
ExploreProgress_69_Desc_Text:
Control a Kernel Puppet, defeat Sparring Echoes along your path, and reach the endpoint to complete Squarefield Sparring and earn rewards.
Before Xuanfang Hold became operational, the Court of Savantae and the Ministry of Development built several testing grounds to verify the Hold's Autopuppets' ability to eliminate Tacet Discords. Once the Hold went into service, the trial Squarefields were abandoned, left to gather dust over the years.
ExploreProgress_70_Desc_Text:
Control a Kernel Puppet, defeat Sparring Echoes along your path, and reach the endpoint to complete Squarefield Sparring and earn rewards.
Before Xuanfang Hold became operational, the Court of Savantae and the Ministry of Development built several testing grounds to verify the Hold's Autopuppets' ability to eliminate Tacet Discords. Once the Hold went into service, the trial Squarefields were abandoned, left to gather dust over the years.
ExploreProgress_71_Desc_Text: Throughout the Land of Xuanfang lie occupied Supply Chests and Tidal Heritages. Defeat the enemies surrounding them to claim the riches within.
ExploreProgress_72_Desc_Text:
Use the Elseway Shroud to travel to specific Chambers within Fogveil Pagoda.
The Elseway Shroud releases a Disorienting Fog that disrupts Tacet Discords' perception and lures them into the Shroud. Once inside, they are rerouted and confined within Fogveil Pagoda.
ExploreProgress_73_Desc_Text: Seats placed at locations of striking scenery. Rest here to capture moments worth remembering.
ExploreProgress_74_Desc_Text:
Unlike the self-operating Autopuppets, Fogveil Pagoda's myriad transformations seem guided by an unseen hand...
Who has been controlling this structure, and for what purpose, for over a century without rest?
ExploreProgress_75_Desc_Text: You encounter Suyu, an injured Midnight Ranger, in Xuanfang. She tells you that she is here on a mission as an Oversight Officer, accompanying a unique Resonator. Seizing the chance, you join this Resonator in investigating a crisis unfolding in the Skyworks, and along the way, uncover the burdens she carries in her heart...
ExploreProgress_76_Desc_Text: A Constable named Weining requests your assistance in investigating suspicious incidents occurring within the Hold.
ExploreProgress_77_Desc_Text: Scattered throughout the Land of Xuanfang are customized Cloud Ride challenge courses. Cross Score Rings to complete the challenges and claim your rewards.
AreaReportContent_Text93:
"Golden Scales of Outer Huanglong" is a narrative performance piece arranged based on historical events, recounting the evolution of Huanglong's Jinzhou region.

The author discovered that many of the historical elements within this performance could serve as reference material for a comparative study of the Land of Xuanfang's history. This piece was written to cross-reference the performance's historical accounts with other documents for textual analysis.

...

The performance refers to Jinzhou as "the foremost fortress beyond Outer Huanglong," a gateway to the six cities and the strategic heart of Huanglong.
In truth, this assessment is intimately tied to the Land of Xuanfang.

Before Jinzhou was established, the eastern coastal regions contained only scattered settlements (the precursors to Qichi Village and Taoyuan Vale). Post Lament, these regions gradually fell into decline. Only a small Huanglong garrison remained stationed there, and it was this outpost that people of the time came to know as "Outer Huanglong." It was only after Huanglong, with the Land of Xuanfang as its home base, gradually reclaimed the lost eastern territories that Jinzhou and the Jinmen Pass mentioned in "Golden Scales of Outer Huanglong" came into being.

Today, Jinzhou sits on the outer edge, the first landfall for ships crossing from the outer seas into Huanglong. The Land of Xuanfang lies deeper inland, a key thoroughfare on the route into Mengzhou. Together, they form Huanglong's bulwark, a paired stronghold guarding the gateway to the one capital and six cities.
AreaReportContent_Text94:
As written in "Golden Scales of Outer Huanglong," the Gorges of Spirits Battle is given particular emphasis as a campaign part of the "Fortress and Gorges War." The "Fortress" refers to Yuan Fortress, a place whose origins trace back to before the founding of Jinzhou.

Before that, the region lay in ruins, with only a few Huanglong border garrisons stationed there. Their duties included re‑surveying the Jinzhou territories after the Lament and responding to small‑scale Tacet Discord outbreaks.
Although Mt. Firmament in the southeastern corner also showed signs of Waveworn Phenomenon, Jué’s descent preserved the people of Hongzhen from the flow of time.

However, Jué had already been gravely wounded upon Its arrival and began experiencing frequency overflow. It was then that Norfall Barrens saw a Tacet Discord outbreak emerge, targeting Hongzhen... For beings that feed on frequency, the Sentinel's frequency was a magnificent feast.

 To protect the newborn flame of civilization from being extinguished, and to prevent the Tacet Discords of Norfall Barrens from spreading to the other cities of Huanglong, Mengzhou, being the closest, made the choice to construct a City of Mechanisms at one of its passes to serve as a blockade. That pass is the Land of Xuanfang.

During this time, Mengzhou's Zhuojun Atelier dispatched large numbers of personnel to support the Ministry of Development, working together to complete Yuan Fortress, which delayed the Tacet Discord outbreak's advance into Mengzhou.

Yuan Fortress, built using Automata Mechanics by human hands, became the predecessor to the Xuanfang Hold that would later hang suspended among the peaks and mists. The aforementioned "Fortress and Gorges War," which erupted at the Gorges of Spirits and Yuan Fortress, led to the completion of Xuanfang Hold, granting the Land of Xuanfang and Jinzhou a completely different future.
AreaReportContent_Text95:
Ladies and gentlemen, today we set aside tales of Sentinels and speak instead of a curious old legend from the Land of Xuanfang, a hundred years past!

In those bygone days, in the Western Fang Peaks of the Land of Xuanfang, there lived a family by the name of "Bi." From the moment Bizhong drew his first breath, he was unlike any other child of his age. While others Twistscales and teased Opus Otters, chattering and clamoring through the days, he remained quiet and reserved. Day in and day out, he loved only to crouch by the wall, stacking stones and dismantling wooden locks.

Time passed, and by the time Bizhong reached his twenties, he had grown into a towering figure—eight feet tall, broad of shoulder, thick of back, built like a mountain of iron. With that size and a perpetually stern face, he rarely cracked a smile. After his mother passed, he had no one left to speak with from the heart. But to mistake him for a simple brute? That would be a grave error!

For when it came to crafting and mechanisms, Bizhong was nothing short of a prodigy. A blueprint that would take an ordinary Artisan half a month to puzzle over, he'd glance at it once and spot every flaw in its load-bearing and joinery. The most intricate puzzle arrays, the grandest city reconstructions—it all came to him as easily as turning his hand. He was unmatched across the Western Peaks, and his resolve was unshakable. Once he had a design in his mind, he held it as absolute truth. There was no obstacle too great, no risk too daunting to face head-on.

Do you know, my fellow listeners? That the magnificent "Skyworks," which now stands towering between the Western Peaks, is intimately connected to this man!

It happened one year. The load-bearing hub of the Hundred-Span Corridor, the entrance to the Skyworks, suddenly tilted. Bricks and stones rained down like a storm, and the whole structure threatened to collapse! If it fell, countless beams of wood, jade, and metal would come crashing down from the peak, straight toward the village below. Panic swept through the people as they fled in terror!

In that moment, when the lives of the Western Peaks' folks hung by a thread, what did Bizhong do? How did he rise to the occasion? Find out in the next telling!
AreaReportContent_Text96:
Previously, we spoke of how the Hundred-Span Corridor teetered on the brink of collapse, and a great calamity loomed! People scattered in all directions, fleeing for their lives. Yet one man alone stood against the tide, hammer on his shoulder, timber in his arms, each step heavy and resolute, charging straight toward that swaying load-bearing pivot. That man was none other than Bizhong! 

He reached the pivot and saw through its structural limits in a single glance. He knew full well that preserving the bearing was beyond reach. All he could do was buy precious time for the people to escape. He had to force the misaligned main shaft back into place, then brace it with heavy timber. But that shaft was immense, and now, white-hot from friction, it burned like glowing coal!

But Bizhong did not yield a single step. He clenched his teeth, the veins in his arms bulging like coiled serpents, each swing of his hammer striking with precision at the misaligned critical points of the load-bearing pivot. Amid the spray of sparks, rubble and broken bricks fell around him, striking his head, shoulders, and body. He remained as silent as ever, unmoving like a mountain.

With extraordinary determination and faith in his understanding of the structure, he continued this for a full hour, pushing the main shaft back into place, then wedging the great timber he had brought to seal the gap. A makeshift measure that bought three hours in time!

Those precious three hours granted the people of the Western Peaks a chance to escape. When the disaster passed and they returned, digging through the ruins, they found only scattered metal fragments. Of Bizhong, there was no sign.

In gratitude, the people of the Western Peaks honored him with the title "Hermit of Unyielding Virtue." "Unyielding" for his steadfastness in the face of peril. "Virtue" for his sacrifice for the many. And "Hermit," for in life he walked alone, with only his shadow for company. 

Some spoke in whispers that Bizhong did not perish. He emerged from the ruins and encountered a group of reclusive masters. They recognized the righteousness of his deeds and treasured his craft, and so this solitary soul at last found kindred spirits.

Yet time turns seas into mulberry fields, and this tale is now a hundred years old. To this day, the truth of the "Hermit of Unyielding Virtue" legend and where he might have gone remain a mystery to all.
AreaReportContent_Text97:
...
That night, the gathering at Xianling Village was a splendid one. I was fortunate to hear an ancient melody of the "Xuanling" sung upon the stage. It was merely a series of lyrics, absent of any imagery, yet it left an indelible impression upon me.
 
I heard the performers upon the stage intone:
 
"On a desolate night of stone, dark clouds rise,
Twin moons share the sky, illuminating tattered banners.
Before Clouded Cliffs, the wind weeps as it blows,
Yuan Fortress's lanterns light the armored steel.
Xuanling flutters gracefully across the long embankment,
Thousand gates and myriad households all depart.
Who ventures forth upon the road to Mengzhou,
Who remains behind, refusing to abandon…"
 
I seemed to witness that night a hundred years past, soldiers standing resolute before the Fortress, common folk departing their homeland with reluctance, mothers cradling infants in their arms, fathers gripping their sons' hands.
Some of them left their native soil and never returned to the Land of Xuanfang. Others forwent evacuation, leaving their blood and bones upon the land that had raised them...
AreaReportContent_Text98:
…
As the drumbeat grew louder, the chorus upon the stage finally reached its crescendo:
"A thousand towers crumble into deep chasms,
A hundred bridges snap asunder, forging a heavenly rift.
Xuanfang's rain of fire eclipses the long moon,
Ten thousand souls' cries shake the desolate wilds."

But suddenly, the voices of all fell silent.
In the next moment, a woman's clear solo voice rose—
"Yuan Fortress's lofty frame left incomplete,
The entire City of Mechanisms turns to dust.
Xuanling once bore witness,
Children chasing lanterns,
Elders listening to dusk.
Yesterday, warmth in a thousand homes,
Tonight, cold bones in ten thousand graves."

Her gentle humming fell like a silent bolt of lightning, yet it struck deep. The quiet that followed was not empty, but heavy.
At last, the chorus rose once more, drawing the night to a close with a long and lingering refrain.

"Xuanling falls, and the abyss is born.
Countless Tacet Discords fade into darkness.
One city's loyal bones buried in endless night,
Half a moon shines alone upon an empty court."

…

Postscript:
When this essay was completed, I had only just returned to Mengzhou from Xianling Village. Yet now, that journey to Xianling Village lies more than a decade behind me.
To this day,  I still remember what the village elders told me as that night's gathering drew to a close: "If you hear a lark call in the dead of night, it is not the wind, but the Xuanling Birds gazing back upon this land from beneath the abyss."
AreaReportContent_Text99:
Each evening, as the last gold of sunset spills across the riverbanks of the Eastern Xuan Peaks, the people of Xuanfang lay down their tools in silent accord. Across the tranquil waters, they wait for the gentle creatures on the far shore to finish their foraging and begin the day's final clamor.

Long before the Land of Xuanfang's ancestors learned to fell wood and craft stringed instruments, these waters already possessed their own natural musicians—Opus Otters.

Their plump, rounded bodies are covered in dense fur, which helps them maintain warmth in the frigid waters. Yet their most curious feature is the smooth, lustrous Opus Stone embedded in their bellies. The very verse every Xuanfang child learns by heart springs from this marvel:

"Water harbors Otters, cradling stones in song,
their voices bright and clear, echoing through the shadowed mountains."

After a meal, the Otters recline on the riverbank, full and at ease. Their plump yet nimble forepaws grasp pebbles or hard shells, striking them in rhythm against the Opus Stone on their bellies. The crisp percussion, woven with piercing calls from deep within their throats, blends into a natural, refined melody that fills the twilight valley.

This is no mere post-meal leisure, nor simply a ritual for transmitting breeding signals. It has become a healing solace for the Xuanfang folk. Workers weary from the day's toil often sit and listen in silence. Sometimes, a musician ventures to the lakeside, draws a bamboo flute, and from across the waters joins in a passage of song. Humans and Otters do not disturb each other, yet in the dusk and notes between them, they achieve a tacit resonance that transcends species.

Yet this harmony is not without its discipline. The communal law of the Opus Otters is governed by something altogether peculiar: a "stern scrutiny."

A young Opus Otter, eager to prove itself, shatters the languid rhythm—striking wildly, without pattern. The sharp, chaotic sounds and coarse cries provoke a strikingly human response from the others. They cease their performance, discard their pebbles and shells, raise their forepaws to clamp over their ears—some even squeeze their eyes shut, as if bracing against a sudden storm. Pushed to their limit, several Otters rush toward the "troublemaker," driving their Opus Stones against it until the noise ceases. Under the protest and pressure of the group, the rule-breaker slinks shamefully to the periphery.

In the world of the Opus Otters, consensus around harmony is the secret bond that holds their order together. Adults often point toward the riverbank, seizing the moment to teach the befuddled children at their side:

"See that? If you're trying to show off and cause a ruckus, even these Opus Otters will butt you out the door!"
AreaReportContent_Text100:
Twistscales
 
Listen. A low whistle, carried on the scrape of friction, approaches from afar. That sphere, draped in hardened scales, bounds and weaves between steep cliff faces.

This is the Twistscale, one of the most peculiar creatures inhabiting these wilds. Each morning as the mist disperses, it is driven by an ancient and powerful instinct—to collect.

Beneath its heavy scales lies an extraordinarily keen nervous system. As it rolls and crawls, these hidden senses precisely map the size of nearby minerals, the position of fallen fruit, the lie of branches upon the ground. Once it locks onto a target, powerful muscles draw the scales tight, gripping nature's gifts firm and fast. Tireless, the Twistscale rolls without rest until nightfall, as if intent on curling away the entire mountainside.

But in the harsh wilds, greed exacts a heavy toll.

As the "spoils" wedged between its scales accumulate, the Twistscale can no longer maintain its compact, nimble form. To bear the weight, it must unfurl its limbs. At this moment, the once-swift cliff-runner moves like an aged tortoise through mud, each step laborious, each breath heavy, stopping often, pressing on.

But the wilds are fraught with danger. Predators lurk in unseen corners, and once a threat is perceived, it curls into a ball at once. With a sharp clatter, its scales snap shut in fright—and the treasures nestled between the seams slip free. A day's labor scatters across the ground.

Typically, the Twistscale remains curled for about ten minutes, then begins to roll slowly until it confirms the danger has passed. Only then does it relax. After a moment's rest, it coils once more and begins gathering its scattered spoils.

Should this occur as the sun descends into the western sky, the Twistscale returns to the safe burrow constructed from Jade Hexahedron, Floral Crest Jade, and tree branches. There, and only there, does it flip onto its belly and spend the night in its most comfortable posture.

FavorRoleInfo_1413_Info:
A reclusive sword cultivator who holds the nominal title of Xuan Paragon of Xuanfang Hold, and a peerless master of both qin and sword. Aloof and distant, she seems untouched by emotion.
The world knows her as the Sword Transcendent. For years beyond counting, she has stood guard over these lands, and the cold light of her blade remains as keen as the day she first drew it.
FavorRoleInfo_1413_TalentDoc: "From the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs, submitted for the review of the Mengzhou Magistrate: On the Establishment of an Additional Xuan Paragon Post in the Land of Xuanfang" ... At the Ministry of War's request, Huaxu Academy has verified that her history of Resonance exceeds one hundred years, and that its origins are all but untraceable. The pair of horns upon her head, shaped like drifting cloud, is a physical trait manifested by that Resonance, and may be related to the all-knowing Auspicious Beast recorded in the Grand Library. Qingxiao's mastery lies in the "Heart Sword." By forging her very thoughts into Sword Intent, she can instantly manifest ten thousand flying blades that answer to her will, purging all evil wherever they fall. Though her swordcraft was learned blade in hand, it has long since carried her beyond the confines of wrought steel. A plucked string, a drifting petal, a falling leaf—to her, any of these may become a sword. The Quietude Art, along with the other techniques she has demonstrated, is believed to be part of the esoteric craft Cultivators use to modulate frequency via their Forte, though much about them remains unverified. ... Magistrate's Reply: I have long heard that her swordcraft is divine and her power formidable. This should be a blessing for the Land of Xuanfang. And as the document comes submitted through the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs, I presume it carries Her instruction. Intendant's Reply: It does. There is no need for concern, Magistrate.
FavorRoleInfo_1413_TalentCertification: "A recent Overclocking assessment report, issued by Huaxu Academy of the Land of Xuanfang" Subject is a Natural Resonator. Rabelle's Curve holds constant in the Time Domain, presenting a steady curve with no anomalous patterns observed. Resonant Criticality: Extremely high. Peak values converge asymptotically toward the threshold. Stability is assessed as high. Cross-referenced against Academy records, the subject's Resonant Criticality and mean curve value show a synchronized upward trend over time. No prior history of Overclocking on file. No psychological counseling required. Physician's Note: The curve hugs the threshold, the peaks climb toward the ceiling, and yet they never cross it. Remarkable. An ordinary Resonator would tip into Overclocking at the slightest swell of feeling. They say Cultivators temper the mind to steady their Forte... could Qingxiao the Perfected be doing this on purpose?
FavorRoleInfo_1212_Info:
A Nethermancer from Mengzhou. An explorer wandering amid Mirage Realms and forgotten ruins. With his own eyes, he beholds the world's lingering echoes and the ancient traces it left behind.

He follows no sect and bows to no doctrine, heeding neither gods nor decrees. Through Mirage Realms and shadowed lands he walks, judging right from wrong by his own heart alone, and in doing so, he has forged a path entirely his own.
FavorRoleInfo_1212_TalentDoc:
[Forte Examination Report RA1169-G]

The subject's <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> is located on the right eye and enables perception of discrete frequencies beyond the standard detectable range. Once the subject's Resonance Energy output exceeds the threshold, the subject is able to construct an isolated field within physical space and force concealed frequencies to manifest.

Frequencies of a high-order Remnant Creature are also detected around the left eye. Analysis has shown the subject and the Remnant Creature are capable of frequency anchoring, perception sharing, and directive transmission via this connection. Of note, the subject may temporarily enhance his degree of control over the Remnant Creature by expending his own life force. No signs of rejection have been observed during the examination period. However, the possibility of future complications—including perceptual abnormalities or accelerated vitality depletion—cannot be completely ruled out. Regular follow-up and long-term observation are therefore recommended.

Analysis of test samples has revealed a bimodal distribution in the <te href=850067>Rabelle's Curve</te>, which classifies the subject as a <te href=850070>Natural Resonator</te>.
FavorRoleInfo_1212_TalentCertification:
Diagnostic Summary: The subject demonstrates a high degree of control over his Forte. However, in high-risk environments, he tends to experience abnormal spikes in <te href=850067>Rabelle's Curve</te> activity. This manifests as a pronounced inclination to actively seek out extreme conditions, suggesting a potential risk of <te href=850073>Overclocking</te>.
That said, simulation analysis suggests negative emotion is not an Overclocking trigger for the subject. Rather, his draw toward life-or-death situations stems from a desire to obtain sustained, amplified Resonance feedback under those conditions. Based on the overall frequency profile, the subject possesses exceptional self-control and cognitive stability. Nevertheless, his threshold for perceiving and evaluating risk and mortality differs significantly rom that of an average subject. It is therefore recommended that the subject avoid prolonged exposure to high-pressure or high-risk environments. Continued monitoring for Overclocking tendencies is also advised.
FavorGoods_141301_Content:
Published by the Pioneer Association, "Records of Huanglong Tacet Discords" catalogs several hundred kinds of Tacet Discord from across the cities of <te href=850093>Huanglong</te>—where they range, how they behave, what they are capable of, and how to handle them. Practical, as these things go. It has remained in print for generations, and since the original's language proved rather impenetrable to readers outside Huanglong, a simplified edition followed. Few explorers or travelers arrive in Huanglong without a copy tucked away somewhere.
Rumor holds that "Qing," the book's mysterious author, is in fact a hermit of formidable attainment. She is said to have roamed all of Huanglong observing its Tacet Discords in her early years, then spent a century compiling what she had seen into this book.
FavorGoods_141302_Content:
A rumor once went around among the common folk: that the pouch Paragon Qingxiao carries is made of some rare and precious material, impervious to fire and water, with a whole world folded away inside. Within it, they said, lie famed swords and antiquities gathered on her travels, along with every manner of talisman confiscated from the wicked she has punished.
The truth is far less wondrous. It holds only small things she might want within reach: a folded map of <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>, a compass, a talisman or two. Before the legend ever started, it was only sewn from a cloth Qingxiao once used to wipe her blade. She had only just set foot on the path of the sword in those days, and she would sit in the moonlight working the cloth over her sword, unwilling to leave so much as a speck on it.
FavorGoods_141303_Content:
A plain red cord strung with beads of jade. Though gentle Sword Energy has soaked into it, the years have still worn it thin. Common things of shadow and malice give it a wide berth on sight. By an old tradition of <te href=850093>Huanglong</te>, elders would tie such a charm on a child to ward off evil and call down blessing, so that the child's life might run safe and smooth.

Qingxiao has kept this cord all along, in memory of the one thread of worldly attachment left to her in this life.
FavorGoods_121201_Content:
This jade pendant was a keepsake given to him the year he was born. The jade itself was nothing precious, and the craftsmanship unremarkable. In a corner of the pendant, two slender characters were carved: Jingran. His parents once gently tied the pendant to his swaddling clothes, gazing at their innocent child with eyes brimming with joy.
"Thank goodness, you're finally here. Thank you for coming to this world."
They gave him the name Ran, or "burn," in the hope that he'd blaze like wildfire that never truly dies. They wanted no life of fame or fortune for him. Their only wish was that he would burn on like a spark upon a grassland—unyielding and enduring. That even when cold nights closed in and the wind howled to break him, he would never bow to despair.
Yet now, a distinct crack ran across the center of the white jade. Jingran traced the fracture with his fingertips, his face unreadable. The Lynx Spirit curled nearby seemed far less at ease, its tail flicking restlessly. After a long silence, it finally muttered under its breath: "Just a fine crack... and you're still hung up on it after all these years?"
FavorGoods_121202_Content:
A worn ledger, its dog-eared pages scrawled with records of monthly expenses:
3rd: Picked up a bronze mirror with a broken handle at the market. The vendor swore it once belonged to a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. Complete hogwash. The pattern caught my eye, though. Thirty Shell Credits. A bargain or a loss TBD.
5th: Still stuck in the Mirage Realm for the time being. Asked a courier to deliver some cash to the old lady—should be around two thousand. Packed along a packet of dried apricots for the little one.
7th: Bought three jin of plums. One jin for brewing, one jin for the lynx (little louse didn't even say thanks), and one jin for myself.
9th: Gambled on rough jade with the folks at the alley entrance. Lost sixty over nothing.
10th: Lost another forty. Damn.
12th: Received my share for the sales of "Mirage Seeker's Tales." Didn't they say it was flying off the shelves? How is it only five hundred?
15th: Replaced a window shutter for the shop. Cost twenty. Smashed by that limp-tailed cat. It's paying for it one of these days!
18th: I won! Came out twenty Shells ahead in the raw jade gambling! Today's a good day. Bought a bowl of sweet fermented rice to celebrate.
Balance of This Month: Don't feel like doing the math. It'll just hurt once I see the number.
FavorGoods_121203_Content:
The original manuscript of "Mirage Seeker's Tales." The edges of the yellowed pages are curled, and the ink has begun to smudge. Most of what's recorded within are Jingran's encounters while traveling through the Mirage Realms—a deserted city where soaring opera melodies rise with the moon, a colossal tree buried deep beneath the earth that feeds on the passage of time, faceless performers who wander around with the entire stage set upon their backs... Sure enough, a fair amount of embellishment found its way in. Truth and fiction grew so tangled together that, at times, even the author himself couldn't be bothered to pull them apart.
At first, these were nothing more than stories he told to entertain the children at the mouth of the alley. Then, one story after another, they added up to a full volume.
His Shifu scoffed at the idea of writing these stories down. "A trip to the Mirage Realms beats anything written on paper." Yet one night, Jingran found the light in the old man's room still lit deep into the hours. He peered in and found his Shifu utterly absorbed in the manuscript, so engrossed that he didn't even notice someone standing at the doorway.
The pages remain to this day. The one who once held them does not.
Whenever Jingran comes across the manuscript, the same thought surfaces: if the old man is truly down there somewhere, bored out of his mind... would he read these stories over and over again?
Jingran pushes the thought aside almost as soon as it appears.
—Why bother? Pointless to dwell on it now.

FavorStory_141301_Content: The Xuan Paragon appearing at the Ministry of War was, admittedly, a rare sight. When Qingxiao stepped down from her flying sword, everyone in the Ministry stopped what they were doing and turned to watch her. A Rafter Kite had carried word to her from Commander Qiuhong, sending her to a certain Censure Court to deal with several dozen Tacet Discords that had escaped. She had come to report the outcome. "It's handled," said Qingxiao. The Commander nodded her thanks, but his brow stayed furrowed. The Censure Court rotations had been going wrong for years now. Either something slipped out while the guard was changing, or a mechanism failed and did something it wasn't supposed to. The current Xuan Triad were brave and fought as one, but one of the three had taken a bad wound and stepped down, and the gap in the formation was being filled, for the moment, by a young Xuanfang Warden. She was new, and there was only so much she could do. They would need a proper third, and soon. None of this, however, was Qingxiao's concern. She was about to step back onto her sword when a hesitant voice called her back. "Lady Transcendent! No, wait, Paragon Qingxiao. I'd like... to learn the sword from you. If you'd have me?" Qingxiao turned to find a girl with a brisk ponytail standing, holding a spear as though not quite sure she was allowed to. "I've been fighting alongside Qingzhi and Duzhong for a while now. I think they're still more used to working with a sword, and I use a spear, so..." "I am not good at teaching," said Qingxiao. "And you have no need to learn the sword." Her voice was as distant as ever. "I see. Of course..." The light drained out of Liangyu's eyes. "Thank you. I'll think of something." "But I could try teaching you the spear." "...Huh?" The woman before her seemed hardly to touch the ground, light as a startled swan. The silver spear went with her, quick and easy, laying pale moon-coloured lines across the air. In her grip, it did not look like a weapon at all. It looked more like a calligrapher's brush. One movement flowed into the next and let go at exactly the right instant. Liangyu's mouth hung open. "Paragon Qingxiao... you know the spear too?" "I watched someone use one, a long time ago. Every martial art in the world shares its roots with the others. Make the spearpoint arrive the instant the thought does, and your spear will stand beside another's blade as well as any sword." Qingxiao held the spear out to her. "Now you." Liangyu steeled herself and worked through the forms Qingxiao had shown her. It came out shapeless, flaws everywhere. "Again," said Qingxiao. They were at it when the light went gold, and still Liangyu hadn't gotten it. Qingxiao offered no gentle progression. The spearwork she demonstrated was simply too far beyond her, every motion bearing ideas she couldn't yet see. But the girl would not give up. She kept reaching for the way the force shifted under her hands. And then, in a moment she wasn't thinking about it at all, the point of her spear tore the air open on a rush of wind, with a power she had never managed before. Still dazed, Liangyu heard soft applause. It was Qingxiao. "You have it." "But I couldn't follow your demonstration at all..." "If you had followed it exactly, you would not have your own understanding." Qingxiao's face was, unusually, almost gentle. "The thought is already there. What's missing is only time." Liangyu gazed at her, and at last nodded, as though something had quietly dropped into place. Some time later the Ministry of War welcomed a new Xuan Watcher, and at the ceremony the Xuan Paragon, who never came to such things, came. From a distance Qingxiao watched Liangyu in her silver armor, bright and unbowed, and for a moment saw the shape of someone she had known two hundred years before. Again you meddle in mortal affairs for no reason, and gather karma to no purpose. The voice at her ear was almost exactly her own. One day she will likely fall on some battlefield against the Tacet Discords. As Lingfang did. As... Ruoyun did. How long do you mean to protect them this time? How long can you? Qingxiao said nothing.
FavorStory_141302_Content:
The rain was going upward. Qingxiao let out a breath, her sword in her hand, and looked up at the two moons hanging in the night.
The brighter of the two was a full moon bathed in violet glow, swallowing the better part of the sky. It was Ovathrax, watching the Gorges of Spirits with cold eyes. Watching her. However many Tacet Discords her flying swords cut down, more poured in to fill the gaps. She had to find the source of the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te>'s power and end it, or the Tacet Discords would never stop.
Faster. She had to be faster. <te href=750052>Yuan Fortress</te> was still waiting for her.

Snow slid off a branch and onto her shoulder. Qingxiao, sitting in meditation, opened her eyes, and the memory let go of her.
Not long after the <te href=750053>Fortress and Gorges War</te> ended, the <te href=270001>Land of Xuanfang</te> saw three days of unseasonable heavy snow, until even the nameless peak she lived on lay under white.
A tall woman with black hair came across the snow and stood behind her, hands folded demurely before her.
"You're... Hsin," Qingxiao said quietly.
"Aw, how did you know, Lady Qingxiao? Was it the smell?"
Hsin seemed genuinely to wonder, and lifted an arm to sniff at herself, here and there. As she did, the black of her hair ran white, and a pair of fox ears that could no longer be hidden pushed up through it, and Her robes and Her face shifted to match. Qingxiao rose and regarded calmly the "divinity" standing before her.
"When the Threnodian came," she said, coldly, "where were you?"
A cold Sword Intent gathered at the edges of the air around them both, sharp and invisible.
"I was inside the Sanctum, Qingxiao. Everyone... did all they could." Hsin's fox ears drooped a little.
The two of them held each other's gaze, until more snow slid from the branches.
"...I spoke in haste," Qingxiao said, lowering her eyes.
"The truth is, I came to ask you something." Hsin took a step closer. "The Land of Xuanfang has everything to rebuild and no shortage of dangers still in it. I'd like to propose a new post to the Ministry of War, one meant for you. The Xuan Paragon. An official standing would smooth a great many roads, I should think."
"Xuan Paragon..."
"No dull duties. Just lend Xuanfang your hand when it truly matters. And if you take it and wish one day to be done, you can leave whenever you please. What do you think?"
Qingxiao said nothing, and Hsin smiled.
"You needn't answer now. Xuanfang Hold is built and standing, after all. You could move down, and think it over."
Qingxiao shook her head. "...No. This place is quiet. Remote. Free from worldly disturbance. It suits cultivation."
"That reason again." Hsin didn't seem to mind. "It's all right. Xuanfang Hold will welcome you whenever."
With that, Hsin turned and started off, as if to leave. A few steps on She stopped, and put Her head to one side.
"In a few more months... it'll be the Waking Moon Festival again. Everyone wants it. Come and celebrate with us, Qingxiao."
Qingxiao watched Hsin thin into the shadow of a fox and go. She walked to the cliff's edge and looked out over the Land of Xuanfang, still smoking from the war. Where Yuan Fortress once stood was nothing now but a deep and silent abyss. A long wind went past her ear, and it sounded like someone weeping.
FavorStory_141303_Content:
For a Cultivator, the true work lies in tempering the mind, reaching always for the far edge of what a Forte can do. And along that path, one must often confront oneself.
Long ago, when Qingxiao had only begun her cultivation in the mountain, her master set her an important task.
"Qing. My cultivation has met a wall, and I mean to cut down the demon in my heart and break through it. For that, I need you to hold the sword."
"Hold the sword?"
"If it goes wrong and the Inner Demon takes me, cut me down."
Jingwei the Perfected said it with a calm face and a level voice, as though it were no more than a remark about what to have for supper.
"I can't do that," Qingxiao said, shaking her head.
"New to cultivation as you are, your swordcraft is exceptional. You are equal to the task."
"No. How could I do such a thing to my own master. It's... unthinkable."
Jingwei smiled, which she rarely did. "The Way is without feeling. Cultivation is like a game of weiqi. Once you set a piece down, you do not take it back. Or would you sooner see me fall into <te href=850073>Overclocking</te> and lose my mind, if I fail?"
Qingxiao was silent a long while, and in the end she agreed.
Late the following night, guided by a wisp of frequency her master had given her, Qingxiao entered Jingwei's inner landscape.
It was a mountain that rose into the clouds, cloaked in snow. Now a heavy fog lay over the whole of it, and nothing could be seen a few paces off. Qingxiao sat at the summit with the sword laid across her knees, ill at ease, waiting for her master and the demon to settle it between them.
If her master lost, could she truly raise a blade against her? Qingxiao did not know.
An incense stick's time later, a shape came up out of the fog ahead of her. She was on her feet at once, sword in one hand, held level across her chest in an opening stance. The fog thinned, and the shape sharpened, until it stood fully revealed.
"Qing. It is done," Jingwei said mildly.
By then the fog at the summit had burned away entirely. The sun rose in the east, and the dawn ran red for miles.
"Master, that bowl of braised pork at my initiation feast... Was it any good?" Qingxiao asked.
"I never ordered braised pork," Jingwei answered.
It really was her master. The sword nearly slipped from her hand, and Qingxiao let out the breath she had been holding.

"On the path of cultivation, does every Cultivator meet an Inner Demon?"
Qingxiao asked the question as they left the inner landscape.
"It is born from the self, yours and mine alike. Live long enough and you will meet yours." Jingwei's face was as remote as ever. Cutting the demon away seemed to have changed nothing in her.
"And when one faces it, is the demise of one side the only ending?" Qingxiao asked, looking down.
"Yes. Drag your feet as long as you like, the day still comes when you have to finish it."
After a moment, Qingxiao lifted her head. "If the Inner Demon is part of the self, then I would like to see whether there is another road to take."
At that, Jingwei stopped walking and narrowed her eyes at the disciple beside her.
"A fine idea. But the day your demon has hold of you, I will not raise a hand to help."
It was the sort of thing her master would say. Jingwei was the perfect Cultivator, and never let a worldly tie or a debt of karma settle on her. Now that she had cut the last stray thoughts from her heart, she was colder than before. Qingxiao was not surprised.
"When that day comes, do as I did. Take yourself a good disciple."
"...What?"
Qingxiao looked at her master's face, and thought that somewhere in all that calm there was, just possibly, the trace of a smile.
FavorStory_141304_Content:
In the half-sleep of deep meditation, Qingxiao slips now and then into the very oldest of her memories.
"Qing! That old swordsman you sent packing, he's back!"
When the village children came running with the news, Qing was sitting in the shade of a tree, leafing through a sword manual and sketching out the moves with a stick. The jade beads on the red cord at her wrist caught the dappled sunlight and shone.
The manual laid out a great deal of difficult sword moves. She had drilled against it more times than she could count and could still only approximate the shapes, let alone catch the spirit of them.
"Cough. Keep an eye on my sheep, would you? I'll go and have another word with him."
The chill she had caught the month before hadn't quite finished with her, and a few coughs got out before she could stop them.
A few days earlier, the old swordsman, an outsider, had drunk some medicine wine at the village's little inn, and then, well warmed up, tried to bully his debt into a tab. He put down every inn hand who came to stop him without ever drawing his sword. In the end it was Qing who, armed with nothing but a stick and the swordcraft she knew by heart, jabbed the webbing of his right hand and knocked the sword clean out of it.
The old swordsman was sitting dead in the middle of the inn's hall again, sword in his arms. Only this time there was a second sword lying on the table.
"Sit. I've waited a good while for you, girl. That was no ordinary swordcraft you used."
"And what's that to you?"
Qing sat herself down across from him without the slightest hesitation.
"Allow me to ask you one thing. Why do you learn the sword?"
"To keep myself strong... And to deal with troublemakers. People like you."
The old swordsman gave a dry laugh. "It won't do. Even if your sword could hold off a thousand men, or ten thousand maybe, it would never be enough. Not in a world like this. The troubles coming for you will always be larger than the blade you carry."
"At the least..." Qing said, "I can keep the people near me safe."
At that, the old swordsman shoved the sword on the table toward her.
"Good. Then don't forget your words today. Practice with this from now on. A stick will never be a real blade."
Qing picked the "sword" up, not quite trusting the old swordsman. It sat heavy in her hands, and she would need time to get the hang of it. And then she noticed something odd.
"This... is more of a <ano=single-edged sword>dao</ano>."
It looked plain and understated, with a single bright stroke of gold at the guard, and yet there seemed to be no small weight of power in it.
"If it's {Male=his;Female=her} sword you wish to learn, this will get you started faster."
Then one day, Tacet Discords came surging in and destroyed the village Qing was born in, and she began her wandering. Her sword, in those days, was barely enough to keep herself alive against the Tacet Discords. For all her effort, she saved a dozen or so of her neighbors. No more. Leading them out, she saw from far off several great columns of Sword Energy tear up into the sky, and soon after, the assault subsided. For some reason, it reminded her of the old swordsman.
FavorStory_141305_Content: One day, after that person had gone, Qingxiao returned to the little house at the summit. As she sat, the old mirror across the room gave back a different woman. In the mirror, the blue-haired woman in the moon-white dress had a pair of violet eyes. She was looking straight into her own. Is that enough for you? "It is." No, no. You've kept a great deal in there. Qingxiao, why is it that you took {Male=him;Female=her} as your disciple and still never said it? That you once thought of being {Male=his;Female=her}... disciple? "I have a master." Hah. Master Jingwei never claimed she was the one who taught you the sword. You told that person the manual was a stroke of fortune. But you never told of the nights you spent as a girl, tracing its pages, wondering who {Male=he;Female=she} might be. You told {Male=him;Female=her} you once searched Huanglong for {Male=his;Female=her} traces. But you never told that when you came down the mountain, it wasn't only to answer that question your master put to the heavens. It was to find {Male=him;Female=her}. "Mm. That is indeed something Qingxiao... once thought." "Had the chance come, it would have been a road worth taking." Then why? If you are keeping these stray thoughts, why not say them? "It isn't that I dare not. I cannot." "{Male=He;Female=She} chose to begin again. I won't trouble {Male=him;Female=her} with matters this old." Very good. Before long, {Male=he;Female=she} will set out again for the sake of this world. And you, the master, what will you do? "...Cherish the present. My disciple was always going to travel far, and I have my own work in the Land of Xuanfang." "The little time we spent walking together is enough to answer for all the years behind me." I'm tired of your grand justifications. And your careful little postures. "I will not lie to myself. And besides..." Qingxiao laid her fingertips on the strings and played. Clear, graceful music filled the house. The woman in the mirror let out a sigh, then smiled. Mountains and seas can be crossed. Parting always ends in meeting.
