FavorRoleInfo_1311_Info: Sentinel Hsin, guide of Mengzhou's civilization. Deeply emotional and fond of worldly joys, She has long kept the fires of mortal life burning amid the bustle of trade and the shifting of seasons.
FavorRoleInfo_1311_TalentDoc: [Mengzhou Ministry of Sentinel Affairs: Comprehensive Record of the Sentinel] ... According to repeated observations by the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs, Sentinel Hsin the Moon Fox's power can divide one into many, proliferating new forms at will. She can command such entities to divide and extend according to their essential nature, along with their consciousness, perception, and constitutive essence, each taking shape as a distinct Fractal Form. Though each Fractal Form maintains its own existence, it remains tethered to the source, sharing sensation across all proliferations, and can ultimately converge back into a single whole. ...It is also known that Hsin the Moon Fox possesses exceptional mastery in the construction of mechanisms. Her grasp of the principles governing interlocking mechanisms far surpasses current-day craftsmanship. By virtue of Her power of Fractal Proliferation, she can extrapolate, reproduce, and even reconstruct existing designs. Her handiwork can be seen behind many of the ingenious devices found throughout Mengzhou City... However, Fractal Proliferation is no mere art of mirroring or replication. When separated from the source, each Fractal Form undergoes its own experience of the world, its perception shifting with all it sees and feels. Over time, even those born of the same origin may ▉▇▇▂... Ministry of Sentinel Affairs Personnel Annotation Current inspections show no irregularities. This record continues to be filed under the old designation, "Hsin the Moon Fox, Sentinel of Mengzhou." Further examination of Her origins is suspended by order of the Intendant until further notice.
FavorRoleInfo_1311_TalentCertification: [Work Log: H001] Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows a constant Time Domain, with no abnormal fluctuations detected. Examination results are determined to be within normal parameters. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality exceeds standard range (counter has reached its upper limit and maximum value cannot be confirmed). Stability is determined to be exceptionally high, with no risk of Overclocking. However, frequency fluctuations show an extremely minor attenuation. For now, it has been recorded as a margin of error, pending re-examination. "...No past history of Overclocking either, so no need for psychological... Uh, do I really need to write this part down too?" "...Wait, who told you to run a Rabelle's Test on the Sentinel?" "What else were we supposed to do? It's the only thing we've got right now. Weren't you the one always going on about wanting to study the Sentinel?" "Yeah, well, at least we got a reading out of it!" "Actually... are you sure this data is even valid...?" "What do you mean?" "Well... after Lady Hsin read the report, She just smiled and asked, 'Is this closer to what you're used to seeing?'" "..." "...Let's hold off on filing this one." Addendum: H001 was conducted as a single interim observation, utilizing existing Resonator equipment and analytical models. As the subject falls outside their intended scope of use, certain metrics exceeded instrument range, precluding verification of whether the waveform originates from the Sentinel's intrinsic frequency or constitutes an active adjustment of the test output. The Sentinel's structural composition and powers lie far beyond the purview of existing detection systems. Further study will require a dedicated case file...
FavorGoods_131101_Content:
Even a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> has things She is not particularly good at, like preparing a thank-you gift for the Arbiter with Her own hands.

She had meant to make it something dignified, but Her mind wandered, and by the time She had gathered Herself, the fluff gathered in Her palm had been shaped into a little fox far too round. It was a far cry from the imposing miniature Sentinel She had first envisioned.

Of course, unlike the fox forms Hsin conjures using Fractal Proliferation, this is only an ordinary handicraft. It cannot move. It cannot speak. And it certainly cannot feel the warmth of being cradled in someone's palm, or pressed close against their chest.

...Truly, it cannot.
FavorGoods_131102_Content:
The <te href=270001>Land of Xuanfang</te>'s first <te href=750051>Rafter Kite</te>, crafted by Hsin's own hand.

She shaped this ingenious mechanical bird in the likeness of Her cherished friend, the <te href=750054>Xuanling Bird</te>, and placed within it the last frequency the Xuanling Bird had left behind. Her wish was that it might still spread its wings and soar across the Land of Xuanfang.

Later, Xuanfang's Artisans modeled their own after its design, and from then on, Rafter Kites gradually found their way into every household, carrying on the work of conveying people's feelings and words. This very first Rafter Kite became the prototype etched into the memory of countless craftsmen, who spent their lives refining their skill, hoping that one day they might recapture the lifelike brilliance of the bird they once beheld.
FavorGoods_131103_Content:
A special space within the Heart Realms, and the place where Hsin now most often lingers in rest. The flowers and trees, the streams and pools, and the Moon Lanterns flickering within it were all drawn from the sights She once beheld with Her own eyes as She walked the mortal world, and from the hopes and blessings solemnly entrusted to the Sentinel. Hidden here, too, are many old crafts and forgotten cultures now nearly impossible to find... These fragments, fine as motes of dust adrift on the long river of civilization, She gathered one by one, piecing them together into a world where She might find respite.

Once in a while, a special guest finds their way here. And when they do, when the stream murmurs its ancient tune and the night falls just as it always has, the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> sets aside the weight of distant affairs. She sits before the lamplight, takes up a plate of pastries, and speaks with Her visitor of things that can only be said in dreams.
FavorStory_131101_Content:
Legend has it that every year, at the Waking Moon Festival, when a thousand lanterns drift down the river, <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> Hsin the Moon Fox watches for the first lantern to reach the lake's heart. She takes that lantern for her own, then slips into the shape of a little fox and pays a visit to the household that set it afloat.

Of course, there are many such rumors. Some say Hsin the Moon Fox sends a fox envoy to roam the mortal world, and whenever it finds a lantern inscribed with some especially delightful wish, it simply snatches it up and carries it back to the Sanctum to be savored at leisure. Others swear with utter certainty that the Sentinel delights most in teasing lovesick fools and pining maidens, singling out lanterns inscribed with wishes for marriage and forcing the hopeful to endure trials more torturous and fantastical than any storybook romance, until their love is tested true as gold and worthy of its happy ending.

Later, a certain storyteller found the legends of the Moon Fox not nearly strange enough. He added his own embellishment, claiming that once, a reckless soul dared chase the Moon Fox across three streets and alleys, only to come upon a woman in red atop a rooftop, cradling a Moon Lantern, laughing in a way that chilled the bones: "You have seen my secret. Are you ready to pay the price?"

The tale became a sensation, soon spawning several sequels, each in a wildly different style. After a while, no one cared whether any of it was true. But every story has its origin. And as it happened, right beside the storyteller's stall sat an old sugar painting vendor who, rumor had it, had lived the story himself. Whenever anyone asked, the old man would only wave his hand and smile.

It got twisted," he'd say. "Somewhere along the way, it all got twisted."

That year, a sudden downpour broke over the <te href=270001>Land of Xuanfang</te>. The river swelled, turned treacherous. A child, separated from his family, huddled beneath a bridge's archway. He wept, clutching a Moon Lantern he had written for his late mother. The rain had soaked through the paper, and no matter how he tried, the lantern would not light.

Then, from the shadows, a small fox appeared, its fur white as fresh snow. It seized the drenched lantern in its jaws and bolted.

Where the boy found the courage, he could not say, but he chased that fox through the rain, down nearly the whole length of the street, until at last it stopped beneath the eaves of a house. Inside, his father stood, eyes red with worry, begging every passerby for news of his missing son.

By the time father and son embraced and turned to look, the fox was gone. Only the Moon Lantern remained, whole and untouched, resting upon the stone steps. It should have been ruined by the rain.

No one knew when it happened, but the lantern had somehow been lit.

"...So that's how it happened?"

The woman seated before the stall pressed her palms together in wonder. Clad in red, with hair black as ink,  she was strikingly beautiful. At first glance, she looked to be a spirit stepped straight out of the mist in one of the old tales. Now she watched the shopkeeper with keen interest, chin propped on her hand.

"And that story, 'The Fox Who Bound Fate,' is that true as well?"

The shopkeeper looked at her smiling face and had the peculiar sense that she wasn't really asking for an answer. She simply enjoyed the asking. He shook his head and laughed.

"Ah... after all these years of retelling, who can still tell what's true and what's not?"

The onlooking listeners nodded in agreement, then fell into discussing the topic among themselves.

"Still, the eerie tales are the ones that stick. If it's just about helping some lost child find his way home, what's there to tell for a hundred years?"
"I don't agree. A story doesn't need monsters or tragic romance to be good. It just needs to be told well."

The shopkeeper let them bicker, casting a glance at the woman in red, clearly listening on with delight. He then lowered his head and returned to shaping the sugar painting in his hands.

Before long, he set a new sugar painting of a fox on the counter. Its tail was held high, its fur tipped with a touch of red, a tiny Moon Lantern clutched between its teeth. 

At that moment, the storyteller next door struck his gavel-block and cleared his throat, taking up the tale where he'd left off. The listeners, who moments before had been shouting at each other, soon fell to sighing and cheering with every twist of the story. When that chapter ended, some still clamored for more, unwilling to let the night rest.

The storyteller pressed his fists together in a bow. His gaze fell on the woman in red, who had sat before the sugar painting stall the entire time.

"You've listened all evening, but you've said nothing. Strange tales, tragic romances, heroes of old... which kind do you favor most?"

The woman paused. To everyone's surprise, she considered the question seriously.

Night had fallen completely. The lanterns along the long street swayed, casting gold and crimson light into her eyes. From the food stalls came the clink of cups, the murmur of laughter. A child darted past, a sugar painting held high above the crowd.

"All of them," she said at last, chin resting on her hand, gaze drifting across the bustling street. "As long as the story comes from this place, I love it."
 
She paused, then added with a soft smile.
 
"So... please, do go on, storyteller."
"Well then, settle in, everyone. The next one's a doozy..."

The gavel-block struck again. The listeners fell quiet.

And so, a new story began.
FavorStory_131102_Content: In the instant her consciousness first took shape, the first feeling She knew was loss. The shadow coiled in Mengzhou City Hall had lain in wait for years, a parasitic vine, slow and patient, eating into the Sentinel's foundations. By the time its true killing intent surfaced, everything had already spiraled past the point of return. Even now, Hsin returns to that moment, again and again. Perhaps Hsin the Moon Fox had long sensed the rot. Perhaps It had only glimpsed, among countless branching calculations, a hundred shades of dark possibility. But how far It truly saw, and what judgment It finally rendered, these are questions Hsin will never know the answer to. Mortals call Sentinels gods, for they share knowledge and unveil what is hidden. Yet that reverence is, in the end, merely a difference in perspective across vast spans of time. Sentinels, too, will decline and fade, becoming whale falls that guide the current of those who follow, carrying them toward shores unknown. Hsin the Moon Fox understood well that civilization is a long river, its waters both clear and murky by turns. A Sentinel may guide its current, but cannot walk its length in place of all living things. Hsin could only imagine that, until the very last breath of that moment, Hsin the Moon Fox was still choosing, still reaching, among infinite threads, for a future It could believe in. Then, in that same instant, power, memory, and feeling were torn apart. Emptiness and terror swirled together, and through them, the little fox running with the Civilization Capsule between its teeth seemed to hear a gentle voice. "Do not try to become me. Become yourself. Choose. Walk toward a future beyond all calculation." But who, then, was "herself"? Was She the Sentinel, Hsin the Moon Fox? Or an expedient measure, conjured to fulfill a duty in a moment of crisis? Or was She... simply Hsin? The Civilization Capsule laid before Her the thousand years of Mengzhou's rise and fall. Prosperity. Collapse. Peace. War. All of it calculable. All of it traceable to a source. But it unspooled before Her like a scroll too long to hold. She had inherited the memories, but not the weight of having lived them. And yet the grief, the terror, the longing—they churned within Her, as vivid as open wounds, as inexplicable as the memories she had never earned. If the Sentinel, the one mortals turned to for answers, had Itself grown lost, then where could She turn? If a Sentinel's judgment was meant to rest on reason and calculation alone, then why had Hsin the Moon Fox filled Her with feeling so abundant, so unwieldy, so utterly beyond the reach of logic? A sharp, crystalline cry cut through the storm of Her thoughts. The Xuanling Bird swooped down and landed on Her head, pecking her without the least ceremony, scolding her for sinking into that old spiral again, even in rest. "...Ow." The newly awakened Sentinel mumbled, Her fox ears drooping in guilty acknowledgment. ...The road ahead was long. Great swaths of Xuanfang Hold's structure still lay unfinished. The founding of a single Censure Court would require calculations numbering in the trillions. Hsin pushed Herself upright, burying once more the grief, confusion, and longing She could not yet name back into the Heart Realms. She raised Her hand and set the Ring Formation to continue its turning.
FavorStory_131103_Content: When the people of the Court of Savantae surrendered themselves to the Lexicon Axis and opened their eyes once more, they found themselves in Xuanfang Hold's mainframe, within Sentinel Hsin's Manifold Sactum. The roar of the Fortress and Gorges battlefield still rang in their ears. But before their eyes there was only silence, only emptiness, only the endless blank of nowhere at all. Frequencies threaded through one another like currents in a deep sea. Information unfolded in shapes they had no words for. Theories that had once required lifetimes to glimpse even a fragment of now stood legible in their minds, as though, having shed their earthly bodies, the Celestials had at last found a way to see the world as the Sentinel saw it. And when the glow enveloping them receded, they discovered, to their astonishment, that they still wore the faces they had carried in life. Some remained frozen, breathless, unable to move. Others had already begun to study the strange new architecture of their own existence. One by one, in silence, they accepted what they had become. And then, like stars flickering to life in an empty sky, new calculations kindled across the space, each one a small light in the dark. As Celestials, they no longer felt time pass. They no longer hungered, no longer tired. On the rare occasions when they withdrew from the Celestial Ring Formation, all that met their eyes was still the same endless, patient data. Hsin, ever burdened by guilt, took the form of a fox and roamed the Sanctum's halls—guiding, jesting, distracting, never quite still. At one point, She passed by a certain chamber where several Celestials had gathered around a construct of data. They spoke in hushed tones, their voices thick with something that sounded like homesickness. She drew closer and saw what they had made: jade-green outlines rose in mountain ranges, a ribbon of flowing light wound between them like a river, and scattered points of brilliant starlight settled among the peaks, like towns glowing in the distance. The fox watched for a long moment, and then quietly withdrew. When the Celestials returned to that same chamber not long after, they found the emptiness gone. Clouds rolled across distant mountains. A stream made its way down through the stones. Trees grew thick and green, their leaves catching light like water. Pavilions waited half-hidden in bamboo groves and drifting shadow. A wind moved through the eaves, carrying the cool, green smell of grass and damp earth—all of it, remarkably, resembling the homeland they remembered. The Sentinel stood at the Inner Threshold, Her smile bright as a blade, Her hands spread with an air of courtly grace, though Her fox ears twitched with barely concealed pride. She looked at the stunned assembly before Her and spoke cheerfully. "What, just because you've become Celestials, does that mean the mortal world is somehow lost to you?" "...Don't just stand there gawking. Tell me, is there anything you dislike? Oh, and while you're at it, I've been trying to name this place. Any ideas? Nothing I come up with quite fits..." Later, this landscape received its name—Mengxuan Vale. Hsin bound it to Xuanfang Hold's workings, thread by thread, node by node. When a node failed, leaves would wilt on the branches. When the modular parts' operations slowed, the stream's current would likewise grow sluggish. One day, a group of Celestials passed the stream and noticed a tree whose leaves had drooped on one side. They stopped at once. "Sector Wuchen has a few corrupted registers." The Celestials vanished from where they stood, moments later returning from within the modular parts to find green already returning to the branches. Hsin, watching with amusement nearby, propped her chin in her hand and said, "Tsk tsk. Mirroring the myriad mechanisms of Xuanfang across mountains and streams, are we? Reading disorder in the droop of a single leaf… Heh. In your old lives, you'd have called that 'dashboard maintenance,' wouldn't you?" The Celestials exchanged glances, then shook their heads with quiet laughter, long since used to their Sentinel's jests. And so the years flowed on here, in a different form. Outside the Simulacrum Nexus, Xuanfang continued turning. Inside the Vale, the mortal world was never truly far away.
FavorStory_131104_Content: A single petal spun loose from the branch and drifted down, landing right upon the little fox's nose. She held still for a breath or two, then sneezed, scattering the petal to the ground. The little fox shook her head and looked up at the blossoming boughs reaching out from behind the wall. Years had passed since the Fortress and Gorges War, and this tree, transplanted here to Xuanfang Hold, had finally bloomed again. Hsin lingered beneath it for a long while before continuing down the lane. The people who had once resettled here from Yuan Fortress had slowly made homes for themselves throughout the city. Old signboards hung once more beneath the eaves, their painted letters faded but legible. Dust-worn tools had been wiped clean and laid out upon tables before the new houses. Shopfronts had risen one by one along the street, their hearth-smoke curling lazily into the sky, and from somewhere down the long avenue came the intermittent clang and hum of the Ministry of Development repairing Autopuppes. Ever since that cold yet tender-hearted Sword Transcendent had agreed to hold, in name only, the post of Xuan Paragon, the Land of Xuanfang had grown only more settled. People had begun to speak of next year's trade, to discuss what their village houses still lacked, to make plans in anticipation for days further off still, like next year's Waking Moon Festival. Not far off, children chased a Rafter Kite across the courtyard, their laughter fading into the depths of the blossoming trees. The little fox listened beneath the eaves for a while, the tip of her tail swaying quietly. The Xuanfang Hold first shown within the Civilization Capsule had never looked like the city before her now. Its original design was solely to contain Tacet Discords, a fortress of mechanical order, its blueprints drawn in straight lines and cold logic. There had been no room in those plans for lamplight, ot the smoke of burning hearths, no corner set aside for the small, fragile warmth of human life. Yet Hsin had always known that this City of Mechanisms, which defied the laws of civilization's evolution, which drew against a future not yet earned, should never have been allowed to remain in this world. Nor should the technology within it, so far beyond its age, ever be permitted to spread. Knowledge cannot be commanded unless it is truly understood. And if it spread, if it fell into the wrong hands, if it was misused—the very decisions meant to shelter civilization could instead become the seeds of endless disaster. That was why the Sentinel's restrictions existed at all. But the Xuanfang Hold before her now had, ever since the Court of Savantae took part in its building, long since woven itself into the flesh and blood of this age, nourished in turn by the soldiers and civilians who now lived within its walls. Its roots had grown deep into the earth. It was no longer merely a machine. It was a home. Even if it had been born of technology that did not belong to this age, this city was, in the end, still theirs. And after that choice She had made, the Civilization Capsule, too, had long since become inseparable from Xuanfang Hold. And so, for the first time, Hsin attempted to cross beyond the boundaries of authority set for the Sentinel. She began to unravel the structure thread by thread, searching for some space that might hold new rule within it. All the while keeping Xuanfang Hold running, repairing the damaged Civilization Capsule, within which still lingered a possibility She had never once let go of. Just as the first cycle of overwrite calculations began, a pair of eyes quietly opened deep within the Sanctum. Sentinel authority deviation detected. Initiating correction protocol. Standard Sentinel model reconstruction commencing. Hsin saw that face, no different at all from the Sentinel's own, and knew then that this long contest of wills had only just begun.
FavorStory_131105_Content:
Hsin held a Moon Lantern and stood alone on a secluded lakeshore. Not long ago, She had invited the Arbiter here to release lanterns, and {Male=he;Female=she} had asked what She would write upon Hers.

The <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> exists only to receive the wishes of others and offer guidance. Since when has there ever been a "deity" who made a wish for themselves? Back then, Hsin had only smiled and replied: I am entrusted with the wishes of all. How could I release a lantern of my own?

Spoken with such easy grace.

Yet now, with no one around, She had quietly returned to this very spot, brush lifted and lingering over the lantern's face for a long while. Her wish was not hard to write, for it was also Her charge: May civilization flourish, may the lanterns burn eternal, may the people of this land find their belonging, and peace attend every year.

And yet there seemed to be something else. Something simple, yet somehow more complicated still.

The tip of the brush hesitated over the paper when Her fox ears gave a faint twitch. She had caught the sound of children's startled cries in the distance.

A Moon Lantern had drifted among the rocks along the shore and lodged there. A child lay stretched along the bank, gripping a branch, trying again and again to nudge it free, while a companion tugging at his sleeve grew tearful with worry. Hsin let out a soft sigh, set Her own lantern aside, and flicked a finger idly toward the distance. As though moved by some unseen hand, the trapped lantern gave a gentle spin, slipped free of the rocks, and rejoined the river of lights.

The child's sobs turned to laughter, and the Sentinel's lips curved to match. Lantern after lantern drifted past Her, each bearing wishes for safety, reunion, honor, or love, and countless small, trivial hopes besides. Hsin watched them flow with the current as though watching the countless lives of this land, long or brief, each carrying its own flickering light, journeying onward in cheerful procession. She walked slowly back through the Xuanfang Gardens on the night wind. On the water stage, "The Fox and the Moon" had reached its liveliest scene. The fragrance of wine and the sweetness of pastries wove through the air, rushing toward Her together with waves of laughter rising and falling all around.

Before She realized it, Her gaze had drifted past the bustling crowd to find Her Arbiter standing amid the brightest lanterns, surrounded by the throng. Moonlight and the glow of lanterns fell across that ever-composed face, gilding those golden eyes, often veiled in quiet distance, with an unmistakable tenderness.

Look... the figure who, in Hsin the Moon Fox's memory, had always walked alone now stood among the crowd, lit by the lights of this mortal world. Watching that figure, She realized the distant notion of the "Arbiter" in Her heart had, without Her noticing, taken on an unmistakably clear shape. And on this night when the lanterns burned bright as day, the "She" that belonged to the Sentinel seemed, for a brief while, to have receded somewhat.

...{PlayerName}.

"She" repeated the name softly in her heart, the name the Arbiter had chosen for {Male=himself;Female=herself}, one that connected past and present as if by chance, and yet as if by fate. A name that reached past old duties and an unspeakable history, to settle simply on the person standing before her now.

—Just as She, upon first arriving in Xuanfang, had once carried a wish not yet fully understood, and named herself "Hsin."

To the Sentinel, the "Arbiter" was simply Its connection to {Male=him;Female=her}. Yet in this moment, She found herself wanting to speak {Male=his;Female=her} name instead.

...Was it because doing so felt like She, too, had truly stepped into this mortal world of lights She so cherished? The thought made Her lower her eyes and smile despite Herself. When She looked up again, that unspoken feeling had been quietly tucked away in her heart, carried off along with the Moon Lantern she had never managed to release.

Just then, as if sensing something, that person looked toward her across the crowd and drifting lantern light.

...Perhaps it was not so complicated after all. In this moment, Hsin simply wanted to go to that person's side.

She met that smiling gaze with a crinkle of Her own eyes, and walked through the lantern-lit crowd toward {Male=him;Female=her}, steps light and quick, fox tail swaying softly with each stride.

"Arbiter—!"
FavorWord_131101_Content: Hsin the Moon Fox wields the power of Fractal Proliferation—the ability to replicate, divide, and extend anything without end, giving rise to countless forms, each shifting and changing, only to converge once more into a single whole... That is how I came to be. And now, I can do the same. I could create more "Hsins," if I wished. You've seen them many times, haven't you? My Fractal Forms share senses and memories. So if, somewhere out there, you happen upon a little fox and give her a gentle pat... I'll feel it, you know.
FavorWord_131102_Content: When I first came to the <te href=270001>Land of Xuanfang</te>, I kept returning to the same dream. In it, I was but a small fox padding quietly behind Hsin the Moon Fox all across <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>. I watched It coax spring from the barren mountains, and kindle lanterns in the cold, empty streets... It showed me the joys and sorrows of the mortal world, and taught me that emotion has many faces, far more than fear. But It never taught me how to be a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. Every time the dream reached its end, I would turn and look back... only to find that It had never been there at all.
FavorWord_131103_Content: We make our choices with only the present and the near future to guide us, like carrying a lantern through thick fog, searching for a wish, a way forward. But a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s projections... they allow us to see the ripples of a single choice, years or even centuries hence, returning as a great tide. To see so clearly... is to learn when to grit one's teeth and stand aside at certain junctions. For a civilization is not merely a moment, it is a river that stretches without end. If you had no heart, then such dilemmas would be far less agonizing. But the Moon Fox entrusted me with the <te href=800053>Civilization Capsule</te> and with Its emotions. In the moment the die is cast, I know what my heart seeks. And I find I will not simply stand aside.
FavorWord_131104_Content:
Would you care to know my impression of the Arbiter of old? In that year, the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s Fractal Proliferation was made in haste, and I did not inherit the fullness of Its stores of memory. All I truly remember is that you rarely smiled. And from a distance, your silhouette always seemed to grow lonelier the further you walked.
Ah, when we first met in Xuanfang Hold, I confess I was a little afraid of you. At that time, I was still... well. In any case, I see you more clearly now. Not as some distant, untouchable Arbiter from a half-remembered dream, but as you are. 
See, this is both a reunion and a first meeting. Isn't that rather charming?
FavorWord_131105_Content: ...You know, sometimes I find myself grateful. A <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s lifespan may not rival the heavens, but it is long enough... to walk beside you for a while yet.
FavorWord_131106_Content:
Naturally, that would be... <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> itself. Its mountains, its waters, its people. I may carry the memory of guiding civilizations, but I have only walked among the living for a few short centuries. In that time, I have seen bustling streets full of craftsmen, stages alive with joy and sorrow, children chasing each other as they grow, each with a future to call their own. It is a hundred times more alive than any projection. No, a thousand times...
Mm. Speaking of which, I find myself longing for the delicacies of Yuan's Flavors again... Arbiter, when you have a moment, would you accompany me into the city? And perhaps help me pick out a few hairpins while we're at it? Oh, why wait? Shall we go now?
FavorWord_131107_Content: Ah... Arbiter, why is it that even a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> must suffer the indignity of shedding Her own tail fur?
FavorWord_131108_Content: Obviously... Moon Fox Rice Cakes! They were the Moon Fox's favorite, and I inherited that preference as naturally as I inherited everything else. Though I confess, I have not set foot outside the Sanctum in a while, and it seems the varieties have grown rather ambitious in my absence...
FavorWord_131109_Content:
I am a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> of <te href=850093>Huanglong</te>. I would never turn away the world's delights. Sweet, sour, bitter, spicy, each has its own story, its own place in the seasons and in the lives of the people. How could I possibly dislike any of it?
This is... Moon Fox Rice Cakes stir-fried with chili?! Preposterous! Take it away at once! Hm...? The taste is... actually rather pleasant...
FavorWord_131110_Content: A flourishing civilization, enduring onward without end. This is the duty of the Oracle Engine... and it is also my wish.
FavorWord_131111_Content: When there was not enough computational power to sustain a full Fractal form, I would often walk the world as a little fox. And I would return draped in all manner of small gifts, tokens from the people of <te href=270001>Xuanfang</te>. I have kept them all here. When I feel I cannot go on, I take them out and look at them... and I find the strength to carry on. Hmm? This one? Ah... this is a fox I have been shaping using the strands of fur closest to my heart. It is not finished yet. When it is, I will give it to you.
FavorWord_131112_Content:
From within the Sanctum, I have watched the lanterns of <te href=270001>Xuanfang</te> light up, one by one. And I have watched them fade, one by one. In their flickering, I found my own heart growing brighter. And I thought to myself: "Let them stay lit, just like this, forevermore."
The rivers and seas do not concern themselves with the clarity of each wave. They simply flow, ever onward. That is the way of civilization. And I... I too wish to guard the lights I love, until the end of time.
FavorWord_131113_Content: When I was wholly consumed by remolding the <te href=800053>Civilization Capsule</te> and building Xuanfang Hold, <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> weathered its trials alone. It was Intendant Suoming who bore the weight of the region's affairs on my behalf. I know she clings to obsessions she has no intention of releasing, using them as fuel to walk through storm and calm alike... Every time I think of it, I am flooded with guilt. I long for the day she finds what she seeks—the peace that only home can bring. For that to happen, I must be the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> she deserves.
FavorWord_131114_Content: The Xuan Paragon appears cold and distant, but she is softer than she lets on. If you need something from her, all it takes is a little persistence, and she will fold. "I will not go," she says of the Waking Moon Festival, yet she never misses a single one. I have always seen that she carried the answer within her heart. She simply needed someone to give her a gentle push. Seeing her finally lay that burden down... it brings me immense joy. Come to think of it, if we were to count by age, I might even call her "Sister Qingxiao"... Oh my, but she must never hear me say that. She would tell me to stop foxing around.
FavorWord_131115_Content: Now there is a remarkably clever young woman. I have seen so many lose their way in the world of commerce, but she navigates it with purpose, her heart set on something larger than profit, pursuing it with the same innate force as the wind rising over water. She even dared to try and outmaneuver me, a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>, heedless of the consequences! And yet, I knew at a glance—her wish is the same as mine. Besides, she has long since seen through me. So I let her be. And as it turns out... I chose well.
FavorWord_131116_Content: Though I never truly met her, she remains vividly undimmed, unfaded, as real as breath and bone within the Moon Fox's memories. I sometimes wonder, had she never existed, would the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> have ever thought to create me? Emotion... is the hardest thing to put into words.
FavorWord_131117_Content: ...It said I did not betray Its faith in me. But the road is long, and <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>'s future is still uncertain. There is much I must do. So I hope... Its faith does not end here. I hope it continues, on and on.
FavorWord_131118_Content: Jué... It is the youngest of all the <te href=850093>Huanglong</te> <te href=850083>Sentinels</te>, and yet no one is more rigid in following the ordained path. Perhaps it is because of Its Temporal Mandate that It values the weight of each "choice" so dearly. When It came to consult with the Moon Fox on the raising of a city, It had exhausted every ounce of Its computational power in seeking a future for the people... Had I not acted in the Fortress and Gorges War, its fires would have reached the very heart of the Jinmen Pass. Jué had cultivated the seeds of <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te> with such care, I could not bear to watch them wither. And now, Jinzhou flourishes with lanterns and laughter, year after year. Jué's gambit... was not made in vain.
FavorWord_131119_Content: ...Where did that whole "Fox Chasing the Moon" tale even come from? The Moon Fox only wanted to retrieve a stolen mirror. How did it become a story of chasing the poor thing? Now, that little hare may seem quiet, but It is full of tricks. If you ever cross paths with It... you would do well to be careful.
FavorWord_131120_Content:
To be born into this world, to walk its winding roads, to taste its joys and sorrows and carve yourself, slowly, until the will you hold is truly your own... that is a precious and extraordinary thing. Arbiter, happy birthday. May each day ahead gift you a little more ease, a little more delight.
Look, the Moon Lanterns fill the sky. Every last one of them, lit for you.
FavorWord_131121_Content: Oh... Shedding again.... Hm? Mischievous little thing... Off you go.
FavorWord_131122_Content:
This world's bright glory lives within a gaze,
as stars that spill through river-ways.
Mortal hearths kindle with a light unending,
and in this corner, my heart finds its tending.
FavorWord_131123_Content: If I do not stir myself from time to time, I fear I shall rust.
FavorWord_131124_Content: To walk among their joys, and stand guard... over the everglowing lanterns.
FavorWord_131125_Content:
I am the guide of <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>'s civilization, <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> Hsin the Moon Fox. Arbiter, at last we meet.
Mm. That is a fitting opening for a "first meeting," is it not? But... from now on, please. I insist you call me "Hsin."
FavorWord_131126_Content: I have tasted every longing beneath the heavens, and at last... I know where my heart belongs.
FavorWord_131128_Content: Xuanfang's manifold forms, all within my grasp.
FavorWord_131129_Content: As is my duty as <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>.
FavorWord_131130_Content: This body is not my own, merely lent from the dust of the mortal world.
FavorWord_131131_Content: The <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s power... restored? I am indebted to you for your guidance, Arbiter. Tell me, how shall I ever repay such a debt?
FavorWord_131132_Content: Mm... to be so thoroughly guided by the Arbiter's own hand, I do believe I am the first <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> to be granted such an honor.
FavorWord_131133_Content: All that the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> knows was bestowed by the Arbiter. But I find myself curious. When you look upon me now, do you see the "Sentinel of <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>"... or do you see "Hsin"?
FavorWord_131134_Content:
The cardinal pivot of every mechanism, the laws of all creation, the blueprint of civilization's evolution... the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s knowledge was laid before me from the very beginning. But to know is one thing. To feel, quite another. If you had not pulled me back into this world... how would I ever have learned that all these truths are born from the smoke of hearths and the quiet of streets?
Arbiter, from this day forth, allow me to walk beside you. Even should the echoes of fate rise against us, you will have your Hsin, and we shall face them together.
FavorWord_131150_Content: All kneel... the Waking Moon has risen!
FavorWord_131151_Content: By Sentinel's decree... the field is set.
FavorWord_131153_Content: Within this domain, I am the law.
FavorWord_131161_Content: A third of my power... is more than enough.
FavorWord_131169_Content: See? There's no hiding from me.
FavorWord_131170_Content: Fancy yourself able to keep up?
FavorWord_131172_Content: This land knows to treat us well.
FavorRoleInfo_1312_Influence: Ten Seals Covenant; Mengzhou - Ministry of Sentinel Affairs
FavorRoleInfo_1312_Info: Born in Huating, Mengzhou, she founded the Ten Seals Covenant as its Seal Master to liberate her homeland from the Evil Miasma. Later, by the Sentinel's decree, she served as Intendant of the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs, watching over all of Mengzhou.
FavorRoleInfo_1312_TalentDoc: [Mengzhou Ministry of Sentinel Affairs - Resonator Archive] ... The art of Frequency-Locking seals a fragment of a target's frequency within a lock. By design, a Covenant demands the subject’s explicit consent, yet should a dying target's consciousness begin to scatter, the bond may be forcibly forged in the moment their will breaks. Securing a frequency grants the wielder access to the subject’s Forte, though diminished in strength. Constrained by physical limits, she can anchor no more than ten frequencies within her body, allowing her to command no more than ten Fortes. ... "So Intendant Suoming can lock in ten different frequencies, and when she opens a Vermillion Lock, she can use part of the locked person's ability?" "Seems so. Reading a century-old file like this is a real headache... No wonder they had us comb through it again." "Say, if Intendant Suoming went to every city's Sentinel and asked for a bit of frequency, wouldn't she be unstoppable?" "Don't be silly. The report says only a sliver of frequency can be locked. For something at the level of a Sentinel, what gets sealed in wouldn't even be enough to wield the corresponding power." "Okay, a Sentinel is a stretch. But locking the frequencies of some strong Resonators should work fine, right? Why doesn't Intendant Suoming do that?" "I suspect she only calls the frequencies held in her locks these days. For her, the only ones she'd ever forge a Covenant with are those nine..."
FavorRoleInfo_1312_TalentCertification: [Mengzhou Ministry of Sentinel Affairs - Resonator Archive] ... Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows an elliptical oscillation pattern and a stable Time Domain, with no anomalous fluctuations. Assessed as normal. Resonant Criticality: Extremely high. Her frequency holds steady, with no risk of Overclocking and no prior history of it. Note: Her frequency output runs somewhat weak, and her Resonance Ability shows signs of gradual decline. Worth keeping an eye on. ... "'Stable'... well, that's hardly news. I don't think I've ever seen Intendant Suoming's mouth so much as twitch, let alone her waveform." "You really need to work on that flair for drama... The point is this: 'her Resonance Ability shows signs of gradual decline.' Don't you find that odd?" "Indeed. This record dates from almost a century ago. It's been so long. Could the initial examination have been flawed?" "Perhaps. But if the records are accurate... how has Intendant Suoming survived for over a century when her Resonance Ability was already fading?"
FavorGoods_131201_Content:
Upon meeting the Second Seal, Suoming asked him to forge her a mechanical weapon. The Second Seal first proposed twin blades or a sword, arguing that shaping it as a standard weapon first would allow ten thousand variations to flower from its form. But Suoming simply replied: "An umbrella would be best." The Second Seal mused in silence, and at last understood. Against the Evil Miasma that came howling with wind and rain, Huating needed an umbrella to shield its people from the storm.

Thus was born the mechanical umbrella that would one day be known as Nine Shadows. Capable of shifting at will into weapons both long and short, it breaks apart into a rain of fine hidden darts to strike distant foes, or unfolds into an impenetrable shield against ferocious assaults. Its hundred mechanisms and thousand transformations stand ready to answer every hardship.
FavorGoods_131202_Content:
Casting the Power of Ten usually demands the target's willing consent and constant focus to maintain. Should Suoming's concentration slacken for even a moment, the borrowed Forte dissolves into nothing. Remarkable as the art is, she rarely found occasion to use it.

That changed as she bound her heart to the Ten Seals Covenant. With her own hands, she forged ten Vermillion Locks, crafting each from twelve pitch-black columns capped in vermillion red. Nine were cast to match the First through Ninth Seals, and the last one was held in reserve to seal the Evil Miasma itself. Through these locks, she could sustain the power of all nine Seals indefinitely, freed from the old constraints.

Yet even as her hands shaped the metal, Suoming harbored a silent hope: that if fate were to tear those nine away from her one day, she would not be the one to let go...
FavorGoods_131203_Content:
When the Fourth Seal left her family mansion with Suoming, she brought only one heirloom: a hairpin inspired by the intricate design of a Gilded Ball, anchored by a spherical mechanism lock. Once among the prized treasures gifted to her house by <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>'s dignitaries, she chose it above all else for one simple reason—she felt the Orb Hairpin suited Suoming's red hair best.

From that day on, combing Suoming's hair became the Fourth Seal's "privilege," a habit later shared when the Ninth Seal joined their ranks. In tranquil moments when the Evil Miasma relented, the two would dress her hair while sharing stories of the day's events.

Even now, before binding her hair, Suoming places the Vermillion Locks of the Fourth and Ninth Seals upon her dressing table. She speaks to them of all that has transpired, as if they were still by her side, gathering her hair and laughing over the news of the world.
FavorStory_131201_Content:
The rain stung Suoming's eyes. Wiping the drops away with her shoulder, she cleared her vision for one last look at her parents' faces worn past recognition by the Evil Miasma. She gripped a spade nearly as tall as herself and laid the final clod of earth upon the grave. Across the mound, the girl who would become the First Seal lowered her own spade. Raised by Suoming's parents, she had long considered them her own family.

"So... what do we do now?"

Suoming looked into the distance, raising a hand toward Huating. Its massive gates were sealed tight against the black curtain of rain.

"They shut us out to be bait for the Evil Miasma... but I will bring everyone home."

Beyond the walls, the land had long been forsaken. Alongside the constant threat of the Evil Miasma, bands of ruthless outlaws ran rampant. Suoming walked every village outside Huating, bearing witness to orphans left adrift, families driven out, and survivors who had lost everything. The people beyond the walls needed order, and Suoming needed the supplies and strongholds to keep them alive. She scattered the bandits, stood against the Evil Miasma, and shielded the villages. Year by year, people gathered at her side until a true sanctuary took shape. 

Suoming was ready.

When the Evil Miasma finally pressed down upon the city once more, Huating's garrison retreated behind their walls as always, intent not on saving, but only on keeping the desperate out.

Suoming advanced alone to face the <te href=850081>Tacet Discord</te>s surging from the Evil Miasma. Meanwhile, the First Seal brought the Thousandweight Pin to the city gates. As its heavy gears turned, the mechanism pried the massive gates open, and the waiting crowd surged inside. By the time Suoming cut down the final Tacet Discord and stepped through the entrance, the guards were clutching their weapons in terror. They fruitlessly ordered the crowd back, frantically demanding the gates be shut, as if sealing out the world would keep calamity at bay.

Suoming's gaze passed over the anxious crowd, over the sprawling rooftops, and rested on the grand manor towering above the city center. Resplendent amid the storm-tossed ruins, it was the residence of Huating's Chief of Records.

Suoming nodded quietly to herself. The path she had spent years planning had finally taken its first step.
FavorStory_131202_Content:
Suoming knew taking Huating by force and striking down its Chief of Records would be easy. But the city's power play ran deep and tangled. Eliminating the chief would not bring true peace, nor would it win the trust of the people. To destroy his hold, she had to dismantle the pillars supporting his authority.

The first was the city's most arrogant swordsman. Hired at great expense by the Chief of Records, his formidable Forte allowed his blade to slice through iron like mud. Relying on that reputation, he gathered a gang of his own. Many who despised the Chief of Records still trembled before his steel.

When Suoming tracked him to a tavern, his men snickered as they let the petite young woman upstairs: "What does a kid know about drinking?"

Moments later, the second-story window shattered. A single sword hurtled downward, embedding itself in the street below. The gang fell dead silent as they recalled a rumor from the West Gate: the leader who had broken into Huating was a short girl with red hair.

Sobered instantly, the swordsman picked himself up and clashed with Suoming for dozens of rounds before collapsing in exhaustion. Suoming looked down at him. "With skill like yours, why serve evil? Come with me, and we'll wipe out the Evil Miasma."

The swordsman would go on to become the Third Seal. He later admitted that Suoming's grand ambitions had meant little to him at first. What won him over was her willingness to wield absolute power without ever bullying the weak, and the shame that realization stirred in him.

With the chief's blade dealt with, Suoming turned her sights toward the city's other power—its wealthiest merchant clan. For generations, they had amassed inexhaustible fortunes in gold, jade, and brocade. Suoming intended to request their financial support, but upon her visit, she met only the clan’s young lady. The girl asked hesitant questions about the outside world, hiding a secret too heavy to speak aloud.

The First Seal sensed something amiss and advised caution. But when the clan head openly boasted that the Evil Miasma was an opportunity to hoard goods and inflate prices rather than fight, Suoming realized words were pointless. That night, she slipped into the estate and brought the young lady out, learning the truth from her own lips.

The young lady possessed a Forte that could replicate any object, which is in fact, the true secret behind her family's vast fortune. In return, they had kept her imprisoned in the inner halls year after year, forcing her to copy every treasure brought before her. Once the Evil Miasma isolated the city, she became the clan's source of endless treasures. However, years of captivity and constant depletion of her Forte had left her spirit withered.

Suoming told her plainly: "I can free you, but beyond freedom, I have nothing to give." The young lady followed without a second thought.

Years later, whenever the Fourth Seal combed Suoming's long hair, Suoming would often sigh: "I should have simply freed you from that mansion and left it at that. I never should have dragged you into this war."

The Fourth Seal would only shake her head, gather up Suoming's red hair, and hum a quiet verse of her own making. It's her gentle way of giving thanks.
FavorStory_131203_Content:
"How many years has it been since you came to me for the Thousandweight Pin? You kept your word. You brought our people back to Huating and tore down that accursed regime. When the gates opened and the crowds flooded in, the city didn't collapse into chaos. It took on new life. Every bit of it was bought with you and your followers."

"Huating hangs on your every word now. People placed faith in your strength. If you raised a single hand, the whole city could march out and wipe the Evil Miasma away forever."

"But the people behind these walls haven't seen the true calamity. They've never watched black rain drown the soil and wither the earth. They've never seen a loved one eroded past recognition. We have. When I built that pin for you, my only goal was to bring the stranded home. As for defeating the Evil Miasma... I never thought it possible. So don't try to talk me into this again. I won't waste what little strength I have left on a futile cause. And I suggest you... stop chasing it, too."

Suoming looked down at the cup of clear local white tea before her. At the bottom, the emblem of the <te href=850085>Ministry of Development</te> rippled faintly in the brew.

"Huating today isn't my doing alone. The Sixth Seal reads people well and is eloquent beyond measure. It was she who walked the streets, maneuvering deftly among the city's competing factions to earn the people's trust for me. Without her, Huating might never have believed."

"As for the Evil Miasma... there is a physician who, too, has witnessed firsthand the Blight Rain that gnaws bone and the Miasmic Thunder that devours men. Had she surrendered to grief, she would never have probed the nature of the Evil Miasma, nor found a way to combat it. The Fifth Seal has designed a mask capable of resisting the erosion. It awaits only a master craftsman to forge it. Once complete, the Fourth Seal can replicate as many as we require. With those, we will finally be equipped to step into the Blight Rain. But that alone is not enough. I need you to forge a weapon..."

The old man leaned in, waiting for her to continue.

"I will claim its power. In battle, I will weaken the Evil Miasma. Even if I can seize only a wisp of Blight Rain or a thread of Miasmic Thunder, I will seal it within the weapon. My body may have its limits, but I will master its power and find a way to conquer it."

"Then... what kind of weapon do you envision? A sword? A broadblade? With internal mechanisms, it could—"

"An umbrella would be best."

"An umbrella...?" He turned toward the window, gazing into the distance. "I see. Against the Blight Rain that fills the heavens, there is indeed no finer shield than an umbrella to shelter Huating from the storm."

He turned back to Suoming.

"Very well... by your own ranking, where do I stand now? Am I the Seventh Seal?"

Suoming finally raised her teacup, a rare smile gracing her lips.

"I have been holding that place for you all along, Second Seal."
FavorStory_131204_Content:
Not long after the Eighth Seal joined the Covenant, the Vermillion Locks were finally complete. Suoming intended to use them to borrow the other nine Seals' abilities against the Evil Miasma. Yet, having never attempted such a feat, even her calm expression hid a trace of hesitation. For a brief moment, she pondered who should step forward first.

It was the Seventh Seal who volunteered. As a soldier of the <te href=260010>Ministry of War</te>, he insisted it was only right that he take the lead.

When Suoming had originally ousted Huating's Chief of Records, the Ministry of War was freed from its shackles. Most of its soldiers eagerly pledged their support, save for the Seventh Seal, who stubbornly refused to yield. To him, no matter how heinous the chief's crimes, he remained Huating's legitimate authority. Suoming, a mere commoner, had no right to replace him. In those early days, the Seventh Seal opposed her at every turn.

It was only when Suoming escorted him beyond Huating's walls to witness the villages buried beneath the Blight Rain that his resolve shattered. Standing silent among the ruins, he asked her with reddened eyes: "Could Huating truly be spared such tragedy from now on?"

The answer needed no words. From that day forward, the Seventh Seal remained the same steadfast, rule-abiding soldier. He shouldered every burden while insisting that, regardless of Suoming's standing, she was still a citizen of Huating, and it was his duty to protect her.

Accepting his goodwill, Suoming set about sealing a fragment of his frequency into her lock. Moments later, a wisp of mist materialized in her palm—faint, but unmistakably the Seventh Seal's Forte. Simultaneously, the umbrella resting beside her violently shuddered. With a deafening roar, a bolt of crimson-black thunder burst from the umbrella, shattering the courtyard wall.

As the others stood in stunned silence, the Eighth Seal approached the rubble, inspecting the Miasmic Thunder still crackling among the debris.

"Have you ever wielded two powers at once before?" she asked after a quiet pause.

Suoming shook her head.

"A fraction of your mind is constantly spent suppressing the Evil Miasma sealed within your umbrella. Borrowing the Seventh Seal's power alongside it likely triggered the instability."

The Eighth Seal had been brought into the fold by the Seventh Seal. Suoming remembered their first meeting, when the Eighth Seal had bypassed formalities to ask for an exhaustive account of every battle she had fought against the Evil Miasma over the years. They spoke for an entire day, emerging only as dusk faded into night. Afterward, Suoming announced to the others that their plan was complete.

According to the Eighth Seal's design, one would have to venture directly into the swirling black clouds alongside Suoming. The moment Suoming bound the entity, this ally would drive a dagger charged with the Eighth Seal's Forte into its core, forcing it out of the cloud's protection and into an open battle with them all.

Yet every Seal already bore a vital role, and none could be spared for such a perilous gambit.

They needed someone else. One last person...
FavorStory_131205_Content:
"And that is how I came to know the Eighth Seal." Suoming let out a quiet breath, relaxing into the back of her chair. "As for the last one... the Ninth Seal..."

She paused, taking a moment before continuing. "Our meeting was rather ordinary. That day, I was walking down the street alone when I spotted a piece of... floating rice cake."

At that, the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> gave a slight nod. Suoming guessed It might be smiling.

"She was starving, and using her Forte to stay invisible, she was stealing food from the street vendors. So I stood there and waited. When she drifted past me, I stuck out my foot and tripped her. Ninth tumbled to the ground, her invisibility breaking. She turned around to curse me, but stopped dead in her tracks."

"You frightened her."

"Yes." Suoming nodded gently. "My expression must have been terrible, because I knew she was the one—the Ninth Seal. I would have her draw close to the Evil Miasma to strike the killing blow, and then... she would be discovered and killed on the spot."

"And you told her all of this."

"I did." Suoming reached out, her fingers brushing the Vermillion Locks at her side. "But what good did it do? Ninth loved to trail behind me, calling me 'Sister Suoming' at every turn. Whatever I said, she simply nodded along. She even styled her hair to match mine. Within days, she had stopped fearing me entirely. No matter how I reasoned with her, no matter what I told her, she only smiled... afraid of nothing."

Suoming's voice grew softer, fading into silence with a quiet sigh. The Sentinel knew she needed no comfort. Even this grief, she wished to carve deep into her heart. It required no empty words, only a path forward.

"Suoming, I appreciate everything you have done for Huating. But I have nothing left to reward you with. I must even ask you to keep fighting for <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>."

"It's fine." Suoming lifted her head, the gloom vanishing from her eyes. "Tell me what you need of me. Tell me how to ensure the Evil Miasma never threatens Mengzhou again."

"...Very well. Take out the Vermillion Locks. I have one final duty to entrust to you."
FavorWord_131201_Content: For a century, the <te href=260002>Ministry of Sentinel Affairs</te> has spoken on behalf of Hsin the Moon Fox to every <te href=850084>Magistrate</te>. It has held the line, generation after generation, through every crisis <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> has faced. I deeply respect that. Now, with you, the Arbiter, aiding Hsin the Moon Fox in fulfilling Her grand cause, the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> has returned. Remnants of the threat remain, but Mengzhou's future now holds promise.
FavorWord_131202_Content: Beyond <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> affairs, the Ministry also handles astronomy and the calendar. Each city's branch has its own duties, and here in <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>, we—Ahem... Pardon me. You mentioned you weren't very familiar with the Ministry's responsibilities, and I've let myself ramble. In short, we serve the Sentinel. So, Arbiter, if you have need of anything, regardless of what it is, I will see to it.
FavorWord_131203_Content: At Sentinel Hsin's behest, I joined the <te href=260002>Ministry</te> to purge Balanophora's remnants, restore order, and find a path forward. When I first read of the "Arbiter" in the <te href=850117>Grand Library</te>, I wondered what kind of person could guide a <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. Meeting you today... I can tell that you truly live up to your title.
FavorWord_131204_Content: The members of the Ten Seals Covenant were all bound by their obsessions—for a vow, for family, or for me. They said they were drawn to me. That they would follow wherever I led. But... it was their refusal to yield, their unrelenting drive toward what they wanted, that moved me and pushed me forward. Arbiter... you, too, have that effect on me.
FavorWord_131205_Content: Arbiter, if you stood where I did back then, what would you have chosen? Your homeland ravaged, completely alone. Facing it head-on might buy a glimpse of hope, but at the cost of your friends' lives. Apologies. Forget I asked. It's just... I've never been able to let it go. And I just knew you would understand. I just... needed to say it out loud.
FavorWord_131206_Content: Rain clouds gather in the afternoon. A cool breeze, a light drizzle against the eaves… I sit by the window listening, dusting the Vermillion Locks. A somber scene, I know... and yet, I find I quite like it.
FavorWord_131207_Content: As for my major concerns, they are the future of <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> and Balanophora's whereabouts. Beyond that... I cannot say if it's just my imagination, but ever since Sentinel Hsin returned, Mengzhou seems to have more sunny days. My eyes have always been sensitive to light, so this has become a bit of a personal grievance.
FavorWord_131208_Content: The Huating of the past was mired in hardships. Resources were scarce, and fine cuisine a distant dream. The only exception was the local white tea. Truly exceptional. Even now, at the <te href=260002>Ministry</te>, I often find myself craving it. Every time I drink it, I think of them. As if that chapter of my life is... steeped in the color of the tea.
FavorWord_131209_Content: There is nothing I truly dislike. But ever since I mentioned, rather casually, that bitter things do not agree with me, sweets began to appear on my desk with some regularity. I've even heard them call it "feeding the beast." Heh... Youthful antics. I let them have their fun.
FavorWord_131210_Content: I've always dreamed of returning to Huating one day to live in a small cottage. If I am needed, I will help. If not, I will simply watch the world go by in peace, alongside Ninth and the others. That would be enough for me. But of course, that is still a long way off. For now, Hsin and <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>'s future must come first.
FavorWord_131211_Content: "If we fall, Seal Master, lock our frequencies away." Knowing my Forte, that was what they asked of me. I didn't refuse. Together with the Second Seal, we forged the Vermillion Locks. When the work was done, the others gathered around, laughing—praising the Second Seal's craftsmanship, remarking on how the color suited me. They treated them like mere keepsakes, rather than vessels for their final rest. The least I can do now... is not waste what they gave me.
FavorWord_131212_Content: My past? Mm... it's been ages since I last spoke of it. Very well, then. I will share it with you one rainy day.
FavorWord_131213_Content: After our bitter victory over the Evil Miasma, I resented the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> for failing to appear while the black rain fell upon Huating. But when I finally stood before It, seeing <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> as it was and finding It gravely wounded yet still straining to hold the enemies at bay... How could I hold onto my hatred? In the end, I accepted the <te href=260002>Ministry of Sentinel Affairs</te>' mandate and dedicated everything I have to It and to Mengzhou.
FavorWord_131214_Content: If we speak of age, Hsin is actually a bit younger than me. Having assisted the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> for so long, watching Her grow into who She is today naturally carries a certain fondness. Whether it was Her solitary effort to remold the <te href=800053>Civilization Capsule</te> in the past, or Her finally stepping into Her role as the Sentinel now... Hsin has never once let the Sentinel down.
FavorWord_131215_Content: When I took up the Intendant's mantle, the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> and I made a pact: It would find the root of the Evil Miasma's spawning, and I would end it with my own hands. Now that I know it all stems from Balanophora's wounding of the Sentinel... her fate is sealed.
FavorWord_131216_Content: She was a pitiful child. The Evil Miasma had left her stealing food on the streets, and out of all people, I was the one who discovered her ability to turn invisible. If I were to start talking about how she might've lived longer if she'd never met me, she'd only be upset... How I wish to hear her calling me Sister Suoming again.
FavorWord_131217_Content:
I was wondering what blessing would be fitting for an Intendant to offer the Arbiter. In the end, I realized that words from the heart are what matters most on this special day.
So, happy birthday, Arbiter. The <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te> <te href=260002>Ministry of Sentinel Affairs</te> will always have your back. May all be well in Hsin's keeping, and may your journey ahead be safe.
FavorWord_131218_Content:
Ninth Seal: Sister Suoming!
Suoming: Mm.
Ninth Seal: Whoa!
Suoming: Look.
Suoming: Mm...
FavorWord_131220_Content: Hm? You don't even think to call me Seal Master? Hehe, just kidding.
FavorWord_131221_Content: Suoming, Seal Master of the Ten Seals Covenant, and Intendant of <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>'s <te href=260002>Ministry of Sentinel Affairs</te>. Any enemy of Mengzhou is an enemy of mine.
FavorWord_131222_Content: When the Blight Rain and Miasmic Thunder fade, what remains is only... locked obsessions.
FavorWord_131223_Content: To battle? Alright. May all be well in Hsin's keeping.
FavorWord_131226_Content: I'd almost forgotten this feeling of being honed.
FavorWord_131227_Content: Each form of the Nine Shadows demanded rigorous practice to master. Ah, those old training days are coming back to me.
FavorWord_131228_Content: The Third Seal taught me the sword. The Seventh, the spear. And now, you've left your mark on me as well.
FavorWord_131229_Content: This is the quiet at the center. Arbiter, for a breath, the weight of my obsessions lifted. But only for a moment.
FavorWord_131230_Content: I know the Ten Seals Covenant fell to the Evil Miasma, but I still carry the guilt. It was my weakness that led to that tragedy. I will never let history repeat itself.
FavorWord_131249_Content: I put my body on the line.
FavorWord_131257_Content: A mere smudge on the hem.
FavorWord_131260_Content: Finally... I'll see you all again.
FavorWord_131265_Content: Canopy out, I'll take it from here.
FavorWord_131271_Content: Mm, you'll have use for this.

HelpText_694_Content:
Replay Mode
1. You can replay any Main Quest you've already completed using Replay Mode.
2. Your progress is automatically saved when you exit Replay Mode. You can resume from where you left off in the Journey Log, or reset your progress manually.
3. You'll have a separate Backpack while in Replay Mode. Items obtained during Replay Mode only exist there and won't carry over.
4. Some features are unavailable while in Replay Mode.
ExploreProgress_84_TypeName: Tales from the Capsule: Ashen Fox
ExploreProgress_78_Desc_Text: The larger and more far-reaching anomalies of the Heart of Flames are all sealed inside an Inner Threshold, and their repair progress is recorded by a broken Dream Fox Statue. Take the Heart of Flames Key from the statue to enter the matching Inner Threshold. Once the anomaly has been repaired, set the Realm Key back in place and the Dream Fox Statue will be reconstructed and restored to what it was.
ExploreProgress_79_Desc_Text: The larger and more far-reaching anomalies of the Heart of Frost are all sealed inside an Inner Threshold, and their repair progress is recorded by a fallen Dream Kernel Puppet. Take the Heart of Frost Key from the puppet to enter the matching Inner Threshold. Once the anomaly has been repaired, set the Realm Key back in place and the Dream Kernel Puppet will be mended and move once again.
ExploreProgress_80_Desc_Text: The larger and more far-reaching anomalies of the Heart of Bloom are all sealed inside an Inner Threshold, and their repair progress is recorded by a withered Dream Jade Rootstone. Take the Heart of Bloom Key from the rootstone to enter the matching Inner Threshold. Once the anomaly has been repaired, set the Realm Key back in place and the Dream Jade Rootstone will proliferate with it and grow into a Dream Jade Tree.
ExploreProgress_81_Desc_Text: Some areas contain more than one anomaly, with Reconstruction, Stasis, and Proliferation Anomalies blending into one another. Only Rover, who bears the Prism of Fate, can repair such anomalies using different types of Realm Keys.
ExploreProgress_82_Desc_Text: Smaller anomalies whose spread has already been contained are scattered throughout the Simulacrum Nexus. You can repair them with the matching Realm Key or with the help of the Nexus Fox Shadow via the Shadow Binder.
ExploreProgress_83_Desc_Text: At Chenghuai's request, you travel to the Heart of Flames to investigate an anomalous disturbance. Along the way, you become acquainted with a dancer named Mashan and, together with him, step into a strange, uncanny "Waking Moon Festival." There, the two of you rescue several of Mashan's junior sisters, yet the anomaly is far from resolved. At last, within the Lantern Carriage, you grasp the key to the anomaly and break through the delusion buried deep in the human heart...
ExploreProgress_84_Desc_Text:
Guided by Youfang, you recover an unusual Kernel from the wreckage of an Autopuppet in the Heart of Frost, and it seems able to open a separate, secret space.
Everything that unfolds inside feels strangely familiar, and yet has nothing at all to do with the real world. Whatever it may be, all it holds is only a phantom of some distant past.
ExploreProgress_85_Desc_Text:
A mysterious girl named Xuanqing asks for your help collecting the Feeling Capsule shards scattered by the Tuntun.
As you go deeper into this matter, a story surfaces about Hsin the Moon Fox, the Sentinel of the past.
AreaReportContent_Text101:
Project Celestial was proposed because Yuan Fortress, a human tech-based mechanical citadel built by the Ministry of Development and Zhuojun Atelier, could no longer keep the enemies at bay.
Hsin the Moon Fox was therefore forced to propose building Xuanfang Hold, a new fortress based on ███ technology this time, to divert the Tacet Discord hordes away and eventually contain them.
The project's first step was for Hsin the Moon Fox to provide the necessary ███ technology, which humans would then use to construct the Hold.
The second step, however, would require the builders to transform into Celestials—pure frequency-based lifeforms perpetually stationed within Xuanfang Hold's boundary, responsible for the Hold's operations and never able to leave. This was the only way to keep the technology safe, and it required each builder's own willing consent to become a Celestial.
The name "Celestial" derived from an opening line in Comprehensive Mirror for Historians: "...A celestial being descended, wielding the limitless might of the universe, embracing the inaugural Echo within..." The project was named so in the hope that, like the Golden-Eyed One, the Celestials could fulfill the task of building the Hold and safeguarding Huanglong.
...
Both the Court of Savantae delegate and Flowerveil Puppet, head of Zhuojun Atelier's main branch, accepted the project's unusual requirements.
To the City Hall's surprise, Hsin the Moon Fox entrusted the project not to Zhuojun Atelier, the builder of Yuan Fortress and expert in defense fortifications, but to the Court of Savantae instead.
...
AreaReportTitle_Text101: Minutes of the Meeting: On Project Celestial
AreaReportContent_Text102:
...
A significant number of Censure Courts lie scattered across the mountain range surrounding Xuanfang Hold. The Censure Cages inside these Courts imprison the Tacet Discords that once swarmed into the Hold from Norfall Barrens.
Under the control of their respective Celestials, the Cages inside a Censure Court periodically open, releasing the Tacet Discords into the courtyard. There, the decorative structures transform into Autopuppets and systematically eliminate them.
When Xuanfang Hold was first completed, seventeen mountain peaks encircled it, each with a large Censure Court perched at its summit. The Celestials entrusted with these Courts carried out their duties without fail, clearing out Tacet Discords in regular cycles.
Yet, the day inevitably comes when all Tacet Discords within a Court have been fully eradicated, and that will mark the end of that facility. Once its duty is fulfilled, the Court initiates its self-destruction protocol to preserve the secrets of its technology not of this age. The Celestial administrators, their task complete, will also meet their end.
Today, more than half of the 17 peaks have collapsed, and only a few Censure Courts remain in operation. On those empty peaks, no traces of a Censure Court, a Tacet Discord, or a Celestial remain, as if none of them ever existed. All that's left is the rustling of leaves in the wind. Perhaps one day, even the last Censure Court will fall silent. Will that mark the same fate for Xuanfang Hold, and for every Celestial within it?
...
